docs.name: 工程導論
docs.text: 工程導論課程大綱 一、本課程前兩週為工學院大一學生之共通課程，隨後進入四大主題課程（每主 題各為期三週），由不同學系教師分別講授。 二、工程導論課程之授課教師如下： ◼ 化學工程學系－林育正老師 ◼ 動力機械工程學系－李明蒼老師 ◼ 材料科學與工程學系－許瑋麟老師 ◼ 工業工程與工程管理學系－洪一峯老師：114/9/3 更新成績考核。 三、成績考核： ◼ 各主題課程各佔總成績之 25%，合計為 100%。 ◼ 各主題課程之成績評量方式略有不同，請參閱各授課教師之課程大綱以 了解詳細規定。 國立清華大學課程大綱－化工系 林育正教授 課程簡述 本課程旨在引導工學院大一學生建立低碳與永續能源的基本認知，涵蓋再生能源、發電碳排放、 碳足跡計算等主題。學生將學習如何分析不同能源形式的碳排強度，並進行簡易計算與小組討 論。透過實作與案例探討，培養學生對低碳轉型的理解與工程應用敏感度。 課程內容「中文暨英文關鍵字」 低碳能源 Low-carbon energy;碳足跡計算 Carbon footprint calculation;永續發展 Sustainable development;發電碳排 Electricity emissions;工程減碳 Decarbonization in engineering 課程大綱 ● 課程說明(Course Description) 本課程透過六堂課引導學生了解低碳與永續能源的核心議題，從基礎能源知識出發，進一步探討 碳排放與碳足跡的計算方式。學生將學習如何查找資料並估算各種能源與電力來源的碳排強度， 並進行小組簡報與討論，以提升跨領域整合與溝通能力。 ● 指定用書(Text Books)：無指定教科書，教師將提供講義及補充資料。 ● 參考書籍(References)：無指定教科書，教師將提供講義及補充資料。 ● 教學方式(Teaching Method)：講授與互動討論; 小組作業與簡報; 線上資料查詢與實作練習 ● 教學進度(Syllabus) 1.低碳能源與電力概論 2. LCA 碳足跡計算方法介紹 3. 碳足跡計算結果與分析報告 ● 成績考核(Evaluation)：書面報告（60%）及口頭報告（40%），佔總成績 25% ● 採用下列何項 AI 使用規則(Indicate which of the following options you use to manage student use of the AI) 有條件開放，請註明如何使用生成式 AI 於課程產出 Conditionally open; please specify how generative AI will be used in course output 可參考下列網頁範例 See the following web page for examples. https://curricul.site.nthu.edu.tw/p/404-1208-248357.php?Lang=zh-tw 國立清華大學課程大綱－動機系 李明蒼教授 課程簡述 機械工程涵蓋四個基礎專業領域：熱流與能源、機電控制、機械結構與材料力學，以及設計製 造。機械工程技術的應用範圍廣泛，包含光機電、生醫、動力、能源、微奈米科技等。本課程 將介紹機械工程的專業與應用，以及討論近年快速興起的人工智慧以及永續發展目標 (Sustainable Development Goals, SDGs)等議題與機械工程的相關性。 課程內容「中文暨英文關鍵字」 機械工程(Mechanical Engineering)，光機電系統(Opto-mechatronic systems)，人工智慧 (Artificial Intelligence)，永續發展目標(Sustainable Development Goals, SDGs) 課程大綱 ● 課程說明(Course Description) 本課程將介紹動力機械工程的專業與應用，以及討論近年快速興起的人工智慧以及永續發展目 標(Sustainable Development Goals, SDGs)等議題與動力機械工程的相關性。 ● 指定用書(Text Books)：無 ● 參考書籍(References)：課程投影片 ● 教學方式(Teaching Method)：課堂講授 ● 教學進度(Syllabus) 1. Power Mechanical Engineering: Fields, Scales and Applications 2. Virtual vs. Reality; PME: Now, the Future, and Sustainability 3. Mini project ● 成績考核(Evaluation)：小實作專題（100%），佔總成績 25% ● 採用下列何項 AI 使用規則(Indicate which of the following options you use to manage student use of the AI) 有條件開放，請註明如何使用生成式 AI 於課程產出 Conditionally open; please specify how generative AI will be used in course output 可參考下列網頁範例 See the following web page for examples. https://curricul.site.nthu.edu.tw/p/404-1208-248357.php?Lang=zh-tw 國立清華大學課程大綱－材料系 許瑋麟教授 課程簡述 本課程首先介紹材料科學與材料工程的關聯性、材料科學與工程與在科技與產業上的角 色、能源及環境永續發展的關係。接著介紹材料科學與材料工程的基礎：材料科學工程學習材 料之結構、性質與製程，並研究三者之間的關聯性。材料結構包括晶體結構與微結構，材料性 質涵蓋機械性質、物理性質與化學性質，材料製程則包括熔煉、鍛造、軋延、熱處理等傳統製 程。第三部分則進一步介紹數種現代工業中重要材料技術與實際應用情形: 如積層製造技術 (如 選擇性雷射熔融與電子束熔融等)、以及熱噴塗技術 (如電漿噴塗與高速氧燃燒噴塗) 等進階製 程。這些技術能應用於國防與航太元件、能源轉換裝置、生醫植入物與高溫防護塗層等領域， 展示了現代材料技術如何支援高階產業發展並因應極端環境需求。最後介紹半導體材料相關製 程，以晶圓代工產業之乾蝕刻製程為例，體現材料科學對現代科技發展的深遠影響。 課程內容「中文暨英文關鍵字」 材料結構，材料製程，材料性質 (機械性質、物理性質、化學性質) ，積層製造技術，熱噴塗 技術，半導體材料製程 Material Structure, Material Processing, Material Properties (Mechanical, Physical, Chemical), Additive Manufacturing Technology, Thermal Spray Technology, Semiconductor Material Processing 課程大綱 ● 課程說明(Course Description) 本課程介紹材料科學與工程的基礎概念，包括材料的結構、性質與製程及其相互關係，並延伸 至現代材料技術如積層製造、熱噴塗與半導體製程。課程同時探討材料技術在國防、航太、能 源、生醫等高階應用中的重要角色，說明其對科技與永續發展的關鍵影響。 ● 指定用書(Text Books) Materials, 3rd Edition, Engineering, Science, Processing and Design, eBook ISBN: 9780080982816 ● 參考書籍(References) Thermal Spray Fundamentals, eBook ISBN: 978-0-387-68991-3 Dry Etching Technology for Semiconductors, eBook ISBN: 978-3-319-10294-8 ● 教學方式(Teaching Method) 投影片上課 ● 教學進度(Syllabus) 1. 材料的重要性 (Importance of Materials in human society) 2. 材料科學與工程基礎 (The basics of Materials Science & Engineering) 3. 進階材料技術應用 (Applications of Advanced Materials Technology) ● 成績考核(Evaluation) docs.text: 工程導論課程大綱 一、本課程前兩週為工學院大一學生之共通課程，隨後進入四大主題課程（每主 題各為期三週），由不同學系教師分別講授。 二、工程導論課程之授課教師如下： ◼ 化學工程學系－林育正老師 ◼ 動力機械工程學系－李明蒼老師 ◼ 材料科學與工程學系－許瑋麟老師 ◼ 工業工程與工程管理學系－洪一峯老師：114/9/3 更新成績考核。 三、成績考核： ◼ 各主題課程各佔總成績之 25%，合計為 100%。 ◼ 各主題課程之成績評量方式略有不同，請參閱各授課教師之課程大綱以 了解詳細規定。 國立清華大學課程大綱－化工系 林育正教授 課程簡述 本課程旨在引導工學院大一學生建立低碳與永續能源的基本認知，涵蓋再生能源、發電碳排放、 碳足跡計算等主題。學生將學習如何分析不同能源形式的碳排強度，並進行簡易計算與小組討 論。透過實作與案例探討，培養學生對低碳轉型的理解與工程應用敏感度。 課程內容「中文暨英文關鍵字」 低碳能源 Low-carbon energy;碳足跡計算 Carbon footprint calculation;永續發展 Sustainable development;發電碳排 Electricity emissions;工程減碳 Decarbonization in engineering 課程大綱 ● 課程說明(Course Description) 本課程透過六堂課引導學生了解低碳與永續能源的核心議題，從基礎能源知識出發，進一步探討 碳排放與碳足跡的計算方式。學生將學習如何查找資料並估算各種能源與電力來源的碳排強度， 並進行小組簡報與討論，以提升跨領域整合與溝通能力。 ● 指定用書(Text Books)：無指定教科書，教師將提供講義及補充資料。 ● 參考書籍(References)：無指定教科書，教師將提供講義及補充資料。 ● 教學方式(Teaching Method)：講授與互動討論; 小組作業與簡報; 線上資料查詢與實作練習 ● 教學進度(Syllabus) 1.低碳能源與電力概論 2. LCA 碳足跡計算方法介紹 3. 碳足跡計算結果與分析報告 ● 成績考核(Evaluation)：書面報告（60%）及口頭報告（40%），佔總成績 25% ● 採用下列何項 AI 使用規則(Indicate which of the following options you use to manage student use of the AI) 有條件開放，請註明如何使用生成式 AI 於課程產出 Conditionally open; please specify how generative AI will be used in course output 可參考下列網頁範例 See the following web page for examples. https://curricul.site.nthu.edu.tw/p/404-1208-248357.php?Lang=zh-tw 國立清華大學課程大綱－動機系 李明蒼教授 課程簡述 機械工程涵蓋四個基礎專業領域：熱流與能源、機電控制、機械結構與材料力學，以及設計製 造。機械工程技術的應用範圍廣泛，包含光機電、生醫、動力、能源、微奈米科技等。本課程 將介紹機械工程的專業與應用，以及討論近年快速興起的人工智慧以及永續發展目標 (Sustainable Development Goals, SDGs)等議題與機械工程的相關性。 課程內容「中文暨英文關鍵字」 機械工程(Mechanical Engineering)，光機電系統(Opto-mechatronic systems)，人工智慧 (Artificial Intelligence)，永續發展目標(Sustainable Development Goals, SDGs) 課程大綱 ● 課程說明(Course Description) 本課程將介紹動力機械工程的專業與應用，以及討論近年快速興起的人工智慧以及永續發展目 標(Sustainable Development Goals, SDGs)等議題與動力機械工程的相關性。 ● 指定用書(Text Books)：無 ● 參考書籍(References)：課程投影片 ● 教學方式(Teaching Method)：課堂講授 ● 教學進度(Syllabus) 1. 許瑋麟教授 課程簡述 本課程首先介紹材料科學與材料工程的關聯性、材料科學與工程與在科技與產業上的角 色、能源及環境永續發展的關係。接著介紹材料科學與材料工程的基礎：材料科學工程學習材 料之結構、性質與製程，並研究三者之間的關聯性。材料結構包括晶體結構與微結構，材料性 質涵蓋機械性質、物理性質與化學性質，材料製程則包括熔煉、鍛造、軋延、熱處理等傳統製 程。第三部分則進一步介紹數種現代工業中重要材料技術與實際應用情形: 如積層製造技術 (如 選擇性雷射熔融與電子束熔融等)、以及熱噴塗技術 (如電漿噴塗與高速氧燃燒噴塗) 等進階製 程。這些技術能應用於國防與航太元件、能源轉換裝置、生醫植入物與高溫防護塗層等領域， 展示了現代材料技術如何支援高階產業發展並因應極端環境需求。最後介紹半導體材料相關製 程，以晶圓代工產業之乾蝕刻製程為例，體現材料科學對現代科技發展的深遠影響。 課程內容「中文暨英文關鍵字」 材料結構，材料製程，材料性質 (機械性質、物理性質、化學性質) ，積層製造技術，熱噴塗 技術，半導體材料製程 Material Structure, Material Processing, Material Properties (Mechanical, Physical, Chemical), Additive Manufacturing Technology, Thermal Spray Technology, Semiconductor Material Processing 課程大綱 ● 課程說明(Course Description) 本課程介紹材料科學與工程的基礎概念，包括材料的結構、性質與製程及其相互關係，並延伸 至現代材料技術如積層製造、熱噴塗與半導體製程。課程同時探討材料技術在國防、航太、能 源、生醫等高階應用中的重要角色，說明其對科技與永續發展的關鍵影響。 ● 指定用書(Text Books) Materials, 3rd Edition, Engineering, Science, Processing and Design, eBook ISBN: 9780080982816 ● docs.text: 工程導論課程大綱 一、本課程前兩週為工學院大一學生之共通課程，隨後進入四大主題課程（每主 題各為期三週），由不同學系教師分別講授。 二、工程導論課程之授課教師如下： ◼ 化學工程學系－林育正老師 ◼ 動力機械工程學系－李明蒼老師 ◼ 材料科學與工程學系－許瑋麟老師 ◼ 工業工程與工程管理學系－洪一峯老師：114/9/3 更新成績考核。 三、成績考核： ◼ 各主題課程各佔總成績之 25%，合計為 100%。 ◼ 各主題課程之成績評量方式略有不同，請參閱各授課教師之課程大綱以 了解詳細規定。 國立清華大學課程大綱－化工系 林育正教授 課程簡述 本課程旨在引導工學院大一學生建立低碳與永續能源的基本認知，涵蓋再生能源、發電碳排放、 碳足跡計算等主題。學生將學習如何分析不同能源形式的碳排強度，並進行簡易計算與小組討 論。透過實作與案例探討，培養學生對低碳轉型的理解與工程應用敏感度。 課程內容「中文暨英文關鍵字」 低碳能源 Low-carbon energy;碳足跡計算 Carbon footprint calculation;永續發展 Sustainable development;發電碳排 Electricity emissions;工程減碳 Decarbonization in engineering 課程大綱 ● 課程說明(Course Description) 本課程透過六堂課引導學生了解低碳與永續能源的核心議題，從基礎能源知識出發，進一步探討 碳排放與碳足跡的計算方式。學生將學習如何查找資料並估算各種能源與電力來源的碳排強度， 並進行小組簡報與討論，以提升跨領域整合與溝通能力。 ● 指定用書(Text Books)：無指定教科書，教師將提供講義及補充資料。 ● 參考書籍(References)：無指定教科書，教師將提供講義及補充資料。 ● 教學方式(Teaching Method)：講授與互動討論; 小組作業與簡報; 線上資料查詢與實作練習 ● 教學進度(Syllabus) 1.低碳能源與電力概論 2. LCA 碳足跡計算方法介紹 3. 碳足跡計算結果與分析報告 ● 成績考核(Evaluation)：書面報告（60%）及口頭報告（40%），佔總成績 25% ● 採用下列何項 AI 使用規則(Indicate which of the following options you use to manage student use of the AI) 有條件開放，請註明如何使用生成式 AI 於課程產出 Conditionally open; please specify how generative AI will be used in course output 可參考下列網頁範例 See the following web page for examples. https://curricul.site.nthu.edu.tw/p/404-1208-248357.php?Lang=zh-tw 國立清華大學課程大綱－動機系 李明蒼教授 課程簡述 機械工程涵蓋四個基礎專業領域：熱流與能源、機電控制、機械結構與材料力學，以及設計製 造。機械工程技術的應用範圍廣泛，包含光機電、生醫、動力、能源、微奈米科技等。本課程 將介紹機械工程的專業與應用，以及討論近年快速興起的人工智慧以及永續發展目標 (Sustainable Development Goals, SDGs)等議題與機械工程的相關性。 課程內容「中文暨英文關鍵字」 機械工程(Mechanical Engineering)，光機電系統(Opto-mechatronic systems)，人工智慧 (Artificial Intelligence)，永續發展目標(Sustainable Development Goals, SDGs) 課程大綱 ● 課程說明(Course Description) 本課程將介紹動力機械工程的專業與應用，以及討論近年快速興起的人工智慧以及永續發展目 標(Sustainable Development Goals, SDGs)等議題與動力機械工程的相關性。 ● 指定用書(Text Books)：無 ● 參考書籍(References)：課程投影片 ● 教學方式(Teaching Method)：課堂講授 ● 教學進度(Syllabus) 1. Power Mechanical Engineering: Fields, Scales and Applications 2. Virtual vs. Reality; PME: Now, the Future, and Sustainability 3. Mini project ● 成績考核(Evaluation)：小實作專題（100%），佔總成績 25% ● 採用下列何項 AI 使用規則(Indicate which of the following options you use to manage student use of the AI) 有條件開放，請註明如何使用生成式 AI 於課程產出 Conditionally open; please specify how generative AI will be used in course output 可參考下列網頁範例 See the following web page for examples. https://curricul.site.nthu.edu.tw/p/404-1208-248357.php?Lang=zh-tw 國立清華大學課程大綱－材料系 許瑋麟教授 課程簡述 本課程首先介紹材料科學與材料工程的關聯性、材料科學與工程與在科技與產業上的角 色、能源及環境永續發展的關係。接著介紹材料科學與材料工程的基礎：材料科學工程學習材 料之結構、性質與製程，並研究三者之間的關聯性。材料結構包括晶體結構與微結構，材料性 質涵蓋機械性質、物理性質與化學性質，材料製程則包括熔煉、鍛造、軋延、熱處理等傳統製 程。第三部分則進一步介紹數種現代工業中重要材料技術與實際應用情形: 如積層製造技術 (如 選擇性雷射熔融與電子束熔融等)、以及熱噴塗技術 (如電漿噴塗與高速氧燃燒噴塗) 等進階製 程。這些技術能應用於國防與航太元件、能源轉換裝置、生醫植入物與高溫防護塗層等領域， 展示了現代材料技術如何支援高階產業發展並因應極端環境需求。最後介紹半導體材料相關製 程，以晶圓代工產業之乾蝕刻製程為例，體現材料科學對現代科技發展的深遠影響。 課程內容「中文暨英文關鍵字」 材料結構，材料製程，材料性質 (機械性質、物理性質、化學性質) ，積層製造技術，熱噴塗 技術，半導體材料製程 Material Structure, Material Processing, Material Properties (Mechanical, Physical, Chemical), Additive Manufacturing Technology, Thermal Spray Technology, Semiconductor Material Processing 課程大綱 ● 課程說明(Course Description) 本課程介紹材料科學與工程的基礎概念，包括材料的結構、性質與製程及其相互關係，並延伸 至現代材料技術如積層製造、熱噴塗與半導體製程。課程同時探討材料技術在國防、航太、能 源、生醫等高階應用中的重要角色，說明其對科技與永續發展的關鍵影響。 ● 指定用書(Text Books) Materials, 3rd Edition, Engineering, Science, Processing and Design, eBook ISBN: 9780080982816 ● 參考書籍(References) Thermal Spray Fundamentals, eBook ISBN: 978-0-387-68991-3 Dry Etching Technology for Semiconductors, eBook ISBN: 978-3-319-10294-8 ● 教學方式(Teaching Method) 投影片上課 ● 教學進度(Syllabus) 1. 材料的重要性 (Importance of Materials in human society) 2. 材料科學與工程基礎 (The basics of Materials Science & Engineering) 3. 進階材料技術應用 (Applications of Advanced Materials Technology) ● 成績考核(Evaluation) docs.name: 經濟學原理一
docs.text: 經濟學原理一 課程大綱 Instructor: 余朝恩 Email: chaoenyu@mx.nthu.edu.tw 本門課程簡介經濟學的基本原理。經濟學不是一門教人自私的社會科學，而 是研究個人、廠商和組織如何做選擇的社會科學。 本課程主要介紹理性消費者和廠商決策的最適化，以及市場如何運作和達成 均衡的原理。本課程也將介紹在不同市場結構下，廠商的訂價和合作競爭等 決策行為。最後，本課程將分析政府在經濟社會運作中可以和應該扮演的角 色（或者不扮演）。鑑於近年來各國對公平、正義的呼聲日益高漲，本課程 也將針對部分大眾對於經濟學的迷思進行答辯和剖析。本門課程也將以數理 套裝軟體和 Python 程式設計展示經濟分析常用的繪圖和運算。 評分方式： 兩次期中考(10/13 和 11/17)，一次期末考(12/15)，佔總成績 80%; 課堂小考佔 20%，缺考扣分。 教科書： Hubbard and O'Brien (2022), Economics, Pearson Education Limited, 8th edition (滄海圖書) Steven Pinker (2022), 理性：人類最有效的認知工具, 商周出版社. 考試規則： (1) 考試時禁止使用手機。 (2) 請同學務必參加考試。考試時應按時進入試場，遲到逾 20 分 鐘者不得入場，遲到或缺席者以「缺考」處理。 生成式人工智慧倫理聲明：禁止使用 經仔細考量後，本課程授課教師認為不宜於此門課程當中使用生成式人工智慧於課堂學習當 中。因本課程的內容於生成式 AI 中尚有諸多錯誤，且容易影響學生對基礎核心知識之判讀。 根據本校公布之佈的「大學教育場域 AI 協作、共學與素養培養指引」，本門課程採取禁止使 用，以下為相關的監管機制 • 修讀本門課程之學生應注意本門課不得繳交使用生成式人工智慧所產出的作業、報告 或個人心得。若經查核發現，教師、學校或相關單位有權重新針對作業或報告重新評 分或不予計分。 • 修讀本課程之學生於選課時視為同意以上倫理聲明。

docs.text: 1 11410ECON100102 Principles of Economics I Instructor: Prof. Hui-chen Wang (王惠貞) Fall 2025 (114上) Office: 台積館 810 Classroom: TSMC (台積館) 224 Office Hours: TBA Lecture Time: R5R6R7 (150 minutes on Thu 13:20-16:20) Email: huichenwang@mx.nthu.edu.tw Principles of Economics (I) Syllabus (Preliminary) Course Description This course offers an introduction to microeconomic theories and applications. We will discuss the basic economic concepts and theories concerning market functions and the choices of individual decision makers, including people and firms. This course is offered in English. Learning Objectives After successful completion of this course, students will be able to (1) define and discuss the key economic concepts including the basic principles of rational choices, (2) identify and analyze the fundamental microeconomic issues using verbal, graphical and simple mathematical techniques, and (3) apply economic thinking to daily decisions and events. Course Requirements and Policies Examinations There will be an in-class midterm exam and a final exam. The exams are not strictly cumulative; however, previously tested concepts may be covered in the final exam to the extent that they are the bases of a current topic. The format of the examinations will be a combination of multiple-choice questions and short written problems. The midterm and final exam dates will be announced in the first class meeting. All students must take the exams at their scheduled times. Make-up exam policy: No make-up exam will be given for the midterm exam. The weight for a missed midterm exam, if excused, will be reallocated to the final exam. Make-up exam for the final exam will only be given under unexpected, extremely unusual and justifiable circumstances. Students who miss an exam due to an unexpected emergency should inform professor Wang within 24 hours from the missed exam and provide official documentation for the absence within one week. Pop quizzes: Short, unannounced quizzes will be given throughout the semester. For each student, the lowest score of all quizzes given in the semester will be excluded from the calculation of quiz average. It is important to note that NO makeup quiz may be given for any reason since the one quiz waiver (indicated above) already takes into account the occasional illness or unexpected personal situations that may prevent you from taking a quiz. However, under extremely unusual and justifiable circumstances 2 (official documentation required), extra quiz waivers may be granted on a case- by-case basis, at professor Wang’s discretion. Homework assignments: Problem sets will be assigned throughout the course. Your homework will not be graded; however, all students are expected to complete all assignments in a timely manner for effective learning and preparation of the tests. Attendance and Participation: Students are required to attend the lectures regularly. Participation in class discussion is expected and appreciated. You will be held responsible for all assignments, tests, and any announcement made in class, even in your absence. Your attendance and participation may affect your overall course grades on the margin. Grading Course letter grades will be assigned based on the weighted sums of the graded components of your performance: Midterm exam: 40 % Final exam: 45 % Quizzes: 15% The grades are not negotiable. No individual request for extra credit work will be taken. Textbook Glenn P. Hubbard and Anthony P. O'Brien (2022), Economics: Global Edition 8/e. Pearson. (ISBN-13: 978-1292430645) Our class discussion and test coverage may include some material not from this textbook. Class Communication and Resources TA Office hours: In addition to Professor Wang’s office hours (see header), there will be weekly office hours held by one of our teaching assistants. The time and location of the TA office hours will be announced separately on eeclass (see next). eeclass: In addition to in-class communication, email and office hours, we will utilize the eeclass digital course tool maintained by the university. Class announcements, lecture slides (student version), homework assignments, answer keys, grades and other course-related material will be posted. You are expected to check your email as well as your eeclass account regularly to remain up to date. Note: The posted version of the lecture slides will be incomplete by design with spaces to be filled out in class. You are expected to print out the slides in advance and bring them to the class. Keep in mind that the lecture slides will not remove the need for your class attendance and note taking efforts Regulation on AI Usage The usage of AI is irrelevant in this course since student learning will be assessed by in-class closed-book tests. 3 Tentative Course Outline Topics Textbook Chapters 1. Introduction 2. How Market Works: Demand and Supply; Market Equilibrium; Economic Efficiency and Government Intervention; Elasticity 3. Consumer Choices: Budget, utility, and consumer’s demand 4. Production Theory: Output and cost 5. Market Structure and Profit Maximization: Perfect Competition; Monopoly and Price discrimination; Monopolistic Competition and Oligopoly 1-2 3, 4, 6 10 11 12, 15, 13-14

docs.text: ECON100103 經濟學原理一 課程大綱 Instructor: 李翎帆 Office: 台積館 703 Email: lilf@mx.nthu.edu.tw Office Hours: 週二 12:00-13:30 經濟學是研究理性個人如何做選擇的社會科學。本課程主要介紹消費者與廠商如何做決策。在消 費者理論方面，本課程將探討影響消費者購買行為之因素與其決策準則。在生產者理論方面，將 介紹在不同市場結構下，廠商的生產與定價決策行為。此外，也將分析政府在經濟社會所扮演之 角色。 主要用書: M. Parkin, Economics, 14th edition (雙葉書廊) 評分方式 : 本學期總成績由一次期中考試(50%)和一次期末考試(50%)評定，時間如下： 期中考: 2025/11/03。 期末考: 2025/12/15。 考試規則 : (1) 考試時禁止使用手機。 (2) 請同學務必參加考試 ，考試當天缺席者以 〝缺考 〞處理。 若遇不可抗拒之因素需 請事假 ，於考試前向授課教師申請補考，無法事後申請補考。 課程相關連結 : 清華大學 eLearn https://eeclass.nthu.edu.tw/ 授課內容 : 1. 經濟學基本概念 (Ch.1, ch.2) 2. 供需均衡與彈性 (Ch.3) ➢ 分析在完全競爭市場下，商品 (或服務) 的價格如何決定 3. 價格彈性(ch.4) ➢ 價格變動與消費數量之間的關係 4. 效率與平等(ch.5) ➢如何分配資源 5. 市場機能與政府干預 (Ch.6) ➢市場管制 ➢最低工資 6. 消費者決策 (ch.8, ch.9) ➢效用和需求 ➢消費者在既有的資源(財富)下，如何選擇市場上個別商品的消費量 7. 生產者決策 (ch.10, ch.11) ➢ 介紹廠商生產理論與成本分析 8. 競爭與獨佔 (ch.12, ch.13) ➢ 介紹在不同市場結構下廠商的訂價決策行為 9. 外部性與公共財 (ch.16, ch.17) ➢ 分析在市場經濟發生缺陷時(市場失靈)，政府可以介入市場提升社會福利 ➢ 分析政府設立關稅對一國福利之影響

docs.text: 經濟學原理一 Fall 2025 教師: 唐震宏 E-mail: jhtang@mx.nthu.edu.tw Office: TSMC727 有關加簽的常見問題 1. 如果有加簽需求的同學，請在加簽期間登入學校系統提出要求。 2. 教室有容量限制，我能加簽的名額等於教室容量減去已選課人數。如果有加簽需求的 人數超過可加簽人數，原則上以大四同學優先，再來依序是大三、大二、大一。若同 一順位要求加簽人數超過空位 (例如有 N 個空位，但有 N+1 位大四同學要加簽)，則 以亂數抽籤決定。 課程概述 本課程目的在介紹經濟學的基本分析工具與核心議題。內容以市場機制之運作為主軸， 包括經濟學的基本概念，如機會成本、比較利益、專業分工，以及個體經濟學的議題，如 供給與需求、市場均衡、消費者行為、生產者行為、和產業組織等。 課程目標 本課預期能協助同學 (1) 瞭解經濟學基本原理；(2) 應用經濟理論分析經濟問題。 參考用書 1. Mankiw, N.G. (2024), Principles of Economics, 10th Edition, Cengage Asian Edition. 授課方式 1. 授課以教師講解為主，歡迎同學隨時發問並提出意見。 2. The lectures are taught in Chinese (Mandarin). Students who have diffi- culties in understanding Chinese are advised not to take this course. 1 3. 上課投影片會在上課前公布在 eeclass: http://eeclass.nthu.edu.tw。投影片的內 容是演講的重點與綱要，但不可能是文理清晰邏輯通順的文章。建議同學上課時記下 重要的邏輯推論及實例，或是準備一本課本，方便日後複習。 4. 如果你常來聽課，遇到聽不懂的地方，或是不會答的題，我有責任，也很樂意回答你 的問題，讓你明白。但有些同學平常不來上課，自己看課本講義又看不懂 (或是不想 費神)，然後考前發 email 給我問問題，或是考前才來課堂上，利用下課來問一大堆我 早已反覆講過多次的內容，把我當成函授學校或是私人家教。占用我的時間，也排擠 掉其他同學發問的時間，甚至影響到正常上課。這對我或是對其他同學，應該都是不 公平吧？所以如果你有缺課，又想補上進度，請你自己想辦法。 5. 考試命題範圍以上課投影片為準，所有在課堂上講解過的內容都包含在內。大致上與 課本一致，但會有所增減。 放假與上課時間 • 放假：10/10 (雙十節) • 上課：九月 (5、12、19、26)、十月 (3、17、24、31)、十一月 (7、14、21、28)、十二 月 (5、12、19)。 成績計算、考試時間、及相關規定 1. 期中考 50%，期末考 50%。 2. 期中及期末考時間：10/24、12/19，3:30–5:20pm。 3. 上述考試時間若無法出席參加考試，請依本校請假辦法辦理。任何事假歉難同意，且 無法給予補考。公假需出示本校派遣單位核發之公假單，喪假需請家長、監護人、或 直系尊親屬來信 (電郵) 代為請假，病假需請校醫或醫院開立證明，否則視同無假缺 考。因懷孕、分娩或為撫育三歲以下幼兒而核准之事病假及產假視同病假。 4. 考試以中文或英文出題，可以中文或英文回答。如果你自認中/英文不好，請自己加 強中/英文閱讀能力。 2 課程進度 • 經濟學簡介 • 供給與需求 • 市場均衡 • 價格彈性 • 效用與消費者的選擇 • 期中考 • 生產者決策的基礎 • 競爭市場的供給線 • 市場機能與經濟效率 • 獨占 • 不完全競爭市場 • 要素市場 • 期末考 3

Perlo§ (2020). Course Description: This course is o§ered in English and is the Örst part of an one-year course of Microeconomics which is a requirement for Economics program. Knowledge of calculus will be expected as it is used frequently for solving problems. The course starts with the introduction of supply and demand, and it studies how a consumer makes choices about which good to consume. After understanding consumer theory, the demand curve and its properties can then be analyzed in a more rigorous manner. Moreover, we will discuss how to measure the consumer welfare and provide policy implications. In the second half of the course, we study how Örms make choices on how much to produce for both short and long- run analysis. Similar to the consumerís problem of maximizing utility, Örms minimize their costs, and the properties of the cost function will be studied. We then introduce the most important mode of market structure, namely the perfect competition and discuss how Örms and consumers interact in such environment. Lastly, we extend the partial analysis of an economy to a general equilibrium setting and discuss the economic welfare of such setting. The emphasis throughout the course is on using accounting information in managing an organization. In this course, the traditional tools of managerial accounting, like product costing, budgeting, and performance evaluation, will be augmented and updated with contemporary approaches such as activity- based costing, customer profitability analysis, value-chain analysis, target costing, balanced scorecard, and strategic cost management. Prerequisite: Accounting(I)、(II)。 Topics Cost Concepts for Decision-Makers 1 Managerial Accounting 2 Job Order Costing 3 Process Costing 4 Activity-Based Costing Decision-Making Concepts 5 Cost-Volume-Profit 6 Cost-Volume-Profit Analysis: Additional Issues 2 7 Incremental Analysis 8 Pricing Planning and Control Concepts 9 Budgetary Planning 10 Budgetary Control and Responsibility Accounting 11 Standard Costs and Balanced Scorecard 12 Planning for Capital Investments Performance Evaluation Concepts 13 Statement of Cash Flows 14 Financial Analysis: The Big Picture Required Materials: Weygandt, J. J., Kimmel, P. D., Kieso, D. E., & Aly, I. M. (2024). Managerial accounting: Tools for business decision-making 9/e IA . John Wiley & Sons.

docs.text: 1 Financial Reporting： Theory and Practices College of Technology Management, National Tsing Hua University (Fall 2025) Instructor: 沈瑜峰 Shen Yu-Feng Office Hour: By appointment E-mail: shenyf@mx.nthu.edu.tw Class time: 12:10-15:10, Wednesdays, WnW5W6 Classroom: TSMC 台積 205 Course Objective: This course is designed to provide a strong conceptual, analytical and procedural foundation for the study of financial reporting and practice. The historical development of accounting thought and the role of financial accounting in today’s economy are investigated. Socioeconomic, political, legal, and ethical influences on financial reporting are considered. Discussions include procedures to record, summarize, and report results of business events; content and presentation of financial statements and specific reporting issues related to cash and receivable. An overview of financial statement analysis is also presented. International issues are addressed as appropriate. The aims and objectives of the course are to: • stimulate theoretical enquiry into financial accounting issues • develop the student’s knowledge and understanding of financial accounting • prepare students for further academic study in accounting and related areas • enable students in the pursuit of a professional accountancy qualification • equip students for employment in areas where an understanding of accounting issues and tools is helpful. Prerequisite: Accounting(I)、(II)。 Topics Module 1 Theory and Conceptual Framework Module 2 Depreciation Policy and Analysis and Interpretation of Statements of Changes in Financial Position Module 3 Accounting Information And Disclosure 2 Module 4 Financial Accounting and Reporting Standards Module 5 Corporate Reporting and Accounting for Multinational Corporations Module 6 Contemporary Issues in Accounting Required Materials: Higson, A. Course Description: There are two sequences for undergraduate econometrics. This course is the first part of the introduction to econometrics sequence. We will review probability and statistics at the first beginning and then introduce the basic idea of regression models. You are expected to have a firm grasp of the types of empirical research designs that can lead to convincing analysis and be comfortable working with actual data sets. Although the aim will remain on the underlying theory, students will be given several opportunities to gain “hand on” experience with real data set through homework assign- ments. I would encourage students to make use of my office hours (or TA’s office hours) during the semester and not wait until the day before the exam. If you are having difficulty with concepts early on, then it is likely that your difficulties will snowball and that there will be insufficient time to deal with your puzzles close to the exams. So please make use of my office hours to sort out difficulties as they arise. Prerequisites: Calculus, Probability, and Statistics Syllabus Fall 2025 Required Textbook: Basically, I will hand out weekly lecture notes which are the summary of textbooks.  Stock, J. H. and M. W. Watson, 2020, Introduction to Econometrics, 4th edition, Addison-Wesley. Of course, there are lots of textbooks related to this course. If you have enough time, it would be also beneficial to check out some of the following references. References: Note that you don’t need to buy the following books. The book list is just for your reference.  Gujarati, D. N., 2003, Basic Econometrics, McGraw-Hill. It is the former textbook in this course.  Wooldridge, J. M., 2003, Introductory Econometrics: A modern approach, South- Western. It is a very popular undergraduate level textbook adopted in US. This book gives a huge amount of empirical examples and illustrates econometric concepts intuitively.  Maddala, G. S., 2001, Introduction to Econometrics, 3rd edition, Wiley. This book is well written and in general is deeper than our textbook. You could also find some fancy topics in Maddala’s book such as bootstrap, Jackknife and GMM.  Kennedy, P. A., 1998, A guide to Econometrics, 4th edition, MIT Press. This book tries to verbally explain difficult econometric ideas and avoids heavy math.  Pindyck, R. S. and L. R. Rubinfeld, 1998, Econometric Models and Economic Forecasts, McGraw-Hill. Ths is my econometric textbook when I was a junior. It is quite easy to read.  Ramanathan R., 2002, Introductory Econometrics with Applications, 5th edition, South- Western. This book provides a number of practical applications. It is also self-contained. In Chapter 14, the author demonstrates the various steps involved in carrying out an empirical research project.  Johnston and DiNardo, 1997, Econometric Methods, 4th edition, McGraw-Hill. If you are sort of familiar with matrix algebra, it is a nice book to build up the foundation of econometrics. docs.text: 1 ECON 3131 Syllabus: Globalizing Economy I Spring 2024 General Information. Instructor: Elaine Chyi Email: ylchyi@mx.nthu.edu.tw Office Hours. Weds. 3-5 pm or by appointment. (Email is the best way to reach me.) Classroom: TSMC #223 Course Home Page: eLearn 數位學習平台 Course objective and design. The growing economic openness expressed in the globalization of independent economic systems has created problems as well as opportunities in new and unexpected ways. In particular, globalization has allowed many counties to emerge from underdevelopment, as well as increase world production and employment. Outward-oriented policies brought greater prosperity to much of East Asia, transforming it from one of the poorest regions of the world about sixty years ago. Multinational firms have been the driving force behind these transformations, favoring the international division of productive processes and the spread of technologies and know-how. This course focuses on the aspects of economic globalization, such as the role of multinational firms as major participants of the globalizing world, global trade, and foreign direct investment, by providing an analytical framework for students to understand decisions of multinational firms. This course is primarily lecture style in around 80 percent of the semester. There will be some class activities, such as coursework or case discussion, held. A final team project with presentation in class is required. Grading. The final grade will be determined by classwork and homework (30%) and a final report and presentation of projects (70%). Course Material. − Head, Keith, Elements of Multinational Strategy, Berlin, Springer. − Related Articles from various books, issues of the Economists, NYT and economic journals. docs.text: 11410ECON316100 Public Finance (I) Instructor: Prof. Hui-chen Wang (王惠貞) Fall 2025 (114上) Office: 台積館810 Classroom: TSMC (台積館) 224 Email: huichenwang@mx.nthu.edu.tw Lecture Time: WnW5W6 (150 minutes on Wed 12:10-15:10) Office Hours: TBA Public Finance (I) 財政學一 Syllabus (Preliminary) Course Description This is the first course in the two-semester undergraduate sequence of Public Finance. Public Finance is the branch of economics that studies the role of the public sector in the economy, and the approach is primarily based on microeconomics. In this semester, we will have a focus on the expenditure side of public finance. The course will begin with an introduction to the public sector and basic economic tools, followed by the economic reasons and outcomes of government interventions. We will then look at what the public sector actually does using examples from the expenditure policies in the United States and in Taiwan, and how it affects individual decision-making and welfare. This course is offered in English. Learning Objectives After successful completion of this course, students will be able to (1) define and discuss the key economic concepts pertinent to the public sector, (2) analyze the fundamental issues in public finance using microeconomic theories and tools, (3) have a basic understanding of the important public expenditure policies in the world, and (4) apply economic thinking to the issues in the public expenditure policies in Taiwan. Prerequisite Principles of Economics I and II. Textbook and References Teaching material will be primarily drawn from the following textbooks: Hyman, David N. (2021), Public Finance: A Contemporary Application of Theory to Policy, 12th Edition. Cengage. (ISBN-13: 978-0357442159.) Rosen, Harvey S. and Ted Gayer. (2014). Public Finance. 10th global edition. McGraw-Hill/Irwin. ISBN-13: 978-0077154691 Some material that is not in the textbooks may be presented in the lectures. Course Requirements and Policies Examinations There will be two in-class examinations: one midterm exam and one final exam. The exams are not strictly cumulative; however, previously tested concepts may be covered in a later exam to the extent that they are the basis of a current topic. The midterm and final exam dates will be announced in the first class meeting. 2 All students must take the exams at their scheduled times. Make-up exam policy: No make-up exam will be given for the midterm exam. The weight for a missed midterm exam, if excused, will be reallocated to the final exam. Make-up exam for the final exam may be given under unexpected, extremely unusual and justifiable circumstances. Students who miss an exam due to an unexpected emergency should inform professor Wang within 24 hours from the missed exam and provide official documentation for the absence within a week. Pop Quizzes: Four short quizzes will be given in the semester. These quizzes will not be pre-announced. For each student, only the highest three quiz scores of the four will count towards the course grade calculation. NO makeup quiz may be given for any reason. However, under extremely unusual and justifiable circumstances (official documentation required), additional quiz waiver(s) may be granted on a case-by-case basis, at professor Wang’s discretion. Homework assignments: Problem sets will be assigned throughout the course. Your homework will not be collected nor graded; however, all students are expected to complete all assignments in a timely manner for effective learning and preparation of the tests. Attendance and Participation: Students are required to attend the lectures regularly. Participation in class discussion is expected and appreciated. You will be held responsible for all assignments, tests, and any announcement made in class, even in your absence. Your attendance and participation may affect your overall course grades on the margin. In addition, we reserve the right to impose penalty in terms of course grades if high frequency of unexcused absences is observed for a student. Grading Course letter grades will be assigned based on the weighted sums of the graded items: Midterm exam: 40% Final exam: 45 % Quizzes: 15% (5 for each of the three highest quiz scores) Your grades are not negotiable. No individual request for extra credit work will be taken. Class Communication and Resources TA Office hours: In addition to Professor Wang’s office hours (see header), there will be weekly office hours held by one of our teaching assistants. The time and location/format of the TA office hours will be announced separately on the eeclass learning platform (see next). Digital learning platform: We will utilize eeclass (https://eeclass.nthu.edu.tw) digital learning platform maintained by the university. Announcements, slides, assigned problem sets, solutions, grades and other material related to the course will be posted. Please check the designated platform regularly to remain up to date. You are expected to check your email as well as your eeclass account regularly to remain up to date. Note: The posted version of the lecture slides will be incomplete by design with spaces to be filled out in class. You are expected to print out the slides in advance 3 and bring them to the class. Keep in mind that the lecture slides will not remove the need for your class attendance and note taking efforts. Regulation on AI Usage The usage of AI is irrelevant in this course since student learning will be assessed by in-class closed-book tests. Tentative Course Outline 1. docs.text: 1 China’s Public Finance and Economic Development 中國大陸財政與經濟發展 Instructor: Pi-Han Christine Tsai Email: pihantsai@mx.nthu.edu.tw Course Description: This course provides a foundational understanding of China’s public finance and examines the country’s economic development through the lens of its political and fiscal institutions. We begin with an overview of China’s fiscal reforms, tracing their historical evolution and assessing their current implications. The core of the course focuses on the structure and dynamics of China’s political and fiscal systems. In addition, we will explore a range of contemporary issues in public finance, including expenditure allocation (e.g., education, healthcare, and pension systems), intergovernmental fiscal relations, the budget cycle, government debt, and land finance. The course concludes with a forward-looking discussion on the future trajectory of China’s economic development. Ethics Statement on Generative Artificial Intelligence: Grounded in the principles of transparency and responsibility, this course allows students to leverage AI for collaboration and mutual learning, thereby enhancing the quality of their midterm critical reports. In accordance with the published Guidelines for Collaboration, Co-learning, and Cultivation of Artificial Intelligence Competencies in University Education, this course adopts the following policy: Conditionally open. Students may briefly explain how generative AI was used for topic ideation, sentence refinement, or structural reference in the footnotes of the title page or after the bibliography in their final reports. However, students are not permitted to use generative AI tools for writing the reports. If such usage is discovered without proper disclosure, instructors, the institution, or relevant units have the right to reevaluate the report, or withhold scores. Students enrolled in this course agree to the above ethics statement by registering for the class. Course Objectives: 1. To learn the development of China’s fiscal policies and their economic outcomes. 2. To understand China’s budget system and intergovernmental fiscal arrangement. 3. To be able to analyze the causes and results of current public economic issues and problems in China. Textbooks and Related Materials: No textbook is required, but students are encouraged to read the supplemental materials. Please also refer to the instructor’s PPT. Additional reading materials will be announced during the semester. 1. Chen, T., and Kung, J., 2009. “Do Land Revenue Windfalls Create a Political Resource Curse? Evidence from China.” Journal of Development Economics 123: 86-106. 2. Han, L., and Kung, J., 2015. “Fiscal Incentives and Policy Choices of Local Governments: Evidence from China.” Journal of Development Economics 116: 89-104. 3. Jin, Hehui, Qian, Yingyi, Weingast, Barry R. 2005. “Regional Decentralization and Fiscal Incentives: Federalism, Chinese Style”, Journal of Public Economics 89: 1719-1742. 4. Justin Lin, and Zhiqian Liu, 2000. “Fiscal decentralization and economic growth in China”, Economic Development and Cultural Change, 49(1), 1-21. 5. Li, H., and Zhou, L., 2005. “Political Turnover and Economic Performance: the Incentive Role of Personnel Control in China.” Journal of Public Economics 89: 1743-1762. 6. Shah, Anwar, Shen, Chunli. 2006. “The Reform of the Intergovernmental Transfer System to 2 Achieve a Harmonious Society and a Level Playing Field for Regional Development in China”, World Bank Policy Research Working Paper 4100. 7. Shen, Chunli, Jin, Jing, Zho, Heng-fu. 2012. “Fiscal Decentralization in China: History, Impact, Challenges and Next Steps”, Annals of Economics and Finance 13-1: 1-51. 8. Shiyu Li and Shuanglin Lin, 2011, “The size and structure of China’s government debt,” Journal of Social Sciences, Vol. 48, No. 3, 527-542. 9. 蘭小歡, 2021, 置身事內：中國政府與經濟發展, 北京市紀文景文化傳播有限責任公司 Grading Policy: Class Participation 15% Midterm Exam 20% News Report or Critical Report 30% Final Debate Competition 35% Assessment Components (1) Class Participation (15%): • Attendance (10 Points): Attendance will be checked randomly three times during the course. To receive full credit for attendance, students must be present for at least two of these checks. Each attendance check is worth 5 points. • Participation in Discussions (5 Points): Active and meaningful participation in class discussions is essential and valued. Engagement in discussions will be worth 5 points towards the class participation grade. (2) Midterm Exam (20%): scheduled for 10/9. (3) News Report or Critical Report (30%): • News Report: Starting from Week 2, two students each week will present a recent news article or event related to China’s public finance and related phenomena. Students are expected to provide background or historical context and analyze the issue from an institutional perspective. Each presentation should be approximately 15–20 minutes in length. • Critical Report: Students will select a public policy or phenomenon related to China for critical analysis. The report should be 3–5 pages in length (including figures, tables, and references). Deadline: 11/6. (4) Final Debate Competition (35%): Each group will consist of five students, whether participating in the final debate or the in-class presentation. The presentation should last 60 minutes, followed by 30 minutes of Q&A. • Structured Debate or Final in-class Presentation (30%): Students will either participate in a structured debate on a public policy in Taiwan related to Mainland China, or deliver an in-class presentation comparing institutions or policies between Taiwan and Mainland China. • Experience Report (5%): Submit a 1-page report detailing your experience and learning outcomes from the debate. Deadline: 12/20. docs.name: 數理經濟學一
docs.text: 數理經濟學一 Fall 2025 Friday 12:30–15:20 @ TSMC 205 教師: 唐震宏 E-mail: jhtang@mx.nthu.edu.tw Office: TSMC727 課程介紹 數理經濟學是什麼？ 數理經濟學是一門經濟學的分支，其目的在為經濟分析提供嚴謹的架 構，尤其當經濟理論過於複雜而超過口語或圖形的表達範圍時，數理經濟學提供分析 的工具。除了在經濟理論的發展中發揮了關鍵的作用，數理經濟學也普遍應用於經濟 學的各個領域，提供數學工具對經濟現象進行建模及分析，進而發展出明確且可檢驗 的理論假說。 本門課的目標是什麼？用到那些數學工具？ 經濟學家視研究目的及分析難度來選用適當 的數學工具，常用的包括微積分、線性代數、微分方程、最優化理論、和機率論等。經 濟系的同學在大二的個體經濟學都上過 Perloff 的教科書，對微積分、靜態優化等應 該都不陌生。所以本門課將建立在這個基礎上，以總體經濟學的內容及其所使用的數 學工具為主要教學目標，會用到微積分、線性代數、靜態最適化、基礎微分方程、差 分方程。我們希望用這些數學工具來幫助同學學習總體經濟學，就如同 Perloff 的課 本用微積分來幫助同學學習個體經濟學。 數理經濟學有什麼用？ • 幫助學習及深入瞭解經濟理論：學習使用代數等數學工具的輔助，以及使用抽象 簡潔的數學表達，有助理解複雜的經濟理論，提高學習效率，並為未來學習更進 階的經濟理論奠定基礎。 • 提高分析和解決問題的能力：數理經濟學可以幫助學生將複雜多變的經濟問題 化繁為簡，並應用適當的模型進行分析，進而培養解決問題的能力。 • 培養跨領域的數學技能：數理經濟學需要使用微積分、線性代數、微分方程、最 優化理論等數學工具，而數學是科學之母，這些數學工具也都普遍應用在大數據 分析、機器學習、和人工智能等其他領域。尤其現在人工智能的時代已經來臨， 1 學習人工智能已不再是理工科系的專利。經濟主修的同學熟練應用數學工具可 以培養數學技能，除了提高經濟理論的學習效率，也有助於渉獵其他領域。 數理經濟學適合那些同學選修？ 選不選修數理經濟學要根據學生自身的興趣、職業規劃和 學術需求等因素來考慮。如果學生對數學和統計比較感興趣，且想將這些技能應用於 經濟學分析中，那麼選修數理經濟學會是一個不錯的選擇。這些技能可以幫助學生更 深入地理解經濟學理論和應用，並提高升學或就業競爭力。 但如果學生對數學和統計沒有太大的興趣，或者想在其他領域發展自己的職業生涯， 那麼選修數理經濟學可能不是必需的。學生可以根據自己的興趣和職業規劃選擇相應 的選修課程，以發揮自己的潛力。 課程目標 本課程預期能協助同學瞭解及學習 1. 如何應用數學工具有效學習經濟理論 2. 如何應用數學工具模型化並解決經濟問題 參考用書 C & W 是主要的教科書，其他參考書會隨主題進行介紹. • Chiang, A.C. and K. Wainwright (2004). Fundamental Methods of Mathematical Eco- nomics, 4th Ed. 放假與上課時間 • 放假：10/10 (雙十節) • 上課：九月 (5、12、19、26)、十月 (3、17、24、31)、十一月 (7、14、21、28)、十二 月 (5、12、19)。 2 成績計算與考試時間 • 作業 (4 次) 20%、期中考 40 %、期末考 40%。 • 期中及期末考時間：10/24、12/19，12:30–15:20。 課程進度 1. Linear system of equations 2. Determinants 3. Linear economic models (C & W, Chs.4, 5) 4. Comparative-static analysis (C & W, Chs.6, 7, 8) 5. Euclidean spaces 6. Eigenvalues and eigenvectors 7. Static optimization (C & W, Chs.9, 11, 12, 13) 3

docs.text: 1 ECON412100 國際經濟學一(International Economics (I)) 課程大綱 (temporary) Instructor: 李 宜 助教: TBA Office: 台積館 812 Email: ylee@mx.nthu.edu.tw Office: Office Hours: M 12pm-1pm Office hour: 在全球化的潮流下，近 30 年來世界各國紛紛降低貿易障礙，加速商品貿易的流量。 此外，國際間生產分工的方式，已從過去產品之間的分工，逐漸轉為生產同一種商品 在不同製程上的分工。在貿易自由化與國際分工的趨勢下，加速商品、人才與資金的 跨國移動，提升國家與國家間生產活動的關聯性。透過國際貿易，各國可專注於本國 較具生產優勢的商品，在國際市場換取本國生產成本較高的商品，進而提升本國的生 產效率與福利。雖然自由貿易可提升一國福利，但同時也可能對一國所得分配造成不 均度惡化。因此，各國政府在制定貿易相關政策時多受到許多爭議。 本課程主要介紹當前國際貿易理論模型，分析國家間為何會進行貿易，以及自由貿易 與貿易政策(如:關稅)下對一國福利的影響，期望學生未來能對國貿相關議題有初步認 識及相關分析能力。 主要用書: International Economics Theory and Policy, by Paul Krugman, Maurice Obstfeld and Marc Melitz (KOM) [華泰書局代理] 評分方式: 本學期成績評定內容涵蓋： (1) 作業: 本課程將依照授課進度不定期發放作業，學生由 6 人組成小組， 每組繳交一份作業。作業需於指定日期(時段)繳交，逾期不收。 (2) 期中考: 期中考於 2025,10,21 課堂中舉行 (3) 期末考: 期末考於 2025, 12,16 課堂中舉行。 學期總成績計算方式如下: A =﹝作業(30%)，期中考(35%)，期末考(35%)﹞ B =﹝作業(30%)，期中考(25%)，期末考(45%)﹞ 學期總成績將取 A 與 B 兩者中較高者(Max{A,B})。 考試規則: (1) 考試時禁止使用手機。 (2) 請同學務必參加考試，考試當天缺席者以〝缺考〞處理。若遇 不可抗拒之因素需請事假，需於考試前向授課教師請假申請補考。 2 授課大綱: 1. Introduction 2. 李嘉圖模型 (KOM: Ch.3) ➢ 以國家間生產技術的差異解釋國家間貿易形成的原因 3. 特定要素模型 (KOM: Ch.4) ➢ 分析自由貿易在短期間對一國不同生產要素擁有者所得之影響(如:雇 主 vs 勞工) ➢ 分析勞工的跨國移動(如:外國白領人才、藍領勞工、移民)在短期與長 期下對一國所得分配的影響 4. HO 模型 (KOM: Ch.5) ➢ 以國家間生產資源分佈差異解釋國家間貿易形成的原因 ➢ 分析自由貿易在長期下對一國不同生產要素擁有者所得之影響 ➢ 分析勞工的跨國移動(如:外國白領人才、藍領勞工、移民)在長期下對 一國所得分配的影響 5. 經濟成長與國際貿易 (KOM, Ch.6) ➢ 當國家生產技術進步或生產資源增加，對一國貿易條件與福利之影響 6. 外部規模經濟與國際貿易 (KOM: Ch.7) 7. 內部規模經濟、不完全競爭與貿易 (KOM: Ch.8) ➢ 解釋產業內貿易發生的原因 ➢ 解釋個別廠商出口決策與對外投資(國際分工)的行為 ➢ 分析廠商國際分工對勞動市場的影響(FT: Ch. 7) 8. 貿易政策 (KOM: Ch.9) ➢ 關稅的經濟效果-大國 v.s. 小國 ➢ 關稅與配額比較: 完全競爭市場 v.s. 不完全競爭市場 ➢ 出口補貼、傾銷與其他非關稅貿易政策工具 9. 貿易干預的理論基礎 (KOM: Ch.10,11,12) ➢ 介紹政府限制貿易的理由與工具

docs.text: ECON 504200 Machine learning and econometrics: concepts and procedures (機器學習與計量經濟: 概念與程序) National Tsing Hua University 1st semester, 2025-2026 Time: 3:30pm - 6:20pm, every Tuesday (T7T8T9) except September 23. Make-up class will be arranged. Venue: TSMC 205 Office hours: By appointment Instructor: CY (Chor-yiu) SIN (Office: CTM-804, Email: cysin@mx.nthu.edu.tw, Phone: 03-516-2134) Course description: Since Varian (2014), people have been believing that machine learning uses data to predict some variable as a function of other variables, while econometrics use statistical methods for prediction, inference, and causal modeling of economic relationships. However, nowadays some tend to believe that machine learning is the new generation nonparametric statistical and econometric methods, branded as machine learning (Chernozhukov et al. 2017). While academically rigorous theorems are much appreciated, they are not the focus of this course. Instead, this course starts with basic concepts of machine learning and econometrics; and ends with procedural computer codes. Students are required to be familiar with at least one software such as Python, R or C++. This course discusses the basic concepts with examples in economics and management. Hands-on exercises with the software “Python”. Course topics: 1. Revision on (a) prediction with linear regression (b) classification with logit/probit model 2. The essential tools in computer age statistical inference: (a) Monte-Carlo simulation; (b) Bootstrapping; (c) Cross-validation (CV) 3. Linear model selection and regularization: (a) Ridge regression; (b) Elastic net; (c) Lasso; (d) Best subset regression plus CV/information criterion (IC) 4. Tree-based methods and boosting: with an introduction to gradient boosting 5. Baic topic in deep learning: Feedforward neural network 6. Baic topic in deep learning: Recurrent neural network (RNN) and Long short-term memory network (LSTM) 7. Intermediate topic in deep learning: Convolutional neural network (CNN). 8. Intermediate topic in deep learning: “You only look once” (YOLO) 9. Introduction to basic generative adversarial network (GAN); 10. Introduction to reinforcement learning (RL) 11. Generalized linear model: with an introduction to support vector machine (SVM) 12. Re-sampling approach to (a) Interval estimation; (b) P-value Textbooks and papers: (1) Chernozhukov, V., Chetverikov, D., Demirer, M., Duflo, E., Hansen, C., Newey, W., 2017. Double/debiased/Neyman machine learning of treatment effects. American Economic Review: Papers and Proceedings 107, 261-265. (2) Efron, B., Hastie, T., 2016. Computer age statistical inference: algorithms, evidence and data science. Cambridge, U.S.: Cambridge University Press. (3) Hansen, B.E., 2022. Econometrics. New Jersey, U.S.: Princeton University Press (4) James, G., Witten, D., Hastie, T., Tibshirani, R., Taylor, J., 2023. An introduction to statistical learning with applications in Python. New York, U.S.: Springer Science+Business Media (https://www.statlearning.com/) (5) Varian, H.R., 2014. Big data: new tricks for econometrics. The Journal of Economic Perspectives 28, 3-27. Assessment: Attendance and participation in discussions 40%, mid-term examination 30%, final examination: 30%. (Only grades will be given for each part of the assessment. Student leave applications must be submitted in-person to the instructor.) Attitude taken in this course: Be humble, careful and simple, positive and gentle. Needless to say, be logical. - End -

docs.text: 1 Family Economics Spring 2023 M7M8M9 Classroom: TSMC(台積館) Room 428 Course Description: This course focuses on research on family and demographic economics. Students will be introduced to a wide range of research topics related to family and demographic economics and learn to develop the ability to conduct research in this field. The study of families and households is an important research area given the increasingly complex organization of families, which have produced substantial effects on behavior of households and welfare of children as well as spouses. We will focus on the theoretical modeling and empirical investigation of how individuals sort into families (cohabitation, marriage and divorce) and of the major economic outcomes determined in a family context (such as spousal time allocation, labor supply (particularly the changing role of women in the labor force), fertility, consumption, investments in children and intergenerational transfers. Of particular importance are the various classes of household models and their testable implications on family decisions. We will also investigate family laws and policies from the economic perspective and draw insights from research studies in sociology and demography on the family. Method of Instruction: Lecture/Discussion Course Website and Communication: Courses materials are available on our course website in the eeclass system (eeclass 數位學習 平台). Readings, usually academic articles, will be assigned throughout this course. Students are expected to participate in the discussion of papers covered in each topic. The links for the papers and selected articles and lectures notes will be posted on the course website. So please make sure to regularly check the course website. Instructor: Crystal Wong (黃賀寶) Office: TSMC (台積館) Room 704 Office Hours: By Appointment Email: hpwong@mx.nthu.edu.tw 2 Requirements: This course is intended for students interested in learning and conducting demographic research. Knowledge of calculus, and statistics are required. (We will discuss both theoretical and empirical studies on the subject and you will be required to provide critiques of these works.) In-Class Presentation (in English) Each student would be assigned a paper on the reading list and present it in class. The presentation should be about 40 minutes long. Current Affair Discussion (in English) Each student is required to present a news article and lead a small discussion on one current affair (e.g. dropping fertility rate in Taiwan, some newly enacted laws and their economic consequences, intended or unintended etc…). All the students will participate in the discussion. Attendance counted for participation Tentative Topics (subject to revision): 1. Introduction and Demographic Trends 2. Why Marry? 3. Earlier Population Theory 4. Gender and Household Decision Making 5. Allocation of Time 6. Altruism in the Family 7. Assortative Matching in Marriage 8. Family Background and the Opportunities of Children 9. Divorce, Divorce Laws and Child Support 3 References: Becker, Gary S. (1991). A Treatise on the Family. Havard University Press. Bergstrom, Theodore (1997). “A Survey of Theories of the Family.” In Mark Rosenzweig and Oded Stark, eds., Handbook of Population and Family Economics. Amsterdam: North-Holland. Goldin, Claudia (2006). The Quiet Revolution That Transformed Women’s Employment, Education, and Family. American Economic Review, vol.96(2), 1-21. Weiss, Yoram (1997). “The Formation and Dissolution of Families: Why Marry? Who Marries Whom? And What Happens Upon Marriage and Divorce?” In Mark Rosenzweig and Oded Stark, eds., Handbook of Population and Family Economics. Amsterdam: North-Holland. 4 Grading: Your total score (out of 100) will be converted into a letter grade (also your GPA) based on the list below: Letter Grade A+ A A- B+ B B- C+ C C- D E X GPA 4.3 4.0 3.7 3.3 3.0 2.7 2.3 2 1.7 1 0 0 Score Range 100- 90 89- 85 84- 80 79- 77 76- 73 72- 70 69- 67 66- 63 62- 60 59- 50 49-1 0 Academic Integrity Statement: I will enforce rigorous standards of academic integrity in all aspects and assignments of this course. docs.text: 1 National Tsing Hua University Department of Economics Theory of Public Economics I, Fall 2025 Time: Wednesday 9-12noon Classroom: 732 TSMC Building Professor: Wu, Shih-Ying Office: 711 TSMC Building, Tel: ext 62031, E-mail: wus@mx.nthu.edu.tw Office hours: by appointment Introduction: The course will analyze issues in public economics, which can be categorized into four parts: (1) tax effects on economic behaviors; (2) issues on the income and wealth inequality in Taiwan and the world; (3) individual charitable donations; and others. The part of tax effects will investigate the tax effects on individuals’ economic behaviors, mainly including business investment and tax compliance. The part on inequality will discuss empirical evidence on income and wealth inequality and examine various rationales for the increasing inequality around the world since the 1980s. It will also analyze the negative impacts of income and wealth inequality on the society and evaluate possible remedies, especially tax policies, to alleviate the increasing inequality. The part on individual charitable donations will discuss the theoretical rationales underlying individuals’ charitable giving and analyze the buzzing empirical studies based on field experiments in the past decade. Besides, depending on students’ interest, the topics in some weeks listed below can be adjusted. Prerequisite: Undergraduate-level intermediate microeconomics Readings: The readings for this course are mainly journal articles and working papers. Lecture notes for most of the weeks will be available on the website of eeclass. docs.text: ECON 7063 Economics of Education: Theory and Application National Tsing Hua University Fall 2025 Instructor: Eric S. Lin Contact Information: Office: CTM-712, Email: slin@mx.nthu.edu.tw, Phone: 574-2729 Time and Location: Friday 9–noon, CTM-XXX Office Hours: By appointment Course Webpage: Course materials will be handed in class. Teaching Assistant: Not Offered Teaching Assistant Hours: Not Offered Course Description: This is a topic course in economics of education. We will discuss central issues regarding this field such as estimating the returns to education, human capital and signaling theories of education, education and economic growth, education and economic equality, peer effects, entrance channels and students academic performance,..., etc. We will primarily focus on empirical applications while sometimes theoretical work will be referred to. The introduction of suitable empirical strategies (i.e., a variety of econometric techniques) along with the search for identification will be much emphasized throughout this course. The utimate goal of this course is to motivate PhD or master students conducting a quality research on economics of edcucation. Thereby, students will be required to initiate a new project related to the course, survey the literature, collect data, summarize basic statistics, estimate the specified model, test certain hypothesis, conduct sensitivity analysis, discuss empirical findings, propose policy suggestions (if any), present the process regularly in class, and lastly end up with writing a formal article (ready for submission if possible). docs.text: 偏微分方程與複變函數−課程大綱 (10410 EE 202002, Partial Differential Equations and Complex Variables) 一、課程說明(Course Description) 本課程銜接常微分方程，涵蓋偏微分方程及 複變數函數兩者，提供修習其他工程或物 理學科所需之數學基礎。修完本科目 可對偏微分方程之物理意義、基本解法與複變函 數之理論、應用等有一概括性 之認識，有助於修習電磁學、近代物理、控制系統、電力工程等課程。本科目 需具有大一微積分、常微分方程(Ordinary Differential Equations) 及傅氏/拉氏 (Fourier/Laplace)變換之基礎。 二、教科書(Text Books) E. Kreyszig, Advanced Engineering Mathematics, 9th Ed., John Wiley & Sons, Inc., 2006. 三、參考書籍(References): n/a 四、教學方式(Teaching Method) 課堂講授(中文授課) 五、教學進度(Syllabus) 1. 偏微分方程簡介;一維波動方程式之物理模型 2. 解偏微分方程的方法:分離變數法、本徵函數展開法、積分轉換法 3. 二維波動方程式:直角座標、極座標 4. Laplace 方程式:直角座標、極座標、球座標;正交函數展開 5. 以數值方法解偏微分方程 6. 複變函數簡介:解析函數(Analytic functions)、Cauchy-Riemann 方程組 7. 複變函數之路徑積分、Cauchy 積分定理 8. Taylor 級數、Laurent 級數、留數(Residue)積分法 9. 複變之應用:以留數積分法計算實變函數積分，解二維 Laplace 方程式 六、成績考核(Evaluation) 1. 兩次 Quiz(分別為 25%, 30%)，期末考(涵蓋全學期範圍 45%) 作業僅為練習用，不計分。 2. 按照上述權重算出原始總分，之後還會根據分數分佈進行調分 3. 調分二原則：(1) 只調高不調低 (2) 調分後大小關係不變 七、可連結之網頁位址 （於 eLearn）

Strang, Introduction to Linear Algebra, 6th Ed., Wellesley-Cambridge Press, 2023 [ISBN: 978-626-97081-0-9]. • Handouts prepared by the instructor. References: 1. D. C. Lay, S. T. Lay, and J. J. McDonald, Linear Algebra and Its Applications, 6th Ed., Pearson, 2022 [ISBN: 978-1-292-35121-6]. 2. S. Friedberg, A. Insel, and L. Spence, Linear Algebra, 4th Ed., Prentice Hall, 2014 [ISBN: 1-292- 02650-2]. Overview: This course offers a rigorous and foundational journey through one of the most elegant and widely applied branches of mathematics. Using Linear Algebra by Stephen H. Friedberg, Arnold J. Insel, and Lawrence E. Spence as our primary text, we will explore the theory and applications of vector spaces, linear transformations, matrices, and inner product spaces with a level of depth suited for serious study in mathematics, physics, computer science, and engineering. This course emphasizes both conceptual understanding and abstract reasoning. We will not only learn how to perform computations with matrices and vectors but also delve into the theoretical structure that underpins these operations. By the end of the course, you will have a solid grasp of the fundamental concepts of linear algebra, such as • Vector spaces and subspaces • Linear independence, bases, and dimension • Linear transformations and their matrix representations • Eigenvalues, eigenvectors, and diagonalization • Inner product spaces and orthogonality Lectures will follow structured handouts and slides. Active class participation is required and strongly encouraged. Students can use AI to assist their learning with cautions on its correctness. Course materials and announcements will be posted on eeClass. 1 加簽順序：(加簽至教室最大容量) 1. 電機系、電資院學士班二年級同學 2. 電機系、電資院學士班高年級學生(含雙主修、但不包含輔系、第二專長) 3. 電機系、電資院學士班一年級學生 4. 其他學院以電機系為輔系之同學 5. 其他學院以電機系為第二專長之同學 6. 其他學院學生(依年級高低排序) PS. 雙主修、輔系、第二專長之認定以校務資訊系統之登載為基準 申請加簽方式: 步驟 1) 於 2025 年 8 月 25 日 23:59 前 email 至 irat@ee.nthu.edu.tw，信中敘明姓名、學號、系級， 未事先 email 或有資訊缺漏恕無法加簽。 步驟 2) 於 2025 年 9 月 4 日至網頁 https://irat.ee.nthu.edu.tw 查詢申請加簽成功名單 步驟 3) 申請成功者請上校務資訊系統遞交電子加簽申請

docs.text: National Tsing Hua University 11410 EE 211000 Modern Physics 近代物理 Page 1 of 2 Course syllabus Basic Information: Course title (中文): 近代物理 Course title (English): Modern Physics Instructor: 大江昌人 (Oh-e, Masahito) (oh-e@ee.nthu.edu.tw) @台達館#838 Language for teaching: English Class time: T7T8R7 Location: DELTA 台達 209 Course Description: This course offers introduction to “Modern Physics” established in the 20th century. Knowledge on “Modern Physics” is fundamental to understanding practically developed various optoelectronic contemporary devices such as transistors and lasers. The main purpose of this course is to learn fundamentals of relativity and quantum mechanics, which are representative fields beyond the concept of Newtonian mechanics. Relativity is the law for time and space and is usually concerned with high velocities comparable to the speed of light. Quantum mechanics is the law of the microscopic world for atoms, molecules and nuclei. Throughout this course, we mainly focus on learning how relativistic effects appear when dealing with high velocities, how ways of viewing materials have been developed and how materials are structured from microscopic viewpoints. * The course is offered in English. Textbook  “Concepts of Modern Physics”, sixth edition or others (McGraw-Hill) by Arthur Beiser and Kok Wai Cheah (2015). Course materials: Available on https://eeclass.nthu.edu.tw/ References:  Physics for Scientists and Engineers with Modern Physics (Thomson Higher Education) by Raymond A. Serway and John W. Jewett, Jr. (2004).  Modern Physics (Pearson Addison Wesley) by Randy Harris (2008). Teaching Method: Lecture style by combining power point viewgraphs and blackboard teaching. Syllabus: Session 0: Introduction – Course guide – National Tsing Hua University 11410 EE 211000 Modern Physics 近代物理 Page 2 of 2 • What is “Modern Physics?” Session 1‒4 (5): Relativity • Special relativity; • Michelson-Morley experiment; •Postulates of special relativity; • Time dilation; • Length contraction; • Lorentz transformation; • Mass and energy; • Spacetime; • Twin paradox; • Basic general relativity …etc. Session 5‒8: Problems with classical physics – Duality of photons and electrons – • Blackbody radiation; • Photoelectric effect; • Compton scattering effect; • What is light; • Wave-function and density of probability; • de Broglie matter wave; • Uncertainty principle; • Particle in a box; • Bohr theory and atomic spectra …etc. Session 9: Atomic structure • The nuclear atom; • Electron orbits; • Rutherfords’s Nuclear Atom; • Bohr atom; • Atomic spectra; • Atomic excitation …etc. Session 10‒11: Introduction to quantum mechanics • One dimensional Schrödinger equation and wave-function; • Simple model of square well potential box; • Linearity and superposition; • Harmonic oscillator; • Operator; • Expectation value; • Tunneling phenomena …etc. Session 12‒13: Atomic and molecular physics • Electron orbit; • Atomic spectra; • Three-dimensional Schrodinger equation; • Hydrogen atom; • Quantum number; Session 14‒15 Electron spin • Spin; • Electron probability density; • Periodic law of the elements; • Exclusion principle; • Two atomic molecule; • Hydrogen molecule; • Bonding structures …etc. Session 16: Final ** The contents and plans will be appropriately changed and adjusted during the course. Grading: 1. Midterm I, Midterm II (can be turned into quizzes, a report, or others), and Final exams are main factors to determine the grades and will be equivalently treated. 2. Attendance, participation, homework, and quizzes will be used to adjust some points to finalize the grades. *** This may be slightly altered and adjusted in the end of the semester. Rules for students to use AI: AI tools are prohibited for any assignment, and all work must be the student's original creation.

docs.text: 11410 EE214000 課名 (Course title): 電磁學 Electromagnetics 上課時間 (Time): M3M4W2 上課教室 (Classroom): 台達館 Delta Building 216 一、課程說明 (Course Description) 本課程為電磁波、光電工程、固態電子元件以及光電領域各項研究的基礎，課程 內容將帶學生了解電磁學理論基礎與應用，搭配數學公式和物理圖像幫助學生理 解靜電場、靜磁場、電磁互作用用以及輸線理理論等物理現象，最後將推廣至馬 克士威爾方程式以及時變電磁場。 This course serves as the foundation for studies in electromagnetic waves, optoelectronic engineering, solid-state electronic devices, and various fields in photonics. The content is designed to help students understand the theoretical foundations and applications of electromagnetism. Through the use of mathematical formulas and physical visualizations, students will gain insight into physical phenomena such as electrostatic fields, magnetostatic fields, electromagnetic interactions, and transmission line theory. The course will ultimately extend to Maxwell’s equations and time-varying electromagnetic fields. - 建議先修課程 (Prerequisite): 普通物理 (General Physics)、積分 (Calculus)、 電路學 (Electric Circuit) 二、使用書籍 (Text Books) David K. Cheng, "Field and Wave Electromagnetics, 2nd Edition." (2016) 三、參考資料 (References) 1. Inan, Umran S., Aziz S. Inan, and Ryan K. Said. "Engineering electromagnetics and waves." (2016). 四、教學方式 (Teaching style) 課程投影片 Lecture Slides 五、教學內容 (Course Content) - Vector analysis - Electrostatics - Magnetostatics - Transmission line - Time-varying fields, Maxwell’s equations and wave equations 11410 EE214000 六、成績考核 (Evaluation) 小考 Quiz ------------------ 30% 期中考 Midterm exam --- 35% 期末考 Final exam ------- 35% 七、課程準則 (Policy) 1. 抄襲或是用弊一律以零 計算，對自己的的學和和成績責 。Any instance of plagiarism or cheating will result in a score of zero. Please take responsibility for your own learning and performance. 2. 本課程無涉及 AI 使用。No AI tools will be required in this course.

Course Contents This course starts with a review of electromagnetic wave, followed by geometric optics for optical systems and resonators. We will then study the polarization state of lights and the use of it in some devices. The wave nature of light generates many interesting phenomena, including interference and diffraction etc. Once the concept and theory are introduced, we will learn useful devices, such as diffraction grating, etalon, and laser cavity. Finally, we study Fourier optics and coherence of light, which are important for image manipulation and optical signal processing. Handouts: The lectures of this course will follow the sequence in the course reader Modern Optics, which will be available for distribution at the beginning of the semester. docs.text: Prof. Yen-Chieh Huang tel: +886-3-5162340 Dept of Electrical Engineering office: HOPE 301 National Tsing-Hua University email: ychuang@ee.nthu.edu.tw Hsinchu, Taiwan 300044 EE315000 Electromagnetic Waves, Fall, 2025 __________________________________________________________________________________ 1 Last update Aug. 31st, 2025 EE 315000 Electromagnetic Waves 國立清華大學電機工程科學系 Fall, 2025 Prof. 黃衍介 Class location: Delta 212 ychuang@ee.nthu.edu.tw Class schedule: M3M4W2 Teaching Assistants (TAs): 彭 奎 鈞 pkg0916@gapp.nthu.edu.tw (40%), 林 鈺 謙 s114066521@m114.nthu.edu.tw (40%), 郭柏瑋 legendzeus121693@gmail.com (20%) Tel: 03-5162333 General Information This course is to study electromagnetic waves. We will first understand the basic concepts of a wave. An electromagnetic wave contains vector components of electric and magnetic fields. It is better to learn the subject from the viewpoint of a scalar field. Following the conceptual understanding of a wave, we will start to study the voltage and current (scalar quantities) waves on a transmission line. We then study the vector components of electric and magnetic fields in a plane wave. Once we learn about the reflection and transmission of an electromagnetic wave at boundaries, we will try to understand waveguide and cavity as elements for propagating and storing electromagnetic waves in a confined space, respectively. To send and receive an electromagnetic wave, one needs an antenna. The last part of the course is about transmission and receiving antennas for electromagnetic waves. The textbook chosen for this course is Field and Wave Electromagnetics by D. K. Cheng. As electromagnetics is a well-established knowledge, most other textbooks also serve well for this course. This course will be lectured mostly in English and slightly in Chinese for clarity. This course is synchronized with the pre-recorded DELTAMOOCx at https://deltamoocx.deltaww.com/course/preview/123e7dc280013 You are encouraged to view the MOOCx course recordings by yourselves before or after the class. Since the lectures are pre-recorded, please view the lectures before the class. Initially, I will give a 2-hour lecture in the Monday class. Later, I will randomly pick YOU to present the course content so that you have enough participation in the class. Your performance will be graded between 1-5 and counted jointly with that of your review/quiz performance toward 30% of your final grade. Before each lecture (likely to be on each Saturday), you will receive a review sheet with the content to be lectured on Monday. In every Wednesday class, if time allows, we will spend some time to help you answer the review sheet. You must turn in the review Prof. Yen-Chieh Huang tel: +886-3-5162340 Dept of Electrical Engineering office: HOPE 301 National Tsing-Hua University email: ychuang@ee.nthu.edu.tw Hsinchu, Taiwan 300044 EE315000 Electromagnetic Waves, Fall, 2025 __________________________________________________________________________________ 2 sheet electronically through the EECLASS by noon every Wednesday. Homework assignments will be given every 2-3 weeks, containing problems in Cheng’s textbook. Textbook David K. Cheng, Field and Wave Electromagnetics 2nd Ed., Addison Wesley, 1989. Reference book Fawwaz T. Ulaby, Fundamentals of Applied Electromagnetics 6th Ed., PEARSON Prentice Hall, 2007. (新月圖書，東華書局代理) Ramo, Whinnery, and van Duzer, Fields and Waves in Communication Electronics, 2nd Ed., John Wiley & Sons, 1984. In this course, students will learn important topics such as semiconductor band theory, carrier transportation and conduction in semiconductors, semiconductor junctions and diodes, MOS capacitors, MOSFETs, bipolar transistors, as well as VLSI memory technologies. Additionally, this course incorporates contemporary knowledge on semiconductor devices, ensuring students stay up to date with the latest advancements in the semiconductor field. docs.text: 國立清華大學課程大綱 科號 Course Number 11410EECS341000 學分 Credit 2 人數限制 Class Size 30 人 中文名稱 Course Title 音樂 x 科技：互動與生成式音樂設計 英文名稱 Course English Title Interactive and Generative Music 任課教師 Instructor 紀柏豪 上課時間 Time W5W6 上課教室 Room 炯朗 106 課程簡述(必填) Brief Course Description 本課程以音樂、聲音為媒介，探討互動裝置、系統與工具之設計與應用，並鼓勵學生探索其於 藝術創作、創意實踐及健康促進等跨領域應用。學生將透過理論講授與實務操作，學習互動音 樂與生成式音樂之基本概念，並整合音樂軟體（如 Ableton Live、Max/MSP）、微控制器、 MIDI 裝置、聲音及影像輸入及感測器等，實踐創意互動音樂體驗。 This course explores the design and application of interactive music and sound systems, encouraging cross-disciplinary projects in art, creativity, and health. Through theoretical lectures and practical exercises, students will learn the fundamentals of interactive and generative music, integrating music software (e.g., Ableton Live, Max/MSP), microcontrollers, MIDI devices, sound and video input, and sensors to create innovative interactive music experiences. 課程內容「中文暨英文關鍵字」(必填) 至少 5 個,每個關鍵字至多 20 個中文,以半形逗點分隔 Please fill in at least 5 course keywords (up to 40 letters for each keyword) and use commas to separate them.(required) 互動設計 Interactive Design, 生成式音樂 Generative Music, 資料聲音化 Sonification, 跨領域創作 Cross-disciplinary Creation, 演算法作曲 Algorithmic Composition, 數位訊號處理 Digital Signal Processing, 健康促進 Health Promotion 課程大綱(必填)Detailed Course Syllabus ● 課程說明(Course Description) 本課程聚焦於音樂、聲音相關的互動裝置、系統與工具設計與應用，探索其在藝術創作、創意 實踐及健康促進等領域的可能性。學生將透過理論講授與實務操作，理解互動音樂與生成式音 樂的基本概念，並學習如何利用軟硬體工具（如 Ableton Live、Max/MSP、Arduino、MIDI 裝置、 各式感測元件如觸控、環境感測器等）來實現創意互動音樂體驗。 先修建議（非必修但有助於課程參與）： • 熟悉基本電腦操作與軟體安裝（Windows 或 macOS 皆可） • 對數位音訊與 MIDI 有初步認識 • 對音樂創作（作曲、即興演奏或其他音樂實踐）有基本了解 • 對 Max/MSP 或其他視覺化程式語言（如 Pure Data）具基礎認識尤佳，若無經驗建議 先參考：Max/MSP 官方入門教學 ● 參考教材(References) • Alessandro Cipriani & Maurizio Giri《Electronic Music and Sound Design Vols. 1-3》 • Miller Puckette《The Theory and Technique of Electronic Music》 • Andy Farnell《Designing Sound》 • Massimo Banzi《Getting Started with Arduino》 • Gareth Loy《Musimathics–The Mathematical Foundations of Music》 ● 補充閱讀(Readings) • Garnett, G. (2001). "The Aesthetics of Interactive Computer Music", Computer Music Journal, 25(1). • Hunt, A. & Wanderley, M. (2002). "Mapping performer parameters to synthesis engines," Organised Sound, 7(2), pp. 97–108. • Eigenfeldt, A. (2008). "Emergent Rhythms through Multi-agency in Max/MSP," LNCS, vol. 4969. • Gartland-Jones, A. & Copley, P. (2003). "The Suitability of Genetic Algorithms for Musical Composition," Contemporary Music Review, 22(3). • Miranda, E. & Wanderley, M. (2006). "New Digital Musical Instruments", MIT Press. • Nierhaus, G. (2009). "Algorithmic Composition", Springer. • Roads, C. (2002). "Microsound", MIT Press. • Tom Mudd, Interactive and Generative Music Mapping • Nathan Wolek, Granular Toolkit • Organised Sound Journal ● 教學方式(Teaching Method) 理論講授、軟體操作、實務案例分析、工作坊與分組實作、個別指導與跨領域協作 ● 教學進度(Syllabus) 週次 主題 內容 01 課程概要 互動與生成式音樂概念介紹 02 音樂語言與聲音科技導論 聲音感知、音訊基礎、樂理、音樂元素、數位工具初探 03 軟體環境介紹 編曲軟體 Ableton Live、Max/MSP 基礎教學 04 MIDI 與數位音樂實務 MIDI 應用與數位音樂編輯 05 Max 與生成式音樂設計 軟體操作、生成式音樂邏輯、應用與範例展示 06 聲音合成基礎 振盪器、濾波器與聲音設計基礎 07 感測器與互動技術初探 Arduino、MIDI 裝置與感測器的互動設計基礎 08 期中專題提案 提出期中專題概念與設計規劃 09 進階聲音合成 FM 合成、顆粒合成與物理模擬技術進階介紹 10 音樂互動與健康促進案例 互動音樂設計、案例介紹與分析 11 資料聲音化概論 資料轉換聲音的基本技術與實作 12 影音互動與跨平台整合 影音互動、通訊協定(Protocol)與數值映射(Mapping)策略 13 使用者體驗設計 互動邏輯與介面設計 14 期末專題製作（一） 初步實作與測試 15 期末專題製作（二） 專案優化與展示準備 16 期末專題展示與講評 學生作品公開展示與成果講評 ● 成績考核(Evaluation) • 出席與課堂參與（30%） • 課堂練習與作業（20%） • 期中分組專題提案（20%） • 期末分組專題作品與公開展演（30%） ● 採用下列何項 AI 使用規則(Indicate which of the following options you use to manage student use of the AI) (1) 有條件開放，請註明如何使用生成式 AI 於課程產出 Conditionally open; please specify how generative AI will be used in course output 可參考下列網頁範例 See the following web page for examples. https://curricul.site.nthu.edu.tw/p/404-1208-248357.php?Lang=zh-tw ● 可連結之網頁位址(Course-related Website) 數位資源與補充硬體參考： • Max/MSP 官方文件 • Ableton Learn Synth • Ableton Learning Music • Cycling74 論壇 • 融聲創意部落格 • 音樂科技產品：Playtronica、Makey Makey、Bare Conductive Touch Board

docs.name: 運用生成式AI學習學術英語寫作
docs.text: 國立清華大學課程大綱 科號 Course Number EECS3060 學分 Credit 2 人數限制 Class Size 中文名稱 Course Title 運用生成式 AI 學習學術英語寫作 英文名稱 Course English Title Academic Writing based on Co-Intelligence 任課教師 Instructor 張俊盛（清華大學資訊系） 林子渝（凌格爾語言科技） 上課時間 Time R3R4 上課教室 Room 台達館 106 課程簡述(必填) (最多 500 個中文字) 本欄位資料會上傳教育部課程網 Brief Course Description (required) (50-200 words if possible, up to 1000 letters) 本課程結合寫作理論、範本應用與生成式 AI，系統性教授學術與科學寫作，涵蓋從標題、摘 要、簡介、相關研究、方法、結果、討論到結論的完整架構。課程以經典寫作理論為基礎，如 John Swales 的 CARS 模型，解析論文「簡介」的撰寫策略，並參考 Writing up Research 指導 「相關研究」的組織方式。此外，透過分析 Learning to Find Answers to Questions on the Web 這篇 經典論文，說明方法章節的撰寫技巧，強調問題陳述、步驟描述與虛擬碼應用，以取代過時的 流程圖呈現方式。對於數據與圖表的使用，則參考《Presenting Numbers, Tables, and Figures》，介 紹 Edward Tufte 的資訊設計理論，幫助學生提升研究成果的視覺化表達能力。 課程採翻轉教學模式，結合實體與線上學習，在課堂上以作業解答、問題討論與論文修改示範 為主，強調即時實作與累積評分制度，以提升學習成效。此外，課程導入生成式 AI，協助範本 分析、草稿修改與文獻檢索，並提供寫作輔導時段（Writing Clinic），讓學生獲得個別指導。透 過傳統與 AI 工具的結合，本課程幫助學生掌握學術英文寫作，提升論文品質與寫作效率。 課程內容「中文暨英文關鍵字」(必填) 至少 5 個,每個關鍵字至多 20 個中文,以半形逗點分隔 Please fill in at least 5 course keywords (up to 40 letters for each keyword) and use commas to separate them.(required) 學術英文寫作, 生成式 AI, 論文結構, 提示工程, 資訊設計 Academic English Writing, Generative AI, Thesis Structure, Prompt Engineering, Information Design 課程大綱(必填)Detailed Course Syllabus ● 課程說明(Course Description) 本課程融合傳統學術英文寫作理論與生成式人工智慧工具應用，從論文寫作基本概念著手，逐 步引導學生掌握文章之篇章結構、文脈連貫、語法與詞彙選擇。依據 John Swales 的 Create A Research Space (CARS) 理論，課程將詳述如何撰寫標題、摘要、簡介、相關研究、方法、結果 及結論，並運用實例分析與作業練習促進理論與實務的結合。 課程結合三大要素： 1. 寫作基本理論（一般寫作、學術寫作、科學研究寫作、資訊設計） 2. 範本 3. 生成式人工智慧和提示工程 主要是古典寫作理論技巧，再加上運用 Gen AI 的實際例子： 課程基本上照著論文（報告）的循序講授標題、摘要（關鍵詞、學科分類）、簡介、相關研究、 方法、實驗＋評估＋結果＋討論、結論。 1. 首先，用 John Swales 的論文簡介的理論（Create A Research Space, CARS」，說明如何寫「簡 介」。 2. 接著用 Writing up Research 這本書的 Related Work 那一章，來講如何寫「相關文獻」（現在 流行寫在「簡介」之後，而不是在「結果」）。 3. 接著用 Learning to Find Answers to Questions on the Web 這篇研究論文，來講如何寫「方 法」的小簡介、問題陳述、階段、步驟、虛擬碼 （pseudocod），而不要寫現在不流行的流 程圖。這篇經典論文宛如油畫中的「蒙娜麗莎的微笑」，實現了幾乎所有的寫作理論之原 理。 4. 然後，以 Presenting numbers, tables, and figures 這本牛津大學出版社的 OneStepAhead 系列 小冊子，講授 Edwards Tufte 的資訊設計理論，如何運用在「結果」章節的圖表和圖表說明 （data commentary)）。 課程的進行，希望實體、線上兼具，課程內外都有安排（翻轉教室）。在教室不做死板的講授， 而是以作業解答 （演習課）、問問題、討論、論文修改演示為教學模式。每次上課都有現場作 業，並累積評分。 課程特色： 1. 學術英文寫作（報告、學位論文、期刊論文） 2. 導入生成式 AI ：分析範本修改草稿檢索文獻 3. 任務導向學習 （Problem-based Learning），寫自己的論文，或改別人論文 4. 老師、助教定點定時值班，提供寫作輔導 （Writing Clinic / Help Room） 5. 利用傳統和 AI 參考工具（詞典、語料庫工具） 例如：ChatGPT、NotebookLM、Linggle Search、NetSpeak、Linggle Write、 Linggle Read、Linggle EMI ● 指定用書(Text Books) （指定用書部分將依後續課程公告補充） ● 參考書籍(References) 1. Swales, J. M., & Feak, C. B. (2012). Academic Writing for Graduate Students: Essential Tasks and Skills (3rd ed.). University of Michigan Press. 2. Swales, J. M., & Feak, C. B. (2009). Writing Up Research: Experimental Research Report Writing for Students of English (2nd ed.). University of Michigan Press. 3. Alexander, J., Argent, S., & Spencer, J. (2004). Learning to Find Answers to Questions on the Web. The Open University. 4. Sowey, E. R. (2006). Presenting Numbers, Tables, and Charts. Oxford University Press. 5. Williams, J. M., & Bizup, J. (2016). Style: Lessons in Clarity and Grace (12th ed.). Pearson. 6. Macmillan Education. (2007). Improve Your Writing Skills. In Macmillan Dictionary for Advanced Learners. Macmillan. 7. Longknife, A., & Sullivan, K. (2012). The Art of Styling Sentences: 20 Patterns for Success (6th ed.). Barron’s Educational Series. ● 教學方式(Teaching Method) 1. 採用同步線上及非同步預錄課程相結合的模式 2. 課堂內設有翻轉教室、實作練習與現場討論 3. 課外輔以作業答疑、論文修改演示與寫作輔導 (Writing Clinic/Help Room) 4. 利用傳統資源（詞典、語料庫工具）搭配生成式 AI 工具（ChatGPT、Linggle Search、 NotebookLM、Linggle Write、Linggle Read、Linggle EMI）共同提升寫作技巧 ● 教學進度(Syllabus) 週次 主題 內容 01 課程概要 說明課程大綱、課程介紹 02 單元一：基本概念（一） 篇章、文脈、文法、詞彙基本概念講解 作業 1：分析範本、改寫論文 03 單元一：基本概念（二） 篇章、文脈、文法、詞彙基本概念講解 練習：編輯 TOEFL‑11 04 單元二：〈摘要〉〈簡介〉 〈總結〉（一） 範本分析與結構講解 作業 2：寫作簡介（預設題目） 05 單元二：〈摘要〉〈簡介〉 〈總結〉（二） 範本分析與結構講解 作業 2：寫作簡介（預設題目） 06 單元三：〈相關研究〉 分析說明相關研究範本 作業 3：寫作研究相關 07 單元四：〈方法〉（一） 分析說明〈方法〉範本（一） 作業 4：寫作方法 08 單元四：〈方法〉（二） 分析說明〈方法〉範本（二） 作業 4：寫作方法 09 單元四：〈方法〉（三） 分析說明〈方法〉範本（三） 作業 4：寫作方法 10 單元五：〈結果〉（一） 圖表、說明圖表文字、後測 PR（一） 作業 5：寫作結果 11 單元五：〈結果〉（二） 圖表、說明圖表文字、後測 PR（二） 作業 5：寫作結果 12 單元五：〈結果〉（三） 圖表、說明圖表文字、後測 PR（二） 作業 5：寫作結果 13 單元六：〈結論/摘要〉 分析說明範本 14 期末專題製作（一） 期末專題選題與初步撰寫 15 期末專題製作（二） 深入撰寫與修改 16 期末專題展示與講評 學生成果展示與口頭講評 (1) (2) 課程時間：16 週 (3) 主要採用以下 AI 工具：(a) ChatGPT (b) Linggle Search, Read, Write ● 成績考核(Evaluation) 1. 課堂作業佔平時成績（含前測、各單元作業及討論參與） 2. 期末報告、口頭發表與後測成績作為最終評量依據 3. 成績將依作業完成度、寫作質量與參與程度進行綜合評核 ● 採用下列何項 AI 使用規則(Indicate which of the following options you use to manage student use of the AI) (1) 完全開放使用且無須註明 Unrestricted use with no disclosure required (2) 有條件開放，請註明如何使用生成式 AI 於課程產出 Conditionally open; please specify how generative AI will be used in course output 學生在撰寫學術文章過程中，可運用生成式 AI 工具（如 ChatGPT、Linggle 系列工具等）進行 語句改良、提示工程與資料檢索；但最終稿件需明確註明所使用工具及使用情形，並接受教師 與助教的定期檢核與指導，以確保學術倫理與寫作原創性。 (3) 禁止使用，請註明相關的監管機制 Prohibited use; please specify relevant oversight (4) 本課程無涉及 AI 使用 Not applicable 可參考下列網頁範例 See the following web page for examples. https://curricul.site.nthu.edu.tw/p/404-1208-248357.php?Lang=zh-tw ● 可連結之網頁位址 相關網頁(Personal Website)
