docs.name: 策略性人力資源管理
docs.text: 1 Strategic Human Resource Management Instructor Information Instructor George S. Benson, Ph.D. Office Number COB 209 Office Telephone Number 817-272-3412 Email Address benson@uta.edu Faculty Profile https://www.uta.edu/profiles/george-benson Office Hours By Appointment via Teams Course Information Description of Course Content This is an applied course that examines how modern corporations use human resource management (HRM) to enhance organizational capabilities and achieve strategic objectives. Through the assigned readings, case discussion and various class exercises we will examine how the acquisition, deployment, assessment and retention of an organization’s workforce impacts productivity and firm performance in various contexts. Readings will cover the theory and research on strategic HRM as well as the various parts of a typical HR system. Some of the topics we will discuss include HR planning, recruitment, methods of selection, job design, and implementation of performance management processes. Cases will then be used to focus on specific strategic issues faced by companies including talent management, selecting for cultural fit, incentive pay, and organizational culture. No prior knowledge of HR is assumed and there are no prerequisites for this course. The approach of the course will be practical guidance for making staffing and management decisions in organizations based on explanatory theory and scientific research. In addition to learning the theory and topics of human resource management through readings and classroom lecture, this course cover the skills required for HR planning, selection, and conducting performance evaluations. The course material is not only useful for working in human resource departments, but for all managers who hire, train, and evaluate employees. 2 Student Learning Outcomes 1. Recognize the practices that comprise human resource management in modern corporations: a) Work design b) HR Planning c) Recruiting and selection d) Performance Management e) Total Rewards 2. Apply concepts and approaches to align HRM systems with business strategy. 3. Evaluate the role of HR in developing and maintaining organizational culture. 4. Discuss an analytics driven approach to developing HR practices. Required Textbooks and Other Course Materials Jeffrey A. Mello, Strategic Human Resource Management, 5th edition (Cengage Learning). Harvard Publishing Cases 1. Talent Recruitment at frog design Shanghai (#411040) 2. Box: The Evolution of Management Practices in a Startup (#HR43) Follow this link: https://hbsp.harvard.edu/import/785425 Required Readings in Canvas 1. Wright (2008). Human Resource Strategy: Adapting to the Age of Globalization. Alexandria, VA: Society for Human Resource Management. 2. Porter (2008). The Five Forces That Shape Strategy. Harvard Business Review, 86:1. 3. Bartlett & Ghoshal (2002). Building Competitive Advantage Through People. Sloan Management Review, 43:2. 4. Capelli and Tavis (2019). HR Goes Agile, Harvard Business Review, 96:2. 5. Ton (2012). Why good jobs are good for retailers. Harvard Business Review. 6. Donovan & Benko (2016). “AT&T’s Talent Overhaul,” Harvard Business Review. 7. Stahl et al. (2012). “Six Principles of Effective Talent Management,” MIT Sloan Management Review. 8. Nisen, M. (2015). Why GE had to kill its annual performance reviews after more than three decades. http://qz.com/428813/ge-performance-review-strategy-shift/ 9. Schaerer, M. & Swaab, R. Are You Sugarcoating Your Feedback Without Realizing It? Harvard Business Review Online. https://hbr.org/2019/10/are-you-sugarcoating-your-feedback-without- realizing-it? 10. Pfeffer (1998). Six Dangerous Myths About Pay. Harvard Business Review. 11. Huselid, Becker & Beatty (2005). “A players” or “A positions”? Harvard Business. 12. Davenport, Harris, Shapiro (2010). Competing on Talent Analytics. Harvard Business Review. 13. Chatman & Cha (2003). Leading by leveraging culture. California Management Review 45:4. 14. Porath (2016). Creating a More Humane Workplace Where Employees and Businesses Thrive. Society for Human Resource Management. 3 Grading Information GRADING A grade of A (90%), B (80%), C (70%), D (60%), or F (<60%) will be earned based on: Group Assignments HR And Strategy Example 10% Job Design Example 10% Total Rewards Example 10% Organizational Culture Scavenger Hunt 10% frog Design Selection Case 15% Box: The Evolution of Management at a Start-Up Case 15% Peer Evaluation 10% Individual Paper 20% Total 100% GROUP ASSIGNMENTS (80%) You will work in groups do a number of assignments and exercises. These will be done as a group and every group member will receive the same grade. Group members will be asked to rate teammates on group participation at the end of the class. Peer evaluation is 10% of the total grade. HR And Strategy Example (10%) Groups will give an example of how HR practices match or mismatch the strategy at an organization you are familiar with. Describe the organization and its strategy using the language from Mello Chapter 3. Then give an example of how a specific HR practice (job design, recruiting, selection, training, compensation, or performance appraisal) either supports that strategy by encouraging specific employee behaviors or works against the intended strategy by encouraging the wrong behaviors. Job Design Example (10%) Groups will give an example of an organization that you are familiar with that uses either a high involvement work design or a control-oriented work design. Describe the organization, the strategy and the nature of the work. If high involvement work designs such as those described in The Good Jobs Strategy lead to superior performance, why don’t all organizations use high involvement work design? Total Rewards Example (10%) Groups will give an example from an organization you are familiar with about a way in which total rewards practices demonstrate one of the myths from Jeff Pfeffer "Six Dangerous Myths About Pay". What would you recommend to change to improve this practice based on the concepts we have covered in this module. OR Give an example from an organization you are familiar with about a way in which total rewards practices has overcome one of these myths. Why is this practice effective total rewards based on the concepts we have covered? 4 Organizational Culture Scavenger Hunt (10%) This assignment requires you to do a "Scavenger Hunt" for organizational culture artifacts. Artifacts are representations or manifestations of culture - symbols or practices that reinforce organizational values. Then discuss how these artifacts work to reinforce company culture. What values are they intended to promote? How do they work to guide employee behavior? The scavenger hunt asks you to find: 1. Mission Statement 2. Founding Story 3. Story / Legend 4. Language – Shorthand / Lingo / Terminology 5. Visual or Graphic Identity / Logo 6. Ritual or Ceremony 7. Physical space 8. HR Practices: Recruiting 9. HR Practices: Socialization / Training 10. HR Practices: Rewards frog Design Selection Case (15%) This case requires you to develop rubrics for assessing job candidates for fit of job requirements and organizational culture. The case involves a very unique design firm called frog and requires you to select between two finalists for a job. Assess the candidates for the jobs of Associate Creative Director and Business Development Director against (1) the job requirements in Exhibit 6 and (2) the archetypes as detailed in Exhibit 7. (Hint: Make a spreadsheet). Resumes for the four finalist are in Canvas. This case can be accessed through Harvard Publishing. 1. Make recommendations for hiring decisions among the finalists. Who did you recommend and why? What factors did you weigh most heavily for each of the jobs? 2. How can hiring managers balance job-related skills and cultural fit when assessing candidates? Box: The Evolution of Management at a Start Up Case (15%) Each group will read and analyze the case “Box: The Evolution of Management Practice in a Start- up.” The case analysis should be approximately 6-8 pages in length double-spaced and presented in a narrative form with headings and sub-headings. Case questions are provided to guide your analysis. You will be graded on your response to each of these but the paper does not have to be written in question and answer format. Apply the concepts that we have covered over and give your assessment of the issues at Box and how HR matches company strategy as Box has grown and matured. Case write-ups will be graded based on your substantive response to each of the discussion questions. 1. Give a short overview of Box. 2. Describe Box’s strategy. How does Box compete? 3. Describe the culture at Box. What are its basic values and operating principles? 4. How is Box’s culture evolving as it grows and matures? 5. How do Box HR practices fit with the corporate strategy and culture? Asses the evolution of HR practices as the company has grown and matured. 6. What are the biggest HR challenges that Box faces with growth? Make some HR practice recommendations. 5 INDIVIDUAL PAPER (20%) This paper requires you to analyze a significant HRM issue in a large organization. The paper can be done in one of two ways: 1) identify an HRM problem and recommend a solution, or 2) detail how the organizational has already responded to a HRM issue and critique that response. Research should include interviewing relevant employees including an HR manager. All assessment should be based on the principles covered in the course and consistent with business strategy. The paper should include the following: Background information: You should begin with a basic description of the organization, the mission, strategy and relevant company history. Attach to your completed paper information on your source materials. This should include information on personal interviews conducted. Description of the issue and how it was handled: Summarize the issue which you have identified. Provide a short history of events including how the issue came about and what the organization did to address the issue. Assess the effectiveness of the HR practices in this situation and indicate the shared roles of HR department and line managers. Obtain copies of forms/documents such as job descriptions, employee selection tests, performance evaluation forms, organizational career management or succession plan, exit interview schedule, and any other item that helps to explain the issue. Your assessment: Give either recommendation for future action or your critique of the organization’s previous actions using the concepts discussed in class. Include reasons why the organization was successful or unsuccessful in dealing with the issue as well as specific recommendations for what managers could have done differently. Particular emphasis should be given to the alignment or misalignment of company strategy and the HR practices examined. The report should be approximately 6-8 pages, excluding exhibits, and presented in a narrative form with headings and sub-headings. The report will be evaluated primarily in terms of content, but 20 percent of the report score will be allocated to organization, compositional quality (style, spelling, grammar, and syntax), and appearance (typed or word-processed, headings and sub-headings, etc.) If two of you work for the same business organization, you can work together to obtain information. However, each of you must prepare a different individual HR report.

docs.text: 國立清華大學工業工程與工程管理學系張國浩林東盈©2025 114 學年度第 1 學期 11410 AIMS Fellows EMIM5002 大數據與決策分析 Big Data and Decision Analysis 任課教授：張國浩 教授 (Professor Kuo-Hao Chang, Ph.D.) E-Mail: chang@mx.nthu.edu.tw 辦公室：清華大學工程一館 713 室 Tel: 03-5742337 林東盈 教授 (Professor Dung-Yin Lin, Ph.D.) E-Mail: dylin@ie.nthu.edu.tw 辦公室：清華大學工程一館 814 室 Tel: 03-5742694 上課時間：每週五(Friday) 18:30~21:20 上課教室：綜四 223 (上機實做課程 工程一館 829) 一、課程說明 (Course Description) 學習有系統地分析策略決策問題、架構目標、評估方案的預期結果和可能的風 險、探討決策方案的執行，並應用數位決策與大數據分析技術並結合模擬分析，從巨 量資訊找出問題，並提出解決方案，透過大數據輔助決策，從問題架構、資料收集、 資訊整理、決策分析乃至決策輔助的完整思維過程，提供系統化、數位化之決策依據 與實行策略。除介紹大數據、作業研究與決策分析方法和工具外，並利用演講、個案 討論、上機實做和實證案例研究，培養策略性決策思維及應用資料挖礦解決相關問 題，進而提升大數據分析和數位決策能力。 二、課程大綱(Agenda) 週次 單元主題及參考資料 授課教 授 附註 1 最佳化簡介 林東盈 2 運輸與指派問題概念 林東盈 3 運輸與指派實務案例分析與應用 林東盈 4 生產排程問題概念 林東盈 5 生產排程問題案例分析與應用 林東盈 6 10/10 雙十節停課一次 7 人員排班問題與維修排程概念與案例應用 林東盈 8 期中報告 林東盈 9 Decision Analysis (1) 張國浩 現場練習並繳交作業 與 Case study 10 Decision Analysis (2) 張國浩 現場練習並繳交作業 國立清華大學工業工程與工程管理學系張國浩林東盈©2025 114 學年度第 1 學期 11 Simulation (1)(2) * A refresher on Probability and Statistics [Video] 張國浩 現場上機練習並繳交 作業 12 Simulation (3) 張國浩 現場上機練習並繳交 作業 13 Stochastic Optimization: Introduction 張國浩 現場上機練習並繳交 作業 14 Stochastic Optimization: Direct Search Method 張國浩 現場上機練習並繳交 作業 15 Stochastic Optimization: Stochastic Approximation 張國浩 現場上機練習並繳交 作業 16 期末報告 張國浩 三、成績考核 (Evaluation) 1. 課堂練習與作業 15% (個人) 2. 軟體實做 15% (2 人一組為原則，上課完成) 3. Case study 10% (4 人一組為原則，每人報告兩次) 4. 期中報告 50% (4 人一組為原則) 5. 期末報告 10% (4 人一組為原則) 四、課程網頁資源(Resources) 講義及案例的原始論文和相關資料：https://elearn.nthu.edu.tw/

docs.name: 跨領域研究方法
docs.text: 國立清華大學課程大綱 科號 Course Number 11410EMIM501700 學分 Credit 3 人數限制 Class Size AIMS Fellows 中文名稱 Course Title 跨領域研究方法 英文名稱 Course English Title Interdisciplinary Research Methods 任課教師 Instructor 曾元琦 上課時間 Time RaRbRc 上課教室 Room 綜四 223 課程簡述(必填) (最多 500 個中文字) 本欄位資料會上傳教育部課程網 Brief Course Description (required) (50-200 words if possible, up to 1000 letters) 本課程旨在引導學生掌握進行跨領域研究所需的核心方法與學術寫作能力，涵蓋從研究設 計、資料蒐集到成果撰寫的完整研究流程，並透過實作經驗逐步深化理解與應用。學生將 學習如何依據具體問題與情境背景，選擇與整合適切的研究策略，提出具備實證基礎的創 新解方。課程前半段聚焦於研究設計與方法論建構，內容涵蓋研究問題的界定、資料蒐集 與分析策略、跨領域合作的實務挑戰，以及研究倫理與學術責任。透過案例分析與小組討 論，學生將培養實務敏感度，並強化與異質專業背景研究者協作的能力。後半段則專注於 科技論文撰寫技巧，依序涵蓋文獻綜述撰寫、研究方法與結果呈現、討論與結論發展，進 一步延伸至標題設計與摘要撰寫。課程將寫作視為研究思維發展與深化的關鍵歷程，透過 書寫的過程，學生將學習如何釐清問題意識、反思研究決策、修正論述方向，進而強化其 跨領域整合與溝通能力。學生將透過漸進式的寫作演練與回饋修正，有系統地提升論文的 結構邏輯、語言表達與學術溝通力，最終能完整表達其研究成果，並與相關領域進行有效 交流。 課程內容「中文暨英文關鍵字」(必填) 至少 5 個,每個關鍵字至多 20 個中文,以半形逗點分隔 Please fill in at least 5 course keywords (up to 40 letters for each keyword) and use commas to separate them.(required) 研究方法, 跨領域合作, 研究設計, 研究溝通, 研究成果展示 Research Methods, Cross-disciplinary Collaboration, Research Design, Research Communication, Research Presentation 課程大綱(必填)Detailed Course Syllabus ● 課程說明(Course Description) 本課程旨在引導學生掌握進行跨領域研究所需的核心方法與學術寫作能力，涵蓋從研究設 計、資料蒐集到成果撰寫的完整研究流程，並透過實作經驗逐步深化理解與應用。學生將 學習如何依據具體問題與情境背景，選擇與整合適切的研究策略，提出具備實證基礎的創 新解方。課程前半段聚焦於研究設計與方法論建構，內容涵蓋研究問題的界定、資料蒐集 與分析策略、跨領域合作的實務挑戰，以及研究倫理與學術責任。透過案例分析與小組討 論，學生將培養實務敏感度，並強化與異質專業背景研究者協作的能力。後半段則專注於 科技論文撰寫技巧，依序涵蓋文獻綜述撰寫、研究方法與結果呈現、討論與結論發展，進 一步延伸至標題設計與摘要撰寫。課程將寫作視為研究思維發展與深化的關鍵歷程，透過 書寫的過程，學生將學習如何釐清問題意識、反思研究決策、修正論述方向，進而強化其 跨領域整合與溝通能力。學生將透過漸進式的寫作演練與回饋修正，有系統地提升論文的 結構邏輯、語言表達與學術溝通力，最終能完整表達其研究成果，並與相關領域進行有效 交流。 ● 指定用書(Text Books) Wallwork, Adrian. English for writing research papers. Springer Nature, 2023. ● 參考書籍(References) Research Papers in ACM digital library; IEEE Xplore; Related SCI/SSCI Journals ● 教學方式(Teaching Method) 本課程採多元教學方式進行，以理論與實作並重，強調學習過程中的思辨與應用能力： • 講義授課：系統性介紹研究方法與論文寫作相關理論基礎。 • 文獻導讀與分享：閱讀與分析關鍵研究方法文獻，並由學生進行簡報與反思討論。 • 實務專家經驗分享：邀請具跨領域研究實務經驗的專家學者進行現身說法與案例講 解。 • 小組討論與研究專案演練：透過實際研究設計與模擬練習，深化跨領域整合與合作 能力。 • 論文撰寫練習與回饋：分階段進行科技論文各部分的撰寫練習，搭配師生個別回饋 與同儕互評。 ● 教學進度(Syllabus) • 課程導論與跨領域研究導引 • 研究問題的界定與提問技巧 • 研究方法概論與分類 • 資料蒐集與分析方法（一）：訪談與觀察 • 資料蒐集與分析方法（二）：問卷與實驗設計 • 跨領域研究的挑戰與協作 • 研究倫理與學術責任 • 研究設計工作坊與初步提案分享 • 文獻綜述與資料整理技巧 • 論文撰寫架構與標題、摘要設計 • 撰寫研究方法與研究結果章節 • 撰寫討論與結論章節 • 學術表達與邏輯建構 • 初稿發表與同儕回饋 • 完稿修訂與成果呈現 • 成果發表與課程總結 ● 成績考核(Evaluation) • 相關研究方法閱讀報告 (個人) 20% • 相關研究方法課堂分享 (小組) 20% • 研究方法應用實作與發表 (小組) 30% • 專案報告 (小組) 20% • 課程參與 (個人) 10% ● 採用下列何項 AI 使用規則(Indicate which of the following options you use to manage student use of the AI) 本課程鼓勵學生在透明與負責的原則下，適度使用 AI 工具進行課業協作。學生應在作業或 報告的標題頁註腳或引用文獻部分簡要說明 AI 工具的使用情況，並遵循學校的相關指引。 如未明確標註，教師有權重新評分或不予計分。 ● 可連結之網頁位址 相關網頁(Personal Website) https://mx.nthu.edu.tw/~yc.tseng/zh-tw.html

docs.text: National Tsing Hua University College of Technology Management Course Syllabus 科號 Course Number EMM 6009 學分 Credit 2 人數限制 Size of Limit 50 中文名稱 Course Title 大數據與商業決策分析 英文名稱 Course English Title Big Data Analytics and Business Decision Making 任課教師 Instructor 林世昌 教師聯絡方式 Contact Information slin@mx.nthu.edu.tw 上課時間 Time December 2025 上課教室 Room Malaysia or Thailand 先修科目 Prerequisite(s) 本課程對應之學習目標與核心能力 Aligned Learning Goals and Learning Objectives We have entered the era of Big Data in recent years. Big Data has been taken as the savior to troubling business and there are tons of magic applications throughout the private sector. 課程目標 Course Objectives 1. To develop students’ understanding of core concepts and techniques in big data analytics 2. To enhance data-driven decision-making skills for solving real-world business problems 3. To improve students’ ability to visualize, interpret, and communicate data insights effectively 4. To equip students with hands-on experience in using big data tools and platforms 5. To broaden students’ awareness of how big data is applied across various business domains such as marketing, finance, and operations 課程說明 Course Description In the era of digital transformation, data is not just an asset -- it is a strategic imperative. This course equips EMBA students with the analytical mindset, frameworks, and tools necessary to harness big data for effective business decision making. Designed for experienced professionals, the course bridges the gap between data science and executive leadership, focusing on how to interpret data-driven insights and translate them into strategic actions. Through hands-on exercises, real-world case studies, and interactive lectures, students will learn to apply core concepts of big data analytics -- including data visualization, predictive modeling, machine learning, and business intelligence -- to solve complex challenges in areas such as marketing, operations, finance, and human resources. Students will also explore ethical and governance issues in data use, and gain practical exposure to widely-used analytical tools such as STATA (no prior coding experience required). The course culminates in a team-based project where students tackle a real business problem using data analytics to drive decision-making and value creation. 指定用書 Textbooks National Tsing Hua University College of Technology Management Course Syllabus Lecture notes TBA 參考書籍 References TBA 教學方式 Teaching Approach Lectures Class participation Discussion 評分標準 Grading [tentative and subject to change] Participation, assignment, or presentation (term paper) required by the instructor 教學進度 Course Schedule 1. Introduction of the basic idea of Big Data 1) Concepts of data (file, image, video etc) 2) Concepts of database (relational/ non-relational) 3) Concepts of AI, deep learning and blockchain 2. Application of the Big Data in general business 1) Dealing with hands-on “huge” data 2) Some business applications 課程相關連接 Course Related Links

docs.text: 國立清華大學科技管理學院 MBA Program HUMAN RESOURCE MANAGEMENT 授課教師：劉玉雯 ( ywliu@mx.nthu.edu.tw) 助教：TBD 教學目標： 本課程介紹人力資源管理相關的基本原理和應用。希望學員們通過本課程的學 習與課堂實踐，能夠： • 理解人力資源管理在組織中的作用及其對提升組織工作效能的意義。 • 掌握制定企業人力資源管理策略和管理制度的常用方法。 • 懂得現代人力資源管理原理和實踐中意義及操作實施方法。 • 探討組織中人力資源管理的現實問題。 • 闡述人力資源實踐在企業變革和發展中的作用。 • 結合課堂學習，工作單位的具體情況和個人的工作及管理實踐經驗，每 個參與學員都能學習，理解，並且一定程度上運用相關人力資源管理的 知識和技能。 AI 使用規則 (The conduct used in managing student use of the AI): 報告及作業內容，有條件開放使用 AI，但請註明如何使用生成式 AI 於課程產 出 (Conditionally open; please specify how generative AI will be used in course output.) 課程大綱： 日 期 課程內容 (tentative) Session 1 人才甄選 Session 2 績效管理 & Coaching Session 3 激勵 Session 4 國際人管、個案討論 演講安排：TBD。 學期成績： 課堂討論與參與（50％） 個案討論 (50%) 中文翻譯參考書籍： 如果有興趣人力資源管理與行為研究的學員，以下列舉的書籍都是值得閱 讀，這些書籍的共同特色是，他們的寫作都是建構在理論和研究的基礎上， 大部份的都是以實驗來說明個人、群體、組織的行為議題，與坊間的勵志書 籍是非常不同。而且這些書籍作者大部份都是非常知名的學者，有些是非常 有名的專欄作者。任何一本書都可以讓各位同學把管理理論和實務連接。建 議同學可以挑選 1 本書籍來閱讀。 Jeffrey Pfeffer，善良心機(Power)，時報文化 Jeffrey Pfeffer & Robert Sutton，真相，傳言與胡扯，紅螞蟻出版 Jeffrey Pfeffer，破除舊思維建立管理新觀念，梅霖文化 David Surowiecki， 群眾的智慧，遠流 Malcolm Gladwell，決斷 2 秒間，時報出版 Malcolm Gladwell，異數，時報文化 Robert Cialdini，影響力，久石文化 Christopher Hsee（奚愷元），別當正常的傻瓜，久石文化 Rom Brafman，左右決策的迷惑力，遠流 Kay-yut Chen & Marina Krakosky，金錢實驗室的人性考驗，財信 Dan Ariely，誰說人是理性的，天下文化 Dan Ariley，誰說人是誠實的！天下文化 Sheena Iyengar，誰在操縱你的選擇，漫遊者 Peter Ubel，直覺 (Free Market Madness)，中信出版（簡體字翻譯） Steven Levitt & Stephen Jubner，超爆蘋果橘子經濟學，時報 Steven Levitt & Stephen Jubner，蘋果橘子思考術，大塊文化 Brian Wansink，瞎吃，木馬文化 Daniel Pink，動機：單純的力量，大塊文化 Richard Thaler，推力，時報 Gerd Gigerenzer，半秒直覺，大塊文化 Joseph Hallinan，我們為什麼老犯錯，時報 Richard Layard，快樂經濟學，經濟新潮社 Michael Sandel，正義，雅言文化 Michael Sandel，錢買不到的東西，先覺 Francesca Gino, 為什麼我們的決定常出錯？ 商周出版 Christopher Chabris & Daniel Simons，為什麼你沒看見大猩猩，天下文化 Rolf Dobelli，行為的藝術，商周出版社 David McRaney，任何人都會有的思考盲點，李茲文化出版 Uni Gneezy & John List，一切都是誘因的問題，天下文化 Richard Wiseman，怪咖心理學 1&2，漫遊者文化 Sendhil Mullainathan & Eldar Shafir，匱乏經濟學，遠流出版 Douglas Kenrick & Vladas Griskevicus，誰說人類不理性，橡實文化 鄭毓煌、蘇丹，理性的非理性，中國出版社（簡體字） Niven,Paul R.,& Ben Larmorte. 執行 OKR, 帶出強團隊 : Google、Intel、 Amazon……一流公司激發個人潛能、凝聚團隊向心力、績效屢創新高的首選目 標管理法, 采實文化, 2019. John Doerr, 2019, OKR : 做最重要的事, 許瑞宋譯. 遠見天下文化 Charles Hany, 2020, 你是誰，比你做什麼更重要：英國管理大師韓第寫給你的 21 封信！，天下文化, Reed Hastings, Erin Meyer (2020), 零規則, 天下雜誌 Amy Edmondson(2023), 心理安全的力量, 天下雜誌

docs.name: 營銷管理
docs.text: 清華 EMBA『營銷管理』課程介紹 授課教師：丘宏昌 課程說明（introduction） 市場的變化一向是詭譎莫測的。2000 年以前，沒人會認為摩托羅拉也會沒落；2005 年，也沒人相信諾基亞會產生這麼大的衰退。對企業來說，行銷的重點，在於洞察顧客 需求、並替企業替客戶創造價值之後，更要能為自己帶來利潤，進而持續成長。本課程 主要針對企業負責人或高管，針對戰略行銷的相關內容加以探討，並搭配行業的實務案 例來進行講授，協助企業獲得更高利潤、達到成長目的。 Understanding customer behaviors is difficult. The fallings of Motorola and Nokia imply the rapid change of markets, technologies, and competitors. To a business manager, marketing is a process to create, communicate, and deliver values to target customers and make profits. This course is specifically designed for top managers. 教學目標（Objective） 1. 認識現階段行銷的觀念 2. 瞭解策略性行銷的流程與差異化 3. 瞭解 B2B 與 B2C 的行銷方式 4. 討論實務案例並與理論相結合 參考用書 Philip Kotler; Marketing Management: Analysis, Planning, and Control; Prentice Hall. 教學方式（teaching methods） Lecture, discussion, presentation and case studies 成績考核 Participation: 80%; Final report: 20% 教學安排 模組 1：行銷、價值與洞察  模組主題：價值銷售、價值拆解與價值主張、洞察力  案例材料：蘋果公司 模組 2：互聯網行銷  模組主題：行銷思維的演進、互聯網口碑行銷的創造方法、互聯網與物聯網思 維  案例材料：O2O 的機會與威脅 模組 3：行銷與差異化  模組主題：行銷短視症、差異化的迷思、行銷差異化的方式 模組 4：戰略行銷  模組主題：STP＋4P、B2B 市場區隔、戰略行銷與競爭優勢  案例材料：主題遊樂園 模組 5：戰略行銷實戰分析  模組主題：戰略行銷、功能行銷、戰術行銷、錨點效應、誘餌效應 模組 6：品牌戰略  模組主題：知名、聯想、品質、忠誠

docs.name: 公司金融
docs.text: 課程大綱 課程名稱(中)： 公司金融 課程名稱(英)： Corporate Finance 授課教師： 朱玉杰 /北京清華大學經濟管理學院金融系教授 辦公室： 李華樓 309 電子郵件： zhuyj@sem.tsinghua.edu.cn 辦公電話： 62796232 課程描述（教學目標，主要內容，授課方式） 1、公司金融課程涵蓋了現代財務管理的基礎知識，幷會對企業一些基本財務政策的影響進行分 析。通過學習現代公司金融基本原理及其在實踐中的運用，使學生瞭解企業財務决策過程及影 響財務决策各因素相互之間的關係，爲將來的管理實踐和進一步研究打下基礎。 2、本課程的教學手段是課堂講授與案例教學相結合，通過講課形式傳授公司財務方面的基本知 識，通過案例討論加深對公司金融理論知識的理解和實際分析能力本課程將通過（1）外請講座 （2）案例研究和（3）對現代公司金融理論和公共觀點的討論，使學生系統掌握公司金融和財 務管理的基本理論、基本方法、基本技能；熟練運用理財技術進行投資、融資和收益分配决策。 3、本課程包括以下幾個主題: (1) 財務管理的目標爲導向，以金融市場爲背景，系統介紹了證 券估價模型、風險與收益權衡模型；投資决策模型。(2) 資本成本的計量與分析；長短期融資 方式的特點及運作方式；證券投資；資本結構和股利政策等。(3)企業引進風險投資、上市、幷 購、重組等。 教材與參考資料 指定教科書：公司理財，Stephen A. Ross 等著，吳世農等譯，機械工業出版社 授課主題 1 導論、淨現值與證券估值 2 投資决策分析 3 風險與資本資産定價模型、企業融資 4 資本結構、有效資本市場 5 估值 6 股利政策、併購

docs.name: 價值投資-公司併購與重組
docs.nameEn: Value Investment-Equity Investment and Corporate Restructuring
docs.text: National Tsing Hua University College of Technology Management Course Syllabus 科號 Course Number EMS 501300 學分 Credit 2 人數限制 Size of Limit 中文名稱 Course Title 價值投資—公司併購與重組 英文名稱 Course English Title Value Investment — Equity Investment and Corporate Restructuring 任課教師 Instructor 陸瑤 教師聯絡方式 Contact Information luyao@sem.tsinghua.edu.cn 上課時間 Time 上課教室 Room 深圳研究生院 先修科目 Prerequisite(s) 無 本課程對應之學習目標與核心能力 Aligned Learning Goals and Learning Objectives 併購重組是現代企業快速發展和價值提升的重要戰略行為。如何通過資本市場併購重 組實現企業價值1+1>2和1-1>0？課程將從不同層次全面介紹併購重組的動機，交易的實操 過程，以及如何對併購重組交易進行科學的決策與效果的評估。最終，課程將幫助你從 理論到實操全方位瞭解企業如何進行價值投資，通過併購與重組的管道來提升價值和創 造財富，成為資本市場運作的精英。 課程目標 Course Objectives 併購重組是現代企業快速發展和價值提升的重要戰略行為。如何通過資本市場併購重 組實現企業價值1+1>2和1-1>0？課程將從不同層次全面介紹併購重組的動機，交易的實操 過程，以及如何對併購重組交易進行科學的決策與效果的評估。最終，課程將幫助你從 理論到實操全方位瞭解企業如何進行價值投資，通過併購與重組的管道來提升價值和創 造財富，成為資本市場運作的精英。 課程說明 Course Description 課程將包括併購動機，盡職調查，併購交易結構的設計，資產估值，控制權設計與爭 奪，交易後整合，其他的企業重組方式以及數位經濟轉型下的公司併購重組與產業發展 新趨勢8個模組。課程通過8個模組打造了完整的併購重組價值投資的知識體系。課程不僅 包括併購重組相關的基本理論知識，還將帶領你瞭解中國民營企業吉利汽車如何規避資 本市場風險成功並購國際大公司賓士汽車母公司戴姆勒；中國上市公司西王食品如何蛇 吞象併購全球最大保健品公司加拿大公司KERR；國際知名高科技公司思科如何通過與紅 杉資本多年的“上市公司+PE”的協同並購保持30年全球技術領先等鮮活經典商業案例。 指定用書 Textbooks 講義。 參考書籍 References  Mergers and Acquisitions (Text and Cases), by B. Rajesh Kumar Published by The McGraw-Hill Companies  Mergers Acquisitions from A to Z, by Andrew J. Sherman by The McGraw-Hill Companies 教學方式 Teaching Approach 理論講授與案例教學相結合。 評分標準 Grading 課堂表現（30%），小組案例分析（70%） 教學進度 Course Schedule 日期 授課內容 未定 課程介紹：併購與股權投資動機 未定 盡職調查：併購與股權投資交易結構設計 未定 併購與股權投資交易結構設計 未定 資產估值 未定 股權與控制權設計；併購後整合 未定 其他重組方式；數字經濟轉型下的公司併購重組與產業 發展新趨勢 期末並購案例展示 課程相關連接 Course Related Links 無 未定 *若有任何異動會於課堂上佈達 陸瑤 清華大學，經管學院，金融系 教授(長聘)，金融系副主任 辦公室 清華大學，經管學院，偉倫樓 347 電話 (86) (10) 62797399， 13691288499 郵箱 luyao@sem.tsinghua.edu.cn 陸瑤，清華大學經管學院, 金融系，教授（長聘），副系主任。教育部青年長江學者； 2009 年獲得美國密西根大學-安娜堡分校(University of Michigan -- Ann Arbor)羅斯商學院(Ross School of Business) 博士 Ph.D. in Business Economics; 在這之前獲得美國紐約大學斯特恩商學 院 (New York University, Stern School of Business) 統計學-金融工程方向碩士學位，中央財經 大學經濟學學士學位。 主要研究領域為公司治理，企業並購與重組，企業投資與融資，技術變革對企業投融資 以及發展的影響，資本市場改革與發展等。講授課程包括《公司組織與治理》（EMBA， MCFO，MBA）、《公司金融》（MBA，金融碩士）、《公司並購與重組》（MBA，金融 碩士，慕課）等。 曾獲清華大學經管學院教學優秀獎；清華大學經管學院高管教育培訓中心（EE）教學新 星獎；清華大學經管學院 EMBA 優秀責任教授。 曾獲國家自然科學基金委，“優秀青年科學基金”，“清華大學學術新人獎”，國家自然科 學基金 “特優” 結題。 曾經在國內外頂級權威學術期刊發表論文 39 篇。其中，包括《Journal of Finance》， 《Management Science》，《Journal of Financial Economics》，《Journal of Financial and Quantitative Analysis》，《Review of Finance》，《Journal of Corporate Finance》，《經濟研 究》，《管理世界》，《金融研究》，《管理科學學報》，等頂級國內外學術期刊。 目前擔任清華大學公司治理中心副主任；清華大學經管學院高管培訓中心（EE）學術委 員；經管學院 EMBA 學術委員；TIEMBA（Tsinghua-INSEAD EMBA）專案學術主任：清華 大學中國現代國有企業研究院執行委員會委員。曾經擔任清華 X-lab (清華大學創意創新創業 教育平臺)學術副主任。 其他學術兼職還包括：中國金融學會理事；清華大學產業創新與金融研究院，研究員； 清華大學國家治理與全球治理研究院，研究員；中國交叉科學研究會金融量化分析與電腦專 業委員會，常務委員；清華大學現代管理研究中心，兼職研究員，等。 另外，她的多篇文章被哈佛大學公司治理論壇所收錄。主要學術兼職包括擔任《Pacific- Basin Finance Journal》(SSCI)亞洲太平洋地區最主要的金融學學術期刊，副主編。 擔任 《Corporate Governance: An International Review 》(SSCI) 的編委會成員(Editorial Board）。

docs.name: 公司治理與企業社會責任
docs.text: National Tsing Hua University College of Technology Management Course Syllabus 科號 Course Number EMS 502000 學分 Credit 2 人數限制 Size of Limit 30 中文名稱 Course Title 公司治理與企業社會責任 英文名稱 Course English Title Corporate Governance and Corporate Social Responsibility 任課教師 Instructor 蔡昌憲、謝英哲 教師聯絡方式 Contact Information chstsai@mx.nthu.edu.tw; ych@mx.nthu.edu.tw 上課時間 Time 上課教室 Room 台積館 先修科目 Prerequisite(s) 無 本課程對應之學習目標與核心能力 Aligned Learning Goals and Learning Objectives Graduates will demonstrate their abilities to identify and evaluate ethical issues in business decisions, probable outcomes and effects on stakeholders. (a). Students will identify and analyze ethical issues facing management problems. (b). Students will formulate an argument about an ethical issue from multiple perspectives. 課程目標 Course Objectives 本課程旨在引導學生分析、討論公司治理和企業社會責任相關議題與全球發展趨勢，以 及與前述議題有關之法律及公共政策對於企業運作的影響。通過本課程的學習，同學們 能夠：  明確理解公司治理、企業社會責任和可持續發展的內涵與影響。  培養學生對相關商業倫理議題的敏銳度與分析判斷能力。  深入了解公司治理與企業社會責任的概念，內涵與發展趨勢，並能夠運用於實際 商業場域。  了解公司治理和企業社會責任與商業行為的關聯，以及在不同行業的操作和影 響。 課程說明 Course Description 課程內容包含：  公司治理與法律風險控管  企業倫理、企業社會責任與永續發展 指定用書 Textbooks 參考書籍 References National Tsing Hua University College of Technology Management Course Syllabus 無 教學方式 Teaching Approach 教師講授，課堂討論，案例分析，小組任務，實踐案例分享與討論 評分標準 Grading 課堂出勤和參與: 40% 個案討論和小組報告: 60% 教學進度 Course Schedule （內容暫定） Day 1: 認識董事與經理人的法律風險 Day 2: 因應財務風險的公司治理對策 Day 3: 企業倫理與實務（利害關係人與倫理決策、倫理領導 、企業倫理角色扮演） Day 4: 企業社會責任（氣候變遷及企業永續發展、聯合國永續發展目標 SDGs、企業社 會任報告書、重大永續議題矩陣、循環經濟、社會創新與永續發展） 課程相關連接 Course Related Links None

docs.text: 1 INTRODUCTION TO WESTERN LITERATURE Instructor: Chien-heng Wu COURSE DESCRIPTION This course introduces the first-year student of literature to some of the major concepts, themes, as well as some of the most famous narratives, characters, and literary forms of the western literary tradition. The aim of such a course is to provide students the basic tools, concepts, and reading knowledge for more advanced study of western literature in upper-level courses beyond their first year at the university. While such a course does not offer a comprehensive coverage of all the major texts of western literature, it conceptualizes the western literary tradition as a series of debates and issues for discussion. We will analyze the literary texts in their historical, cultural, and political contexts, and we will examine the significance of these texts for the western literary tradition. COURSE OBJECTIVE 1. Introduce students to the masterpieces of Western literature from its inception to the 16th century. 2. Develop students’ appreciation for values and ideals that have come to shape societies and cultures in the West. 3. Cultivate students’ analytic skills (e.g. textual and contextual analysis). GRADING • Participation: 35% • Presentation: 20% • Midterm: 15% • Final: 30% * Please apply for a free Office365 account at http://learning.cc.nthu.edu.tw/p/412-1319- 12292.php?Lang=zh-tw. After registration, please download the application Teams. I will set up a forum for online discussion and communication. GENERATIVE AI USAGE POLICY In this course, we encourage the responsible and ethical use of generative artificial intelligence (AI) tools, such as ChatGPT, to assist in the learning process. These tools can be valuable for 2 generating ideas, providing inspiration, and enhancing your understanding of course material. However, it is crucial that students transparently indicate where and how AI-generated content has been used in their work. To promote academic integrity and ensure appropriate use of AI tools, please adhere to the following guidelines: 1. Citing AI-generated content: If you use any AI-generated content in your assignments, papers, presentations, or other course-related work, you must clearly cite the AI tool used as a source. Include the name of the AI tool, version, and date of access in your citation. For example: Generated with the assistance of ChatGPT-4, OpenAI, accessed on May 5, 2023. 2. Originality and authenticity: While incorporating AI-generated content is allowed, it should not be the sole basis for your work. You are expected to use your own thoughts, ideas, and understanding of the course material to create original and authentic work. AI- generated content should be supplementary and contribute to your overall argument or analysis. 3. Collaborative use of AI tools: If you are working on a group project or engaging in a class discussion, ensure that all group members or participants are aware of the use of AI- generated content. Discuss and evaluate the generated content together, to promote transparency and shared understanding. 4. Ethical considerations: Be mindful of the potential biases and limitations of AI-generated content. Always critically evaluate the accuracy, relevance, and ethical implications of AI- generated content before incorporating it into your work. 5. Continuous learning and reflection: Use AI-generated content as a tool to expand your knowledge and understanding of the course material, rather than as a shortcut to complete assignments. Reflect on how the AI-generated content has contributed to your learning process and consider what you have learned from the interaction. By adhering to these guidelines, you will be able to harness the power of generative AI in a responsible and ethical manner, while ensuring academic integrity and maintaining a focus on your own learning and development. * This policy is generated with the help of ChatGPT-4, accessed May 05, 2023. The students will get to practice English listening and speaking under different contexts, and they will learn to use English comfortably to communicate their ideas with others. The first semester focuses on using idioms in conversations, impromptu speech, and doing interviews in English (Language exchange project). The second semester focuses on debates and negotiation in English and producing English videos (Youtuber project). ● Textbook No textbook for this class. You are encourage to prepare a personal notebook (for taking notes!). Relevant handouts or supplementary materials will be distributed in class. All announcements will be posted on the course website at https://eeclass.nthu.edu.tw/ ● Course requirement and evaluations Class attendance / Participation / Learning attitude 10% Attendance is required and important because you get to interact with other classmates and have an opportunity to practice English directly. Your active participation during the class are highly encouraged. The more you speak and participate in the class discussion, the better score you get for this category. Absence should be notified before the class, and absences will result in grade deduction. If you have more than THREE absences (regardless of the reason), you get ZERO for this category. Voluntary Speaking in class 5% Everyone is required to participate in class. You are asked to raise your hand and respond to questions under discussion, at least FIVE times! (The class TA will help to keep the records!) Weekly Listening Exercises [Website Discussion Forum] 20% To improve your listening ability, there will be weekly listening exercises that you are required to do as your individual homework. The students will take turns each week (from Week 3~13) to post their interested English-spoken video (at least 6~10 min long) and propose THREE relevant open-ended questions on the course website (at the discussion forum section 討論區). All the other classmates will go to the website, watch the posted videos, and then respond to the questions in English directly on the website. docs.text: Department of Foreign Languages and Literature National Tsing Hua University Fall 2025 Course Outline Course: Reading ＆ Writing I Lectures: Tuesday 10:10 am -12:00 pm Instructor: Dr. Fan-pei Gloria Yang Office: HSS A526 Office hours: Tuesdays 6:30~7:30 pm by appointment only email: fpyang@faculty.hss.nthu.edu.tw (include FE in the subject line) Aim of class: This 16-week course is designed to develop students’ writing skills through the study of narrative craft, rhetorical techniques, and reflective writing. Students will read and analyze three texts—"The Strength in Our Scars" by Bianca Sparacino, "A Man Called Ove" by Fredrik Backman, and "The Cat Who Went to Heaven" by Elizabeth Coatsworth—to explore storytelling, emotional resonance, and persuasive techniques. The course emphasizes the writing process, as outlined by Purdue OWL’s Writing Process resources, with a focus on prewriting, drafting, revising, and editing. Through discussions, writing assignments, workshops, and a culminating term paper, students will refine their ability to craft compelling narratives and arguments. Course requirement: ➢ Master the stages of the writing process: prewriting, drafting, revising, and editing. ➢ Analyze narrative structures and rhetorical strategies in the assigned texts. ➢ Develop clear, persuasive, and emotionally engaging written work. ➢ Engage in critical discussions about literature and its societal implications. ➢ Practice peer review and collaborative feedback to improve writing. ➢ Produce a well-researched term paper synthesizing themes and rhetorical techniques across the texts. ➢ Each student has to turn in assignments on time. Grading Criteria: Your grade will be calculated based on the following components: ➢ Personal Narrative (15%): 750-word narrative (Week 4). ➢ Rhetorical Analysis Essay (20%): 800-word analysis of '’The Strength in Our Scars'’ (Week 7). ➢ Narrative Scene (15%): 750-word scene inspired by '’A Man Called Ove'’(Week 10). ➢ Short Story (15%): 750-word story inspired by '’The Cat Who Went to Heaven'’ (Week 13). ➢ Term Paper (25%): 1500–2000-word comparative analysis of all three texts (Week 16). ➢ Participation and Workshops (10%): Engagement in discussions and peer reviews. ● Send all the assignments to Discord channel before the class time, late submission will be 0 point. ● Please ask for assistance at least 2 days before the deadline, or we have the right to ignore your questions. Teaching method: ➢ Presentation by the instructor. ➢ Tutorial by the instructor. ➢ Reading and discussion. Required Texts: ➢ Sparacino, Bianca. *The Strength in Our Scars*. Thought Catalog Books, 2018. ➢ Backman, Fredrik. *A Man Called Ove*. Atria Books, 2014. ➢ Coatsworth, Elizabeth. *The Cat Who Went to Heaven*. Simon & Schuster, 1930. ➢ Purdue OWL. “The Writing Process.” https://owl.purdue.edu/owl/general_writing/the_writing_process/index.html Fan-pei Gloria Yang Fall 1 Course outline Note: the weeks on the syllabus are idealized chunks of time. Not all have the same absolute duration. We will be somewhat flexible. Week 1: Course Introduction ➢ Topic: Overview of course goals, expectations, and the writing process. ➢ Readings: Purdue OWL: “Starting the Writing Process.” ➢ Activities: ○ Discuss syllabus, course objectives, and the importance of writing as a process. ○ In-class exercise: Write a brief introduction (200 words) about your writing experiences and goals. ➢ Assignment: Submit introductory reflection (200 words). Week 2: Prewriting and Invention ➢ Readings: Purdue OWL: “Introduction to Prewriting (Invention),” “Brainstorming,” “Developing an Outline.” ➢ Discussion: ○ Explore prewriting techniques (brainstorming, freewriting, clustering, questioning). ○ Discuss how prewriting shapes effective writing. ➢ Activities: ○ In-class: Practice brainstorming and clustering for a personal narrative topic. ○ Group activity: Share and refine prewriting ideas. ➢ Assignment: Create and submit a detailed outline for a personal narrative (300 words). Week 3: Drafting and Organization ➢ Readings: Purdue OWL: “Drafting,” “Developing Strong Thesis Statements,” “Organizing Your Writing.” ➢ Discussion: ○ Analyze strategies for drafting (overcoming writer’s block, structuring ideas). ○ Discuss the role of a thesis statement in guiding a draft. ➢ Activities: ○ In-class: Draft a 500-word personal narrative based on Week 2 outline. ○ Workshop: Peer feedback on draft organization and thesis clarity. ➢ Assignment**: Submit draft of personal narrative (500 words). Week 4: Revising, Editing, and Proofreading ➢ Readings: Purdue OWL: “Revising for Clarity and Organization,” “Editing and Proofreading,” “Proofreading for Common Errors.” ➢ Discussion: ○ Explore revision strategies for improving clarity, cohesion, and style. ○ Discuss editing and proofreading techniques to polish writing. ➢ Activities: ○ In-class: Revise personal narrative drafts using Purdue OWL strategies. ○ Practice proofreading exercises from Purdue OWL. ➢ Assignment: Submit revised personal narrative (750 words). Week 5: Introduction to *The Strength in Our Scars ➢ Readings: *The Strength in Our Scars* (selected poems/essays). ➢ Discussion: ○ Analyze Sparacino’s use of emotional appeals (pathos) and vivid imagery. ○ Explore how the fragmented structure enhances personal reflection. ➢ Activities: ○ Group discussion: How does Sparacino’s tone create intimacy with the reader? ○ In-class: Write a short response (300 words) to a selected poem/essay. ➢ Assignment: Submit response to *The Strength in Our Scars* (300 words). Week 6: Rhetorical Analysis of *The Strength in Our Scars* ➢ Readings: Continue *The Strength in Our Scars*. ➢ Discussion: ○ Examine rhetorical devices (repetition, metaphor, anaphora) in Sparacino’s work. ○ Discuss how her rhetoric addresses themes of healing and resilience. ➢ Activities: ○ In-class: Draft a rhetorical analysis of a selected passage (500 words). ○ Group activity: Identify examples of rhetorical appeals in the text. ➢ Assignment: Submit draft of rhetorical analysis essay (500 words). Week 7: Refining Rhetorical Analysis ➢ Readings: Revisit *The Strength in Our Scars*. ➢ Discussion: ○ Discuss strategies for strengthening rhetorical analysis (e.g., evidence selection, argument clarity). ○ Explore how Sparacino’s rhetoric connects to broader audiences. ➢ Activities: ○ Peer review of rhetorical analysis drafts. ○ In-class: Revise essays for stronger arguments and coherence. ➢ Assignment: Submit revised rhetorical analysis essay (800 words). Week 8: Introduction to *A Man Called Ove* ➢ Readings: *A Man Called Ove* (Chapters 1–10). ➢ Discussion: ○ Analyze Backman’s use of character-driven storytelling and humor. ○ Explore how flashbacks build Ove’s character and evoke empathy. ➢ Activities: ○ In-class: Create a character sketch inspired by Backman’s techniques (300 words). ○ Discuss how humor serves as a rhetorical tool. ➢ Assignment: Submit character sketch (300 words). Week 9: Narrative Techniques in *A Man Called Ove* ➢ Readings: *A Man Called Ove* (Chapters 11–20). ➢ Discussion: ○ Examine Backman’s use of dialogue and pacing to enhance narrative flow. ○ Discuss how ethos and logos balance humor and tragedy. ➢ Activities: ○ In-class: Draft a narrative scene (500 words) using Backman’s techniques. ○ Group discussion: Analyze a key scene for rhetorical effect. ➢ Assignment: Submit narrative scene (500 words). Week 10: Deepening Analysis of *A Man Called Ove* ➢ Readings: *A Man Called Ove* (Chapters 21–end). ➢ Discussion: ○ Analyze how Backman resolves Ove’s arc and its emotional impact. ○ Discuss how narrative closure reinforces rhetorical goals. ➢ Activities: ○ Peer review of narrative scenes, focusing on pacing and dialogue. ○ In-class: Revise narrative scenes for emotional impact. ➢ Assignment: Submit revised narrative scene (750 words). Week 11: Introduction to *The Cat Who Went to Heaven* ➢ Readings: *The Cat Who Went to Heaven* (full text). ➢ Discussion: ○ Analyze Coatsworth’s use of allegory and spiritual themes. ○ Discuss how simple prose enhances the story’s moral complexity. ➢ Activities: ○ In-class: Brainstorm a short story with a moral theme (outline). ○ Group discussion: How does Coatsworth use pathos to convey compassion? ➢ Assignment: Submit short story outline (300 words). Week 12: Rhetorical Techniques in *The Cat Who Went to Heaven* ➢ Readings: Revisit *The Cat Who Went to Heaven*. ➢ Discussion: ○ Examine Coatsworth’s use of rhetorical simplicity and cultural symbolism. ○ Discuss how the narrative appeals to universal values. ➢ Activities: ○ In-class: Draft a short story (500 words) based on Week 11 outline. ○ Group activity: Present examples of symbolism in the text. ➢ Assignment: Submit draft of short story (500 words). Week 13: Refining Creative Writing ➢ Readings: None (focus on writing). ➢ Discussion: ○ Discuss strategies for revising creative writing (e.g., clarity, tone, imagery). ○ Explore how Coatsworth’s style can inform student work. ➢ Activities**: ○ Peer review of short story drafts. ○ In-class: Revise stories for stronger thematic impact. ➢ Assignment**: Submit revised short story (750 words). Week 14: Comparative Analysis Preparation ➢ Readings: Review key passages from all three texts. ➢ Discussion: ○ Compare rhetorical strategies across the texts (e.g., pathos in Sparacino, humor in Backman, allegory in Coatsworth). ○ Discuss how to structure a comparative term paper. ➢ Activities**: ○ In-class: Develop a term paper outline comparing themes and rhetoric. ○ Group activity: Share and refine thesis statements. ➢ Assignment**: Submit term paper outline (500 words). Week 15: Term Paper Drafting ➢ Readings: None (focus on writing). ➢ Discussion: ○ Discuss strategies for synthesizing textual evidence and building arguments. ○ Review techniques for cohesive and persuasive writing. ➢ Activities: ○ In-class: Draft term paper introduction and first section (500 words). ○ Peer review of outlines and partial drafts. ➢ Assignment: Submit term paper draft (1000 words). Week 16: Term Paper Submission and Course Reflection ➢ Readings: None. ➢ Activities: ○ Peer review of term paper drafts, focusing on style and argumentation. ○ In-class: Reflect on growth in writing and rhetorical analysis skills. ➢ Assignment: Submit final term paper (1500–2000 words). ➢ Final Discussion: Reflect on lessons from the texts and the writing process.

docs.text: Chang 1 Reading and Writing I Fall 2025 Instructor: Yu-jung Chang Class Time: Tues 10-12 Classroom: TBA E-mail: yjchang@mx.nthu.edu.tw ___________________________________________________________________________________________________ COURSE DESCRIPTION This is the first part of a year-long course designed to improve your English reading and writing skills. You will develop your ability to critically engage with assigned texts, participate in class discussions, and produce clear, coherent expository writing. Through a series of assignments, you will learn to explain ideas logically, organize information effectively, and support your points with relevant evidence. This semester, you will: • Respond to a variety of reading sources, connecting ideas from texts to your own experiences and knowledge. • Write multi-paragraph expository essays using strategies such as exemplification, extended definition, and classification. • Provide constructive, supportive feedback on your classmates’ writing. • Revise your own work based on feedback from your teacher, peers, and digital tools. • Interact with AI chatbots to support your writing process. You will be expected to critically evaluate the feedback these tools provide, making thoughtful choices about what to incorporate or reject. TEXTBOOK Steps to writing well, by Jean Wyrick EVALUATION  Class attendance & participation:10  Essays 1-3 (drafts, peer-reviews, writing logs):75  Essay 4: 15 Chang 2 Course Schedule: Week Topics 1 9/2 Course Introduction 2 9/9 Essay 1 Essay basics 3 9/16 Essay basics 4 9/23 Essay Basics 5 9/30 Essay Basics 6 10/7 Essay basics 7 10/14 Peer review: Essay 1 8 10/21 Writing conference 1/Essay 2 9 10/28 Definition 10 11/4 Definition 11 11/11 Peer Review: Essay 2 12 11/28 Writing conference 2/Essay 3 13 11/25 Classification 14 12/2 Classification 15 12/9 Peer view: Essay 3 16 12/16 Writing Conference 3/Essay 4 This syllabus is a guide and every attempt is made to provide an accurate overview of the course. However, circumstances and events may make it necessary for the instructor to modify the syllabus during the semester and may depend, in part, on the progress, needs, and experiences of the students. Course information 課程代碼 Course Number 11410FL 201101 課程名稱 Title in Chinese 初級日語 (一) 課程英文名稱 Title in English Beginning Japanese (I) 全/半年 Two/one semester 全年 必/選修/通識 Required/ Elective/ General Education 必修 總學分數 Credits 3 每週上課時數/ 教室 Lecturing hours/ classroom 週一 M789 (15:30-18:20) / 人社院 C407 開課系所 Class standing 外語系 授課教師 Instructor(s) 簡嘉菁 kankasei88@gmail.com 先修課程 Prerequisites 歡迎零基礎者。上課時間較短，建議在開學初期多練習假名拼音與寫法。 適合自學能力較佳者 關鍵字 Keywords 日語 Japanese, 聽力 Listening, 會話 Conversation, 閱讀 Reading, 寫作 Writing 課程簡介 Course Description 1. 教學目標：培養日語零基礎的學生具備日語基礎溝通與表達能力。透過討論、 聽力練習與會話演練來培養溝通簡單的日語表達能力。提升至日語 JLPT N5 實力。 2. 指定教科書：上・下學期《大家的日本語 初級 I 改訂版》 3. 教學進度：上學期為日語基礎發音、假名習字與《大家的日本語初級 I 改訂 版》第 1-5 課。下學期為同一本課本的第 6-12 課。 4. 課程說明：本課程主要以日語零基礎學生為學習對象。 (1) 上學期是學習日語發音與日語平假名・片假名的書寫方式，並學習簡單 日語會話與名詞、動詞基礎句型等。以期運用在自我介紹、購物點餐、 介紹時間地點事物等簡單溝通能力（五十音教學進度較快，建議在課 外勤加練習）。下學期是著重在動詞、形容詞等詞尾變化與相關句型， 以期運用在表達個人情感、動作授受表現、數量唸法等，達到適時適 所的日語溝通能力並且了解日本文化。 (2) 利用書籍或網路視聽教材，輔以平時作業來培養寫作與閱讀能力。課程 中適時加入相關句型的日語會話、日語歌曲或新聞日文以期有效應用 本學期的學習內容。 5. 成績考核：期中考（40%）、期末考（30%）、作業（10%）、小考（10%）、 出席（10%） 備註：教學方法、評量方式、參考書目、教學網頁、AI 使用規則等請參考課 綱附檔。第一週將詳細說明。 注意事項 Please note 注意事項： (1) 除特殊狀況，不開放加簽或申請二退（需當面晤談。未經同意，不審核二退 的電子簽單）。申請旁聽者請事先來信聯絡。 (2) 部分專有名詞與內容將以中文介紹。 114-1 NTHU 初級日語 課程綱要 Ｍ789 簡嘉菁 2 (3) 詳細教學方法、評量方式、參考書目、教學網頁等將在第一週說明。 (4) 關於 AI 使用規則：有條件開放. 基於透明與負責任的原則，本課程可以利 用 AI 進行查詢，以提升本門課品質。但是本課程的個人報告或分組報告中, 不得使用生成 AI 工具撰寫報告. 若經查核使用卻未在作業或報告中標明， 教師、學校或相關單位有權重新針對作業或報告重新評分或不予計分。 (5) 出席: 重要考試或個人上台報告日，都必須出席。請假時請利用學校請假 系統的上網登記。除了緊急重大意外，請假時都必須在上課前完成請假。 如果是公假、喪假、病假、婚假、赴日（來回機票證明，一學期最多申請 2 次，1 次一週為上限）需附上相關證明單。不需要再給紙本請假單。詳 細規定請參考學校請假系統通知。缺課達五週以上（或 1/4）不給予學期 成績。 課程目標 Course Outcomes 此科目對應之系所課程規畫所欲培養之核心能力 Core capability to be cultivated by this course 1 培養基礎日語表達能力 溝通表達與語文能力、創作與創新能力 2 理解日本社會與文化 問題發掘與研究能力 3 透過與日本的比較, 提高對台灣的關心 全球化與國際視野及多元文化認知能力 二、教學大綱 II. ( ✓ ) 有（ 42 人） 教 室 人社 C512 選修資格限制 限外語系: ( ✓ )是 限外語系: ( ✓ )否 課程綱要 ❤ 課 程 說 明 學習目標： 認知 ● 習得字母與日文基礎句型。 ● 藉由日語學習同時玩味日本文化。 技能 ● 奠定基礎日語會話技巧。 ● 培養基礎日文讀寫能力。 情意 ● 以日語與他人溝通，獲得成就感、增添學習興趣。 ● 觀察日語表達的習慣與特色，體察日本文化。 核心能力： 溝通表達與語文能力：70% 問題發掘與研究能力：15% 全球視野與多元文化認知能力：15% 教 學 方 式 (1)平假名、片假名的書寫方式及發音學習階段中以板書、自製教學影片、 (1) 公布教材…等幫助學習者進行口頭練習及書寫練習，並適時 (1)以日常生活用語及日語歌曲、網路資源等幫助複習以增進學習效果。 (2)善用自編單字表等補充教材、 （e.g. 日本留學經歷及文化 (3)體驗相關相片、手縫小月曆、生活小物）等以 (不藉由媒介語) (3)導入，引導同學們以教科書、PPT 簡報、紙本講義…等循序學習重要 (3)概念，藉由淺顯易懂的文法說明幫助學習者理解後立即應用。 (3)各課採用「導入句型、文法說明、口頭練習、聽力練習」等方式進行， (2)「形、音、義」並重地培養學習者提升閱讀能力及口語表達能力。 (4)適時以日常生活用語、文化方面題材、自編補充教材、日語相關有益 (2)網站及搭配所學進度或因應時節之歌曲(教師譯註 PDF 檔)、（廣告或 (2)日劇）影片等幫助學習者藉由觀察日語表達的習慣與特色來體察日本 (2)文化、提升學習興趣，期能更加提升學習效果。 (5)以作業、分組練習等方式確認聽說讀寫能力。 (6)課前、課後善用 教材及測驗區等各項功能，幫助學習者藉由 (6)按部就班預習及複習的過程中熟習實用語彙及自然的日語表達方式。 2 指 定 用 書 ●教師自編講義 ●『大家的日本語 初級Ⅰ 改訂版』大新書局 參 考 資 料 (1)『みんなの日本語 初級Ⅰ 第２版 聴解タスク２５』 スリーエーネットワーク (2)日語歌曲、其他與課程相關之資料等。 教 學 進 度 單元主題（課程進度謹供參考，可能視班級實際學習情況調整） 第 1 週( 9/11) 課程簡述； docs.name: 初級日語一
docs.text: 授 課 大 綱 課程資訊 課程名稱：初級日語（一） Beginning Japanese I 任課教師：王瑋婷 (WANG,WEI-TING) 上課時間：T34n 學分數：3 此科目對應之系所課程規畫所欲培養之核心能力 ■ 溝通表達與語文能力 (70%) □ 文學經典的分析與詮釋 ■ 問題發掘與研究能力 (15%) □ 創作與創新能力 ■ 全球化與國際視野及多元文化認知能力 (15%) 課程簡述 本課程授課對象為尚無日文基礎之學生，課程自日文發音、五十音寫法開始教起，隨課本進度授課， 協助學生奠定良好的日語發音及文法概念基礎，建立簡單會話溝通能力。本學期預定進度為五十音 及指定教科書 1~5 課內容。 教學目標： 1. 學會聽、說、讀、寫日語基礎語彙及句型。 2. 能於生活中聽、說應用所學句型，具基礎日語溝通能力。 3. 理解日本文化，提升國際視野。 4. 提升學生生活品質及未來發展潛力。 課程大綱 課程說明 課程自日文發音、五十音寫法開始教起，隨課本進度授課，本學期預定進度為五十音 及指定教科書 1~5 課內容。下學期教學 6~12 課內容。 課程中將隨各課主題內容講解語彙，並逐項分析主題句型，透過口說及書寫練習強化 同學們對句型的掌握度，也將透過會話演練及課堂活動、聽力練習等，讓同學們進一 步活用句型內容。課程中亦將視情況帶入日本文化介紹、推薦線上學習資源等，以強 化同學的學習興趣，培養主動自發的學習精神。 指定用書 《大家的日本語 初級Ⅰ 改訂版》，大新書局 參考書籍 1.《大家的日本語 初級Ⅰ 文法解說書》，大新書局 2.《大家的日本語 初級Ⅰ 聴解タスク》，大新書局 3.《大家的日本語 初級 讀本篇》，大新書局 4. PPT 文法說明、其他課程補充講義等 教學方式 1. 五十音教學階段中，將以投影片、板書、講義等授課，請同學進行書寫及口頭練習， 並輔助實用單字教學、聽寫、流行歌曲辨音或其他小遊戲等，以加深學習印象。 2. 進入課本內容後，將以「單字講解、文法導入及說明、口頭及書寫練習、造句及問 答應用、會話活動、聽力練習」等方式授課，以讓同學充分掌握文法，培養聽說讀 寫能力。 3. 適時補充日本文化、時事等內容，以增進同學對異文化的理解，提升學習興趣。 教學進度 W1 9/2 課程介紹、 日語 50 音及發音方式：平假名 W2 9/9 日語 50 音及發音方式：平假名、片假名 W3 9/16 日語 50 音及發音方式： 片假名、促音、長音、重音、句調等發音規則 W4 9/23 打招呼用語、數字(1~10) L.1 (名詞句 1：自我介紹－職業、國籍、年齡的說明等) W5 9/30 L.1 W6 10/7 L.1 W7 10/14 L.2 (名詞句 2：物品的指示詞、表達物品相關資訊及擁有者等) W8 10/21 L.2、L.3 (名詞句 3：場所指示詞、說明出身地及所屬、物品產地、 場所位置、詢價等) W9 10/28 期中考、L.3〔*上課 90 分鐘，剩下時間考試〕 W10 11/4 L.3 W11 11/11 L.4 (動詞句 1：時間及星期說法、簡單說明日常行動) W12 11/18 L.4 W13 11/25 L.4 W14 12/2 L.5 (動詞句 2：表達所前往的目的地及其交通工具、共同動作者、 時間等；學習日期說法) W15 12/9 L.5 W16 12/16 期末考、L.5 〔*上課 90 分鐘，剩下時間考試〕 成績考核 小考及作業 30% *小考進行數次(原則上每課 1 次，測驗字彙及文法內容；課程內容較多時，有可能 視情況改為單字小考+作業；五十音教學期間，每週小考前一週教完的字母)， 期末將刪除其中成績最差的 1 次。 *小考週次如請公假/喪假/病假等，出示證明則可以免考不計分。 事假及無證明的病假、生理假可補考，必須於隔週第一節下課補考完成， 字母小考：限時 7 分鐘；每課文法+詞彙小考 15 分鐘。 遲到同學當天下課 10 分鐘內補考完，以-5 計算成績；曠課不可補考，以零分計算。 課堂參與 15% (含出缺席及課堂參與度) *無故曠課一次扣 2 分；課堂參與度欠佳者，視其參與程度減扣 0.5-1.5 分。 *為維護課堂參與成績公平性，各類請假評分規則如下： 1. 公假/喪假/具醫療證明的病假：不扣分 (病假可接受請假日 3 日內的藥袋或掛號資訊、快篩、體溫計畫面為證明) 2. 生理假：不扣分，每月最多以 1 次為限 3. 事假/無證明的病假：1-2 次不扣分；第 3 次扣 0.5 分；第 4-5 次扣 1 分； 第 6 次起不再接受請假，會登記為曠課扣 2 分。 4. 不接受事假/無證明病假連續請假 2 週以上。自第 2 週起將登記為曠課。 5. 上課遲到 15 分鐘以上，自第 3 次起將會扣分，每次減扣 1 分。 *如有特殊身心狀況，請另來信提供醫療證明並討論課堂參與事宜。 期中考 25% 期末考 30% 其他注意 事項 1. 請謹慎評估個人日語程度合適與否、以及作息/時間分配等因素，無法配合認真參 與課堂者，請勿選課。 2. 課程中常常進行小組(大部分是兩人一組)會話練習，不願參與練習者建議勿選課。 3. 生成 AI 使用原則：本課程無涉及 AI 使用

Course information 課程代碼 Course Number 11410FL 201115 課程名稱 Title in Chinese 初級日語 (一) 課程英文名稱 Title in English Beginning Japanese (I) 全/半年 Two/one semester 全年 必/選修/通識 Required/ Elective/ General Education 必修 總學分數 Credits 3 每週上課時數/ 教室 Lecturing hours/ classroom 週四 R567 (13:30-16:20) / 人社院 D201 (人限 30) 開課系所 Class standing 外語系 授課教師 Instructor(s) 簡嘉菁 kankasei88@gmail.com 先修課程 Prerequisites 歡迎零基礎者。上課時間較短，建議在開學初期多練習假名拼音與寫法。 適合自學能力較佳者 關鍵字 Keywords 日語 Japanese, 聽力 Listening, 會話 Conversation, 閱讀 Reading, 寫作 Writing 課程簡介 Course Description 1. 教學目標：培養日語零基礎的學生具備日語基礎溝通與表達能力。透過討論、 聽力練習與會話演練來培養溝通簡單的日語表達能力。提升至日語 JLPT N5 實力。 2. 指定教科書：上・下學期《大家的日本語 初級 I 改訂版》 3. 教學進度：上學期為日語基礎發音、假名習字與《大家的日本語初級 I 改訂 版》第 1-5 課。下學期為同一本課本的第 6-12 課。 4. 課程說明：本課程主要以日語零基礎學生為學習對象。 (1) 上學期是學習日語發音與日語平假名・片假名的書寫方式，並學習簡單 日語會話與名詞、動詞基礎句型等。以期運用在自我介紹、購物點餐、 介紹時間地點事物等簡單溝通能力（五十音教學進度較快，建議在課 外勤加練習）。下學期是著重在動詞、形容詞等詞尾變化與相關句型， 以期運用在表達個人情感、動作授受表現、數量唸法等，達到適時適 所的日語溝通能力並且了解日本文化。 (2) 利用書籍或網路視聽教材，輔以平時作業來培養寫作與閱讀能力。課程 中適時加入相關句型的日語會話、日語歌曲或新聞日文以期有效應用 本學期的學習內容。 5. 成績考核：期中考（40%）、期末考（30%）、作業（10%）、小考（10%）、 出席（10%） 備註：教學方法、評量方式、參考書目、教學網頁、AI 使用規則等請參考課 綱附檔。第一週將詳細說明。 注意事項 Please note 注意事項： (1) 除特殊狀況，不開放加簽或申請二退（需當面晤談。未經同意，不審核二退 的電子簽單）。申請旁聽者請事先來信聯絡。 (2) 部分專有名詞與內容將以中文介紹。 114-1 NTHU 初級日語 課程綱要 Ｍ789 簡嘉菁 2 (3) 詳細教學方法、評量方式、參考書目、教學網頁等將在第一週說明。 (4) 關於 AI 使用規則：有條件開放. 基於透明與負責任的原則，本課程可以利 用 AI 進行查詢，以提升本門課品質。但是本課程的個人報告或分組報告中, 不得使用生成 AI 工具撰寫報告. 若經查核使用卻未在作業或報告中標明， 教師、學校或相關單位有權重新針對作業或報告重新評分或不予計分。 (5) 出席: 重要考試或個人上台報告日，都必須出席。請假時請利用學校請假 系統的上網登記。除了緊急重大意外，請假時都必須在上課前完成請假。 如果是公假、喪假、病假、婚假、赴日（來回機票證明，一學期最多申請 2 次，1 次一週為上限）需附上相關證明單。不需要再給紙本請假單。詳 細規定請參考學校請假系統通知。缺課達五週以上（或 1/4）不給予學期 成績。 課程目標 Course Outcomes 此科目對應之系所課程規畫所欲培養之核心能力 Core capability to be cultivated by this course 1 培養基礎日語表達能力 溝通表達與語文能力、創作與創新能力 2 理解日本社會與文化 問題發掘與研究能力 3 透過與日本的比較, 提高對台灣的關心 全球化與國際視野及多元文化認知能力 二、教學大綱 II. 作業(10%): 相關句型之日語歌曲或新聞內容以及日本文化探悉(請需附上日語假名拼音與相 關翻譯(英文或中文)). 小考(10%): 本學期所補充單字與教科書詞彙等 出席(10%): 請假需附上相關證明單與填寫假單 三、教學方法、評量方式、指定書目與參考書目等 教學方法 lecturing methodologies 方式 methods 說明 notes o 講述法 formal lecture 由教師引導發音･單字･句型練習。 授課內容以教科書為主,講義與線上網路報導為輔。 o 討論法 group discussion 由學生分組討論,共同解決發表的課題 o 合作學習 cooperative learning 分組口頭會話發表 o 媒體融入教學 media, audio, visual materials 使用電腦或多媒體播放相關日文,練習日語聽力與閱讀 o 專題研究 case studies 日語報告或詞彙整理等 評量方法 assessment methodologies:有 “等級制” 和 “百分制” 備註 notes: (1) 請掌握學習狀況,勿在考後要求補寫報告、調整成績等。 (2) 公佈成績:小考約 2 週後、期中考約 4 週後、學期成績約 2-3 週後。 (3) 可能會申請二退或應屆畢業生請留意成績出爐時間,再決定是否選課。 方式 methods 百 分 比 詢重點句型，用螢光筆標示，加上簡易文法分析)。日語漢 字與阿拉伯數字都必須加上日語假名拼音、另附上中文或 英文翻譯。 (2) 日本文化探析:手寫或打字皆可。有主題、3-5 則日語關鍵字、 內文、參考資料、網路來源等。約 500 字以上。注意：關於 AI 使用規則：有條件開放. 基於透明與負責任的原則， 本課程可以利用 AI 進行查詢，以提升本門課品質。但是 docs.name: 當代文學
docs.text: 1 Course Title: Contemporary Literature Instructor: Shuyu Lee Course TA: Gwen Huang (blueclark0117@gmail.com) Credit Hours: 3 Classroom Language: English Course Description: Twenty-eight years after “The End of Postmodernism” cultural-studies seminar in Stuttgart, and eighteen years after 9/11 ended the “end of history,” we look at what, if anything, has taken the place of postmodernism as the prevailing aesthetic and cultural agenda for American fiction. In our exploration of novels, short stories, and films released in the last thirty years, we will focus on issues around technology, counterculture, celebrity culture, social media, globalization, post-truth, and economic inequality. The goal of the course is to familiarize students with contemporary sociocultural issues and to help them develop literary interpretive skills informed by the relationship between text and context. This course is conducted mainly through lectures, with a strong emphasis on active student participation. Required Texts: Zadie Smith “Kelso Deconstructed,” from Grand Union (2019) John Patrick Shanley Doubt: A Parable (2004) https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yPLEyLGdcmE&ab_channel=Videoinvision Jennifer Egon A Visit from the Goon Squad (2010) (ISBN: 9780307477477) Steven Millhauser “Miracle Polish,” from Voices in the Night (2015) George Saunders “Sea Oak,” from Pastoralia (2000) “Escape from Spiderhead,” from Tenth of December (2013) Charlie Brooker (Story) & Joe Wright (Directing) Nosedive (episode of Black Mirror) (2016) 2 Assessment Attendance 10% Active Participation (raising and answering questions, volunteering to read texts, and other behaviors that prove mental presence in class) 20% Active Participation (Forum Discussion) 15% Mid-Term Exam 25% Final Exam 30% Class Policies: 1. Attendance 1-A: Regular attendance is expected. Absences can be excused for medical conditions, family emergencies, and natural disasters, provided there is evidentiary documentation, such as medical certificates. 1-B: Attention may be taken anytime during the class meeting. Students found absent at roll call will be marked absent for the day. 1-C: Three unexcused absences will incur a half letter grade reduction in semester grade. That means your semester grade will go, for example, from an original A to A-. Four unexcused absences will lead to a full letter grade reduction for the entire semester, which means your semester grade will turn, for example, from an original B into C. 2. docs.text: 1 PRAGMATICS Fall 2025 Instructor: Chen-Yu Chester Hsieh Email: hsieh.cy@mx.nthu.edu.tw Class time: Thursday, 10:10~13:00 Office: HSS-B505 Office hours: By appointment Course Description When do you use “that” instead of “this”? Why do we know “can you pass the salt” is not really a question and “I pronounce you man and wife” not just a statement? Does adding “please” to your utterance always make it sound more polite? Why shouldn’t you express agreement when your boy/girlfriend says they look fat? Why do we sometimes have problems communicating with people from a different culture even when we’re speaking the same language? We will try to address those questions and many others in this course. This course, primarily conducted in English, introduces the basic theories and approaches in the field of pragmatics and explores pragmatic phenomena in various forms of language and realms of life. We will learn about important theoretical constructs of pragmatics, such as implicature, speech acts and politeness, and find out how these concepts are realized in different linguistic and cultural contexts. We will also discuss how pragmatics research can be conducted and how one’s pragmatic competence is developed. By the end of this course, students are expected to be able to (1) define and describe important concepts in pragmatics; (2) explore and explain pragmatic phenomena based on the theoretical frameworks discussed; (3) analyze and account for data using the research methods taught in class; and (4) conduct a pragmatics research project and present the findings in an appropriate style. Grading 1. Attendance and Participation 20% 2. Quizzes 20% 3. AI Assignments 20% 4. Term Project 20% (Midterm and Final Presentations) 5. Final Exam 15% 6. Self-evaluation 5% Textbooks and Readings 1. Birner, B. J. (2013). Introduction to Pragmatics. Malden, MA: Wiley-Blackwell. 2. Cummins, C. (2019). Pragmatics. Edinburgh: Edinburgh University Press. 3. LoCastro, V. (2013). Pragmatics for Language Educators: A Sociolinguistic Perspective. 2 London: Routledge. 4. O’Keeffe, A., Clancy, B., & Adolphs, S. (2020). Introducing Pragmatics in Use. (2nd Edition). New York, NY: Routledge. 5. Ren, W. (2022). Second Language Pragmatics. Cambridge: Cambridge University Press. 6. Strauss, S. & Feiz, P. (2013). Discourse Analysis: Putting Our World into Words. New York, NY: Routledge. 7. Only your 3 highest quiz scores will be counted toward your final grade. 4. Late submissions of assignments will be accepted up to two weeks after the deadline. A deduction of 10 points per week will be applied. 3 Academic Integrity 1. Cheating and plagiarism are strictly prohibited. Any student caught engaging in such behavior will face serious academic consequences. 2. If you use words, data, or ideas from other sources, you must clearly indicate where the materials come from and whether they are quoted verbatim. 3. If you're unsure whether something constitutes plagiarism, ask the instructor for guidance. 4. While academic performance matters, integrity and genuine learning are more important. If you encounter difficulties with quizzes or assignments, don't hesitate to talk to the instructor. Use of Generative AI 1. The reasonable and responsible use of Generative AI tools (e.g., ChatGPT) is permitted and even encouraged in this course. 2. docs.name: 文學翻譯一
docs.text: 113 學年度上學期 上課時間：W 56 課程名稱：文學翻譯（一） Literary Translation I 課號：11310FL 213900 教室：人社 412 授課教師：李康莉（strawnana64@gmail.com） 教師時段：每週三 課後 3:20-4:00 老師會在外語系教師休息室。歡迎同學來訪。 助教：尚無 課程資料：每週上課內容及閱讀材料將公告在數位學習平台 Elearn 系統，繳交 作業也都會使用 Elearn 系統。因此請同學記得開啟追蹤訂閱呦！^_^ （https://elearn.nthu.edu.tw） 課程名稱：文學翻譯（一） • 課程說明 本文學翻譯課程，為初階課程。以翻譯實作為主，講述理論與技巧為輔 。目的 在於讓同學體驗文學翻譯的過程、挑戰與樂趣，希望能建立對文學翻譯初步的 信心與成就感。 依「難度」與「文類」分級，區分為上下學期課程—— 文學翻譯Ｉ — 文學翻譯基礎理論與技巧、小說（一）、散文（一）、劇本 文學翻譯ＩＩ— 文學翻譯進階理論與技巧、小說（二）、散文（二）、詩歌 本課程為文學翻譯實作課程。以「英譯中」為主，「中譯英」為輔。從文本翻 譯的「實作」練習中，培養同學對中英兩種語言的語感，對文本深入閱讀理解 的能力，以及中文遣詞用字的創意，提升對於中英兩種語感差異的辨析與轉換 能力。並透過各種文本的翻譯實作、包括嘗試與 AI 共作、分組討論實作等，掌 握基礎到進階不等的文學翻譯技巧，期能翻譯出深入原文旨趣，通順流暢，具 有文學性與可讀性的翻譯作品。在忠於原文的基礎上，鼓勵同學多多發揮靈 感，個人文字風格，與感性創意。 初階課程：希望修習完本課程的同學，都能從實作中切實感受、體驗文學翻譯 的挑戰或樂趣，建立初步的信心與成就感。初階課程主要著重於翻譯技巧，原 文句法轉換拆解，思索詞彙在上下文脈絡中的細微語意，並開放討論最佳譯 法。同學須按部就班進行教師指定之作業與練習。並每週事先閱讀素材。參與 平時作業。 進階課程：除了是上述翻譯文本程度的「進階版」，希望也能講述較多翻譯策 略、理解不同時期的特殊用語與語體風格。討論時則能更多深入其「境」，思 考文本、語言、文化、社會脈絡等面向。並體驗鑑賞不同的譯本與其翻譯策 略。 二、課程目標 • 對「文學翻譯」產生初步的興趣、信心與成就感。 • 認識小說、散文文類的特質，掌握初階翻譯策略與技巧。 • 累積創意寫作導向的中英文詞彙。 • 能正確且深入地理解原文作品，辨析細微的詞彙語意差意，或能解讀言外之 意。 • 透過網路資源或工具，查詢詞意，段落文意，典故或術語等。 • 能分析並留意到原文的修辭技巧。 • 使用基礎至進階不等的翻譯技巧，將原文轉換為通順流暢的譯文。 • 掌握個人的語感，發揮文字創意風格。 • 能靈活轉換，尋找合於文意，精準貼切的中英文遣詞用字。 • 能掌握基礎翻譯錯誤與病句類型，培養自我校正能力。 • 能清晰說明自己的翻譯理念、翻譯方法。 • 能欣賞不同譯本的利弊得失，並忠肯客觀地提出個人的翻譯見解。 三、指定用書： 1. 上課指定教材 2. 教師提供的補充資料 四、參考書目 1. Bassnett, Susan, Translation Studies, Methuen & Co. Ltd, 1980. 《翻譯研究：理 論、簡史、實務》林為正譯。五南。 2. Bassnett, Susan, “From Comparative Literature to Translation Studies”, Comparative Literature: A Critical Introduction, Blackwell, 1993. 3. Catford, J. C., A Linguistic Theory of Translation, OUP, 1965. 4. Venuti, Lawrence, Rethinking translation: discourse, subjectivity, ideology, 1992 5. Venuti, Lawrence, Translation changes everything: theory and practice, 2007 6 Venuti, Lawrence, The Translation Studies Reader, Routledge, 2000 7. Rose, Marilyn Gaddis, 《翻譯與文學批評：翻譯作為分析手段》（2007）。 8.《探索翻譯理論》（第二版），Anthony Pym 著，賴慈芸譯。台北：書林， 2016。 9.《英中筆譯 1》《英中筆譯 2》，廖伯森等著。台北：眾文圖書。 10.《英譯中基礎練習》，廖伯森 審訂。台北：眾文圖書。 11.《翻譯進修講堂》，廖伯森 等著。台北：眾文圖書。 五、教學方式： • 本課程鼓勵課堂發言與課堂討論，不預設標準答案。希望同學多能將自己的 想法，細緻的閱讀或思考，對文本或詞彙的理解，帶入課堂發言。也鼓勵課 堂討論互相提問。一起思考文本脈絡情境，決定較適切譯法。 • 以「文學作品細讀」、「開放課堂討論」「翻譯實作練習」、「分組討 論」、「譯文互相觀摩」、「中譯本比較討論」「講師講評回饋」等方式引 導同學掌握「文學翻譯」的初階至進階技巧。 • 本課程以中文授課。 附註—— • 講述部分：教師會「適時」淺述作品的時代背景與用語，補充不同流派的文 學翻譯理論與策略。藉由閱讀經典文學著名段落，欣賞對照不同譯文，從中 培養、感受不同的翻譯途徑，思索翻譯本質與優良譯作的條件。由師生共同 思考譯作的利弊得失。 • 同學翻譯習作：根據文類、作品精神、時代用語、作者文字風格、上下文 意、語境的推敲，思考較佳翻譯的可能性。 六、 評分方式 整學期至少 3 次 『平時作業』。。 同學必須參與 2 次翻譯發表。 1 次病句（AI）修改校訂練習，或中譯本比 較分析評論練習。並視教師意見回饋，繳交後續作業修訂。 另外本學期如有安排業師演講，可繳交「學期翻譯體驗心得」或「業師講 座心得」報告一篇（1500 字）為『加分選項』。 同學期末報告之「自選翻譯作品」，文體以小說、散文、劇本為主（字數 共 3000 字）。 整學期文字量約 7000-8000 字左右。 評分項目—— • 出席（10％）：出席率。 • 事前閱讀、課堂發言、分組討論（10%）：時有課堂習作、課堂分組討論。 • 平時作業：作品發表（30％）：本學期共有 2 次文本翻譯練習。1 次病句校 訂練習，或中譯本分析評比校訂。（或 3 次文本翻譯練習。）並參酌教師意 見進行後續修訂。每次作業（含後續修訂）不超過 1000 字。 • 期中考（20 %）：Take-home or online exam 選擇題/是非題/申論題共 33 題。 • 翻譯探索心得、或業師心得報告一篇（10 %）繳交 1500 字心得報告。為加 分選項。 • 期末作業發表（30 ％）期末作業，除了提供文字檔案，須進行口頭報告說 明：報告內容涵蓋個人翻譯作品、翻譯概念、翻譯策略與方法說明。期末報 告 3000 字。 • Class Attendance 10% • Weekly Reading Responses & Group Discussion & In-Class Activities 10% • Assignments (2+1) or (2+2) 30% - docs.name: 語言與R統計
docs.text: 課程名稱 (中文) 語言與 R 統計 (英文) Language and Statistics in R Fall 2025 Time: Fri 9:00 – 12:00 Location: TBA Instructor: 陳宗穎 chen.ty@mx.nthu.edu.tw Office: HSS-B506 Office Hours: TBA Teaching Assistant: TBA Last Updated May 20, 2025 課程大綱內容 一、課程概述 Life is full of quantifiable questions that can be answered by statistics, and so is language. For example, if vowels before a voiceless consonant is shorter than those before a voiced consonant by 20 milliseconds on average, is this just a coincidence that happens by chance, or is it really because a different articulatory mechanism that does the trick? Or, when bilingual children learn 10 fewer words in their dominant language compared to monolingual children of the same age, is there really some significant delay in word learning driven by multilingual language input? When English speakers respond to spring faster by 50 milliseconds after hearing bring than after hearing duck, can we say spring and bring are linked in their lexicon? In this course, students learn fundamental concepts in statistics and its extension in the field of language science and practice doing statistical analyses using R programming. This course requires neither experience in computer programming nor mastery of mathematics, but students should have completed introductory linguistic courses. 二、課程目標 Students in this course will begin by learning the basic concepts in statistics, such as population, sampling, distribution, variation, and probability. As the course proceeds, they will be familiarized with frequently used parametric and non-parametric statistical analyses (e.g., binomial test, t-test, z-test, chi-square tests, and regression) and their application in the field of language science. Crucially, students will have to learn to explore, visualize, and analyze language data using R programming, which is free and open-source and facilitates analysis replication. After completing this course, students are expected to be capable of not only doing quantified linguistic research but also applying their statistical knowledge to study other subjects in social sciences as well. 三、課程進度表 日期 主題 閱讀範圍 9/5 Course Overview & R Basics Unit 1 Handout 9/12 Fundamental Statistical Concepts Unit 2 Handout 9/19 9/26 Data Exploration and Visualization Unit 3 Handout 10/3 10/10 The National Day (No Class) 10/18 Parametric Statistical Analysis Unit 4 Handout10/25 11/1 11/8 Midterm Exam 11/15 Analysis of Variance (ANOVA) Unit 5 Handout 11/22 11/29 Regression Modeling Unit 7 Handout12/6 12/13 12/20 Final Exam 四、指定閱讀： Course Handouts 五、參考書籍 Baayan, Harald. (2007) Analyzing Linguistic Data: A practical introduction to statistics using R. Cambridge, UK: Cambridge University Press. Chang, Winston. (2018) R Graphics Cookbook: Practical Recipes for Visualizing Data. Sebastopol, CA: O’Reilly Media Inc. Healy, Kieran. (2016) Data Visualization: A practical introduction. New Jersey: Princeton University Press. Levshina, Natalia. (2015) How to do linguistics in R: Data exploration and statistical analysis. Amsterdam: John Benjamins. Wickham, Hadley & Grolemund, Garret (2017) R for Data Science. Sebastopol, CA: O’Reilly Media Inc. Winter, Bodo. (2019) Statistics for Linguists: An introduction using R. New York: Routledge. 六、評量方式 Assignments (40%) Throughout the course, the students will have to complete several take-home assignments that help them practice what they have learned in previous lectures and prepare for the exams. Midterm Exam (30%) In the midterm exam, students will be given two to three linguistic data sets to complete assigned tasks of data visualization and analysis using R within three hours. The midterm exam is an open-book exam and students can also google for helpful information, but cheating in any format (including using any generative AI) will not be allowed and will cost students all the midterm credit. The date of the exam, as specified in the above course schedule, will not be subject to changes unless extremely necessary; students are solely responsible for missing the exam. Since the midterm exam assesses students’ learning of fundamental aspects, which is the key to the successful learning of advanced aspects in this course, students must score at least 50 points in the midterm exam. Students automatically fail this course if they (i) fail to score at least 30 points on the midterm exam or (ii) fail to score at least 50 points on the exam with an average assignment score below 80 before the exam. Final Exam (30%) The final exam is similar to the midterm exam in terms of style and policy, but the final exam is accumulative, so it also covers the lecture contents in the first half of this course. AI Policies Students in this course can freely consult any generative AI (e.g., ChatGPT) when trying to complete their assignments in R but not when doing their exams. When AI helps complete their assignments, students must explicitly explain their use of AI in the assignments. However, students must be aware of the limits of generative AI and are suggested to use the output of generative AI as ‘secondary opinions.’ It is still extremely important for students to understand why and how R codes (do not) work in order to pass the exams and this course. Students are still fully responsible for missing any assignment requirements even if generative AI is used to complete any task.

docs.text: 1/3 【初級韓語一】課程教學大綱 課程資訊 (Course Information) 科號 Course Number 學分 Credit 3 人數限制 Class Size 中文名稱 Course Title 初級韓語一 英文名稱 Course English Title Elementary Korean I 任課教師 Instructor 李伶美 (Lee Yeongmi) 上課時間 Time M789 上課教室 Room 先修課程 Prerequisites 無 此科目對應之 系所課程規畫 所欲培養之核 心能力 Core capability to be cultivated by this course ■ 溝通表達與語文能力 (70%) The ability to communicate and express oneself in the English/a foreign language. (70%) □ 文學經典的分析與詮釋 The ability to analyze classic canons of literature. ■ 問題發掘與研究能力 (10%) The ability to look for problems and conduct research (including conducting linguistic analysis through scientific methods) (10%) □ 創作與創新能力 The ability to think creatively ■ 全球化與國際視野及多元文化認知能力 (20%) The ability to examine issues through global and multicultural perspectives (20%) 課程簡述 (Brief course description) 本課程由韓文字母開始，指導學生熟悉韓語發音及單字、句子之基本構造等，同時由淺入深地介 紹文法關係，以及透過基本句型的學習，期望學生能具有基本之讀、寫及翻譯的能力。同時亦將 配以口語練習的互動方式，讓學生熟悉一般日常生活及各種場合之對話用語。 課程大綱 (Syllabus) 一、課程目標 (Course Outcomes) 1. 能夠讓學生熟悉正確的韓語發音以及書寫方式，建立韓語學習的基礎。 2. 培養自我介紹、購物等基本的日常會話能力。 3. 理解並表現介紹自己、家人、日常活動等日常生活中的基礎內容。 4. 藉由熟悉基本語彙、表現、發音等，以便在日常生活中能夠提問及回答。 5. 理解並且熟悉以個人主題所構成的對話。 6. 瞭解韓語及其基礎構造，並能以文章表現自己的想法 ; 讀完簡單的文章內容後，能夠充 2/3 分理解。 二、教材 1. 指定書目 (Text Books)：《延世大學 韓國語1 (課本及 Workbook)》台北：聯經出版公司。 2. 參考書目 (References)：《我的第一本韓語文法》新北市：國際學村。 3. 韓文學習網站 (web page) (1) https://dict.naver.com/ (Naver 詞典) (2) https://dic.daum.net/index.do (Daum 詞典) 三、教學方式 (Teaching Method) 1. 由教師引導發音、單字練習。 2. 講解韓文之基礎知識及句型。 3. 練習實用日常會話。 4. 不定時小考及作業、上課參與。 四、成績考核 (Evaluation) 1. 期中考試：35% 2. 期末考試：35% 3. 平時成績(包含小考及作業，上課參與情形，出席率及上課態度等)：30% 小考不開放補考（公假不在此限，但須於次週補考完成），上課參與不開放補參與!! 五、上課規範 (classroom rules) 1. 第一堂課不建議缺席！ 2. 準時到課，不建議提早離開，早退必須跟老師說一聲。 3. 不克出席上課須事先請假。 1. 缺課者必須主動向到課同學詢問當天的上課內容與作業，並且自行跟上進度。 2. 務必有教材以及抄寫筆記。 3. 參與課程所進行的活動。 4. 準時繳交作業(如需補交，請於一星期之內完成)。 5. 課程未達 2/3 出席者，會「被當」。 6. 爲了上課品質，不開放旁聽生。 7. 限非韓籍生修習。 3/3 六、教學進度 (Syllabus) ※每週課程進度可能視實際上課情況調整 週次 日期 教學內容 第 1 週 2025/9/1 課程介紹 第一堂課非常重要，不建議缺席！ 課程進度：「基本母音和子音」 韓文字母介紹，了解韓語的基本母音和子音的發音，如何組成音 節?如何書寫韓文? 第 2 週 2025/9/8 課程進度：「其他子音和收尾音」 韓語收尾音的發音、練習和寫法，並學習基本詞彙來練習發音。 第 3 週 2025/9/15 課程進度：「其他收尾音」 韓語收尾音的發音、練習和寫法，並學習基本詞彙來練習發音。 第 4 週 2025/9/22 課程進度：「其他母音」 韓語其他母音的發音、練習和寫法，並學習基本詞彙來練習發音。 第 5 週 2025/9/29 課本進度：1-1 你好 1-2 你是哪國人? 第 6 週 2025/10/6 中秋節 課本進度：1-3 我不是公司職員 1-4 認識你很高興 第 7 週 2025/10/13 課本進度：1-5 閱讀：自我介紹 文化 (韓國人的名字∕韓國人的問候禮節) 第 8 週 2025/10/20 期中考試 第 9 週 2025/10/27 課本進度：2-1 這是課本嗎？ 2-2 也有地圖嗎？ 第 10 週 2025/11/3 課本進度：2-3 銀行在哪裡？ 2-4 你家在哪裡？ 第 11 週 2025/11/10 課本進度：2-5 閱讀：我的房間 寄宿家庭 文化 (周末值得去的地方∕韓國的地理位置) 第 12 週 2025/11/17 課本進度：3-1 我在看家人的照片 第 13 週 2025/11/24 課本進度：3-2 你的父母在哪裡？ 第 14 週 2025/12/1 課本進度：3-3 空氣新鮮，也很安靜。 3-4 他在大學念經濟學 第 15 週 2025/12/8 課本進度：3-5 閱讀：職業 故鄉 文化 (稱呼∕嬸嬸和叔叔) 第 16 週 2025/12/15 期末考試

docs.text: 1/3 【初級韓語一】課程教學大綱 課程資訊 (Course Information) 科號 Course Number 學分 Credit 3 人數限制 Class Size 中文名稱 Course Title 初級韓語一 英文名稱 Course English Title Elementary Korean I 任課教師 Instructor 李伶美 (Lee Yeongmi) 上課時間 Time F34n 上課教室 Room 先修課程 Prerequisites 無 此科目對應之 系所課程規畫 所欲培養之核 心能力 Core capability to be cultivated by this course ■ 溝通表達與語文能力 (70%) The ability to communicate and express oneself in the English/a foreign language. (70%) □ 文學經典的分析與詮釋 The ability to analyze classic canons of literature. ■ 問題發掘與研究能力 (10%) The ability to look for problems and conduct research (including conducting linguistic analysis through scientific methods) (10%) □ 創作與創新能力 The ability to think creatively ■ 全球化與國際視野及多元文化認知能力 (20%) The ability to examine issues through global and multicultural perspectives (20%) 課程簡述 (Brief course description) 本課程由韓文字母開始，指導學生熟悉韓語發音及單字、句子之基本構造等，同時由淺入深地介 紹文法關係，以及透過基本句型的學習，期望學生能具有基本之讀、寫及翻譯的能力。同時亦將 配以口語練習的互動方式，讓學生熟悉一般日常生活及各種場合之對話用語。 課程大綱 (Syllabus) 一、課程目標 (Course Outcomes) 1. 能夠讓學生熟悉正確的韓語發音以及書寫方式，建立韓語學習的基礎。 2. 培養自我介紹、購物等基本的日常會話能力。 3. 理解並表現介紹自己、家人、日常活動等日常生活中的基礎內容。 4. 藉由熟悉基本語彙、表現、發音等，以便在日常生活中能夠提問及回答。 5. 理解並且熟悉以個人主題所構成的對話。 6. 瞭解韓語及其基礎構造，並能以文章表現自己的想法 ; 讀完簡單的文章內容後，能夠充 2/3 分理解。 二、教材 1. 指定書目 (Text Books)：《延世大學 韓國語1 (課本及 Workbook)》台北：聯經出版公司。 2. 參考書目 (References)：《我的第一本韓語文法》新北市：國際學村。 3. 韓文學習網站 (web page) (1) https://dict.naver.com/ (Naver 詞典) (2) https://dic.daum.net/index.do (Daum 詞典) 三、教學方式 (Teaching Method) 1. 由教師引導發音、單字練習。 2. 講解韓文之基礎知識及句型。 3. 練習實用日常會話。 4. 不定時小考及作業、上課參與。 四、成績考核 (Evaluation) 1. 期中考試：35% 2. 期末考試：35% 3. 平時成績(包含小考及作業，上課參與情形，出席率及上課態度等)：30% 小考不開放補考（公假不在此限，但須於次週補考完成），上課參與不開放補參與!! 五、上課規範 (classroom rules) 1. 第一堂課不建議缺席！ 2. 準時到課，不建議提早離開，早退必須跟老師說一聲。 3. 不克出席上課須事先請假。 1. 缺課者必須主動向到課同學詢問當天的上課內容與作業，並且自行跟上進度。 2. 務必有教材以及抄寫筆記。 3. 參與課程所進行的活動。 4. 準時繳交作業(如需補交，請於一星期之內完成)。 5. 課程未達 2/3 出席者，會「被當」。 6. 爲了上課品質，不開放旁聽生。 7. 限非韓籍生修習。 3/3 六、教學進度 (Syllabus) ※每週課程進度可能視實際上課情況調整 週次 日期 教學內容 第 1 週 2025/9/5 課程介紹 第一堂課非常重要，不建議缺席！ 課程進度：「基本母音和子音」 韓文字母介紹，了解韓語的基本母音和子音的發音，如何組成音 節?如何書寫韓文? 第 2 週 2025/9/12 課程進度：「其他子音和收尾音」 韓語收尾音的發音、練習和寫法，並學習基本詞彙來練習發音。 第 3 週 2025/9/19 課程進度：「其他收尾音」 韓語收尾音的發音、練習和寫法，並學習基本詞彙來練習發音。 第 4 週 2025/9/26 課程進度：「其他母音」 韓語其他母音的發音、練習和寫法，並學習基本詞彙來練習發音。 第 5 週 2025/10/3 課本進度：1-1 你好 1-2 你是哪國人? docs.text: Department of Foreign Languages and Literature Reading & Writing II(1) National Tsing Hua University Huang 1 Course description This course is designed to improve students’ writing ability through process writing and the learning of effective writing strategies. Emphasis will be placed on pre-writing activities, self-reflection, reader/audience expectations, topic development, text analysis, organization, argumentation, critical thinking, research, peer review, and revision. Students in this course will explore differences between personal and academic writing, develop written fluency, and improve command over textual, rhetorical, and discursive conventions common in academic writing. Course materials Required:  Spack, R. (2007). Guidelines: A cross-cultural reading/writing text. New York: Cambridge University Press.  An e-mail account. It is essential that you check this e-mail account regularly. Reminders, notes, and extra materials will be sent regularly through email.  A working account at the iLMS website. You will need to upload assignments to this e-learning platform (http://lms.nthu.edu.tw).  A binder/folder for your writing portfolio. All writing you do for this class, during and outside class time, must be saved and kept organized. Requirements and Major Course Projects Class Participation Participation by each student in all aspects of the class is a primary requirement for receiving a passing grade. Evaluation is based on: １. Participation in peer responses, classroom discussions, and collaborative writing ２. Your diligence and the amount of effort you put into this course, into learning about the topics raised, and into your assignments ３. The degree to which you work toward making this course your own. Writing Assignments You will write two main papers in addition to other classroom and/or homework assignments. Each paper will have three drafts (first, second, and final). Paper 1: Position/stance on an issue of interest (5-6 pages for each draft) Paper 2: Response to written argument (6-7 pages for each draft) 閱讀與寫作二(上) Reading & Writing II (1) Instructor: Hung-Tzu Huang Time:T3T4 (Tuesday 10:10-12:00) Location: 人社 C521 Contact information: hthuang@mx.nthu.edu.tw Office: 人社 B507, Phone: 574-2710 Office hours: by appointment Department of Foreign Languages and Literature Reading & Writing II(1) National Tsing Hua University Huang 2 Freewriting The first 15 minutes of each class period will be devoted to freewriting. It is important that you come to class on time and prepare to write. Freewrites will be based on a variety of topics which will be introduced primarily by the students. Homework You will have mostly reading and writing assignments. Occasionally, you will be required to do library, Internet, and/or field research. Conferences Throughout the semester, you will meet individually with me—either during my office hours or during class time—and possibly with other members of the class to share your work and to reflect on your writing process. Writing Portfolio During the semester, you will compile all your freewrites, homework assignments, drafts, peer review forms, revisions, and final drafts into your writing portfolio. This is why it is important to keep all your work from this class organized. Your writing portfolio will be turned in at the end of the semester along with a synthesis essay that describes your writing experience over the course of the semester. Policy for plagiarism and late assignments: *** Plagiarism is a type of academic dishonesty which may result in failing of the class or suspension from the university. Plagiarism includes but is not limited to submitting any work that has been copied in whole or in part from another individual’s work without citation and submitting the same written or oral material in more than one course without obtaining authorization from the instructors involved. Always cite the sources you use in all assignments. If you have any questions regarding plagiarism, please consult the instructor. *** Late assignments will not be accepted. If you are absent on the day of presentations, you will lose all points. Grading Paper 1: 40% (First draft: 10%; Second draft: 10 %; Final draft: 20%) Paper 2: 40% (First draft: 10%; Second draft: 10 %; Final draft: 20%) Freewriting: 10% Writing Portfolio/synthesis essay: 5% Attendance, class participation, preparation: 5 %
