docs.text: 1 Course Title: Reading and Writing II: Media Writing Instructor: Shuyu Lee (shuyulee@mx.nthu.edu.tw) Course TA: Classroom Language: English Course Description: Media writing refers to communication-oriented writing used mainly in the professional fields of journalism, public relations, and marketing. Designed for FLL students, this course focuses on news writing for journalistic and public relations purposes. This year-long course maintains a balance between reading and writing. Using the latest real- life news reports from around the world as our reading materials, we will learn how to find news, understand news, and analyze news. Then, as informed news readers, we will learn to write our own news stories. The first step toward this goal lies in adopting the language of news, a fast-paced, efficiency-minded style that makes news writing unique. We will also look at ethical issues in news writing and how well-written news contributes to social equality and justice. Learning Outcomes: Students will become skillful in communications in different media. Students will develop an awareness of audience and increase their intercultural communicative competence. Students will be able to write clear and concise documents for communicational purposes. Students will be able to balance commercial interest and social responsibility as prospective media professionals. Core Capabilities (大學部學生核心能力): 1. The ability to communicate and express oneself in English (溝通表達與語文能力) 30% 2. The ability to analyze classic canons of literature (文學經典的分析與詮釋) 0% 3. The ability to look for problems and conduct research (問題發掘與研究能力) 20% 4. The ability to think creatively (創作與創新能力) 25% 5. The ability to examine issues through global and multicultural perspectives (全球化與國 際視野及多元文化認知能力) 25% Required Texts: All handouts are to be accessed on the course’s eLearn platform. 2 Supplementary Readings: Smith, Ronald D. Becoming a Public Relations Writer: Strategic Writing for Emerging and Established Media. 5th ed., Routledge, 2017. Bender, John R., Lucinda D. Davenport, Michael W. Drager, and Fred Fedler. Writing and Reporting for the Media. Twelfth edition. New York: Oxford University Press, 2019. Harrower, Tim. Inside Reporting: a Practical Guide to the Craft of Journalism. Third edition. New York: McGraw-Hill, 2013. Whitaker, W. Richard, Janet E. Ramsey, and Ronald D. Smith. Mediawriting: Print, Broadcast and Public Relations. Fifth edition. London: Routledge, 2019. Roberts, Jasmine. Writing for Strategic Communication Industries. Ohio State UP, 2016. https://ohiostate.pressbooks.pub/stratcommwriting/ Assessment: Attendance 5% Active Participation (raising and answering questions, volunteering to read texts, and other behaviors that prove mental presence in class) 10% Quiz 15% Preview Questions (for weeks 6 to 10) 10% Assignments 60% Class Policies: 1. Attendance 1-A: Regular attendance is expected. Exceptions: ⬧ Sick Leave: documentary evidence, such as a doctor’s note or a similar certificate from a healthcare professional, is required to prove the legitimacy of the leave request. ⬧ Compassionate Leave (bereavement leave): documentary evidence is required to prove the legitimacy of the leave request. ⬧ Public Duties Leave: documentary evidence is required to prove the legitimacy of the leave request. ⬧ Personal Leave: documentary evidence is required to prove the legitimacy of the leave request. NOTE: Emails containing no documentary evidence proving the legitimacy of the leave request have no function and therefore will be ignored. 1-B: Attendance may be taken anytime during the class meeting. Students found absent at roll call will be marked absent for the day. 1-C: Three unexcused absences will incur a half letter grade reduction in semester grade. That means your semester grade will go, for example, from an original A to A-. Four 3 unexcused absences will lead to a full letter grade reduction for the entire semester, which means your semester grade will turn, for example, from an original B into C. 2. Assignments 2-A: Assignments should be submitted on time. A full letter grade will be deducted after the deadline, which means, for example, a B becoming a C. An additional letter grade will be deducted per 24 hours after the deadline, which means that the C could turn further into D, E, or X. 2-B: Note that in accordance with the official NTHU grading regulations below, assignment papers submitted 96 hours after the deadline would receive zero points. 2-C: An assignment paper submitted in the incorrect file format would result in one full letter grade reduction. This means, for example, a paper originally getting an A will now be recorded as a B. 2-D: Because of the introductory nature of this course, the use of generative AI for assignments is strongly discouraged. 2-E: Regarding the ethics of using generative AI technology in news writing, the current 4 consensus among journalists is that news outlets should practice full disclosure if generative AI is used at any stage of the writing of their stories. As aspiring media writers, we will follow the same ethical principles as professionals. Therefore, if generative AI is used at any step of the writing of your assignments, you must include a full disclosure statement. The content of your assignment paper should include both the prompts and the outputs (or any other record of the text generation and editing process). Failure to comply with the ethical practice of full disclosure will result in receiving an X for the assignment. 3. Quizzes 3-A: Failure to be present for a quiz will result in receiving zero points for the quiz. 3-B: Make-up quizzes are given only in case of absence due to force majeure events. ◆DEFINITION of a force majeure event: the event must be unforeseeable, external, and irresistible. ◆EXAMPLES of force majeure events: earthquake disasters, traffic accidents, emergency hospitalization, armed conflicts (war), and civil unrest (riots). 4. Other Policies ⚫ Course materials (including the syllabus, handouts, and remote class images, audios, and videos) should not be sold to or shared with anyone outside of the class. ⚫ How to do well in this course? Take an active role in class and have a positive attitude to the world. Schedule Note: Schedule is subject to change according to lesson progress. (0%) ■ 問題發掘與研究能力 (15%) The ability to look for problems and conduct research (including conducting linguistic analysis through scientific methods) (5%) ■ 創作與創新能力 (5%) The ability to think creatively (5%) ■ 全球化與國際視野及多元文化認知能力 (20%) The ability to examine issues through global and multicultural perspectives (20%) 課程大綱 (Syllabus) 一、課程說明(Course Description) 該科目原則上實體教學，不過，看疫情情形教育部有特別的需求時，用視訊方式上課。疫情如果 影響到考試，大家討論之後，有可能更改方式。 加強詞彙及句型。重視自己積極學習的態度，鼓勵學生積極參與學習語。增加培養自學日語之基 礎（聽說讀寫）。 另外學日語歌，看DVD，介紹日本文化，習俗等，接觸日本文化。 二、指定用書(Text Books) 『大家的日本語初級Ⅱ』 改訂版 大新書局 2015 自備講義 三、參考書籍(References) スリーエーネットワーク編『大家的日本語 初級Ⅰ・II 改訂版 標準 問題集』 2 『大家的日本語 初級Ⅰ・Ⅱ 改訂版 句型練習冊』 『大家的日本語 初級 II 改訂版 有聲 CD 版（4 片裝，不附書）』 『大家的日本語 初級Ⅱ 改訂版 文法解說・參考詞彙・課文中譯』 『大家的日本語 初級Ⅱ 改訂版 練習 ABC・問題解答（附中譯）』 『大家的日本語 初級Ⅱ 改訂版 會話 DVD（附日中對照會話本）』 『大家的日本語 聴力解説タスク 25』 『大家的日本語 讀本篇 初級 改訂版』 四、教學方式(Teaching Method) 講師授課方式。 每一課先解釋 單字（包括日式漢字寫法和大寫的差異），再套入新的句型及課文，然後以句型再練習實用之短 句對話，聽力等。最後再以短句做應用練習。培養聽・說・讀・寫平衡能力。 五、教學進度(Syllabus) 大概的目標是每3～6小時念完1課。這學期念第13課～第18課。 但看學生的吸收狀態，可能調整進度。 第一週(09/04)：課程說明，複習上學期學過的內容，文法、動詞變化複習。 第二週(09/11)：第13課 單字，句型（欲しい、V-iたい），會話 ，練習及問題 第三週(09/18)：V-Te形（て形）導論 第四週(09/25)：第14課 單字，句型（て形），會話，練習及問題 第五週(10/02)：第15課 單字，句型（V-Teもいいです、V-Teはいけません），會話，練習及問 題 第六週(10/09)：雙十節停課一天 第七週(10/16)：第13課～第15課錯誤分析 第八週(10/23)：期中考 第九週(10/30)：還考卷 內容分析, 16課 單字，句型（V1-Te，V2, V-Teから〜）,會話，練習 及問題 第十週(11/06)： 第16課 練及問題，複習D 第十一週(11/13)：第17課 單字，句型（ない形），會話, 練及問題 第十二週(11/20)：辭典型導論，和禮貌形比較（非過去肯定，非過去否定，過去肯定，過去否 定） 第十三週(11/27)：第18課 單字，句型（辞書形），會話，練及問題 第十四週(12/04)：第16課～第18課錯誤分析 第十五週(12/11)：第13課～18課這學期的綜合練習 第十六週(12/18)：期末考 六、成績考核(Evaluation) 期中考 30％ 期末考 30％ 3 出席 20％ （請假一定寫書面上的請假單。不准寄e-mail。遲交3週之後無法接受） 作業 20％（不准沒對過[解答]修改的作。沒修改的作業回扣扣分。不準時交的會扣分，遲交 3週之後無法接受） 七、可連結之網頁位址 web版「エリンが挑戦！にほんごできます」 https://www.erin.ne.jp 清大圖書館電子圖書 「大家學日語」 清大圖書館電子圖書 JLPT模擬考（N1〜N5） 其他上課時隨時加上

教 室 人社 C512 選修資格限制 先修科目： 校內「初級日語二」成績「C-」以上或 通過日本語能力試驗 N5 級 課程綱要 ❤ 課 程 說 明 學習目標： 認知 ● 習得日文基礎句型。 ● 藉由日語學習同時玩味日本文化。 技能 ● 奠定基礎日語會話技巧。 ● 培養基礎日文讀寫能力。 情意 ● 以日語與他人溝通，獲得成就感、增添學習興趣。 ● 觀察日語表達的習慣與特色，體察日本文化。 核心能力： ■溝通表達與語文能力：60% ■問題發掘與研究能力：15% ■創作與創新能力：5% ■全球視野與多元文化認知能力：20% 指 定 用 書 ●教師自編講義 ●『大家的日本語 初級Ⅱ 改訂版』大新書局 參 考 資 料 (1)『みんなの日本語 初級Ⅰ 第２版 聴解タスク２５』 スリーエーネットワーク (2)日語歌曲、其他與課程相關之資料等。 教 學 方 式 (1)期初課堂見面時輔以包含（假期活動分享等）應景話題、既學語彙及 (1)句型相關重要表達學習單進行書寫及口頭（文法、重音、語調）複習。 (1)（來自「初級日語」各班）新加入成員並另發放平假名、片假名字帖 (1)紙本幫助複習時確認字形、發音相關重點及作業、考試批閱標準。 (2)遵循「認知、「技能」、「情意」三種面向之學習目標，循序完成教科書 (2)內預定基礎學習項目的同時亦持續以多種學習資源鼓勵同學培養自主 (2)學習的能力。 (3)善用自編單字表、動詞語尾變化規則表及語彙實例(含重音標示)等 (3)補充教材、 （e.g. 日本留學經歷及文化體驗相關相片、 (3)生活小物）等以 (不藉由媒介語)導入，引導同學們以教科書、 板書、 簡報、紙本講義等循序學習重要概念，藉由淺顯易懂的文法 說明幫助學習者理解後進行應用練習。 (4)以作業、分組練習等方式確認聽說讀寫能力。 (5)適時以日常生活用語、文化方面題材、自編補充教材、日語相關有益 (2)網站及搭配所學進度或因應時節之歌曲(教師譯註 PDF 檔)、（廣告或 (2)日劇）影片等幫助學習者藉由觀察日語表達的習慣與特色來體察日本 (2)文化、提升學習興趣，期能更加提升學習效果。 2 (6)各課採用「導入句型、文法說明、口頭練習、聽力練習」等方式進行， (2)「形、音、義」並重地培養學習者提升閱讀能力及口語表達能力。 (7)善用 教材及測驗區等各項功能：適時將課程相關補充語彙及 (7)文法等補充資料、各課練習題參考解答、日文漢字筆順（動畫示範）、 (7) 日文重音字典（含動詞各種活用變化音聲示範）等資源分享 (7)公布於 ，修課學生可能時時下載補充教材 PDF 檔案自主學習， (7)亦可能因應需求連結有益學習網頁。幫助學習者藉由按部就班預習及 (7)複習的過程中熟習實用語彙及自然的日語表達方式。 教 學 進 度 單元主題（課程進度謹供參考，可能視班級實際學習情況調整） 第 1 週( 9/11) 課程簡述； < 欲求；希求、願望 > 第 1 週( 9/14) 第 13 課：「 」；「 」 第 2 週( 9/18) 第 13 課：「 」 <移動的目的 > 第 3 週( 9/25) 第 14 課：動詞分類；動詞「 」；「 」 < docs.text: 113-1 NTHU 中級日語 課程綱要 W234 簡嘉菁 1 中級日語 課程綱要 一、課程基本資料 I. Course information 課程代碼 Course Number 11410FL 300503 課程名稱 Title in Chinese 中級日語（一） 課程英文名稱 Title in English Intermediate Japanese 全/半年 Two/one semester 全年 必/選修/通識 Required/ Elective/ General Education 選修 總學分數 Credits 3 每週上課時數/ 教室 Lecturing hours/ classroom 週三 W234 (09:10-12:00) 人社院 C512 開課系所 Class standing 外語系 授課教師 Instructor(s) 簡嘉菁 kankasei88@gmail.com 先修課程 Prerequisites 具備日語基礎能力（名詞、動詞、形容詞等時態變化）或通過學校的初級日語 課程（備註：外籍學生須具備中文能力） 關鍵字 Keywords 日語 Japanese, 聽力 listening, 會話 conversation, 閱讀 reading, 寫作 writing 課程簡介 Course Description 1. 教學目標：培養學生具有初中級程度以上的日語進階溝通與表達能力。透過 討論、聽力練習與會話演練來培養溝通表達能力。提升至日語 JLPT N4-N5 實力。 2. 指定教科書：上下學期《大家的日本語 初級 II 改訂版》 3. 教學進度：視學習狀況與學校行事曆適時調整進度。上學期進度為《大家的 日本語初級 II 改訂版》第 13-18 課。下學期進度第 19-25 課。 4. 課程說明：學習動詞活用變化以及動詞活用變化所連用的相關句型 (如 「V- ます形、V-たい形、Ⅴ-る形、V-て形、Ⅴ-た形、Ⅴ-ない形」等)。以其運用 在「請求、動作進行貌、動作持續貌、動作樣貌、(請求)允許、否定、能 力、興趣、事件、經驗、列舉、變化、口語表現、想法、說法、動詞修飾 名詞、條件句、授受表現、逆接表現」等各種日語溝通表達能力。透過教 科書、老師的自製授課講義與各種網路教學平台等，鼓勵學生模擬真實會 話情境，熟練相關句型的口語表達與聽力內容。課程中適時加入相關日語 句型的日語歌曲、日語新聞或日劇動漫台詞，以期有效應用所學內容。 5. 成績考核：期中考（40%）、期末考（30%）、作業（10%）、小考（10%）、 出席（10%） 註：教學方法、評量方式、參考書目、教學網頁、AI 使用規則等請參考課綱 附檔。第一週將詳細說明。 注意事項 Please note 注意事項： (1) 除特殊狀況，不開放加簽或申請二退（需當面晤談。未經同意，不審核二 退的電子簽單）。申請旁聽者請事先來信聯絡。 (2) 部分專有名詞與內容將以中文介紹。 (3) 詳細教學方法、評量方式、參考書目、教學網頁等將在第一週說明。 (4) 關於 AI 使用規則：有條件開放. 基於透明與負責任的原則，本課程可以利 用 AI 進行查詢，以提升本門課品質。但是本課程的個人報告或分組報告 113-1 NTHU 中級日語 課程綱要 W234 簡嘉菁 2 中, 不得使用生成 AI 工具撰寫報告. 若經查核使用卻未在作業或報告中標 明，教師、學校或相關單位有權重新針對作業或報告重新評分或不予計分。 (5) 出席: 重要考試或個人上台報告日，都必須出席。請假時請利用學校請 假系統的上網登記。除了緊急重大意外，請假時都必須在上課前完成請 假。如果是公假、喪假、病假、婚假、赴日（來回機票證明，一學期最 多申請 2 次，1 次一週為上限）需附上相關證明單。不需要再給紙本請假 單。詳細規定請參考學校請假系統通知。缺課達五週以上（或 1/4）不給 予學期成績。 課程目標 Course Outcomes 此科目對應之系所課程規畫所欲培養之核心能力 Core capability to be cultivated by this course 1 培養扎實日語表達能力 溝通表達與語文能力、創作與創新能力 2 理解日本社會與文化 問題發掘與研究能力 3 透過與日本的比較, 提高對台灣的關心 全球化與國際視野及多元文化認知能力 二、教學大綱 II. docs.text: 授 課 大 綱 課程資訊 課程名稱：中級日語（一） Intermediate Japanese I 任課教師：王瑋婷 (WANG,WEI-TING) 上課時間：R34n 學分數：3 此科目對應之系所課程規畫所欲培養之核心能力 ■ 溝通表達與語文能力 (70%) □ 文學經典的分析與詮釋 ■ 問題發掘與研究能力 (15%) □ 創作與創新能力 ■ 全球化與國際視野及多元文化認知能力 (15%) 課程簡述 接續「初級日語」所學基礎，隨課本進度，協助同學熟悉初級程度的主題句型，進一步奠定日語溝 通能力。本學期進度預定為教科書 13~19 課前半內容。 教學目標： 1. 學會聽、說、讀、寫日語初級語彙及句型。 2. 能於生活中聽、說應用所學句型，具初級日語溝通能力。 3. 理解日本文化，提升國際視野。 4. 提升學生生活品質及未來發展潛力。 課程大綱 課程說明 本課程授課對象為修畢初級日語的同學。 隨課本進度授課，上學期教學 13 課~19 課前半，下學期教學 19 課後半~25 課；完成整 冊進度後，可熟悉相當於日檢 N5 程度的日文應用，進而向 N4 程度挑戰。 課程中將隨各課主題內容講解語彙，並逐項分析主題句型，透過口說及書寫練習強化 同學們對句型的掌握度，也將透過會話演練及課堂活動、聽力練習等，讓同學們進一 步活用句型內容，提升日語流暢度及溝通能力。 課程中亦將穿插補充生活會話練習、日本文化介紹、分享線上學習資源等，以強化同 學的學習興趣，培養主動自發的學習精神。 指定用書 《大家的日本語 初級 II 改訂版》，大新書局 參考書籍 1.《大家的日本語 初級 II 文法解說書》，大新書局 2.《大家的日本語 初級 II 聴解タスク》，大新書局 3.《大家的日本語 初級 讀本篇》，大新書局 4. PPT 文法說明、其他課程補充講義等 教學方式 1. 將以「單字講解、文法導入及說明、口頭及書寫練習、造句及問答應用、會話活動、 聽力練習」等方式授課，以讓同學充分掌握文法，培養聽說讀寫能力。 2. 適時補充日本文化、時事等內容，以增進同學對異文化的理解，提升學習興趣。 教學進度 W1 9/4 課程介紹、 L.13 (願望表現：想要的物品〔～が欲しいです〕、想做的事情〔Ｖた いです〕、前往某處的目的〔～に行きます〕) W2 9/11 L.13 W3 9/18 L.13 L.14 (動詞て形應用：表達請託、指示〔Ｖてください〕、動作現在進 行式〔Ｖています〕) W4 9/25 L.14 W5 10/2 L.14 W6 10/9 L.15 (動詞て形應用：表達結果狀態的存續〔Ｖています〕、禁止〔Ｖ てはいけません〕、許可〔Ｖてもいいです〕) W7 10/16 L.15 W8 10/23 期中考、L.16 (て形應用：表達動作進行順序、形容詞及名詞的て形串 連形) (*前 75 分鐘正常上課，後半進行期中考) W9 10/30 L.16 W10 11/6 L.16 W11 11/13 L.17 (動詞ない形應用：表達請託及指示〔Ｖないでください〕、必須/ 不必做某事的句型〔Ｖなければなりません/Ｖなくてもいいです〕) W12 11/20 L.17 W13 11/27 L.18 (動詞辭書形應用：將句子名詞化以表達能力、興趣；表達動作 進行的時間點〔～前に〕) W14 12/4 L.18 W15 12/11 L.19 (動詞た形應用：表達經驗〔Ｖたことがあります〕、列舉動作〔Ｖ たり、Ｖたりします〕；表達狀態變化的句型 〔～なります〕) W16 12/18 期末考、L.19 (*前 75 分鐘正常上課，後半進行期末考) 成績考核 小考及作業 30% *小考進行數次(原則上每課 1 次，測驗字彙及文法內容；課程內容較多時，有可能 視情況改為單字小考或作業)。期末將刪除其中成績最差的 1 次。 *小考週次如請公假/喪假/病假等，出示證明則可以免考不計分。 事假及無證明的病假、生理假可補考，必須於隔週第一節下課(15 分鐘)補考完成； 遲到同學當天下課 10 分鐘內補考完，以-5 計算成績；曠課不可補考，以零分計算。 課堂參與 15% (含出缺席及課堂參與度) *無故曠課一次扣 2 分；課堂參與度欠佳者，視其參與程度減扣 0.5-1.5 分。 *為維護課堂參與成績公平性，各類請假評分規則如下： 1. 公假/喪假/具醫療證明的病假：不扣分 (病假可接受請假日 3 日內的藥袋或掛號資訊、快篩、體溫計畫面為證明) 2. 生理假：不扣分，每月最多以 1 次為限 3. 事假/無證明的病假：1-2 次不扣分；第 3 次扣 0.5 分；第 4-5 次扣 1 分； 第 6 次起不再接受請假，會登記為曠課扣 2 分。 4. 不接受事假/無證明病假連續請假 2 週以上。自第 2 週起將登記為曠課。 5. 上課遲到 15 分鐘以上，自第 3 次起將會扣分，每次減扣 1 分。 *如有特殊身心狀況，請另來信提供醫療證明並討論課堂參與事宜。 期中考 25% 期末考 30% 其他注意 事項 1. 請謹慎評估個人日語程度合適與否、專注力、以及作息/時間分配等因素，無法配 合認真參與課堂者，請勿選課。 2. 課程中常常進行小組(大部分是兩人一組)會話練習，不願參與練習者建議勿選課。 3. 生成 AI 使用原則：本課程無涉及 AI 使用

docs.text: 113 學年度 上學期「中級日語一」課程大綱 任課教師 廖紋淑 科目名稱 中級日語一 Intermediate Japanese (Ⅰ) 課程時段 F2F3F4 擬開設年級 þ大學部 年級 þ研究所 學分數 3 學生人數限制 □無 þ有（ 45 人） 科號 11110FL 300509 修課限制 限外語系：□是 þ否 教室 C412 課程綱要 課程說明 學習目標 認知 l 習得日文基礎句型 l 藉由日語學習同時理解日本文化 技能 l 奠定基礎日語會話技巧 l 培養基礎日文讀寫能力 情意 l 以日語與他人溝通，獲得成就感、增添學習興趣。 l 觀察日語表達的習慣與特色，體察日文文化 核心能力：溝通發表與語文能力：60% 問題發掘發掘與研究能力：20% 全球視野與多元文化認知能力：20% 指定用書 『大家的日本語 初級Ⅱ』 大新書局 參考資料 『大家的日本語』初級Ⅰ『大家的日本語』初級讀本篇 AI 使用規則 有條件開放，請註明如何使用生成式 AI 於課程產出 教學方式 1. 各課採用「單字解說、句型導入、文法解說、口頭演練、聽力練習」 等方式進行，培養學習者閱讀能力以及口語表達能力。 2. 以板書與補充教材等幫助學習者理解文法使用基礎概念，並搭配日 常生活常用語彙練習，增加記憶力外，並達到能夠簡單運用日語會 話溝通的能力。 3. 適時以日語影片等輔助教學，藉由觀察日語表達的習慣與影片中使 用的場景來體察日本文化，提升學習意願。 4. 每堂課都有隨堂小考（所有測驗考試，不接受補考，提前考試） *注意 5. 本課程不接受同學停修申請 6. 為維護上課品質，不接受旁聽 7. 請假（病假、公假、喪假、事假…等）請務必親自提出相關證明， 同時請假期限需在請假日之前後 1 週完成，否則不予准假。 請同學斟酌自身修課狀況，規劃安排課程，並尊重選課結果。 成績比例 1. 課堂參與：15% 2. 課堂中的隨堂測試：20% 3. 作業：10% 4. 期中考：25% 5. 期末考：30% 教學進度 上課的目標是每 6 小時上完 1 課為原則。 *依學生的吸收狀況，隨時調整上課以及考試的進度。 第 1 週：課程說明、第 13 課「〜欲しいです」願望的表達方式 第 2 週：第 13 課 課文及練習 第 3 週：第 14 課「〜てください」指示、輕微的命令、請托等 第 4 週：第 14 課 輕微的命令、請托等、第 15 課 「〜てもいいです」 許可的表達方式 第 5 週：第 15 課 「〜ています」狀態的表達方式 第 6 週：第 16 課 「〜て、〜て、〜ます」動作的順序、「〜くて/〜で、 〜」形容詞接續 第 7 週：第 16 課「〜は〜が形容詞」描述身體特徵或事物特徵 第 8 週：期中考 第 13 課～第 16 課 第 9 週：檢討期中考、第 17 課 動詞「て形」 第 10 週：第 17 課「〜ないでください」不許可「〜なければなりませ ん」義務・必要性「〜なくてもいいです」容許 第 11 週：第 18 課 動詞「字典形」 第 12 週：第 18 課「〜ことができます」能力「〜ことです」興趣、嗜 好、「〜前（に）、〜」明確表達動作執行的時間 第 13 週：第 18 課 課文及練習 第 14 週：第 19 課 動詞「た形」「〜たことができます」經驗 第 15 週：第 19 課 課文及練習 第 16 週：期末考 第 17 課－第 19 課

V ます形ⅠⅡⅢ類還原成 V る(詞書)形 1.單字正音/速讀 2.文法講授 3.句型創作&與老師對話 4.翻譯 5.閱讀 6.雙人會話練習&情境 對話 7.遊戲 測驗 第十三週 第十八課 你的興趣・嗜好是什麼? 表能力之 V、adj.其受詞的助詞為が  (L9) ～ができます ～V る(辭書)ことができます ～です ～V る(辭書)ことです V る(辭書) N の ＋まえに、～ 數量詞(期間) 1.單字正音/速讀 2.文法講授 3.句型創作&與老師對話 4.翻譯 5.閱讀 6.雙人會話練習&情境 對話 7.遊戲 測驗 Adv.: ぜひ與表示[慾望・委託]並用,更表示 強調之意 とくに後接 N 、V、adj 表特別或特定 的人事物 なかなか(adv.)…接否定(亦可肯定獨 立使用,但非本課程) 第十四週 第十九課 減重明天再開始 動詞變化ⅠⅡⅢ類「た」形 1.單字正音/速讀 2.文法講授 3.句型創作&與老師對話 4.翻譯 5.閱讀 6.雙人會話練習&情境 對話 7.遊戲 測驗 第十五週 第十九課 減重明天再開始 ～たことがあります…表經驗 ～たり、～たり します…V 的舉例 [い-adj./な-adj.]與動詞的連接 1.單字正音/速讀 2.文法講授 3.句型創作&與老師對話 4.翻譯 5.閱讀 6.雙人會話練習&情境 對話 7.遊戲 測驗 第十六週 期末考 筆試・話劇 測驗 任 課 老 師 張 嘉 芬 課程說明 本課程以圖文並茂方式導入教學，並重複演練以助加深記憶。每課文法解說 完畢後，指導同學短文創作、會話、發音(配合指定教材 CD) 聽力、閱讀等練 習，並且每課舉行小考&不定期隨堂考，以深耕聽、說、讀、寫能力。調和課程 氣氛，提升學習樂趣，課程間隔時間開放點歌及影片欣賞，課程中安排，日語遊 戲/競賽/桌遊/日本國情與文化相關介紹等活動，以認識與學習他國文化並導入 商業、科技與觀光日語會話教學，擴展學習領域，將本課程之所學適宜地應用於 生活、職場，並透過日本語教育多元思考與溝通合作之影響致力於終身學習。 本學期進度 課程教學目標 「大家的日本語初級IL 改訂版」13～19課 一、實現表達及溝通能力。 二、認識與學習他國文化。 三、創作與創新能力 四、將本課程之所學適宜地應用於生活、職場，並透過日本語教育多元思考與溝 通合作之影響致力於終身學習。 指定用書 《大家的日本語 初級 IL 改訂版》，大新書局 ISBN 978-986-321-087-0 參考用書 日文會話辭典 大新書局 ISBN 978-986-321-132-7 N4N5 日檢閱讀 山田社事業有限公司 ISBN 978-986-246-478-6 全新開始學日語會話 國際學村出版社 ISBN 978-986-454-120-1 評 量 期中分筆試 20%、期末分組話劇表 5%筆試 20%、其他 55%(課程參與、出缺席、每 課小考&不定期隨堂考) 請假申請者請提前告假(病假證明隔週出示亦可)無證明文件者當日以曠課計之

docs.text: 授 課 大 綱 課程資訊 課程名稱：中級日語（一） Intermediate Japanese I 任課教師：王瑋婷 (WANG,WEI-TING) 上課時間：R678 學分數：3 此科目對應之系所課程規畫所欲培養之核心能力 ■ 溝通表達與語文能力 (70%) □ 文學經典的分析與詮釋 ■ 問題發掘與研究能力 (15%) □ 創作與創新能力 ■ 全球化與國際視野及多元文化認知能力 (15%) 課程簡述 接續「初級日語」所學基礎，隨課本進度，協助同學熟悉初級程度的主題句型，進一步奠定日語溝 通能力。本學期進度預定為教科書 13~19 課前半內容。 教學目標： 1. 學會聽、說、讀、寫日語初級語彙及句型。 2. 能於生活中聽、說應用所學句型，具初級日語溝通能力。 3. 理解日本文化，提升國際視野。 4. 提升學生生活品質及未來發展潛力。 課程大綱 課程說明 本課程授課對象為修畢初級日語的同學。 隨課本進度授課，上學期教學 13 課~19 課前半，下學期教學 19 課後半~25 課；完成整 冊進度後，可熟悉相當於日檢 N5 程度的日文應用，進而向 N4 程度挑戰。 課程中將隨各課主題內容講解語彙，並逐項分析主題句型，透過口說及書寫練習強化 同學們對句型的掌握度，也將透過會話演練及課堂活動、聽力練習等，讓同學們進一 步活用句型內容，提升日語流暢度及溝通能力。 課程中亦將穿插補充生活會話練習、日本文化介紹、分享線上學習資源等，以強化同 學的學習興趣，培養主動自發的學習精神。 指定用書 《大家的日本語 初級 II 改訂版》，大新書局 參考書籍 1.《大家的日本語 初級 II 文法解說書》，大新書局 2.《大家的日本語 初級 II 聴解タスク》，大新書局 3.《大家的日本語 初級 讀本篇》，大新書局 4. PPT 文法說明、其他課程補充講義等 教學方式 1. 將以「單字講解、文法導入及說明、口頭及書寫練習、造句及問答應用、會話活動、 聽力練習」等方式授課，以讓同學充分掌握文法，培養聽說讀寫能力。 2. 適時補充日本文化、時事等內容，以增進同學對異文化的理解，提升學習興趣。 教學進度 W1 9/4 課程介紹、 L.13 (願望表現：想要的物品〔～が欲しいです〕、想做的事情〔Ｖた いです〕、前往某處的目的〔～に行きます〕) W2 9/11 L.13 W3 9/18 L.13 L.14 (動詞て形應用：表達請託、指示〔Ｖてください〕、動作現在進 行式〔Ｖています〕) W4 9/25 L.14 W5 10/2 L.14 W6 10/9 L.15 (動詞て形應用：表達結果狀態的存續〔Ｖています〕、禁止〔Ｖ てはいけません〕、許可〔Ｖてもいいです〕) W7 10/16 L.15 W8 10/23 期中考、L.16 (て形應用：表達動作進行順序、形容詞及名詞的て形串 連形) (*前 75 分鐘正常上課，後半進行期中考) W9 10/30 L.16 W10 11/6 L.16 W11 11/13 L.17 (動詞ない形應用：表達請託及指示〔Ｖないでください〕、必須/ 不必做某事的句型〔Ｖなければなりません/Ｖなくてもいいです〕) W12 11/20 L.17 W13 11/27 L.18 (動詞辭書形應用：將句子名詞化以表達能力、興趣；表達動作 進行的時間點〔～前に〕) W14 12/4 L.18 W15 12/11 L.19 (動詞た形應用：表達經驗〔Ｖたことがあります〕、列舉動作〔Ｖ たり、Ｖたりします〕；表達狀態變化的句型 〔～なります〕) W16 12/18 期末考、L.19 (*前 75 分鐘正常上課，後半進行期末考) 成績考核 小考及作業 30% *小考進行數次(原則上每課 1 次，測驗字彙及文法內容；課程內容較多時，有可能 視情況改為單字小考或作業)。期末將刪除其中成績最差的 1 次。 *小考週次如請公假/喪假/病假等，出示證明則可以免考不計分。 事假及無證明的病假、生理假可補考，必須於隔週第一節下課(15 分鐘)補考完成； 遲到同學當天下課 10 分鐘內補考完，以-5 計算成績；曠課不可補考，以零分計算。 課堂參與 15% (含出缺席及課堂參與度) *無故曠課一次扣 2 分；課堂參與度欠佳者，視其參與程度減扣 0.5-1.5 分。 *為維護課堂參與成績公平性，各類請假評分規則如下： 1. 公假/喪假/具醫療證明的病假：不扣分 (病假可接受請假日 3 日內的藥袋或掛號資訊、快篩、體溫計畫面為證明) 2. 生理假：不扣分，每月最多以 1 次為限 3. 事假/無證明的病假：1-2 次不扣分；第 3 次扣 0.5 分；第 4-5 次扣 1 分； 第 6 次起不再接受請假，會登記為曠課扣 2 分。 4. 不接受事假/無證明病假連續請假 2 週以上。自第 2 週起將登記為曠課。 5. 上課遲到 15 分鐘以上，自第 3 次起將會扣分，每次減扣 1 分。 *如有特殊身心狀況，請另來信提供醫療證明並討論課堂參與事宜。 期中考 25% 期末考 30% 其他注意 事項 1. 請謹慎評估個人日語程度合適與否、專注力、以及作息/時間分配等因素，無法配 合認真參與課堂者，請勿選課。 2. 課程中常常進行小組(大部分是兩人一組)會話練習，不願參與練習者建議勿選課。 3. 生成 AI 使用原則：本課程無涉及 AI 使用

Course information 課程代碼 Course Number 11410FL 300503 課程名稱 Title in Chinese 中級日語（一） 課程英文名稱 Title in English Intermediate Japanese 全/半年 Two/one semester 全年 必/選修/通識 Required/ Elective/ General Education 選修 總學分數 Credits 3 每週上課時數/ 教室 Lecturing hours/ classroom 週三 W567 (13:30-16:20) 人社院 C512 開課系所 Class standing 外語系 授課教師 Instructor(s) 簡嘉菁 kankasei88@gmail.com 先修課程 Prerequisites 具備日語基礎能力（名詞、動詞、形容詞等時態變化）或通過學校的初級日語 課程（備註：外籍學生須具備中文能力） 關鍵字 Keywords 日語 Japanese, 聽力 listening, 會話 conversation, 閱讀 reading, 寫作 writing 課程簡介 Course Description 1. 教學目標：培養學生具有初中級程度以上的日語進階溝通與表達能力。透過 討論、聽力練習與會話演練來培養溝通表達能力。提升至日語 JLPT N4-N5 實力。 2. 指定教科書：上下學期《大家的日本語 初級 II 改訂版》 3. 教學進度：視學習狀況與學校行事曆適時調整進度。上學期進度為《大家的 日本語初級 II 改訂版》第 13-18 課。下學期進度第 19-25 課。 4. 課程說明：學習動詞活用變化以及動詞活用變化所連用的相關句型 (如 「V- ます形、V-たい形、Ⅴ-る形、V-て形、Ⅴ-た形、Ⅴ-ない形」等)。以其運用 在「請求、動作進行貌、動作持續貌、動作樣貌、(請求)允許、否定、能 力、興趣、事件、經驗、列舉、變化、口語表現、想法、說法、動詞修飾 名詞、條件句、授受表現、逆接表現」等各種日語溝通表達能力。透過教 科書、老師的自製授課講義與各種網路教學平台等，鼓勵學生模擬真實會 話情境，熟練相關句型的口語表達與聽力內容。課程中適時加入相關日語 句型的日語歌曲、日語新聞或日劇動漫台詞，以期有效應用所學內容。 5. 成績考核：期中考（40%）、期末考（30%）、作業（10%）、小考（10%）、 出席（10%） 註：教學方法、評量方式、參考書目、教學網頁、AI 使用規則等請參考課綱 附檔。第一週將詳細說明。 注意事項 Please note 注意事項： (1) 除特殊狀況，不開放加簽或申請二退（需當面晤談。未經同意，不審核二 退的電子簽單）。申請旁聽者請事先來信聯絡。 (2) 部分專有名詞與內容將以中文介紹。 (3) 詳細教學方法、評量方式、參考書目、教學網頁等將在第一週說明。 (4) 關於 AI 使用規則：有條件開放. 基於透明與負責任的原則，本課程可以利 用 AI 進行查詢，以提升本門課品質。但是本課程的個人報告或分組報告 113-1 NTHU 中級日語 課程綱要 W567 簡嘉菁 2 中, 不得使用生成 AI 工具撰寫報告. 若經查核使用卻未在作業或報告中標 明，教師、學校或相關單位有權重新針對作業或報告重新評分或不予計分。 (5) 出席: 重要考試或個人上台報告日，都必須出席。請假時請利用學校請 假系統的上網登記。除了緊急重大意外，請假時都必須在上課前完成請 假。如果是公假、喪假、病假、婚假、赴日（來回機票證明，一學期最 多申請 2 次，1 次一週為上限）需附上相關證明單。不需要再給紙本請假 單。詳細規定請參考學校請假系統通知。缺課達五週以上（或 1/4）不給 予學期成績。 課程目標 Course Outcomes 此科目對應之系所課程規畫所欲培養之核心能力 Core capability to be cultivated by this course 1 培養扎實日語表達能力 溝通表達與語文能力、創作與創新能力 2 理解日本社會與文化 問題發掘與研究能力 3 透過與日本的比較, 提高對台灣的關心 全球化與國際視野及多元文化認知能力 二、教學大綱 II. docs.text: 1 114 上 中級法語⼀ 課程⼤綱 M789 ⼀、課程說明(Course Description) 本課程透過日常⽣活會話練習、閱讀, 培養學⽣中級法語聽、說、讀、寫能⼒。 ⼆、指定用書(Text Books) Amical 1, CLE International 法語實用進階教材 II 三、參考書籍(References) Grammaire progressive du français, Niveau intermédiaire, CLE international 四、教學⽅式(Teaching Method) 會話、閱讀、⽂法解說、翻譯練習 五、教學進度(Syllabus) 週次 / 教學內容 1 Introduction 課程進度/評分⽅式說明 第 1-7 週 Amical 1 第 13-18 課 + 法語實用進階教材 II 第 1 課 Leçon 1 Excuse-moi de ne pas t’avoir écrit plus tôt. 很抱歉沒有早點寫信給你 第 9-15 週 Amical 1 第 19-24 課 + 法語實用進階教材 II 第 3 課 Leçon 3 Docteur, je tousse, j’ai mal à la gorge. 醫⽣，我咳嗽，喉嚨痛。 Leçon 13 Quelle heure est-il ? 現在是幾點 ? 2 Leçon 14 Je voudrais un rendez-vous... 我想預約... 3 Leçon 15 Qu’est-ce que tu as fait hier ? 你昨天做了什麼 ? 4 Leçon 16 Une famille de toutes les couleurs. 有各種膚⾊的家庭。 5 Leçon 17 Après le bac... ⾼中畢業之後... 6 Congé 中秋節 7 Leçon 18 Ici et là ! 這兒和那兒 ! 8 Examen à mi-parcours 期中考 (Oral+Ecrit 課⽂朗誦+筆試) 9 Leçon 19 On part au soleil ? 我們去有太陽的地⽅吧 ? 10 Leçon 20 C’est la rentrée. 開學了。 11 Leçon 21 C’était un homme très élégant... 他是⼀位非常優雅的男⼈… 12 Leçon 22 C’était il y a longtemps... 那是很久以前的事了… 13 Leçon 23 Il est devenu célèbre ! 他成名了！ 14 Leçon 24 Faits divers 社會新聞 15 Révision 複習 16 Examen final 期末考 (Oral+Ecrit 課⽂朗誦+筆試) 以上進度為參考, 教師可視學⽣學習狀況適時調整。 2 六、成績考核(Evaluation) 課堂表現 40% /期中、期末考 40% /作業 20% ; 出席率列⼊評分考量 七、本課程無涉及AI使用 Not applicable ⼋、可連結之網頁位址 eeclass 學習平台

docs.name: 浪漫主義文學
docs.text: Romantic Literature Fall 2025 Instructor: Huang-hua Chen chenhh@mx.nthu.edu.tw Office/Hour: HSS A413 Monday 12:00-1:00 Course Description: In this course, we will survey important British literary works from the late eighteenth century to the early nineteenth century to explore what it means to be “romantic”. We will begin by tracing the root of the Romanticism in the cult of sensibility and the Gothic to form a greater understanding of the unbounded romantic feeling. At the same time, we will also study the lingering impacts of the contemporary revolutions to see how the Romantic poets respond to the questions of freedom, humanity, and divinity. Required Texts: The Norton Anthology of English Literature, vol. 2, 10th Edition, ed. Stephen Greenblatt, et al. Grading: Group Discussions 20% Pop Quizzes 10% Group Presentation 10% Midterm 30% Final Group Project 30 % Class Policies: As we begin each class, we will ask students to share their opinions and questions one by one. Every week we will use the last hour of the class for class discussions. docs.text: NTHU Fall 2025 Foreign Languages and Literature Course syllabus Shakespeare 莎士比亞 In this course, we will study a series of major plays of Shakespeare that cover the dramatic genres of the Shakespearean corpus. We will begin our course with the study of romance in The Tempest, move on to a further probing of love, family, identity, and power in a problem play, The Merchant of Venice, to As You Like It, a major comedy, and then on to the tragedies, Julius Caesar, Hamlet, and Macbeth. The course ends with a discussion of major history plays that represent Shakespeare’s own interpretation of English history: Richard II, 1 Henry IV, and Henry V. The approach we take to the study of Shakespeare in this course emphasizes literary form and historical contexts. Reading and analyzing these plays in terms of generic development and the playwright’s engagement with the events and major issues and debates of his time, we will examine these plays in terms of their connection to contemporary situations and historical developments. The way power relations and the social order are enacted on Shakespeare’s stage expresses his vision of the dynamic between theater and reality. Our discussion of the plays will focus on Shakespeare’s conceptualization of historical condition and the socio-political dynamic of lived reality. We will investigate the playwright’s engagement with politics and culture in the world of drama, and practice Shakespearean criticism with an awareness of the playwright’s modernity and relevance to recent history, from his concerns with the nature of colonial power, identity and the other, gender relations, to authority and legitimacy. Do not include the instructor’s email in any mass email or email list, and do not forward any email of personal interest to your instructor. If you wish to share with me your personal interest in any extra-curricular programs or any charitable, social, or political cause, feel free to speak to me after class or during my office hours. Ed. Stephen Greenblatt, et al. 3rd ed. (2015). Assessment: The following are the conditions you must fulfill to earn a passing grade in this course: • Statement of academic honesty and integrity 5% • Attendance and class participation 25% • Discussion Forum postings 5% • Papers 50% • Final exam 15% In order to pass the course, you must fulfill all of the above requirements. If you omit any of the above, you will automatically fail the course. No make-up is available for any of the above in this course. N.B. Even though your instructor has taught this course before, the material for the course is updated and may not reflect the material for the same course from previous years. Your instructor does not consult the testing material from previous years when she makes up the tests for this course. While the format for the tests in this course may resemble the format of tests from past years and other courses, the questions and material for the tests this semester are made up entirely afresh. 沒有考古題。 AI policy: Conditionally open for specific assignments Use of generative AI to prepare specific Discussion Forum postings and papers is permitted and required. For all other assignments, the use of AI to prepare and complete coursework submitted for credit and/or evaluation, including the final exam, is not permitted and will likely result in a failing grade or an outright “0” for the exam or assignment. Suspected AI use where it is prohibited will be penalized in grade. **Academic honor Academic honor is vital to sound learning and study on all levels of the university for both professors and students. Plagiarism is a violation of academic honor, and anyone caught cheating or committing plagiarism in any work submitted for grade evaluation for this course will receive a “0” (letter grade “X”) for the entire course. The department’s plagiarism statement and the instructor’s information on plagiarism and academic honor are available to you on eLearn for this course. Read, view, and study all material on plagiarism and academic honor on eLearn carefully and ask your instructor any questions you may have about the content of these files. Besides outright failure of final grade for cheating and plagiarism, other violations of academic honor (including but not limited to lying, bullying, harassment, or the use of disrespectful language in the course and/or in a setting pertaining to the course, online or in person) will earn a “0” grade for class participation and severe penalties in final grade. No make-up is available for any work that is guilty of plagiarism or other violations of academic honor. Policy on required academic work for this course • All required academic work for this course (including the statement on academic honesty and integrity) must be completed by dates specified on the syllabus. No late statement of academic honesty and integrity will be accepted. No makeup for the final exam is available in this course. docs.text: National Tsing Hua University College of Humanities and Social Sciences Syllabus 11410FL 308700 English-Chinese Translation Practice Fall 2025 Instructor: Chen, Kuo-Hua Thursday, 1:20 PM - 3:10 PM chenkuohua@mx.nthu.edu.tw Course Description This course aims to provide students with a practical foundation in English-Chinese translation. Through a combination of lectures, discussions, and translation exercises, students will acquire the knowledge and skills necessary to effectively convey meaning and style between the two languages. As an introductory course in translation, the focus will be on translating from English to Chinese. The course will cover a range of topics related to translation, including syntax, semantics, cultural references, and idiomatic expressions. The course content will encompass an overview of fundamental translation concepts, a comparative analysis of Chinese and English, and a methodology section that addresses linguistic and cultural factors involved in language transfer. Course Objectives Students are expected to enhance skills of news translation through the course, to become news translators in the future. Upon successful completion of the course, the students will be able to: 1) Become familiar with the issues and challenges in translating English news stories. 2) Apply their translation skills to develop the concept of trans-editing. 3) Understand the process of journalistic translation in various news media. 4) Discover errors and problems found in the journalistic English translation. 5) Develop ability to collect and search information from diverse resources. Textbook & References There will be no textbook required for this course, but the following books are recommended should you feel a text would be helpful. 英中筆譯 1：基礎翻譯理論與技巧(廖柏森，眾文) 中英翻譯:對比分析法 (吳潛誠，文鶴) 英漢比較與翻譯(陳安定，書林) 筆譯精華（修訂版）(賴翠玲，文鶴) 新編譯藝譚 (黃邦傑，書林) Grading Policy 15% Exercises 35% Participation 50% Assignments Participation It is vital to participate in classroom activities, such as answering teacher’s oral questions promptly and acquire extra points counted to your final grade. Students are requested to focus properly on course content and classroom interaction. However, laptops, smartphones, tablet computers are permitted and encouraged in class to do note-taking or search for specific information. Students are even required to use an APP to submit their in-class translation exercises. Assignments Translation practice will be done constantly throughout the course, including timed in-class translation exercises and 6 assignments. Promptness in submitting assignments is required. Late submission is not acceptable. Failure to submit assignment on time will result in the deduction of final grade. In accordance with the published Guidelines for Collaboration, Co-learning, and Cultivation of Artificial Intelligence Competencies in University Education, this course adopts the following policy：Conditionally open In the context of translation assignments, students are encouraged to incorporate AI tools to enhance the quality of their translations. Detailed guidelines pertaining to the use of AI tools in these assignments will be communicated and provided throughout the course. By utilizing AI technologies, students can improve their translation output and develop a deeper understanding of the translation process.

docs.text: FALL 2025 INTRODUCTION TO PSYCHOLINGUISTICS _______________________________________________________________________________ Instructor: 蘇怡如 (I-Ru Su) Office: A528 Meeting Time: Tuesday 3:30-6:20 pm Email: irusu@mx.nthu.edu.tw Classroom: C406 Office hours: Monday 3-5 pm Or by appointment _______________________________________________________________________________ Course Description: This course is a general introduction to psycholinguistics. It covers areas such as speech perception, word recognition, lexical ambiguity, sentence comprehension, sentence production, language and thought, and neurolinguistics. We'll look at how language behavior illuminates our understanding of the mind and the brain, and how properties of the mind and brain influence human language. You will learn something about the nature of language, how it is used, and how it can be impaired. 此科目對應之系所課程規畫所欲培養之核心能力： Core capability to be cultivated by this course :  問題發掘與研究能力 (60%) The ability to look for problems and conduct research (including conducting linguistic analysis through scientific methods)  創作與創新能力 (20%) The ability to think creatively  全球化與國際視野及多元文化認知能力 (20%) The ability to examine issues through global and multicultural perspectives Course Text: No textbook is required. The articles to be read are taken from the following books. A packet of articles will be ready for students to purchase at a copy center near the university.  David Carroll (2004). Psychology of Language (4th ed.). Thomson Wadsworth.  Jean Berko-Gleason & Nan Bernstein Ratner (1998). Psycholinguistics (2nd ed.) Earl McPeek.  Danny Steinberg, Hiroshi Nagata, & David Aline (2001). Psycholinguistics: Language, Mind and World (2nd ed.). Pearson Education Limited. Recommended outside readings on the subject:  Jean Aitchison (2008). The Articulate Mammal: An Introduction to Psycholinguistics (5th ed.) Routledge Publisher.  Terry Altmann (1997). The Ascent of Babel: An Exploration of Language, Mind and Understanding. Oxford University Press. Evaluation: Class reflective notes 20% Speech production project 10% Mid-term exam 35% Final exam 35%  Attendance policy: You are allowed to have three absences (including sick leave, funeral leave, business leave, any kind.) You will fail the course if more than three absences are recorded. You should also come to class on time. Frequent late appearances will result in the deduction of points.  Class reflection: You are required to write a one- to two-page reflective note for each lecture. In the note, you should first briefly summarize the lecture, and then write a reflection about what you learn from the lecture. You can relate what you’ve learned to your personal experience, raise questions, or do some more research on the internet about a particular issue addressed in the lecture. The summary-reflection essay should be typed in font size 12, Times New Roman, single spaced.  Being absent is NOT an excuse for not turning in the assignment on time. If you miss a class, you should check with your classmates whether there is an assignment due the following week. No late submission of homework will be accepted. Course information 課程代碼 Course Number 11410FL 327300 課程名稱 Title in Chinese 日語聽解 (一) 課程英文名稱 Title in English Japanese Listening (I) 全/半年 Two/one semester 全年 必/選修/通識 Required/ Elective/ General Education 選修 總學分數 Credits 2.0 每週上課時數/ 教室 Lecturing hours/ classroom 週一 M56 (13:20-15:10) / 人社院 C407 開課系所 Class standing 外語系 授課教師 Instructor 簡嘉菁 kankasei88@gmail.com 先修課程 Prerequisites 1. 建議修畢中級日語(二)或熟悉日語動詞活用變化與相關句型者 2. 因應下學期的教學進度, 建議同時選修高級日語（一） 3. 本課程進度較快，需在課外自行多加練習。請謹慎考量學習狀況不接受二退。 4. 以日語為母語者不能選修。外籍生請具備中文能力。 關鍵字 Keywords 日語 Japanese, 聽力 listening, 會話 conversation 課程簡介 Course Description 1. 教學目標：培養學生具有中級程度以上的日語聽解能力。透過討論、聽力練習 與會話演練來培養溝通表達能力。提升至日語 JLPT N5-N4 實力。 2. 指定教科書：上學期《大家的日本語初級 II 聽解タスク 25（改訂版）》、下 學期《大家的日本語進階 I 聽解タスク 25（改訂版）》。請自備課本。 3. 教學進度：搭配校內中高級日語的學習教材，採用同系列的聽力課本。以指定 教科書為主，輔以日語能力檢定的聽解內容。上學期進度《大家的日本 語初級 II 聽解タスク 25》第 13-25 課＋日檢 JLPT N5 聽解; 下學期進 度《大家的日本語進階 I 聽解タスク 25》第 26-35 課＋日檢 JLPT N4 聽 解。 4. 課程說明：上課方式主要分為「授課」(老師補充詞彙句型)、「發表」(學生上 台報告 JLPT 聽解問題或指定教科書句型)、「聽解」(播放教科書與參考 資料 CD 做聽力與對話練習)。利用指定教科書與網路視聽教材的聽力 練習，輔以平時作業(日檢聽力)的寫作練習，培養日語的聽解、對話能 力。課程中適時加入相關日語句型的日語歌曲或新聞日文，以期有效應 用本學期所學習的內容。 5. 成績考核：期中考（35%）、期末考（35%）、作業（20%）、出席（10%） 備註：教學方法、評量方式、參考書目、教學網頁、AI 使用規則等請參考課綱 附檔。第一週將詳細說明。 注意事項 Please note 注意事項： (1) 除特殊狀況，不開放加簽或申請二退（需當面晤談。未經同意，不審核二退的 電子簽單）。申請旁聽者請事先來信聯絡。 (2) 部分專有名詞與內容將以中文介紹。 114-1 NTHU 日語聽解 課程綱要 M56 簡嘉菁 2 (3) 詳細教學方法、評量方式、參考書目、教學網頁等將在第一週說明。 (4) 關於 AI 使用規則：有條件開放. 基於透明與負責任的原則，本課程可以利用 AI 進行查詢，以提升本門課品質。但是本課程的個人報告或分組報告中, 不 得使用生成 AI 工具撰寫報告. 若經查核使用卻未在作業或報告中標明，教 師、學校或相關單位有權重新針對作業或報告重新評分或不予計分。 (5) 出席: 重要考試或個人上台報告日，都必須出席。請假時請利用學校請假系 統的上網登記。除了緊急重大意外，請假時都必須在上課前完成請假。如果 是公假、喪假、病假、婚假、赴日（來回機票證明，一學期最多申請 2 次， 1 次一週為上限）需附上相關證明單。不需要再給紙本請假單。詳細規定請參 考學校請假系統通知。缺課達五週以上（或 1/4）不給予學期成績。 課程目標 Course Outcomes 此科目對應之系所課程規畫所欲培養之核心能力 Core capability to be cultivated by this course 1 培養扎實日語表達能力 溝通表達與語文能力、創作與創新能力 2 理解日本社會與文化 問題發掘與研究能力 3 透過與日本的比較, 提高對台灣的關心 全球化與國際視野及多元文化認知能力 二、教學大綱 II. 聽解內容（2 次、請需附上日語假名拼音與相關翻譯(英文或中文)). 出席(10%): 請假需附上相關證明單與填寫假單 三、教學方法、評量方式、指定書目與參考書目等 教學方法 lecturing methodologies 方式 methods 說明 notes o 講述法 formal lecture 由教師引導發音･單字･句型練習。 授課內容以教科書為主,講義與線上網路報導為輔。 o 討論法 group discussion 由學生分組討論,共同解決發表的課題 o 合作學習 cooperative learning 分組口頭會話發表 o 媒體融入教學 media, audio, visual materials 使用電腦或多媒體播放相關日文,練習日語聽力與閱讀 o 專題研究 case studies 日語報告或詞彙整理等 評量方式 assessment methodologies:有 “等級制” 和 “百分制” 備註 notes: (1) 請掌握學習狀況,勿在考後要求補寫報告、調整成績等。 (2) 公佈成績:小考約 2 週後、期中考約 4 週後、學期成績約 2-3 週後。 (3) 可能會申請二退或應屆畢業生請留意成績出爐時間,再決定是否選課。 方式 methods 百 分 比 percentage 說明 notes o 期中考試 o 期末考試 midterm/ final docs.text: 1/3 【中級韓語一】課程教學大綱 課程資訊 (Course Information) 科號 Course Number 學分 Credit 3 人數限制 Class Size 中文名稱 Course Title 中級韓語一 英文名稱 Course English Title Intermediate Korean I 任課教師 Instructor 李伶美 (Lee Yeongmi) 上課時間 Time F678 上課教室 Room 先修課程 Prerequisites 「初級韓語一」、「初級韓語二」 建議有修過「初級韓語一、二」或者具備韓文課時數達「96 小時」左右。 此科目對應之 系所課程規畫 所欲培養之核 心能力 Core capability to be cultivated by this course ■ 溝通表達與語文能力 (70%) The ability to communicate and express oneself in the English/a foreign language. (70%) □ 文學經典的分析與詮釋 The ability to analyze classic canons of literature. ■ 問題發掘與研究能力 (10%) The ability to look for problems and conduct research (including conducting linguistic analysis through scientific methods) (10%) □ 創作與創新能力 The ability to think creatively ■ 全球化與國際視野及多元文化認知能力 (20%) The ability to examine issues through global and multicultural perspectives (20%) 課程簡述 (Brief course description) 本課程通過充分運用中級詞彙及所學的文法，進一步提升學生聽、講、讀、寫的能力。本課程同 時著重加強口語訓練，讓學生能使用韓語進行簡短發表。主要課題包括打電話約時間、說明計 畫、介紹烹飪方式、聚會邀請和詢問交通工具及問路等。 課程大綱 (Syllabus) 一、課程目標 (Course Outcomes) 1. 能夠讓學生熟悉正確的韓語發音以及書寫方式，建立韓語學習的基礎。 2. 理解並且熟悉以個人主題所構成的對話。 3. 培養使用公共設施施和維持社會關係時所需的溝通能力。 4. 理解日常生活或社會現象中複雜的內容。 2/3 5. 學習韓語自然的發音，以及分辨随著句子意義的不同而改變的聲調。正確理解演講內容， 並且有效率地表達自己的想法。 二、教材 1. 指定書目 (Text Books)：《延世大學 韓國語1 (課本及 Workbook)》台北：聯經出版公司。 《延世大學 韓國語2 (課本及 Workbook)》台北：聯經出版公司。 2. 參考書目 (References)：《我的第一本韓語文法》新北市：國際學村。 3. 韓文學習網站 (web page) (1) https://dict.naver.com/ (Naver 詞典) (2) https://dic.daum.net/index.do (Daum 詞典) 三、教學方式 (Teaching Method) 1. 由教師引導發音、單字練習。 2. 講解韓文之中級程度的詞彙、文法與句型。 3. 練習學習有關相關主題的實用會話。 表達方法 4. 不定時小考及作業、上課參與。 四、成績考核 (Evaluation) 1. 期中考試：35% 2. 期末考試：35% 3. 平時成績(包含小考及作業，上課參與情形，出席率及上課態度等)：30% 小考不開放補考（公假不在此限，但須於次週補考完成），上課參與不開放補參與!! 五、上課規範 (classroom rules) 1. 第一堂課不建議缺席！ 2. 準時到課，不建議提早離開，早退必須跟老師說一聲。 3. 不克出席上課須事先請假。 1. 缺課者必須主動向到課同學詢問當天的上課內容與作業，並且自行跟上進度。 2. 務必有教材以及抄寫筆記。 3. 參與課程所進行的活動。 4. 準時繳交作業(如需補交，請於一星期之內完成)。 5. 課程未達 2/3 出席者，會「被當」。 6. 爲了上課品質，不開放旁聽生。 7. 限非韓籍生修習。 六、教學進度 (Syllabus) ※每週課程進度可能視實際上課情況調整 週次 日期 教學內容 第 1 週 2025/9/5 課程介紹 第一堂課非常重要，不建議缺席！ 課程進度： 3/3 8-1 전화번호 좀 가르쳐 주세요 8-2 정민철 씨 계세요? 第 2 週 2025/9/12 課程進度： 8-3 늦으면 전화할게요 8-4 웨이 씨 좀 바꿔 주세요 第 3 週 2025/9/19 課程進度： 8-5 ①약속 취소 ②한국어와 전화 第 4 週 2025/9/26 課程進度： 9-1 저는 스키를 탈 수 있는 계절이 좋아요 9-2 날씨가 조금 흐린데요 第 5 週 2025/10/3 課本進度： 9-3 오늘보다 따뜻할 것 같아요 第 6 週 2025/10/10 國慶日 課本進度： 9-4 저기에서 사람들이 운동을 하고 있어요 第 7 週 2025/10/17 課本進度： 9-5 ①계절 ②일기 예보 第 8 週 2025/10/24 期中考試 第 9 週 2025/10/31 課本進度： 10-1 설악산에 가려고 해요 10-2 시간이 있을 때는 여행을 가요 第 10 週 2025/11/7 課本進度： 10-3 극장에 자주 못 가요 10-4 산책을 하고 집에서 쉬었어요 第 11 週 2025/11/14 課本進度： 10-5 ①부산 여행 ②엽서 第 12 週 2025/11/21 課本進度： 《延世大學 韓國語 2》 1-1 도움이 필요하면 언제든지 말씀하세요 1-2 이 회사에서 일한 지 얼마나 되셨습니까? 第 13 週 2025/11/28 課本進度： 《延世大學 韓國語 2》 1-3 이젠 한국 생활에 많이 익숙해졌습니다 第 14 週 2025/12/5 課本進度： 《延世大學 韓國語 2》 1-4 가족도 만나고 친구들도 만나서 좋았겠군요 第 15 週 2025/12/12 課本進度： 《延世大學 韓國語 2》 1-5 ①아름다운 우리 학교 ②소중한 물건 第 16 週 2025/12/19 期末考試

docs.text: COURSE SYLLABUS National Tsing Hua University English for Oral Business Communication Fall 2025 Instructor: I-Tsen Huang Email: itsen1213@gmail.com Course Description The course aims to sharpen students’ verbal communication skills and is designed to arm students with the language they need to speak professionally in a business environment. Engaged in various workplace role-play scenarios, students use language functions presented in class to resolve conflicts, handle delicate issues, demonstrate respectful listening, make polite requests, give advice, solve problems, tackle business dilemmas, participate in meetings, negotiate, make decisions, promote products, and pitch ideas. Office hours by appointment only Tuesday 13:00 - 15:15 Required course materials The course materials are available in each of the weekly folder on the eLearn learning platform. Students are required to access the files and print them out. Grading policies I. Attendance – 10% a. Each late arrival will result in a 2-point deduction of the semester grade. b. Each unexcused absence will result in a 5-point deduction of the semester grade. c. Students are required to email the instructor to request a leave of absence. d. Two unexcused absences will result in a failing grade. e. A total of three absences will result in a failing grade. f. Missing 15 minutes of class—arriving late, departing early, or leaving during class—counts as half an absence. II. Participation: In-class oral contributions – 10% Digital devices such as laptops, tablets, and mobile phones are not allowed in class. III. Assignments (vocabulary and listening) – 40% Please note that late submissions will not be graded. IV. Speaking tasks and presentations – 40% Information about assignments and classroom activities ⚫ An excused absence does not negate the student’s responsibility for assignments due during his or her period of absence. Students are obligated to email any due assignments to the instructor before the deadline. ⚫ Success in this class depends on regular and punctual attendance, active participation in class, and completion of assigned textbook exercises. Weekly schedule Week Date Topic 1 9/2 Making requests 2 9/9 Agreeing and disagreeing 3 9/16 Active listening 4 9/23 Diplomatic language 5 9/30 Handling difficult communicators 6 10/7 Marketing strategies 7 10/14 Responding to compliments 8 10/21 Indirectness 9 10/28 Carrying out a needs analysis 10 11/4 Negotiating skills 11 11/11 Saying ‘no’ firmly and politely 12 11/18 Giving feedback on performance 13 11/25 Mediating 14 12/2 Giving advice 15 12/9 Networking 16 12/16 Presentations

docs.nameEn: English Language Skills with Harry Potter
docs.text: Language Skills with Harry Potter Dr. Katchen TIME: Mon. 1:20 – 3:10 katchen@mx.nthu.edu.tw HSS C412 Rationale: The Harry Potter books have been extremely popular all over the world, including with young people in Taiwan. It is also known that the use of material of interest to students increases their motivation to learn. For these reasons, and because the teacher likes them, the Harry Potter books and films are used for this course. Objectives: To advance students abilities in Reading, Writing, Speaking, and Listening. To expand students’ vocabulary in English. To increase students’ knowledge of British and English-speaking cultures. Prerequisite: This course is aimed at students with a relatively high level of English ability equal to the level of the students in the Department of Foreign Languages and Literature. Many students of other departments do meet these standards and they are welcome to take this course. If you do not feel your level of English is comparable to that of FLLD students or higher, then this course is not for you and you will not do well in this course. Required Materials: Harry Potter and the Philosopher’s Stone (the first book in English). Supplemental Materials: All seven Harry Potter books, all eight DVDs. Before taking the course, students should have either read all seven books (either in English or your first language) or watched all the films because the vocabulary lectures and the essays will be based on all the materials. However, more time will be spent on the first book/video. Materials we will use in class, such as PowerPoint slides, will be uploaded to our class e- learning site (eLearn). For videos, the URL is provided. Your role plays and group reports will be videoed and you will be able to view them on eLearn. Procedure: Some of the time, your teacher will bring to class material to listen to and sheets with comprehension questions to answer or to fill in the blanks. We will also spend a lot of time looking at the vocabulary and cultural background from excerpts of the books and videos. You will have to discuss what you read in Book 1 (Harry Potter and the Philosopher’s Stone) and see on the videos. You will create role plays and give oral reports and also write two out-of-class essays based on ideas taken from the books. All these materials and activities were made for native speakers, so your listening and speaking skills will be challenged, but I think you’ll have fun, too. NOTE: If we do not have enough class time to go through all the lectures in 16 weeks, you can access all the lectures on eLearn. They are the PowerPoint slides with audio. You can also use them for review before exams. Grading: You should be present and should participate every week. Whenever we have activities in class, your participation will be evaluated. The assigned activities, such as reports, role plays, essays, and quizzes, will, of course, receive definite grades. Quizzes will be based on listening to an excerpt of a scene from one of the films (comprehension questions or fill in a cloze). If you come and participate and complete the assignments adequately, you should be able to pass the course. Midterm Exam 25% Final Exam 25% Two Listening Quizzes, 5% each Two Role Plays, 5% each One Group Report, 10% Two Outside Essays, 10% each Attendance: I expect to see an official excuse for missing a class. You must appear for the midterm and final unless you have an official serious excuse (in hospital, death in the family, or another important reason). If you miss a listening quiz without an official excuse, you will get 0 for the quiz. The role plays and the group report can be made up in the following class. Use of A1: The two out-of-class essays should be based on your own ideas. The topics are worded so that you MUST use examples from your own experience! If you use added materials to back up or to supplement your ideas, please add the reference(s) at the end of your essay. For the group reports, you will have to do some outside research. Please add the references/ URLs within or at the end of your ppt files. Calendar NOTE: We will attempt to follow this calendar, but sometimes we may get a little behind or even a little ahead. Unless something unusual happens, the activities will not change. Week 1 Introduction to the course (read syllabus); About teacher; Some general questions about Harry Potter; Lecture 1 Harry’s family; Lecture 2 places. Homework: Read Stone 1-5; Watch accompanying Video clips. Week 2 Lecture 3 Required Textbooks; Lecture 4 Weasley Family; Lecture 5 Classmates; Lecture 6 Hogwarts Places. Homework: Read Stone 6-10; Watch accompanying Video clips; Out of Class: Listen to J.K. Rowling interview (link on e-learn, also transcript and key questions). Week 3 Discuss Chapters 1-5; Lecture 7, Hogwarts Professors; Lecture 8 Creatures; Lectures 9 Objects. Homework: Read Stone 11-14, Watch videos. Give out role plays. Week 4 Student Role Plays (5%); Discuss Chapters 6-10. Week 5 Discuss Chapters 11-14. Read Chapters 15-17 and watch videos. Week 6 Listening Quiz 1 (5%); Lecture 10 English Names. Lecture 11; History of English Vocabulary. Homework: Essay 1 due Week 9 (10%). Week 7 Discuss Chapters 15-17. Preparation for Midterm. Week 8 MIDTERM (25%). Week 9 Lectures 12 and 13 on Chamber; Lecture 14 on Prisoner. Do at Home: Listen to A History of Magic (link and key questions on e-learn). Week 10 Student Group Reports (10%). Week 11 Finish Group Reports. Week 12 Lecture 15 on Prisoner; Lectures 16, 17 on Goblet. Week 13 Listening Quiz 2 (5%); Lecture 18 on Phoenix. Week 14 Lecture 19 on Phoenix; Lectures 20, 21 on Prince; Hallows. Week 15 Student Role Plays (5%). Week 16 FINAL (25%). Essay 2 due at a later date (10%). Stone = Harry Potter and the Philosopher’s/Sorcerer’s Stone Chamber = Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets Prisoner = Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban Goblet = Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire Phoenix = Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix Prince = Harry Potter and the Half-blood Prince Hallows = Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows

docs.text: COURSE SYLLABUS National Tsing Hua University Journalistic English Fall 2025 Instructor: I-Tsen Huang Email: itsen1213@gmail.com Course Description The course is designed to introduce students to the characteristics and conventions of journalistic writing. Great emphasis is placed on honing reading and language skills that students need most in comprehending news reports and articles in English. Training in key vocabulary skills and knowledge includes connotations, loanwords, metaphors, allusions, and idioms. Training in reading is aimed at inferring word meaning from context, identifying contextual clues, and grasping main ideas. A selection of texts will be used to sharpen students’ abilities to detect hidden bias and to raise students’ awareness of cohesive and discourse features that tie a text together. Course Objectives 1. Learn and practice the fundamentals of news writing 2. Understand headlines through contextual clues 3. Infer meanings and learn new words through context 4. Analyze the content and viewpoint of a text 5. Recognize and practice rhetorical devices Office hours by appointment only Thursday 13:00 - 15:15 Required course materials The course materials are available in each of the weekly folder on the eLearn learning platform. Students are required to access the files and print them out. Grading policies 1. Attendance and coursework – 10% a. Success in this class depends on regular and punctual attendance. Each late arrival will result in a 2-point deduction of the semester grade. b. Each unexcused absence will result in a 5-point deduction of the semester grade. c. Students are required to email the instructor to request a leave of absence. The grant of a leave of absence is within the discretion of the instructor. d. Two unexcused absences will result in a failing grade. A total of four absences will result in a failing grade. e. Missing 15 minutes of class—arriving late, departing early, or leaving during class—counts as half an absence. 2. Midterm exam (Journalese, headline grammar, diplomacy, and wars) – 20% 3. Assignments (vocabulary, reading, and listening) – 25% 4. Headline and news writing – 20% ✓ Headline grammar ✓ Journalese ✓ Wordplay and 5W1H questions 5. Newscast project – 15% 6. Headlines in The Economist – 10% ⚫ Information about assignments and classroom activities 1. Please note that late submissions will not be graded. 2. An excused absence does not negate the student’s responsibility for classroom activities or assignments due during his or her period of absence. Students are obligated to email any due assignments to the instructor before the deadline. Course information 課程代碼 Course Number 11410FL 421100 課程名稱 Title in Chinese 商用日語 課程英文名稱 Title in English Business Japanese 全/半年 Two/one semester 半年 必/選修/通識 Required/ Elective/ General Education 選修 總學分數 Credits 2 每週上課時數/ 教室 Lecturing hours/ classroom 週一 M34 (10:10-12:00) 人社院 C412 開課系所 Class standing 外語系 授課教師 Instructor(s) 簡嘉菁 kankasei88@gmail.com 先修課程 Prerequisites 1. 具備 JLPT Ｎ4 以上或修畢高級日語 (約「大家的日本語」50 課) 程度 2. 推薦選修下學期「新聞日語」課程（加強專有術語） 3. 本課程進度較快，需自行多加練習。請謹慎考量學習狀況不接受二退。 4. 以日語為母語者不能選修。外籍生請具備中文能力。 關鍵字 Keywords 日語 Japanese, 商用禮儀 business manner, 敬語 honorific, 商用文書 business document, 致電＆接電話 telephone, 訪問&接待 reception 等各種主題 課程簡介 Course Description 1. 教學目標：教授日語商務禮儀、慣用表現等相關會話。透過討論與演練來培 養溝通表達能力。提升日語 JLPT N3~N1 實力。 2. 指定教科書：《30 小時快速學習職場日本語》台北：大新書局。 3. 教學進度：以指定教科書為主，輔以自編商務日語教材與網路教學影片等。 4. 課程說明：內容涵蓋日本職場中常用的尊敬語・謙讓語等敬語、自我介紹、 社外・社內商用文書、撥打電話、接聽電話與相關會話、訪問禮儀、接 待禮儀、面試技巧、服裝儀容等相關商務內容。透過上台發表與會話演 練，來培養升學或就業時候所需的面試技巧與商務技能。教學方式將由 教師引導專業術語、慣用句或商務背景知識的學習。透過相互會話練習 以及上台發表，讓學生加強商用日語的熟練度。 5. 成績考核：期中考（35%）、期末考（35%）、上台報告（10%）、作業（10%）、 出席（10%） 註：教學方法、評量方式、參考書目、教學網頁、AI 使用規則等請參考課綱 附檔。第一週將詳細說明。 注意事項 Please note 注意事項： (1) 除特殊狀況，不開放加簽或申請二退（需當面晤談。未經同意，不審核二 退的電子簽單）。申請旁聽者請事先來信聯絡。 (3) 部分專有名詞與內容將以中文介紹。 (4) 詳細教學方法、評量方式、參考書目、教學網頁等將在第一週說明。 (5) 關於 AI 使用規則：有條件開放. 基於透明與負責任的原則，本課程可以利 用 AI 進行查詢，以提升本門課品質。但是本課程的個人報告或分組報告 中, 不得使用生成 AI 工具撰寫報告. 若經查核使用卻未在作業或報告中標 明，教師、學校或相關單位有權重新針對作業或報告重新評分或不予計分。 (6) 出席: 重要考試或個人上台報告日，都必須出席。請假時請利用學校請 假系統的上網登記。除了緊急重大意外，請假時都必須在上課前完成請 114-1 NTHU 商用日語 課程綱要 M34 簡嘉菁 假。如果是公假、喪假、病假、婚假、赴日（來回機票證明，一學期最 多申請 2 次，1 次一週為上限）需附上相關證明單。不需要再給紙本請假 單。詳細規定請參考學校請假系統通知。缺課達五週以上（或 1/4）不給 予學期成績。 課程目標 Course Outcomes 此科目對應之系所課程規畫所欲培養之核心能力 Core capability to be cultivated by this course 1 培養扎實日語表達能力 溝通表達與語文能力、創作與創新能力 2 理解日本社會與文化 問題發掘與研究能力 3 透過與日本的比較, 提高對台灣的關心 全球化與國際視野及多元文化認知能力 二、教學大綱 II. 聽力:是非･選擇･問答// 筆試:詞彙･句型･問答･翻譯 (中日) 等 114-1 NTHU 商用日語 課程綱要 M34 簡嘉菁 上台報告(10%) 依照選課學生的程度與人數，決定分組報告(課本相關內容)或個人報告(日語 模擬面試). 作業(10%): 商用日語相關詞彙 50 字. 請需附上日語例句假名拼音與相關翻譯(英文或中文). 出席(10%): 請假需附上相關證明單與填寫假單。 三、教學方法、評量方式、指定書目與參考書目等 教學方法 lecturing methodologies 方式 methods 說明 notes o 講述法 formal lecture 由教師引導發音･單字･相關常套句型練習。 授課內容以教科書為主, 講義與線上網路報 導為輔。 o 討論法 group discussion 由學生分組討論,共同解決發表的課題 o 合作學習 cooperative learning 分組口頭會話發表 o 媒體融入教學 media, audio, visual materials 使用電腦或多媒體播放相關日文,練習日語聽 力與閱讀 o 專題研究 case studies 日語報告或詞彙整理等 評量方法 assessment methodologies:有 “等級制” 和 “百分制” 備註 notes: (1) 請掌握學習狀況,勿在考後要求補寫報告、調整成績等。 (2) 公佈成績:小考約 2 週後、期中考約 4 週後、學期成績約 2-3 週後。 (3) 可能會申請二退或應屆畢業生請留意成績出爐時間,再決定是否選課。 方式 methods 百 分 比 percentage 說明 notes o 期中考試 o 期末考試 midterm/ final exam 35% 35% 聽力:是非･選擇･問答等 筆試:詞彙･句型･問答･翻譯(中日) 等 特殊狀況補考成績打 因為個人請假或曠課未聽到分組報告內容時，請務必字先觀看電子檔 並撰寫評量表，次週交給發表者。未提供者，將扣除個人分數。 o 作業 assignments 10% 等級制評分(請參考附錄) 說明:商用日語相關詞彙 50 字, 需附上日語例句與中文翻譯 (附上 A4 版面的紙本報告與上傳電子檔到 NTHU EECLASS) (1)日語漢字與數字都必須加上日語假名拼音。 docs.text: 國立清華大學學分磨課師課程 NTHU Credit-MOOC 申請學年度 School Year __114_____學年度第＿1＿學期 課程名稱 Course name Myths of the Mongol Empire 課程類別 Course type 人文 開課單位 Offered by 清大外語系 授課教師 Instructors 金守民 教授 課程簡介 Course introduction In this course we will be learning about the Mongol empire by looking at common myths of the Mongol empire and investigating how and why there is a gap between the representation and the historical reality of the Mongol empire. Even today accounts and representations of the Mongol empire in social media contain myths or misconceptions of the Mongols and their historical rise as a world empire. Most of the writers in history who wrote about the Mongols were not from the steppes of Inner Asia and had little sympathy for them. Nor did non- Mongol writers understand the nomads’ way of life. The popular images of the Mongols in social media often can be traced back to myths of the Mongols in written sources from earlier centuries. The aim of this course is to critique and analyze the myths of the Mongols, and to learn about the historical realities of the nomads and their empire beyond the myths. We will investigate the nomads’ own values, cultures, and institutions as a way to develop a sound understanding of the Mongols and their historical expansion in the thirteenth century. ⚫ Learners will learn to analyze popular myths and stories about a much misunderstand people, the Mongols, and understand the historical reality of the Mongol empire from the standpoint of the Mongols themselves. ⚫ Students of all levels from undergraduate and up may enroll in this course. By exploring the myths of the Mongol empire and how they relate to historical reality, students will learn sound historical thinking and understand the fundamental importance of human perception in historical records and materials. ⚫ Learners will learn to analyze popular perceptions and misperceptions about the Mongols and to understand the historical realities behind the myths about the Mongol empire. 學習目標 Learning objectives Learners will learn to distinguish between representation and historical reality in the case of the Mongols and to think analytically about the way popular perceptions shape and inform how human beings think about the historical past. 課程特色 Course features This course features a fun and lively exploration of the myths of the Mongol empire as projections of the human imagination. It tackles the myths about the Mongols in popular culture as a way to understand history. It requires students to examine the gap between the representation of history and the material reality that informed history. While it is a fun course that allows learners to explore Mongolian history and discuss lively popular images about the Mongol people, it also trains learners to think rigorously about historical reality and the perception of alien people such as the Mongols. By discussing and debunking myths about the Mongols, learners will develop a proper appreciation of the Mongols in the historical reality of the Inner Asian steppes and their historical expansion outside the steppes in the thirteenth century. Because it deals with popular perceptions about the Mongols, students are also encouraged to deal with the way their own perceptions shapes and informs their understanding of foreigners such as the Mongols. 教材影音總時數 Total video hours _3.6 _小時 Please note this is the length of the videos. I expect students will spend more time on the material of the videos as they will need to absorb the ideas and review the material to prepare for online discussion, polls, quiz, and report at the end of the course. 學生總學習時數 Total learning hours 約＿＿17＿＿小時 (含影音、閱讀文章、測驗、問卷、報告、互動) Approximate ____17___ Hours (The term "total learning hours" refers to the overall time required for learners to complete the course, including 7.25 hours for watching and reviewing videos, 4 hours for reading articles, 1.25 hours for participating in polls, 0.5 hours for quizzes, and 4 hours for meetings.) 適用對象 Participants This course is designed for general learners interested in the Mongol empire as a historical subject of study. The Mongol empire is a growing subject of history in both serious academic research and popular media. Yet accounts and representations of the Mongol empire in social media and online sources contain myths or misconceptions about the Mongols and their historical rise as a world empire. This course addresses and debunks common myths about the Mongol empire by examining and engaging historical sources and scholarship about the Mongols. Learners will deal with and critique misconceptions about the Mongols that they are familiar with in popular lore as a way to establish a sound conceptual foundation for the study of the Mongol empire. Besides general learners, the course may also be useful to serious academic learners who wish to pursue further studies in the fields of Mongol studies and history. 先備知識 Prerequisite knowledge General world history. Learner should know the basic facts about the Mongol empire, such as when it rose and who the most famous rulers of the Mongol empire were. 開課週數 How many weeks of delivery? ＿3＿ 週/week 學分數 Credits __1__ 學分/credits, 採通過/不通過制(不計入 GPA 計算) Pass/Fail basis and is not included in GPA calculations 評分標準 Course evaluation 討論互動 Class participation and interactive discussion with instructor ＿25＿ ＿ ％ 課程意見測驗 Polls ＿20＿ ％ 小考 Quiz ＿15＿ ％ 期末報告 Final Presentation ＿40＿ ％ 開課期程 Course start date 2025 年__12__月__8__日至 2025 年__12__月__26__日 From_12_Month, _8_ day, 2025_ Year to _12_Month, _26_ day, _2025_ Year 課程平台 Course platform FutureLearn 平台，https://www.futurelearn.com/courses/myths-of-the-mongol- empire/1 上課方式 一、課程進度： 共上線 3 次進行討論，課程影片、意見測驗、小考可自行安排時間。 二、依磨課師微學分課程之規定，上線討論 4 小時，請同 學務必記得上線並完成點名。 上線連結：https://meet.google.com/ida-jcez-tte 上線日期與時間 1、期初：課程大綱與內容說明 上線時間：12/8 星期一 20:00–21:00 Google Meet 2、期初：課程討論 上線時間：12/12 星期五 20:00–21:00 Google Meet 3、期末：期末分享與討論 上線時間：12/26 星期五 19:00–21:00 Google Meet Weekly schedule： Week Topic Assignment, Quiz/Exam or In- class interaction 12/8~12/14 The myths of the Mongol empire Instructor’s Introduction: Interactive Class 1 Welcome introduction from instructor and Q&A on Google Discussion 1.1 Article and Instructor’s Online Introduction Welcome to the course on Google Meet 1.2 Article. docs.text: Bibliography and Research Method Fall 2025 Instructor: Huang-hua Chen Office/Hour: HSS A413 Monday 12:00-1:00 This course involves drafting, revising, and editing research papers derived from reading and analyzing literary and cultural texts. It aims at introducing the challenges and potential ethical problems that young literary researchers might face in the various stages of their academic career. To this end, we will familiarize ourselves with the MLA format, the key research skills in the field of literary studies, and the professional guidelines that help us engage with our peers and researchers in the field. Students will be asked to do close reading on novellas and short stories that each deal with a specific period and eventually produce a research paper that they revise and polish for a mock conference. Grading: 5-page paper 20% 10-page final paper 30% Abstract/Annotation/Introduction/Literature Review/Methods/Analysis/Conclusion 20% In-class Presentations 20 % Class Discussions and Participations 10 % Required Texts: Taiwan Travelogue: A Novel The Great Gatsby The Sand Man Fantomina MLA Handbook 10th Edition Attendance and Class Policies: Please contact me if there is any unusual circumstance. No late paper is allowed. Plagiarism means you copy things from other people’s articles without acknowledging it. You will automatically get 0 in that particular assignment. AI-related policies will be provided in the additional handout. Reading and Class Schedule: You are required to read the material assigned for each week. Always come prepared to the class. We will ask students to provide questions to start each session. Reading Schedule: Week1 Introduction/ Research Resources Week2 Basics of Research Writings/MLA Style Abstract/Proposal Week3 Taiwan Travelogue: A Novel Week4 Taiwan Travelogue: A Novel Week5 Taiwan Travelogue: A Novel Intro/Literature Review Week6 Holiday Week7 The Great Gatsby Week8 The Great Gatsby Annotated Bibliography Week9 OED Exercise Week10 “The Uncanny” Method Week11 “Miracles of the Namiya General Store”/First Paper Due Analysis Week12 The Sand Man Week13 The Sand Man Conclusion Week 14 Fantomina Week 15 Fantomina Week 16 Mock Conference/Final Research Paper Due

docs.text: Course Name: Dystopian Literature Instructor: Yi-Chuang E. Lin Wednesday 10:10~13:10 Course Description: In this course, we will begin with a discussion of the idea of Utopia and consider its im/possibilities. Treating it as a mode of socio-political- economic criticism, we will examine the good intentions behind drive for utopian ideal, alongside the underlying forces – biological, psychological, social, or structural – that continually sabotage such an ideal. To that end, we will study our primary texts and consider them through the lens of political-economic critique, engaging with the works of Fredric Jameson, David Harvey, among others. We will explore its generic features in relation to fantasy and science fiction, analyze its popularity within historical context, and interrogate how late 19th-century fears of degeneration activates the modernist movement and its utopian drive. Towards the end, in this twenty-first century, we would further bring in a reflection on AI. Grading: Class Participation and Contribution 35%, Oral presentation 15%, Midterm Paper (2000 words) 25%, Final Paper (2500 words) 25% Notes: while both midterm and final paper must include materials we have read and. studied in class, students are encouraged to introduce works which we have not covered in our course as their oral presentation. docs.name: 文學理論
docs.text: 1 LITERARY THEORY Instructor: Chien-heng Wu COURSE DESCRIPTION This course will introduce students to major theoretical approaches as well as key contemporary issues. The overall aim is to help student develop critical strategies for engaging with literary and cultural texts, paying to both literary and extra-literary dimensions of these texts. This course is organized around specific ideas and concepts that have shaped literary studies in the 21st century. That is to say, instead of organizing the course either chronologically or into different “-isms,” this course engages with a set of related theoretical issues concerning the individual and the collective, the particular and the universal, power and resistance, difference and relationality, human and nonhuman, subject and object, etc. In general, we will work through these topics and see how they shatter the received knowledge and open up different ways of interpreting the world and the text. Rather than attempting to settle the debate among different theoretical paradigms, the aim is to help students understand core issues involved in the different permutations of a given topic. Throughout the course of our investigation, we will maintain a constant vigilance regarding the ethico-political implications of these important issues—asking not only speculative questions concerning its metaphysical underpinning but also political questions that will force us to negotiate a way between the speculative and the actual. COURSE OBJECTIVES 1. Students will gain a better grasp of contemporary cultural and critical theories. 2. Students will be able to think critically and creatively. 3. Students will demonstrate their ability to apply relevant theoretical perspectives to literary and cultural texts. GRADING • Participation: 25% • Presentation: 20% • Mid-term: 15% 2 • Final: 30% * Please apply for a free Office365 account at http://learning.cc.nthu.edu.tw/p/412-1319- 12292.php?Lang=zh-tw. After registration, please download the application Teams. I will set up a forum for online discussion and communication. GENERATIVE AI USAGE POLICY In this course, we encourage the responsible and ethical use of generative artificial intelligence (AI) tools, such as ChatGPT, to assist in the learning process. These tools can be valuable for generating ideas, providing inspiration, and enhancing your understanding of course material. However, it is crucial that students transparently indicate where and how AI-generated content has been used in their work. To promote academic integrity and ensure appropriate use of AI tools, please adhere to the following guidelines: 1. Citing AI-generated content: If you use any AI-generated content in your assignments, papers, presentations, or other course-related work, you must clearly cite the AI tool used as a source. Include the name of the AI tool, version, and date of access in your citation. For example: Generated with the assistance of ChatGPT-4, OpenAI, accessed on May 5, 2023. 2. Originality and authenticity: While incorporating AI-generated content is allowed, it should not be the sole basis for your work. You are expected to use your own thoughts, ideas, and understanding of the course material to create original and authentic work. AI- generated content should be supplementary and contribute to your overall argument or analysis. 3. Collaborative use of AI tools: If you are working on a group project or engaging in a class discussion, ensure that all group members or participants are aware of the use of AI- generated content. Discuss and evaluate the generated content together, to promote transparency and shared understanding. 4. Ethical considerations: Be mindful of the potential biases and limitations of AI-generated content. Always critically evaluate the accuracy, relevance, and ethical implications of AI- generated content before incorporating it into your work. 5. Continuous learning and reflection: Use AI-generated content as a tool to expand your knowledge and understanding of the course material, rather than as a shortcut to complete assignments. Reflect on how the AI-generated content has contributed to your learning process and consider what you have learned from the interaction. By adhering to these guidelines, you will be able to harness the power of generative AI in a responsible and ethical manner, while ensuring academic integrity and maintaining a focus on your own learning and development. * This policy is generated with the help of ChatGPT-4, accessed May 05, 2023. 3 SCHEDULE Week Schedule 1 General Introduction 2 Alex Williams and Nick Srnicek, “Manifesto for an Accelerationist Politics” & “A New Common Sense” (Inventing the Future) 3 Frédéric Neyrat, The Unconstructable Earth: An Ecology of Separation “Introduction” and Chap. 1 4 Neyrat, Chap. 5, 7 5 Neyrat, Chap. 9 and Conclusion 6 Karl Marx, “The Economic and Philosophic Manuscripts of 1844” 7 Matteo Pasquinelli, The Eye of the Master: A Social History of Artificial Intelligence, “Introduction” and Chap. 1 8 Pasquinelli, Chap. 6, 7, 8 9 Pasquinelli, Chap. 9 and Conclusion 10 Review Session 11 Yuk Hui, “For a Planetary Thinking,” “Machine and Ecology,” “On Cosmotechnics: For a Renewed Relation between Technology and Nature in the Anthropocene” 12 Yuk Hui, Machine and Sovereignty “Introduction” 13 Yuk Hui, Chap. 7 14 Presentation 15 Presentation 16 Final 4 PRE-RECORDED LECTURES 1. docs.text: 國立清華大學課程大綱 科號 Course Number 1141 OFL 532300 學分 Credit 3 人數限制 Class Size 中文名稱 Course Title 英文散文敘述：早期清教文學觀點 英文名稱 Course English Title Prose Fiction: Perspectives on Early Puritan Literature 任課教師 Instructor 紀元文 Yuanwen Chi 上課時間 Time F2F3F4 上課教室 Room HSS C511 課程簡述(必填) (最多500個中文字) 本欄位資料會上傳教育部課程網 Brief Course Description (required) (50-200 words if possible, up to 1000 letters) The topic of the seminar focuses on the institution of prose fiction in terms of religious practice, the change of mode of production, and the transformation of socio-cultural milieu in the eighteen century England. Thus, this is a study of some writers and their rapport with the rise of prose fiction per se. 課程內容「中文暨英文關鍵字」(必填) 至少5個,每個關鍵字至多20個中文,以半形逗點分隔 Please fill in at least 5 course keywords (up to 40 letters for each keyword) and use commas to separate them.(required) 散文敘述， 清教主義，莫頓，布萊德福特，狄福 ，班揚、 prose fiction, Puritanism, William Bradford, Thomas Morton, John Bunyan, Daniel Defoe, Franklin Benjamin. Defoe, Defoe, Defoe, 課程大綱(必填)Detailed Course Syllabus ● 課程說明(Course Description) The topic of the seminar focuses on the institution of prose fiction in terms of religious practice, the change of modes of production, and the transformation of socio-cultural milieu in the eighteen century England. Thus, this is a reading course designed basically for a transatlantic study of some writers and theirrapport with the rise of English prose fiction. By reading our way through selected oeuvres of these writers, we will work towards a definition of prose fiction and its multi-faceted forms of narratology. To become acquainted with a wide spectrum of the works of the long eighteenth century, we will study several Puritan writers, including Thomas Morton (1579-1646), New English Canaan (1637); William Bradford (1588-1657), History of Plymouth Plantation, 1620-1647 (1651); John Bunyan (1628-1688), The Pilgrim’s Progress (1678); Daniel Defoe (1660?-1731), Robinson Crusoe (1719); Benjamin Franklin (1706-1790), Autobiography (1771-1789). Simultaneously, we would juxtapose these works alongside with critiques on the theory of the novel from the inception of the genre to its maturity so as to work towards a view of early fiction that would give us a better view to the history of the novel. To this end, we have set the designated reading materials to include a variety of criticism and discourses on the theory of the novel, cultural studies, and philosophy. These critics play important roles in heralding paradigm change in their respective fields to some extent. These works are Louis Althusser,. “Ideology and Ideological State Apparatuses (Notes towards an Investigation)” (1969); Erich Auerbach, Mimesis: The Representation of Reality in Western Literature (1946); Mikhail Mikhailovich Bakhtin, The Dialogic Imagination (1946); Max Horkheimer and Theodor W. Adornor. “The Culture Industry: Enlightenment as Mass Deception.” (1944); Michael McKeon, The Origins of the English Novel 1600-1740; Ian Watt, The Rise of the Novel: Studies in Defoe, Richardson and Fielding (1957); Max Weber, The Protestant Ethic and the Spirit of Capitalism (1904). Although our emphasis may fall upon the arbitrary conventions, we shall also attempt to read these texts that rework the themes and situations of English society so as to develop a more sustained and critical interpretation of prose fiction. ● 指定用書(Text Books) Bradford, William. History of Plymouth Plantation, 1620-1647. New York: Knopf, 1952. Bunyan, John. The Pilgrim’s Progress. Ed. W. R. Owens. New York: Oxford University, 2008. Defoe, Daniel. Robinson Crusoe. Ed. Michael Shinagel. New York: Norton, 1994. 2nd ed. Franklin, Benjamin. Autobiography. Ed. Joyce E. Chaplin. New York and London: Norton, 2012. Morton, Thomas. New English Canaan. Scituate, MA.: Digital Scanry, 2000 ● 參考書籍(References) Althusser, Louis. “Ideology and Ideological State Apparatuses (Notes towards an Investigation).” Lenin and Philosophy and Other Essays (1969). Trans. Ben Brewster. New York and London: Monthly Review P, 1979. 127-86. Auerbach, Erich. “Odysseus’ Scar.” Mimesis: The Representation of Reality in Western Literature (1946). Trans. Willard R. Trask. Princeton: Princeton UP, 1974. 3-23. Bakhtin, Mikhail Mikhailovich. “Discourse in the Novel.” The Dialogic Imagination (1946). Trans. Caryl Emerson and Michael Holquist. Austin: University of Texas Press, 1981. Horkheimer, Max and Theodor W. Adornor. “The Culture Industry: Enlightenment as Mass Deception.” (1944) Dialectic of Enlightenment. Trans. John Cumming. New York: Continuum, 1988. 120-167. McKeon, Michael. “Parables of the Younger Son (1):Defoe and the Naturalization of Desire.” The Origins of the English Novel 1600-1740. Baltimore: Johns Hopkins University Press, 1987. 315-37. Watt, Ian. “Realism and the Novel Form.” The Rise of the Novel: Studies in Defoe, Richardson and Fielding (1957). Harmondsworth: Penguin Books, 1979. 9-37. Weber, Max. The Protestant Ethic and the Spirit of Capitalism (1904). London: Unwin University Books, 1970. ● 教學方式(Teaching Method) Lectures and discussions are the major pedagogy in the class. The instructor will lecture on the topics and issues concerning the dynamic among prose fiction, Puritan practice, and the rise of capitalism. Specifically, the relationship between the evolution of prose fiction and socio-cultural contexts has much to do with the representation of social reality in terms of religious practice, the change of mode of production, the transformation of social milieu, etc. ever since the late seventeenth and eighteenth centuries. Students are expected to read closely the designated reading materials before class and participate in class discussion so as to articulate their understanding and critiques of materials under study. Beginning from Week 5, the instructor will ask students to present topics of interest on the texts or related literary theory with PowerPoint for about 25 minutes. The student can select one of the texts or critical theory in the reading list to work for the presentation, which may serve as the basis of, and develop into, term paper. The processes of learning include studying texts and designated materials, raising questions, discussing and sharing your findings with peers. Consultation on the presentation is required; the procedure includes information on topics, methodology, writing mechanism, and academic ethic. The instructor will arrange the consultation schedule. ● 教學進度(Syllabus) Syllabus Week Readings Supplementary Readings 1 (Sep. 5) Introduction & a brief history of the English novel 2 (Sep. 12) History of Plymouth Plantation Erich Auerbach, “Odysseus’ Scar.” Mimesis: 3-23. 3 (Sep. 19) History of Plymouth Plantation Erich Auerbach, “Odysseus’ Scar.” Mimesis: 3-23. 4 (Sep. 26) New English Canaan Michael McKeon, The Origins of the English Novel:315-337 5 (Oct. 3) New English Canaan Michael McKeon, The Origins of the English Novel:315-337 6 (Oct. 17) Pilgrim’s Progress Max Weber, The Protestant Ethic, Vols. 1 & 2. 7 (Oct. 31) Pilgrim’s Progress Max Weber, The Protestant Ethic, Vols. 1 & 2. 8 (Nov. 7) Robinson Crusoe Ian Watt, The Rise of the Novel, ch. 1 & 2. 9 (Nov. 14) Robinson Crusoe Ian Watt, The Rise of the Novel, ch. 1 & 2. 10 (Nov. 21) Robinson Crusoe Mikhail Bakhtin. “Discourse in the Novel.” The Dialogic Imagination (1946) 11 (Nov. 28) Franklin’s Autobiography Louis Althusser, “Ideology and Ideological State ....” 12 (Dec. 5) Franklin’s Autobiography Louis Althusser, “Ideology and Ideological State ....” 13 (Dec. 12) Franklin’s Autobiography Horkheimer and Adornor, “The Culture Industry ...” 14 (Dec. 19) Review and Term Paper Due ● 成績考核(Evaluation) There are four assignments in this course—Account of Myself, writing of remarks on critical essay, a class presentation, and a term paper. The test of remarks writing is an exam to test the students’ understanding of basic knowledge about critical essays and writing abilities. The aim of the presentation is to discipline the students’ abilities to probe into the quintessential ideas about the social and cultural contexts of a text or related topic in this period, to report and share their findings in the class, and to get some feedback from peer reviews and discussions. All of these serve for the instructor to understand the validity of the pedagogy, to train the students’ capabilities to organize their perception of the text and some related materials, and to articulate their knowledge of the field in verbal and written forms both logically and coherently. Students who actively participate in class discussions will have some credits for their performance and have favorable consideration for their grades (GPA). 1. Active participation in class discussion and oral conversations (Questions and Answers) are required (15%). 2. Account of Myself and writing of remarks on critical essay (10%). 3. Presentation on topic of interest concerning the text or critical theory (25%) 4. Term paper (50%) Evaluation of students’ performance is based on participation in class discussions, presentation on topic of interest concerning the text or critical theory (25 minutes), and term paper (20 pages). The paper should be typed in the format of 12-point, Times New Roman font, double-spaced with 1 inch margin. Paper copy of term paper is due on Week 13 (Dec. 19). No late paper is allowed. ● 採用下列何項AI使用規則(Indicate which of the following options you use to manage student use of the AI) 完全開放使用且無須註明 Unrestricted use with no disclosure required (1) 有條件開放，請註明如何使用生成式AI於課程產出 Conditionally open; please specify how generative AI will be used in course output (2) 禁止使用，請註明相關的監管機制 Prohibited use; please specify relevant oversight (3) 本課程無涉及AI使用 Not applicable This course is intended to offer graduate students an interdisciplinary training in thinking about the dynamic between the evolution of prose fiction and its social and cultural milieu in the contexts of eighteenth century English society. What we need in the class is close reading of the texts and related literary theory, forming problematic on topics concerning social transformation, Puritanism, and literary genre, as well as active participation in arguing and discoursing on one’s own points of views in fluent and articulate English. 可參考下列網頁範例 See the following web page for examples. https://curricul.site.nthu.edu.tw/p/404-1208-248357.php?Lang=zh-tw ● 可連結之網頁位址 相關網頁(Personal Website)
