docs.text: National Tsing Hua University College of Technology Management Course Syllabus 科號 Course Number 11410IMBA501100 學分 Credit 3 人數限制 Size of Limit 36 中文名稱 Course Title 財務管理 英文名稱 Course English Title Financial Management 任課教師 Instructor 俞明德 Min-Teh Yu 教師聯絡方式 Contact Information 教師: mtyu@mx.nthu.edu.tw Office hours: Fri. 12-17:00; TSMC Bld: 710 上課時間 Time F2F3F4 上課教室 Room TSMC Bldg 903 先修科目 Prerequisite(s) Statistics; Accounting. 關鍵字 Key Words Corporate Finance 公 司 財 務 ; Financial Markets 金 融 市 場 ; Corporate Valuation 企業評價; Investment Decisions 投資策 略; Financing Decisions 融資決策; Dividend Policy 股利政策. 本課程對應之學習目標與核心能力 Aligned Learning Goals and Learning Objectives 1. Multicultural and diversity management skills to effectively make business decisions in a globalized environment (10%). 2. Teamwork, leadership, and communication skills to enable students to work effectively with others in making group decisions (30%). 3. Understanding of ethical standards for evaluating ethical issues and making business decisions (10%). 4. Functional knowledge in accounting, finance, marketing, technology management, and information systems, applicable from a management perspective to address cross-disciplinary issues (40%). 5. Quantitative skills to analyze and use data in business decision-making (10%). 課程目標 Course Objectives This course discusses core concepts and decisions in financial management, with a focus on corporate finance. It is organized into four major parts: 1. Fundamental concepts, 2. Corporate valuation, 3. Investment decisions, 4. Financing decisions and dividend policy. Lectures are designed over a 16-week schedule and include exercises to reinforce learning outcomes. 課程說明 Course Description 1. Understand basic concepts of corporate finance and financial statement analysis. 2. Explain and evaluate corporate bonds and stocks. 3. Analyze and compare investment appraisal methods. 4. Apply capital budgeting techniques to evaluate corporate investments. 5. Measure and explain risk and return in capital markets. National Tsing Hua University College of Technology Management Course Syllabus 6. Understand the concept of market efficiency. 7. Discuss capital structure decisions. 8. Examine dividend and payout policies. Examine dividend and payout policies. 指定用書 Textbooks Ross, S., R. Westerfield, J. Jaffe and B. Jordan, Corporate Finance, 13th ed., McGraw-Hill. Print copy: https://eshop.hwatai.com.tw/SalePage/Index/7810955 E-copy: https://eshop.hwatai.com.tw/SalePage/Index/9064671 參考書籍 References Class Notes and PowerPoint slides. 教學方式 Teaching Approach Lectures and group discussions. (The course is taught in English.) 評分標準 Grading Midterm Exam 50%: There will be two one-hour exams, consisting mostly of multiple-choice questions, but the instructor reserves the right to include essay or computational questions. Final Research Report 30%: A team project (up to 5 students per team) should choose a research question related to the course, review the literature, explain why it deserves further study, and propose how to carry it out (including data and methods). Teams should also describe expected results. Since this is a one-semester course, a full paper is not required. Each team must (1) make a PowerPoint presentation, (2) submit an “incomplete” but as complete as possible research report with the slides, and (3) meet with the instructor at least once to discuss progress before the final report. Class Participation is encouraged. Homework Assignments 20%: 2 to 4 assignments are planned. Points for each will be announced in advance; any unassigned points will be reallocated to the Final Research Report. X= 8?; 75-98 教學進度 Course Schedule (The course is taught in English.) docs.text: National Tsing Hua University College of Technology Management Course Syllabus 科號 Course Number 11410IMBA501200 學分 Credit 3 人數限制 Size of Limit 25 中文名稱 Course Title 科技創新與轉型 英文名稱 Course English Title Technology Innovation & Transformation 任課教師 Instructor 許智強、陳鼎元 教師聯絡方式 Contact Information khsu@gapp.nthu.edu.tw; cd.taic@gmail.com 上課時間 Time R6R7R8 上課教室 Room 先修科目 Prerequisite(s) Economics 關鍵字 Key Words (至少 5 個，請填寫中英文) 破壞性創新 Disruptive Innovation, 產業合作 Industrial Collaboration, 創新型組織 Innovative Organization, 人工智慧共智 AI Co-Intelligence, 產品開發估值 Product Development Valuation 本課程對應之學習目標與核心能力 Aligned Learning Goals and Learning Objectives 1. Critical Thinking 2. Co-Intelligence skills with generative AI 3. Business Valuation 4. Group Collaboration Skills 課程目標 Course Objectives This course focuses on the challenges and opportunities associated with technological innovation and business adapting strategies in the ever-changing global environment, especially with Co-Intelligence of generative AI underway on various aspects of technology innovation. Students shall be prepared to face and alerted with all these upcoming challenges. 課程說明 Course Description This course is intended to be technology innovation management course for International MBA student. We shall explore the impacts of AI on sustainable growth both corporate level and individual development in the future. Students will gain a general overview of the types and patterns and innovation and transformation, open innovation, timing of entry and challenges of sustaining transformation, along with theories, concepts and skills relevant to managing new product development effectively in today’s global environment. Students will be challenged to integrate knowledge they have gained from other business core courses and apply their accumulated knowledge to business case studies. National Tsing Hua University College of Technology Management Course Syllabus Students will engage in case study and business analysis for new product development as well as business transformation, and they will be frequently asked to conduct group discussion and present their findings to the class. This course will utilize modern AGI tools (ChatGPT’s, Grok3,..etc.) and external webinars to encourage students actively involved in-class discussions and their presentations. 指定用書 Textbooks Melissa A. Schilling, “Strategic Management of Technological Innovation”, 7th edition 參考書籍 References l Peter F. docs.text: １ 科目名稱：『國際華語教育發展』課程綱要 Development of International Chinese Education (IMS 500100) 114 學年度第 1 學期 (Fall, 2025) 授課老師： 信世昌 hsins@ntnu.edu.tw LINE ID: hsinscc 學 分： 跨院華語組必修、華文所選修; 3 學分 教 室： 清大校本部綜合二館 2 樓 ____ 教室 時 間： 每週四下午 3:30pm – 6:20pm ============================================================= 課程目的： 本課程的主要目的是從宏觀的角度來探討華語文教育的國際化及其在全球的發展， 並且從國際環境、語文政策、師資培育、課程與教學制度、機構組織等方面切入，此外 並一併探討語言的興盛與衰退，內容包括： 1. 探究影響語言興盛與衰退的因素為何 2. 瞭解華語國際化與多元化之變遷 3. 探討海內外華語文教育與僑教之發展與現況 4. 了解全球華語推廣機構及重要活動 5. 討論如何推動全球的華語文教育 教學方式: 以課堂討論、專案分析、文獻資料研讀為主，並擬邀請專家參與特定主題之討論。 本課並採專題研判方式，根據國內外華語文教育的相關情勢，深入探究其成因與發展之 道。此外，若干與華語文教育有關的特殊問題，也將一併深入討論。 學習評量方式: 文章導讀 (講義與教材) 20% 分組專題報告與資料彙集 30 % 期末報告 (專案 Project 或專題論述) 40% 課程參與 (出席, 討論與服務) 10% (加分 Bonus:於本學期報名參加本課認可之華語教學研討會,每次酌加總分1~2分) 註：出席 (缺席請事先請假，無故曠課每小時扣總分 1 分) 教材: ※ 本課講義 (雲端 Moodle 平台 PDF 檔) ※ Crystal, David (2015) English as a Global Language. Cambridge University Press. (中文譯本：英語憑什麼！英語憑什麼! 英語如何主宰我們的世界 / 英語帝國。台北：貓頭鷹書坊) ２ 教學時程: 09/04 課程介紹 / 國際華語教育綜論 閱讀資料：ppt 講義 (準備訂書, elearn 平台, 群組, 助教) 09/11 華語的傳播、國際化與擴大個人的格局 閱讀資料：ppt, 講義 https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=S0bdJWFevXg https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VsC7vkLQfzY ※ 取得圖書 (英語憑什麼) ※ 導讀分組 09/18 台灣對外華語教育之起始與發展 台灣的族群與語言 閱讀資料：講義 A-2,3 09/25 台灣對外華語教學之、現況與問題 閱讀資料： 10/02 中國大陸的對外漢語教學：制度、政策、方式 中國大陸的族群與語言 閱讀資料：導讀講義 A-1 網頁：漢辦 /語合中心 http://www.chinese.cn/ 10/09 兩岸華語教學發展之比較 參考網頁：教育部國際與兩岸教育司 導讀與討論：英語憑什麼 第一章 10/16 海外華裔中文教育之發展與問題：僑教、中文學校 導讀與討論：英語憑什麼 第二章 閱讀資料：講義 C-1,2,3 (導讀 C-2,C3) ※ 報告分組 10/23 東南亞的華文教育變遷 新加坡的華語發展問題 (導讀 D1,D2) 導讀與討論：英語憑什麼 第三章 閱讀資料：網頁：僑委會、全美中文學校聯合會 10/30 大華語與全球華語 導讀與討論：英語憑什麼 第四章 閱讀資料：導讀講義 B-1,2, 導讀 B3,4 ３ 11/06 各國之華語教學發展：以美國、德國與韓國為例 導讀與討論：英語憑什麼 第五章 閱讀資料：導讀: E-1 網頁：CLTA, CLASS 網頁 11/13 分組主題一：各國之語言推廣機構 (法,德,英,西,義,日,台灣,大陸等) 討論：從國際華語的視角：華語教材應如何處理? 閱讀資料：講義 ※ 決定期末報告主題 11/20 分組主題二：各國的華語學會(美,加,日,韓,德,法,英,澳,紐,泰,星…) 閱讀資料：各學會網頁; 講義 11/27 分組主題三：移民與語言傳播；華人的海外移民情況 閱讀資料：講義 內政部 / 僑委會 之進出移民資料 ※繳交期末報告大綱與參考書目 12/04 分組主題四：留學及跨境交流 與語言傳播 閱讀資料：講義 教育部的僑外生統計數據; 台灣出國留學數據 12/11 分組主題五：國際傳播媒體 (廣播、電視、電影及新媒體) 的華語傳播 閱讀資料：講義 12/18 作業討論 12/25 ※ 繳交期末作業 相關書籍與期刊： Crystal, David (2000) Language Death. Cambridge University Press. (中文譯本：語言的死亡。台北：貓頭鷹書坊) 《語言戰略研究》期刊。北京：商務印書館。 《華語學刊》期刊。台灣華語文教學學會。台北：五南出版社。 生成式人工智慧 (AI) 倫理聲明：禁止使用 根據本校公布之佈的「大學教育場域 AI 協作、共學與素養培養指引」，本門課程 採取禁止使用。 修讀本門課程之學生應有獨立原創的作業，應注意本門課不得繳交使 用生成式人工智慧 (例如 ChatGPT 等軟體) 所產出的作業、報告或個人心得。若經查 核發現，教師、學校或相關單位有權重新針對作業或報告重新評分或不予計分。修讀本 課程之學生於選課時視為同意以上倫理聲明。

docs.name: 華語教學之跨文化溝通
docs.nameEn: Cross-cultural Communication for Teaching Chinese as a Second Language
docs.text: 《華語教學之跨文化溝通》 授課教師：宋怡南 ynsung@gmail.com 時間地點：12:10-15:10 GEN II 綜二 二、課程內容與學習 語言與文化的關係密切，跨文化溝通知識及能力屬華語教學專業知能之 一。華語教師必須充分了解語言與本國文化之間的連結，在生活中與自我經驗 中觀察文化，進而能適當的將之展現在教學中；另一方面，教師在面對來自世 界各地不同背景的學生，必須有足夠的文化敏感度，對各國文化及其相關影響 抱持尊重的態度，進而幫助學生從其母語文化出發，認識目標語的文化，結合 跨文化交際知能，獲得完整之語言溝通能力。 本課程《華語教學之跨文化溝通》由理論與實務出發，首先界定語言與文 化的關係及其定義，介紹語言與文化的研究方法，綜合探討華語教學中合適的 文化範圍。其次在語言交際和跨文化溝通的目的和基礎上，探討語言與文化接 觸與衝擊，經由各種語言現象所反映的文化背景，理解背後不同文化的交際模 式和核心價值。同時選取五類於跨文化溝通中具代表性及差異性的語言主題， 如：借字、禮節語言、禁忌語和委婉語等，通過與不同文化之受訪者對談，真 實觀察跨文化交際衝突和適應過程。最後由本學期探討主題出發，規劃具備華 語教學效能之主題文化課程單元。 三、課程要求 （一）閱讀與討論 課前閱讀教材並於班上積極參與討論，有助於在短時間內 取得最大收穫。請妥善規劃每次出席，課堂參與度將是學期成績的重要參考。 （二）跨文化個案訪談 分組後找到本學期五次文化主題訪談的對象，對象請 鎖定在臺學華語的外籍人士，國籍不拘，華裔背景請排除。 【訪談對象介紹】配合投影片介紹訪談對象：本人華語學習背景所來自國 家/鄰近地區的歷史宗教政治文化背景母語特色華語在該國的發展狀況對 臺灣文化的印象。 【五次訪談與分享】根據大綱上所列主題進行訪談，應輪流分工，於課上口頭 分享後繳交一份 4 頁的訪談書面報告 ※訪談請依照各週規劃之主題，依次完成。每次訪談均需全組到齊，盡量採 實體形式以利觀察跨文化溝通，不可合併主題訪談。書面報告均須附上分工 狀況與全組合照。 （三）華語教學主題文化課程單元設計 根據本學期訪談及探討的主題出 發，練習規劃不同主題之文化課程單元，報告包含海報票選與課堂講述兩部 分，期末前有一次主題簡報。 評量項目（總分 100％）  出席與閱讀討論（個人） 20%  訪談對象介紹（分組） 10%  個案採訪報告（分組） 40% （共 5 次，每次 8%）  期末主題文化課程設計（分組） 30% （簡報佔 5%） 四、每週進度（暫訂） 週 授 課 主 題 活 動 內 容 一 課程介紹與主題討論 語言學習與文化衝突經驗 二 語言與文化的關係 民族價值核心與文化對比 三 語言與文化的研究方法 活動：訪談注意事項 四 跨文化交際理論與實務 序曲：訪談對象介紹 1 五 從造詞心理、親屬稱謂看文化 序曲：訪談對象介紹 2 六 先人的智慧：各類熟語探討 活動：訪談行前討論 七 文化接觸之一：借字 第 1 次訪談與分享 八 文化接觸之二：混合語 第 2 次訪談與分享 九 誰最有禮貌：禮節語言的運用 第 3 次訪談與分享 十 語言的力量：咒罵語、髒話 活動：教學現場的文化議題 1 十一 佛曰不可說：禁忌語與委婉語 第 4 次訪談與分享 十二 男女大不同：性別語言 活動：教學現場的文化議題 2 十三 非語言符號：動作、表情、服飾… 期末主題文化課程簡報 十四 語言教學與文化課程設計 終曲：第 5 次訪談與分享 十五 ～期末主題文化課程單元設計報告與回饋～ 十六 ～期末主題文化課程單元設計報告與回饋～ 五、課程閱讀清單 課程主題指定閱讀文獻，已公告於本課程平台上。請按照進度完成閱讀與 筆記，帶至課堂上討論。

docs.name: 書報討論：國別化教材編寫
docs.text: 1 書報討論：國別化教材編寫 Seminar: Compiling Country-Specific Teaching Materials 一、教師資訊： 授課教師：陳淑芬 電子信箱：chensf@gapp.nthu.edu.tw 辦 公 室：綜二館 A607 聯絡電話：35167 二、課程資訊： 上課時間： 週四 10:10 --- 1:00 上課地點：綜二 608 Office Hours: 週四、週五下午 1 – 3 （請來信預約） 三、課程說明： 本課程旨在瞭解國別化教材之編寫原則，並培養學生從事國別化教材之研究 能力，進而撰寫國別化華語教材。透過系統性與階段性的學習指導，協助學生進 行國別化教材相關之學位論文寫作。本課程有三大學習目標： (1) 確立碩士/博士論文問題意識與研究方法。 (2) 培養國別化教材相關之研究能力。 (3) 培養論證架構的能力與論文寫作能力。 四、參考資料： Brown, J. D. 1988. Understanding Research in Second Language Learning. Cambridge: Cambridge University Press. Fantini, A. E. (1997). New Ways in Teaching Culture. Alexandria, VA: Teachers of English to Speakers of Other Languages, Inc. Kramsch, C. (1988). “The cultural discourse of foreign language textbook”. In A. Singerman (ed.), Towards a New Integration of Language and Culture (pp. 63-68). Middlebury, VT: Northeast Conference. Kramsch, Claire. (1993) Context and Culture in Language Teaching. Oxford: Oxford University Press. Kroeber, A. L., and Kluckhohn, C. (1952). Culture: A Critical Review of Concepts and Definitions. Cambridge, Massachusetts: Peabody Museum. Moran, P. R. (2009). Teaching Culture: Perspectives in Practice. Beijing: Foreign Language Teaching and Research Press. Nemetz-Robinsin, G. L. (1988). Crosscultural Understanding. New York: Prentice-Hall. Oswalt, Wendell H. (1970). Understanding Our Culture. An Anthropological View. New York: Holt, Rinehart and Winston. 2 Seelye, N. (1993). Teaching Culture: Strategies for Foreign Language Educators. Lincolnwood: National Textbook Company. 五、教學方式 上課以報告和討論的方式進行。由學生上台報告最近所研讀國別化教材相關 的文獻，及論文書寫進度，出席同學需要輪流提問以及評論。上課前三日需將全 文寄給評論的同學和任課老師。 六、成績考核： 課堂報告 + 書面報告：40% 提問與同儕評論：30% 期末報告： 30% 七、學生使用 AI 的聲明： 根據本校公布之佈的「大學教育場域 AI 協作、共學與素養培養指引」， 本門課程採取有條件開放，請註明如何使用生成式 AI 於作業或報告，說明如 下： 學生可於課堂作業或報告中的「標題頁註腳」或「引用文獻後」簡要說明 如何使用生成式 AI 進行議題發想、文句潤飾或結構參考等使用方式。然而， 學生不得使用生成式 AI 工具撰寫期末研究報告。若經查核使用卻無在作業 或報告中標明，教師、學校或相關單位有權重新針對作業或報告重新評分或 不予計分。 修讀本課程之學生於選課時視為同意以上倫理聲明。 備註：限碩二以上準備寫畢業論文學生選修。 3 論文撰寫相關書籍： 上野千鶴子著，涂紋鳳譯，《如何做好研究論文？成為知識生產者，從提問到輸 出的18個步驟》，臺北：三采，2021。 安伯托．艾可（Umberto Eco）著，倪安宇譯，《如何撰寫畢業論文：給人文學科 研究生的建議》，臺北：時報，2019。 何德華，《華語教學研究方法與論文寫作》，臺北：正中書局出版，2009。 吳鄭重：《研究研究論論文：研究歷程之科P解密與論文寫作SOP大公開》，臺北： 遠流出版，2016。 孟樊，《論文寫作方法與格式》，新北市：威仕曼文化，2012。 美國現代語言協會編著，《MLA 論文寫作手冊，第9版》，臺北：書林出版有限 公司，2022。 張可婷譯，Diana Ridley 著，《一步步教您做文獻回顧》，新北：韋伯文化，2010。 畢恆達，《教授為什麼沒告訴我？——論文寫作的枕邊書》，臺北：學富文化事 業，2005。 陳信助，《研究方法易上手》，臺北：學富文化，2020。 彭明輝，《研究生完全求生手冊：方法、秘訣、潛規則》，臺北：聯經，2017。 葉至誠，《研究方法與論文寫作》，臺北：商鼎文化，2011。 蔡柏盈，《從字句到結構：學術論文寫作指引》，臺北：臺灣大學出版中心，2015。 顏志龍，《傻瓜也會寫論文（量化+質化增訂版）： 社會科學學位論文寫作指南》， 臺北：五南圖書，2018。 參考資源： 1. 學校授權資源（可至清大圖書館---資料庫檢索/期刊檢索中檢索所需工具） A. 愛如生的《中國基本古籍庫》、《中國方志庫》、《歷代別集庫》、《譜 牒庫》、《典海平台》 B. 讀秀 C. docs.text: 1 漢語語言學 （114學年度第一學期） 一、教師資訊： 授課教師：陳淑芬 電子信箱：chensf@gapp.nthu.edu.tw 辦 公 室：綜二館 A607 聯絡電話：35167 二、課程資訊： 上課時間： 週五早上 9:10 --- 12:00 p.m. 上課地點：綜二 205 Office Hours: 週四、週五下午 1 - 3（請來信預約） 三、課程說明： 本課程向學生介紹漢語語言學知識，包括語音屬性、音韻結構、構詞與詞彙、 句法結構、語意學、篇章結構、語用現象和漢字教學，涵蓋語言分析的基本概念和 方法。通過對漢語結構的分析，學生將更深入地了解漢語的結構以及人類語言的本 質，從而提高漢語作為第二語言/外語教學之教學知識與研究方法。通過對漢語的全 面理解，學生在成為華語教師後，將能夠回答華語課堂中所遇到的各種語言問題， 並可以提高其學生的學習興趣，並獲得更好的學習成果。 四、課堂用書： 1. 舒兆民，2021，《現代漢語語言學概要》，台北：新學林。 2. 自編講義（請見閱讀清單）。 五、參考資料： Chao, Yuen Ren. 1968. docs.nameEn: Travel and Reading for Technology：Computers, AI, and Robotics
docs.text: 授 課 學 期 114 學年度 第 1 學期 開 課 單 位 □ 跨院國際博士班學位學程 □ 跨院國際碩士學位學程 課 程 名 稱(中文) 科技旅讀：電腦、人工智慧、機器人 課 程 名 稱(英文) Travel and Reading for Technology：Computers, AI, and Robotics 授 課 教 師 陳鴻文、陳俊銘 學分數 2 授 課 教 室 ■校本部綜二___________ □南大_________ 上課時間 授 課 語 言 □英文 ■中文 人數限制 20 課 程 限 制 無 課 程 簡 述 本課程以「科技旅讀」為核心，結合理論講授與企業參訪，帶領學 生深入了解台灣在電腦、人工智慧（AI）與機器人產業中的角色 與轉型挑戰。課程從組織設計、產業結構與國家發展等理論出發， 探討台灣企業如何在全球價值鏈中持續升級，並掌握 AI 與智慧製 造對產業生態的影響。 中 文 暨 英 文 關 鍵 字 （ 五 組） 電腦產業 Computer Industry 人工智慧 Artificial Intelligence (AI) 機器人技術 Robotics 產業策略與國家發展 Industrial Strategy and National Development 科技與社會 Technology and Society 課 程 大 綱 Detailed Course Syllabus ● 課程說明(Course Description) 本課程以「科技旅讀」為核心教學方式，結合理論建構與實地 參訪，帶領同學探索台灣科技產業——特別是電腦、人工智慧 （AI）與機器人相關產業——在企業策略、產業結構與全球競爭 體系中的發展脈絡與轉型挑戰。 台灣長年於全球電腦代工產業中扮演關鍵角色，雖然生產線多數外 移中國，但本地廠商憑藉技術整合與供應鏈管理持續鞏固地位。面 對中國崛起與製造外移的壓力，台灣企業如何升級與創新，成為本 課程關注的核心議題。同時，AI 與機器人技術的興起正快速改變 產業生態，進一步牽動半導體與智慧製造等關鍵領域，本課程將帶 領學生從理論與實務雙軌並進，掌握產業變革趨勢。 課程內容分為三大模組： 理論建構：介紹五力分析、全球價值鏈、創新兩難、產業群聚、國 家發展等核心理論，建立學生分析企業與產業的基礎架構。 科技主題探索：聚焦 AI 與機器人的技術演進與產業應用，並探討 其與台灣半導體與製造業的整合關係。 實地參訪與回饋：安排科技企業參訪與業界專家分享，強化學生對 產業現場與實務議題的理解。 本課程適合理工與人文社會領域學生共同修習，並採跨域小組方式 進行學習與專題製作。學生需於期中提出研究提案，並於期末完成 整合報告；每次參訪亦需事前準備提問並繳交心得，以提升批判思 辨與實務觀察能力。透過課堂訓練與現場觀察相結合，培養學生從 科技產業理解社會變遷、從企業決策反思全球結構的綜合能力。 ● 課程單元 週次 課程主題 推薦閱讀 1 課程說明 沈方正（2022）《科技與社會 的交錯：觀點與方法》。左岸 文化。 2 組織設計與核心競爭力 Galloway, R. (2023). Strategic Management. Oxford Univ. Press. 3 產業結構與價值鏈分析 Sturgeon, T. (2021). Global Value Chains. Cambridge Journal. 4 電腦架構與產業分析 Hennessy, J. & Patterson, D. (2020). docs.name: 新生命-混合實境藝術
docs.text: 國立清華大學 114 學年 -上學期 (2025-09) 跨院博密集課程 - 11410IPHD500100 1 / 2 新生命 - 混合實境藝術 New Life - Mixed Reality Art 授課老師 : 陳珠櫻教授 & 李瑞光教授 Pr. CHEN Chu-Yin & Pr. LEE Ray-Kuang 上課時間、地點 : (2 天密集式工作坊) 2025/09/06 (六)，清大校本部 - 綜二 B 側: 204、205 教室 ； 2025/09/20 (六)，桃園科技藝術節展場 - 中原文創園區 https://g.co/kgs/FpFGRdZ 課程學分：1 學分 (16 小時) 授課語言 : 英文/中文 參考圖 : 精緻生命 in XR - 混合實境之共創體驗 關鍵詞 : 科學與藝術，超現實主義、精緻屍骸共創，當代科技藝術，虛擬/擴增/混合實境藝術。 Science & Art, Surrealism, Co-creation of Exquisite Corpses, Contemporary Technological Art, Virtual/Augmented/Mixed Reality Art. 課程簡述： 本課程聚焦於探索未來宇宙及創意生命的無限可能，體驗前所未有的沉浸式科技藝術之旅！ 課程內容主要分為三部份：「科學與藝術」、「精緻生命 in XR」及「參觀桃園科技藝術節」，透過 VR 技術共創模式及沉浸式混合實境體驗，拓展實驗性和趣味性的美感經驗；激發對未來宇宙與新 生命形式的發想，及探索未來世界人類與非人類生命共存的可能性。 國立清華大學 114 學年 -上學期 (2025-09) 跨院博密集課程 - 11410IPHD500100 2 / 2 課程內容說明： 1. 科學與藝術 : 來自一場人類情感智慧與科技力量、藝術想像力的協同合作 ! 探索未來宇宙 : 首先介紹量子科學的最新發展，並以在台灣及日本「黑洞及重力波」展覽為例， 說明如何運用科技藝術、音樂和影像來呈現黑洞和重力波的本質及探測原理。科學如何成為藝術 家的創作靈感，讓觀眾以沉浸式、互動式的藝術聲光效果，進入科學與科技藝術的殿堂了解天文 宇宙的現象，拓展人類的新視野。 開發創意場域: 介紹第二次世界大戰後的「精緻屍骸」共創理念，源自法國超現實主義運動所發起 的創作接龍遊戲，是一種多腦共創形式 ，布魯東、達利和畢卡索等藝術家都是這一運動的積極參 與者。超現實主義者認為這是一種極具挑戰性、但又隱含無限可能的共同創作方式；既是探索集 體無意識的實驗，又能揭示人類心靈深處的想像力。 2. 黑客松 – 精緻生命 in XR： 汲取「精緻屍骸」的共創理念，由法國巴黎第八大學團隊所研發的「精緻生命 in XR」混合實境裝 置模組，提供並賦予了這種獨特的沉浸式集體創作形式。通過 VR 技術及 360°的空間維度，每個 團隊成員在虛擬實境眼鏡裡進行繪圖接龍遊戲，共同創作精美的新生命個體，最後並在虛擬的與 現實的混合實境中，延續富有實驗性和趣味性的美感賞析經驗。 3. 參觀 - 桃園科技藝術節: 2025 年展覽主題為 : 「新生命 New Type」，探索未來的新生命形式。藉由實地觀展、親身體 驗、沉浸作品中，進入藝術家對未來生命演化的想像世界。展覽作品涵蓋 : 「機器（Robot）、人造人（Android）、賽伯格（Cyborg）、混種（Hybrid）、基因改造 （Genetic Modification）、人工智慧（Artificial Intelligence）以及人工生命（Artificial Life）等 全新樣態。[ …. ] 讓我們在科技與生命交融的時代，重新思考生命的本質與邊界，激發對生命形式 演變及倫理挑戰的深刻反思，以及人類與機器未來共存的可能性。」(截自展覽文宣) 教學方式 : 著重跨領域、非邏輯性、非線性思維，對未知好奇、勇於嘗試探討。 共同審思 : 科學和藝術的本質與與現代精神，人類與科技的共生關係。 共創體驗 :「精緻生命 in XR」之多腦共創發想及人機共創協作。 實地參觀 : 桃園科技藝術節 2025「新生命 New Type」。 自我反思 : 未來生命的演化方向及新生命的倫理挑戰。 成績考核 : 上課出席狀況: 30% 異地學習必須全程出席。 分組討論報告: 30% 參與度與創意思維。 心得感想撰寫: 40% 中文為主; A4 紙至少 2 頁 (字體大小 12，每頁至少 1000 字) 。 學生使用 AI 的規則： 本門課程採取禁止使用， 1 國立清華大學 114 學年 -上學期 (2025-09) 跨院博密集課程 - 11410IPHD500100 新生命 - 混合實境藝術 New Life - Mixed Reality Art 陳珠櫻教授 & 李瑞光教授 Pr. docs.name: 透視韓國教育：制度、文化與全球脈動
docs.text: 1 Understanding Korean Education Hwanbo Park, Ph.D. (Professor, Chungnam National University) Course Objectives This course provides a general introduction to Korean education for international students. It will explore four main themes: 1. Korean education system 2. Korea’ educatioanl fever 3. Korean schools and student life 4. The impact of globalization on Korean education Rather than simply presenting factual information, the course explores Korea’s educational system, policies, and challenges as socially and historically constructed phenomena shaped by various actors within Korean society. Students will be encouraged to engage critically with the topics and reflect on similarities and differences between Korean education and their own contexts. Various media will be used to support learning, and class discussions will offer opportunities for students to share their own experiences and perspectives. Readings Course materials will include a variety of sources such as policy documents, videos, newspaper articles, and academic readings. Students are strongly encouraged to attend the first class to receive detailed information about course materials. Class Activities The course consists of lecture and discussion. Each class begins with a short lecture to introduce the topic, followed by interactive discussions. Students are expected to participate actively in every session. They will be grouped in small teams to lead discussions on a rotating basis. Topics, Readings, and Assignments by Class Day Session 1 – Korean Education System - Overview of Korean Educational System - Educational Acheivement (educational expansion and academic achievement) - National Development and the Role of Education in Korea 2 - Key issues and challenges of Korean Education - Comparative Reflections Session 2 – Korea’ educatioanl fever - The meaning and characteristics of educational fever - Root causes: colonial legacy, competition, job market, and college entrance - Family expectations and their influence on education - Comparative Reflections Session 3 – Korean schools and student life - School culture and student in K-drama - Daily life and routines of Korean students - Comparative Reflections Session 4 – Globalization and Korean Education - Internationalization of Korean education - Global citizenship education in Korea - Korea’s role in educational development and cooperation - Comparative Reflections

docs.text: 11320IPHD700100 iPHD Seminar Lecturer: Prof. Hung-Wen Chen hungwen@mx.nthu.edu.tw Course Overview This course is designed for graduate students in iPhD program of NTHU to broaden their horizons in different areas. This course, students will be required to invite speakers from interdisciplinary areas of research to share their cutting-edge results. All students are encouraged to have interactions with the speakers. Please see the Syllabus for more details. Course Policy (Tentative) 1. In this seminar, we have 12 talks in total (12 Attendances). Course introduction and IPhD Orientation are excluded. 2. Students are required to attend the seminar on time (Tues. 16:30) and the TAs will take your attendance. 3. To pass this course, students are required to (1) Attend talks at least 10 times in total (2) Team up, invite a speaker and host the speech on that day as a team. (3) Ask 1 question to at least 2 different speakers during the semester and upload your questions and the responses from the speakers to eeclass platform before the evening of the next day (Thu. 18:00). 4. To facilitate the process of inviting a speaker, please follow the workflow shown below. docs.text: 授課學期 114 學年度 第 1 學期 開課單位 ■ 跨院國際博士班學位學程 □ 跨院國際碩士學位學程 課程名稱 (中文) 科技藝術書報討論 課程名稱 (英文) Seminar of Technology and Arts 授課教師 許素朱 學分數 1 授課教室 綜二館 R603 上課時間 週三 6:30~7:20PM 授課語言 □英文 ■中文 人數限制 10 課程限制 否 課程簡述 「科技藝術-書報討論」課程主要帶領學生了解國際最新科技藝術 創作與研究的趨勢，從該領域最重要之學術會議、期刊及藝術展 覽活動，選讀藝術論文及作品探討報告。課程由授課老師指定閱 讀論文或科技藝術作品清單給學生選讀，從報告與討論交流中， 讓學生獲得科技藝術領域的作品創作、技術研發能力，以及論文 撰寫及投稿的關鍵能力。AI 世代來臨，本課程也會帶領學生探討 「AI 在藝術的典範轉移」與對社會之影響。 中文暨英 文關鍵字 （五組） 科技藝術、Emerging Technology、ARS Electronica Festival、 ACM SIGGRAPH、AI 課程大綱 Detailed Course Syllabus Course content（課程內容）: 本課程帶領學生①了解國際科技藝術創作與研究的最新趨勢，從 該領域最重要之學術會議、期刊及藝術展覽活動，選讀藝術論文 及作品探討報告。課程由授課老師指定閱讀論文或科技藝術作品 清單給學生選讀，從報告與討論交流中，讓學生獲得科技藝術領 域的作品創作、技術研發能力。②課程中會擇期邀請相關專家， 給予跨領域面向的講演或討論交流。③。AI 世代來臨，課程會 探討「AI 在藝術的典範轉移」與對社會影響。④課程也會授予 論文撰寫及投稿的關鍵能力。 課程書報討論之內容包含三個方向： 1. 科技藝術國際知名作品 survey：奧地利林茲電子藝術節 （ARS Electronica）、ARS Archive、SIGGRAPH Art Gallery 2. 技藝術前瞻科技(Emerging Tech)展示(Demo): Emerging Technology 互動前瞻科技 project 或作品 3. 科技藝術與前瞻科技論文研讀： ACM SIGGRAPH (art, tech full paper)、ACM SIGCHI、ACM Multimedia、ISEA、Digital Humanity、ACM SUI、ACM TEI、IEEE VISAP … 等科技藝術國際重要知名研討會與學術 期刊，挑選經典科技藝術或前瞻科技論文選讀。 4. 專家學者分享演講：專家談「AI 生成藝術」，、「GPT 創意應 用」 5. 文撰寫指導：指導同學碩士/博士論文撰寫格式以及國際學術 研討會論文撰寫。 16 週課表： 每週由老師建議、同學選擇閱讀國際作品或論文並做報告，課堂 上老師、同學一起參與討論、講評。 ‧第 1 週：課程介紹 ‧第 2, 3 週：ARS Electronica Festival 最近 4 年 interactive art 作品報告與討論 ‧第 4, 5 週：ACM SIGGRAPH – Emerging Technology、HCI 最近 5 年的跨域 Demo 與技術報告討論 ※ 說明：上面報告重點在「實作」作品，eithhr 藝術作品或是 科藝 project 實作展示。 ‧第 6,7 週：指導論文撰寫架構. ‧第 8,9 週：A 近五年 Art full paper 或是 HCI、AI full paper in ACM Siggraph 、 ACM MM 、SIGCHI、HCII、ArtsIT …等論 文報告與討論 ‧第 10,11 週：A 近五年 Art full paper 或是 HCI、AI full paper in ACM Siggraph 、 ACM MM 、SIGCHI、HCII、ArtsIT … 等 論文報告與討論 ‧第 12,13 週：近五年國內相關博士論文報告與討論 ‧第 14,15 週：AI 生成製作報告：近三年 AI 生成藝術 相關科技 藝術作品或學術論文報告與討論 ‧第 16 週：總結討論 評量方式：  報告分數（70%）  平時參與討論（30%） 參考書籍、文獻： 1. Business Intelligence: From Data Insight to Blockchain Analytics is a hands-on course focused on using Power BI to analyze both traditional business data and real-world on-chain data. Students will learn to transform data, build dashboards, and apply BI techniques to National Tsing Hua University College of Technology Management Course Syllabus massive data such as blockchain data. The course includes practical labs and a capstone project for real-world application. 課程目標 Course Objectives Upon completion of the course, students will be able to: 1. Understand the core concepts, architecture, and lifecycle of Business Intelligence (BI) 2. Build interactive dashboards using Power BI 3. Use DAX to calculate key performance indicators and conduct time-series analysis 4. Access and analyze on-chain blockchain data from public APIs and indexed data platforms 5. Compare traditional and on-chain data structures and assess their business value 6. Design and deliver a BI solution for a real-world business or blockchain use case 課程說明 Course Description Business Intelligence: From Data Insight to Blockchain Analytics is a hands-on, project- driven course that equips students with the skills to extract, model, and visualize both traditional business data and real blockchain data. Centered around Power BI, the course covers the full BI lifecycle including data transformation, DAX calculations, and dashboard design. In the second half, students work with real-world, massive scale data of blockchain, which is open and public, making it a powerful resource for modern analytics. Students will learn to access and analyze this data using public APIs and platforms like Dune Analytics, applying BI techniques to emerging domains such as DeFi and crypto asset tracking. Through labs and a capstone project, students gain practical experience in both enterprise and decentralized analytics. 請輸入課程內容「中文暨英文關鍵字」至少 5 個, 每個關鍵字至多 20 個中文, 以半形逗 點分隔 Please fill in at least 5 course keywords (up to 40 letters for each keyword) and use commas to separate them.(required) 商業智慧, 商業分析, 資料視覺化, 策略決策, 區塊鏈, 去中心化金融 Business Intelligence, Business Analytics, Data Visualization, Strategic Decision Making, Blockchain, DeFi, Power BI 指定用書 Textbooks Albright, S. (30%) 課程目標 Course Objectives 本課程將針對授信、投資、資本市場籌資、人才培育、金融商品發展、資訊揭露、審慎 監理、國際鏈結及誘因機制、反漂綠等面向，帶領修課同學深入了解並共同分析國內外 政策、法令、產業實踐，尤其包括川普 2.0 下對於金融業投入永續活動之反動，期能引 領了解此一牽動技術發展、淨零轉型、以及資本移動的重要趨勢。 課程說明 Course Description National Tsing Hua University College of Technology Management Course Syllabus 我國自 2022 年承諾「2050 年淨零排放目標」以來，戮力推動淨零轉型與永續發展，國 家發展委員會 2022 年發布的「2050 淨零排放路徑」已將「綠色金融」列入十二項關鍵 戰略中，運用綠色金融機制與影響力，將資金導引到符合能源轉型、產業轉型、生活轉 型及社會轉型的企業或專案，並促使企業將永續的概念與精神逐步深化於各產業文化。 前（2023）年我國將 2050 淨零排放目標正式納入《氣候變遷因應法》，確立我國氣候治 理法制化，亦突顯我國實踐淨零排放承諾及落實永續相關行動的決心。去（2024）年賴 總統更進一步成立「國家氣候變遷對策委員會」，集結部會首長、產業界及公民代表、跨 領域專家學者共同就氣候變遷議題，提出因應與調適策略，強化國家永續發展的韌性。 金融業在推動永續轉型的過程中所扮演的角色尤其關鍵，不僅透過投融資、金融商品的 設計、議合等影響力，帶動企業重視 ESG 議題與風險，也可透過自身減碳及對低碳產業 的支持，加速企業布局永續行動。國際上有觀點認為「綠色金融」主要僅支持「綠色」、 「永續」的企業或專案，對於尚未達到綠色、永續標準的企業則應限縮資金的提供，以 促使企業減碳及改善。然而，這些尚未達到綠色、永續的企業，其產業雖是溫室氣體排 放的主要來源，卻也是全球經濟的重要支柱，更應協助其淨零轉型，這些產業例如水泥、 鋼鐵、鋁、肥料、電力業等。由於這些產業尚未符合「綠色」標準，過去往往無法獲得 綠色金融的支持。整體而言，綠色及轉型金融是新興發展並極為重要的問題，深入了解 其背後的政策考量、關鍵面向與影響因素等，是永續管理與金融專業的重要內涵。 請輸入課程內容「中文暨英文關鍵字」至少 5 個, 每個關鍵字至多 20 個中文, 以半形逗 點分隔 Please fill in at least 5 course keywords (up to 40 letters for each keyword) and use commas to separate them.(required) 綠色金融 Green Finance, 轉型金融 Transitional Finance, 淨零排放 Net-Zero, 環境、社會、 及治理 ESG, 永續 Sustainability 指定用書 Textbooks 無 參考書籍 References 由於課程主題新興多元、變化迅速，授課教師將依相關政策發展指定最新、前沿閱讀教 材置於課程網站。 教學方式 Teaching Approach 本課程以教師講授為主軸，但重視學生參與課堂討論。教師並將於每週主題補充最新時 事發展，與學生交流意見。另本課程將視需要部分採取同步遠距授課方式。 評分標準 Grading National Tsing Hua University College of Technology Management Course Syllabus 本課程重視參與，修課同學的學期成績會以課程參與（60%）及期末報告（40%）作為 評量。期末報告字數至多八千字（含註腳）。 1. 期末報告題目須與本課程主題相關，但不限於課綱所列議題。請於第九週前提交期末 報告大綱，並約授課教師討論時間，以確認期末報告與本課程之相關性及適切性。 2. 期末報告切勿堆砌英翻中或網站文章。報告內容請以個人意見或論點為主軸，再進一 步尋找佐證之數據或資料。 教學進度 Course Schedule 第一週 課程導覽與介紹 ➢ Lloyds Banking Group, What is green finance?, https://www.lloydsbankinggroup.com/insights/green-finance.html ➢ World Economic Forum, What is green finance and why is it important?, https://www.weforum.org/stories/2020/11/what-is-green-finance/ 第二週 我國綠色及轉型金融政策（1/2） ➢ 金管會「綠色金融行動方案 2.0」八大面向辦理情形 ➢ 金管會「綠色金融行動方案 3.0」 第三週 我國綠色及轉型金融政策（2/2） ➢ 金管會「綠色及轉型金融行動方案」 ➢ 金管會「轉型計畫建議涵蓋事項」 ➢ 第一屆永續金融評鑑 第四週 從審慎監理到盡職治理：中央銀行及機構投資人的角色 ➢ 中央銀行因應氣候變遷策略方案 ➢ 英國盡職治理守則（The UK Stewardship Code） ➢ 證交所「機構投資人盡職治理守則」 第五週 金融業自己綠不綠：範疇三碳排放的盤查 ➢ 證交所「上市櫃公司範疇 3 溫室氣體盤查作業參考指引」 National Tsing Hua University College of Technology Management Course Syllabus ➢ 金融業範疇三財務碳排放計算指引 ➢ 保險業內控及稽核制度實施辦法第 5、19、41 條修正 第六週 銀行授信的對象綠不綠：永續經濟活動的分類標準 ➢ 金管會「永續經濟活動認定參考指引」第二版 ➢ 歐盟永續分類規則（EU Sustainability Taxonomy Regulation） ➢ 王自雄，永續金融中的企業人權責任—論歐盟永續投資規則之最低限度保障，《台 灣法學雜誌》，411 期，頁 131-147（2021 年 3 月 14 日） 第七週 綠色債券及保險商品及市場 ➢ 綠色債券、社會責任債券、永續發展（連結）債券 ➢ 綠色保險 第八週 企業永續資訊的揭露（1/4） ➢ 歐盟企業永續報告指令（Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive, CSRD） ➢ 歐盟永續報告準則（European Sustainability Reporting Standards, ESRS） 第九週 企業永續資訊的揭露（2/4） ➢ 國際財務報導準則（International Financial Reporting Standards, IFRS）永續揭露準 則第 S1 號－永續相關財務資訊揭露之一般規定 docs.name: 創意思考
docs.text: National Tsing Hua University College of Technology Management Course Syllabus 科號 Course Number IPMT200700 學分 Credit 2 人數限制 Size of Limit 100 中文名稱 Course Title 創意思考 英文名稱 Course English Title Creative Thinking 任課教師 Instructor 洪 嘉駿 / Katsun Ang 教師聯絡方式 Contact Information j.ang@mx.NTHU.edu.tw 上課時間 Time 週一 下午第一 節第二節 上課教室 Room 台積館 224 教室 先修科目 Prerequisite(s) 本課程對應之學習目標與核心能力 Aligned Learning Goals and Learning Objectives 此科目對應之系所課程規劃所欲培養之核心能力 運用專業管理與科技知識的能力。 Our students will master the knowledge of technology and professional management. 整合與活用第一專長及第二專長的專業知識能力，並具備跨領域規劃、領導與執行團 隊合作的能力。 Our students will be able to integrate expertise from their double specialty and thus plan, execute and lead in an interdisciplinary team setting. 具備中文及英文閱讀寫作商業報告與商業口頭簡報能力。 Our students will be able to read and produce professional business documents as well as deliver a professional oral presentation in English and in Chinese. 認識產業的國際發展趨勢，瞭解管理與科技對環境、社會及全球的影響，並培養自 我學習成長的能力。 Our students will develop the ability of self-learning by comprehending the international development trend of the industry and by comprehending the impact of management and technology made on the environment, the society and the world. 理解專業倫理及社會責任的能力。 Our students will be equipped with understandings of professional ethics and social responsibility. National Tsing Hua University College of Technology Management Course Syllabus 課程目標 Course Objectives 問對問題，設計創意解決方案！ 透過創意發想與思考，定義問題並設計問題解決模型。透過創新的設計思考 方式，深入了解需求和問題，創造出更具價值和有意義的產品或服務，且激 發創新思維和創造力。 課程說明 Course Description 本課程以人為核心出發，Design Thinking 設計思考為主體，輔以個案分析、 品牌實務研討與業界專家實務演講，培養「危機處理」與「問題解決能力」 之技能。透過以案例分析與創意思維，深入了解使用者的行為和需求，以獲 取更有價值的問題解決方案，讓學生學習在有限的空間和時間內，用簡短的 方式表達創意並解決問題。 請輸入課程內容「中文暨英文關鍵字」至少 5 個, 每個關鍵字至多 20 個中文, 以半形逗點分隔 Please fill in at least 5 course keywords (up to 40 letters for each keyword) and use commas to separate them.(required) 設計思考（Design Thinking） 設計原則 (Design principles) 創新（Innovation） 設計原則 (Design principles) Brain storming（腦力激盪） 創意發想（Ideate） 定義問題（Define） 指定用書 Textbooks 本課程無特定指定用書，以現代行銷與實務分析探討整合教材，由教師自編 合適之授課題材。 參考書籍 References 無 教學方式 Teaching Approach 1. 個案分析與問題思考。 2. 分組報告與實證反饋討論。 3. 專家演講實務經驗分享。 4. 翻轉學習與情境模擬教學。 評分標準 Grading 1. 課堂參與及討論 (40%) 2. 期中作業(30%) 3. 期末作業(30%) National Tsing Hua University College of Technology Management Course Syllabus 教學進度 Course Schedule 1.創意思維與策略 2.發現問題與技巧實作 3 定義問題 4.問題解決實務研討與設計 5.表達的魅力與舞台技巧 6.行銷策略與市場定位 7.品牌溝通 8.期中評量 9.設計思考 10.廣告文案 11.行銷說服力 12.創新與創意表現 13.廣告創意與案例分析 14.事件行銷與案例分析 15.數位行銷與案例分析 16.期中評量 本課程無涉及 AI 使用 Not applicable 課程相關連接 Course Related Links

docs.name: 統計學一
docs.text: National Tsing Hua University College of Technology Management Course Syllabus 科號 Course Number 11410IPMT2008 00 學分 Credit 3 人數限制 Size of Limit 30 中文名稱 Course Title 統計學一 英文名稱 Course English Title Statistics (I) 任課教師 Instructor 賴怡君 教師聯絡方式 Contact Information Email: lai-ic@mx.nthu.edu.tw 上課時間 Time MnM5M6 上課教室 Room TSMC 台積 429 先修科目 Prerequisite(s) 無 本課程對應之學習目標與核心能力 Aligned Learning Goals and Learning Objectives ▪ 學習基礎統計學知識。 Learn foundational knowledge in statistics. ▪ 培養數據統整、處理及分析能力。 Develop skills in data integration, processing, and analysis. ▪ 應用統計方法解讀商業狀況及提出商業洞察。 Apply statistical methods to interpret business situations and provide business insights. 課程目標 Course Objectives ▪ 本系列課程預計包含兩學期，第一學期會以統計學基礎概念為主，並輔以課堂小 組討論，透過實際資料操作，實踐應用統計學解決商業問題的目標。 This course is part of a two-semester series. The first semester focuses on basic statistical concepts, complemented by group discussions. Through hands-on data manipulation, the course aims to apply statistical methods to solve business problems. ▪ 第一學期會協助同學自行下載公開資料、選擇商業問題，涵蓋部分基礎資料操作 (Excel)，並思考適合應用於該商業問題的統計方法。 In the first semester, students will be guided to download publicly available data, select a business problem, perform basic data operations (Excel), and determine the appropriate statistical methods for the identified business problem. ▪ 第二學期進入較多的 Python 操作，完成整個資料前處理、統計處理流程，最後 進行結果分析。 In the second semester, students will focus more on Python for data processing, covering the entire process from data preprocessing to statistical analysis, and results interpretation. 課程說明 Course Description ▪ 作業繳交以小組為單位，第一學期小組討論總共會有四次，每次一小時；過程中 教師會逐一至每一小組了解討論狀態並反饋，協助小組完成任務。 Assignments will be submitted by groups. There will be four group discussions in the first semester, each lasting one hour. Throughout these sessions, the instructor will approach each group to understand their discussion progress and provide feedback to help complete the tasks. ▪ 期中期末考試以個人為單位，試卷內容涵蓋部份模擬資料表，同學以資料表和所 National Tsing Hua University College of Technology Management Course Syllabus 學統計概念為工具，回答試卷問題。 Midterm and final exams will be individual assessments. The exam will include a simulated data table, and students will use the data table and statistical concepts learned in class to answer the exam questions. 課程關鍵字 Course Keywords 統計學、數據分析、量化方法、機率與統計、假設驗證 Statistics, Data Analysis, Quantitative Methods, Probability and Statistics, Hypothesis Testing 指定用書 Textbooks Lind, D. A., Marchal, W. G., & Wathen, S. A. (2021). Basic Statistics in Business and Economics (10th ed.). McGraw-Hill Education. ISBN: 978-1260597578. 參考書籍 References 教學方式 Teaching Approach ▪ 課程包含授課與小組討論，小組討論共四次，每次一小時；小組討論目的為實際 下載公開資料、剖析資料結構，並規劃如何應用統計方法解析資料並解決商業問 題。 The course includes lectures and group discussions, with a total of four group discussions, each lasting one hour. The purpose of these group discussions is to practically download public data, analyze their structure, and plan how to apply statistical methods for data analysis and solving business problems. ▪ 第一學期以統計概念和基礎資料處理為重點(使用 Excel)，第二學期將涵蓋 Python 操作。 The first semester focuses on statistical concepts and basic data handling (using Excel), while the second semester will cover Python programming. 評分標準 Grading ▪ 小組作業 3 次：30% (分別於 Week7, Week 12, Week14 繳交) 3 Group Assignments: 30% (submitted in Week 7, Week 12, and Week 14) ▪ 小組成員互評：10% Peer Evaluation within Group: 10% ▪ 期中考試：30% Midterm exam: 30% ▪ 期末考試：30% Final exam: 30% 教學進度 Course Schedule ▪ Week 1: Course Introduction ▪ Week 2: Data Types and Data Structure ▪ Week 3: Descriptive Statistics ▪ Week 4: Descriptive Statistics & Group Workshop I: Select and download open-source data for the semester and discuss the business problems to be addressed. ▪ Week 5: Probability Concepts ▪ Week 6: Discrete Probability Distributions ▪ Week 7: Continuous Probability Distributions & Group Workshop II: Explore the dataset variables, the variables to be used, and the reasons for the selection. National Tsing Hua University College of Technology Management Course Syllabus ▪ Week 8: Midterm exam (covering Week 2 to Week 7 content) ▪ Week 9: Sampling and Sampling Methods ▪ Week 10: Estimation and Confidence Intervals ▪ Week 11: Hypothesis Tests ▪ Week 12: Hypothesis Tests & Group Workshop III: Discuss the statistical methods to be used and the rationale behind them. ▪ Week 13: Analysis of Variance ▪ Week 14: Correlation and Linear Regression & Group Workshop IV: Predict the expected results using the selected statistical methods. ▪ Week 15: Multiple Regression Analysis ▪ Week 16: Final exam (covering Week 2 to Week 15 content) 採用下列何項 AI 使用規則 (Indicate which of the following options you use to manage student use of the AI) (2)有條件開放：同學可使用 AI 協助學習，在繳交作業時並註明應用 AI 工具在哪些地 方。期中期末考試不開放應用 AI 工具，讓老師評估每位同學的實際學習狀況。 (2) Conditionally open: Students are allowed to use AI tools to assist with learning. When submitting assignments, students must indicate how AI tools were applied. AI tools will not be allowed during midterm and final exams, so the instructor can accurately assess each student's actual learning progress. 課程相關連接 Course Related Links 國立清華大學 eLearn 數位學習平台 elearn.nthu.edu.tw

Do not infringe copyrights.] Topics in Management and Technology (管理與科技專題) Interdisciplinary Program of Management and Technology (IPMT) College of Technology Management, National Tsing Hua University Course Credit: 2 Class Time: 15:30-17:20, Tuesday Session Location: TSMC Building 224 TA: TBA Instructor: Tonny Menglun Kuo, Ph.D. (郭孟倫) Office: Rm. 617, TSMC Building Tel: (03)571-5131 ext. 42248 Email: tonny@gapp.nthu.edu.tw Office Hours: By appointment 課程概述 Course description 科技的觸角，正無聲地探入管理的殿堂，它們的相遇，將譜寫出怎樣的未來序曲？在新 竹這片科技沃土就學的你，是否洞悉科技產業瞬息萬變的前瞻議題？近三年來，有哪些新興 科技被運用在產業中？當科技被應用到不同領域(如：行銷、財務、法律、生產、研發、供應 鏈)，管理思維會發生哪些改變？這門課會是你走進這些議題的敲門磚。 本課程由科管院莊慧玲教授發起，目的在於幫助學生了解未來世界的科技變遷與產業發 展。在這門課中，我們設計豐富多元的學習活動，包含書報討論、企業參訪、專題講座、學 長姐採訪、個案討論、小組新興科技報告等。課程不僅著眼於拓展你對產業的宏觀視野，更 希冀能助你精雕細琢未來的履歷，從容銜接企業的真實運營。 課程目標 Course objectives 上過這門課程後，學生將能夠： § 辨別科技產業所面臨的管理議題，並提出前瞻的解決策略。 § 比較學術與實務上的差異，準備好自己的認定(目標定位)與在就業市場的履歷。 § 探索近年的新興科技，預想這些科技如何改變我們的未來工作與生活。 § 分析自己有興趣就業的產業，並與同學分享對於產業的分析與觀察。 docs.text: NATIONAL TSING HUA UNIVERSITY College of Technology Management Interdisciplinary Program of Management and Technology Human Resource Management (Offered in English) Fall Semester 2025 Professor: Hua-Wei Hung (hwhung@mx.nthu.edu.tw) Teaching Assistant: Pei-Hua (Luna) Tung (tungpeihua0403@gmail.com) Time: Monday 14:20-17:00 (M6M7M8) Classroom: TSMC building Room#406 Office hours: Please email to make an appointment Course Objectives: This course explores HR's central, strategic role in making organizations competitive. This course focuses on the concepts and practices of human resource management, namely recruitment and selection of employees, equal opportunity, training and development, performance appraisals, compensation, and benefits issues. A special focus on the increase of globalization and workforce diversity in the high-performance organization is also included. By the end of this course, students should be able to: 1) Describe the functions of HR management. 2) Provide examples of the new management practices that are changing HR management. 3) Illustrate how building employee commitment can be a cornerstone of an employer's HR philosophy. 4) Present the basic processes for: developing job specifications; recruiting, interviewing, and placement of employees; compensation and benefits plans; and conducting performance appraisals. 5) Outline the organization's role in the career management process. 6) Explain employee mobility. 7) Understand the impact of globalization on HR management. Teaching Arrangements: Class sessions may include lectures and small and large discussion groups. We will strive to clarify, supplement, and analyze text materials. You are responsible for all assigned readings and all materials presented in class. You are also responsible for all information disseminated in class and all course requirements, including deadlines. Lectures: Each lecture is about 1.5 hours. Please note that all lectures will be taught in English. Topic Presentation (30 minutes): • Presentation (20 minutes): All students will come up with topics they are interested in related to human resources. Some potential topics include how to write a resume, how to write a cover letter, how to dress professionally, how to prepare for an interview, MBTI, etc. • Each group will present fruitful information on this topic that helps deepen the understanding of this topic, some key indications, managerial inspiration, and/or any other issues that you want to share with the class. • Activity (10 minutes): Each group will prepare a small activity to allow interaction with audiences that is related to your topic, be creative. Case Presentation (30 minutes): • Case presentation (20 minutes): Each group will choose a case to present in class, which should include the content and solution of a specific managerial situation. Please upload your case presentation 10 pm before the day you are presenting, so the group preparing to ask questions will have time to review your material. • Q&A (10 minutes): Other groups must prepare at least three questions to discuss with the presenting group. Guest Speaker Reflection • Students are required to write a reflection (1-2 pages) that captures their personal learning and critical thinking about the talk. Your reflection should go beyond simply summarizing the talk - it should demonstrate engagement with the ideas presented and connect them to your own knowledge, experience, or future aspirations. • In addition, attendance will be taken at the start of the invited talk. You must be present for the entire session to be eligible to submit your reflection, unless you have notified me in advance and received approval for your absence. Midterm Individual Essay: • Think of a company/job that you wish to go to in the future. • Conduct research on the company’s corporate culture. What kind of talent are they looking for? What is the job design and description of the position you want to apply for? What are your interview strategies to highlight your value? • Develop a one-page company overview (be concise and to the point), a one-page cover letter, a two-page statement of purpose, and one page with 3 expected interview questions and how you would respond (scoring depends on depth of response). • Conditional accept: AI only when the AI screenshot report is attached, which will also affect the grading. Final Group Presentation (30 minutes): • Select two companies from the same industry. Analyze the characteristics of their HRM and what they need to do to find the right people (their HRM strategies). Analyze how their HRM strategies are different (what aspects are the same and what is different). What are the current operational strengths and weaknesses and how can they be improved (learn from other companies in the same industry)? Final Group Report: • In addition to an oral presentation, a printed paper report must also be submitted. This report will put your presentation into words and should be between 8 and 14 pages. • If AI is utilized, screenshots of conversations with the AI must be included. • APA format: 12 font Times New Roman, 1/1.5 leading, PDF file. • No plagiarism; shall also attach with the Turnitin report (acceptable similarity percentage: below 15%) (please register in advance through NTHU Library: https://learning.site.nthu.edu.tw/p/412- 1319-7120.php?Lang=en) • Conditional accept: AI only when the AI screenshot report is attached, which will also affect the grading. Assessment: • Class Participation: 10%, Case Presentation: 15%, Topic Presentation: 15%, Guest Speaker Reflection: 5%, Midterm Individual Essay: 30%, Final Group Presentation: 10%, Final Group Report: 15%. • Assessing materials are required to be uploaded on eeclass in advance, with less tolerance for additional adjustment/improvement after the deadline (need to be discussed). Audience Scoring will be conducted in class, with group-based scoring from other groups to value each criterion; Peer Scoring will be managed within a group, and each group member will evaluate teammates’ contributions individually. No roll-call in class, therefore you get your participation by speak-up during class, or you may also share your ideas on eeclass. • Sometimes there will be spontaneous pop-up quizzes. Pop-up quiz: this quiz will cover the materials taught in the previous lectures, the top three students who get the highest score will get cards, which will count towards the participation (1st get three cards, 2nd get two cards, and 3rd get 1 card). Nick Wu National Tsing Hua University College of Technology Management Course Syllabus This course focuses on the management and improvement of supply chain processes and performance, providing a comprehensive foundation for students interested in pursuing a career in various sectors, including consulting, operations, marketing, or finance within manufacturing or distribution firms. Throughout the course, we will delve into essential supply chain metrics that are critical for assessing performance and making informed decisions. Students will learn about the primary trade-offs involved in supply chain decision-making, equipping them with the analytical skills necessary to navigate complex scenarios. Basic tools for effective and efficient supply chain management will be introduced, covering key areas such as production planning, inventory control, order fulfillment, and supply chain coordination. In addition to these foundational elements, we will explore advanced topics that are increasingly relevant in today’s global marketplace. This includes global supply chain design, where students will learn how to strategically structure supply chains to optimize efficiency and responsiveness. We will also examine logistics and outsourcing strategies, discussing how companies can leverage external partnerships to enhance their supply chain capabilities. Furthermore, the course will investigate several recent innovations in supply chain management, including the integration of technology and data analytics, which are transforming traditional practices and driving competitive advantage. By the end of this course, students will have gained a robust understanding of the complexities of supply chain management and will be well-prepared to apply their knowledge in real-world settings, docs.text: 1 NATIONAL TSING HUA UNIVERSITY International Business Bachelor Program 11410IPMT300900 ESG and Social Innovation (Offered in English) Fall Semester 2025 Lecturer: Ari Chen (caoiaoi@gmail.com) Time: Tuesday 13:20-16:20 (M5M6M7) Classroom: TSMC building, R121 Office hours: By appointment Teaching Assistant: Course Objectives: With the setting of SDGs (sustainable development goals) by the United Nations General Assembly in 2015, corporations have been motivated to change the way they operate their businesses, and have started to emphasize their contributions towards a better society and the environment. Along with the global announcement of the ESG (Environmental, Social, Governance) trend, hybrid business organizations are an emerging phenomenon that adopts market strategies to solve social and environmental issues. Social innovation has increasingly attracted academic and practical attention for its contribution to global sustainability. Various innovative collaboration and business models have been constructed to deliver social and business value. One of the key trends in the fast development of social innovation worldwide has been the rise of the third sector and hybrid organizations such as social enterprises. This course is designed for undergraduates who find interest in ESG and social innovation issues and, would like to extend their understanding with in-depth study of related concepts (ESG, CSR, social innovation, social enterprise, Benefit corporation, net zero carbon emission). Also, this course is expected to provide basic guidance for those who consider a sustainability-related job position as their potential future career. This course aims to introduce students to the concepts, theories, tools, and insights necessary for sustainability construction, social innovation, and social entrepreneurship. By the end of this course, students should be able to: 1) Elaborate on the nature of ESG-related concepts and topics 2) Understand the international standard and legitimacy of global ESG construction 3) Provide examples of the international/local management practices of ESG 4) Explain how globalization/localization features (dis) empower ESG 2 5) Illustrate how social innovation is being constructed through social entrepreneurship 6) Outline the relationship between social innovation and ESG 7) Present basic ideas of social innovation practice through fieldwork Weekly Modules Week Date Lecture (13:20-15:00) Key Reading (Chapters) Case Discussion (15:20-16:20) 1 09/02 Course Introduction (Kick-off) 2 09/09 Introduction to ESG: Foundations & Differentiators 1 - 3 09/16 Environmental Factor Deep Dive 4 - 4 09/23 Carbon Management Case A 5 09/30 Environmental Sustainability and Challenges Case B 6 10/07 The Pathways to Decarbonizing Key Sectors 16 Case C 7 10/14 ESG Board Game Activity 8 10/21 Midterm Individual Essay (No-class) 9 10/28 Social Factor Deep Dive 5 Case D 10 11/04 Corporate Role and Social Innovation 6 Case E 11 11/11 Governance Factor Deep Dive Case F 12 11/18 ESG Metrics and Standards 7-9 Midterm sharing 13 11/25 Financial Sector and Stakeholder Ecosystem 11-13 Final Project Initiation 1 14 12/02 Future Trends and Challenges in ESG Final project initiation 2 15 12/09 Future Career Training for Sustainability (Entrepreneur Support, Job Position, Certification, Practical skill) 16 12/16 Final Project Presentation (Discussion, Future for ESG, Wrap-up) Teaching Arrangements: Class sessions may include lectures and small and large discussion groups. We will strive to clarify, supplement, and analyze text materials. You are responsible for all assigned readings and all materials presented in class. You are also responsible for all information disseminated in class and all course requirements, including deadlines. Lectures: Each lecture is 1.5 hours. Please note, all lectures will be taught in English. 3 ● The lecture will be delivered in a highly interactive way, speak-up and idea-sharing/discussion is always welcoming through lecturing, which is also counted as class participation. Case Discussion (40 minutes): ● Case presentation (20 minutes): one group will be assigned a case to present in class, which should include the content and solution of a specific managerial situation in sustainability development. Each group will need to introduce the topic and address the discussion issue accordingly. ● Case discussion (20 minutes): The discussion is open to the audience, adding up valuable comments, insight, debate, and discussion that help deepen the understanding of the case. Case Topic Study Target Insights and Discussion Case A Carbon Management The significance of ESG in shaping modern business practices • Explore different products carbon footprint. • Analyze the lifecycle of various products and their carbon hotspots • How can carbon offsets complement product lifecycle emissions reductions? Case B Greenwashing • Case C High-Tech in Sustainability Introduce one High-tech adoption case to sustainability development • Introduce how AI/Big data/Blockchain or other High-tech adoption in sustainability practice • How High-tech adoption helps sustainability development? • What’s next? Predict the future trend. Case D Social Enterprise and Social Entrepreneurship Introduce one foreign social enterprise and one local social enterprise • Introduce the initiative of the social enterprises, and how they operate, how they benefit society. • What is the potential risk they are facing? • Comparing the similarities and differences of social enterprises. Case E Social Innovation Introduce one social innovation case • Explain how the social innovation occurs, what the actors involved, how the actors collaborate, and how actors benefit from the social innovation. • Demonstrate what are the key factors that (dis)empower the social innovation to expand. Case F Benefit Corporation Introduce one B Corp company • Introduce the initiative of the company, and how it operates, how it benefits society. • Explain how it did well on each B-Corp assessment. • Elaborate how it manage hybridity (business and social conflicts) in internal management. Case Circular Economy Introduce one Circular Economy Case • Introduce the initiative of the circular economy case, and how it operates, how it benefits society. • What is the potential risk it is facing? Do not infringe copyrights.] Marketing Management: Service, Technology & Innovation (行銷管理：整合服務、科技與創新) Interdisciplinary Program of Management and Technology (IPMT) College of Technology Management, National Tsing Hua University Course credit: 3 Class Time: 14:20-17:20, Wednesday Session Location: TSMC Building 223 TA: TBA Instructor: Tonny Menglun Kuo, Ph.D. (郭孟倫) Office: Rm. 617, TSMC Building Tel: (03)571-5131 ext. 42248 Email: tonny@gapp.nthu.edu.tw Office Hours: by appointment Course Description In a world where digital innovation evolves at lightning speed, marketing has become more than just product promotion—it’s about designing experiences, telling compelling stories, and leveraging emerging technologies. This course equips undergraduate students with a solid foundation in marketing strategy, covering essential topics such as STP (Segmentation, Targeting, Positioning), branding, pricing, channel design, and integrated marketing communications (IMC). Beyond the fundamentals, students will explore how livestreaming, AR/VR, chatbots, generative AI, and blockchain technologies are transforming customer engagement. We will read and discuss cutting-edge conceptual papers and strategic frameworks to help shape a forward-thinking blueprint for the ever-evolving world of marketing. The course also addresses critical issues such as sustainability, trust-building, and corporate social responsibility (CSR), helping students understand marketing’s expanding role in both business and society. Through interactive lectures, case studies, hands-on workshops, authentic tasks, and a final team project, students will develop strategic thinking and creative agility to solve real-world marketing challenges—and gain the confidence to lead in the marketing landscape of tomorrow. Course Objectives After taking this course, students will be able to: 1. Understand and apply core marketing strategies such as the 4Ps, 7Ps, STP, customer value, and market orientation to develop customer-centric marketing plans. 2. Analyze consumer behavior and interpret marketing research data (qualitative and quantitative) to make evidence-based marketing decisions. 3. Design marketing strategies related to product lifecycle, brand management, pricing, and omnichannel promotion based on customer insights. 4. Evaluate and implement technological tools (e.g., AI, generative AI, chatbots, AR/VR) to enhance service design, customer experience, and relationship marketing. 5. Critically examine emerging marketing trends such as the Metaverse, NFTs, blockchain, and CSR to propose sustainable and value-driven marketing innovations. 2 Learning Methods The course combines different learning methods: Mini lectures, group discussions, case studies, invited speech, project-based learning. Class Policies § Attendance Policy: Missing two or more classes will result in an automatic failing grade (F) for this course. If you must be absent due to unavoidable circumstances, please notify me in advance. Excused absences will be considered on a case-by-case basis (e.g., medical leave with official documentation from a hospital). § Punctuality: Being late is disruptive to the learning environment and is therefore strongly discouraged. Please make every effort to arrive on time. § Academic Integrity: Any form of academic dishonesty—such as cheating, misrepresentation, or plagiarism—will result in a failing grade. Be sure to properly cite and acknowledge all sources to avoid unintentional plagiarism. There is zero tolerance for academic misconduct. § Communication: I welcome open communication. If you have questions, concerns, or simply want to talk about your learning, please don’t hesitate to reach out to me at any time. § Let’s enjoy this semester together! Looking forward to a meaningful and engaging journey with you all. docs.text: 1 NATIONAL TSING HUA UNIVERSITY College of Technology Management Interdisciplinary Program of Management and Technology Innovation Management (Offered in English) Fall Semester 2025 Professor: Hua-Wei Hung (hwhung@mx.nthu.edu.tw) Teaching Assistant: Pei-Hua (Luna) Tung (tungpeihua0403@gmail.com) Time: Thursday 14:20-17:00 (R6R7R8) Classroom: TSMC building, Room#309 Office hours: Please email to make an appointment Course Objectives: This course covers three main contents and objectives, each crucial for developing a comprehensive understanding of innovation and technology strategies in the modern business landscape. The first objective is to impart the abstract theories and systematic knowledge necessary for understanding innovation and technology strategies. This involves exploring fundamental concepts and frameworks that underpin technological innovation, including but not limited to disruptive innovation theory, technology adoption lifecycle, and strategic management of intellectual property. Students will gain a solid theoretical foundation that will enable them to analyze and develop effective strategies in various technological contexts. Secondly, the course aims to train students' thinking, questioning, and communication abilities through discussions and analyses of practical cases. This hands-on approach will expose students to real-world scenarios, challenging them to apply theoretical knowledge to complex business situations. Through case studies and interactive discussions, students will develop critical thinking skills, learn to ask insightful questions, and enhance their ability to communicate complex ideas effectively. This practical component bridges the gap between theory and application, preparing students for the challenges they may face in their future careers. Finally, the course is designed to cultivate students' team spirit and rapport, as well as their understanding of the relationship between industry practices and management theories. Through group projects and collaborative assignments, students will learn to work effectively in teams, mirroring the collaborative nature of modern business environments. Additionally, the course will emphasize the interconnectedness of academic management theories and real-world industry practices, helping students to develop a holistic view of the business world. This understanding will enable them to navigate the complexities of technological innovation in various organizational contexts and industries. 2 Teaching Arrangements: Class sessions may include lectures and small and large discussion groups. We will strive to clarify, supplement, and analyze text materials. You are responsible for all assigned readings and all materials presented in class. You are also responsible for all information disseminated in class and all course requirements, including deadlines. Lectures: Each lecture is 1 hour. Please note that all lectures will be taught in English. • The lecture will be delivered in a highly interactive way, and speaking up and idea- sharing/discussion are always welcome through lecturing, which is also counted as class participation. Book Review (30 minutes): • Book review sharing (25 minutes): Each group will be assigned to review one book at the beginning of the course, and share their review with the class during the discussion session. Each group will finish the book, and you will present feedback to the class, consisting of book summaries, key insights, managerial inspiration, and/or any other issues you want to share with the class. • Q&A (5 minutes): Other groups must prepare at least three questions to discuss with the presenting group. Innovation Case Analysis (30 minutes) • In this assignment, your group will select a real-world innovation to present - a successful breakthrough or a notable failure -and analyze it through innovation management concepts covered in this course. • The chosen innovation may be a product, service, process, or business model from any industry. It could be a disruptive game-changer like Tesla’s electric vehicle strategy, a widely adopted service like Netflix’s streaming model, or a high-profile failure like Google Glass or Juicero. • Your task is to investigate the story behind the innovation, evaluate the factors that influenced its outcome, and present your findings in a way that helps your classmates learn from its successes and challenges. Guest Speaker Reflection • Students must write a reflection (1-2 pages) that captures their learning and critical thinking about the talk. Your reflection should go beyond simply summarizing the talk - it should demonstrate engagement with the ideas presented and connect them to your own knowledge, experience, or future aspirations. • In addition, attendance will be taken at the start of the invited talk. You must be present for the entire session to be eligible to submit your reflection, unless you have notified me in advance and received approval for your absence. Midterm Project: • In this assignment, you will write an individual analytical essay (1-2 pages) comparing two companies in the same industry, one representing the traditional incumbent model (“old”) and the other representing the disruptive challenger (“new”). • Your goal is to examine how the disruptive company changed the competitive landscape and challenged the incumbent’s market position, using innovation management concepts from this course. 3 Final Project Presentation: • In this assignment, your group will select two companies from the same industry and compare their most recent Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) or Sustainability Reports. While reviewing the reports, focus on the areas each company emphasizes most —stakeholder engagement, environmental sustainability, employee safety, diversity and inclusion, or community development. • Your analysis should go beyond identifying differences in emphasis. You should examine how each company’s CSR priorities influence or align with its innovation strategy. Consider questions such as: • Are CSR commitments leading to new products or services (e.g., eco-friendly product lines, inclusive design)? • Is CSR driving process innovations (e.g., sustainable manufacturing, energy efficiency, waste reduction)? • Does the company use CSR as part of its business model innovation (e.g., circular economy models, social enterprises)? • How do CSR-driven innovations contribute to competitive advantage or differentiation in the market? Final Group Report: • In addition to an oral presentation, a printed paper report must also be submitted. This report will put your presentation into words and should be between 8 and 14 pages. • If AI is utilized, screenshots of conversations with the AI must be included. • APA format: 12 font Times New Roman, 1/1.5 leading, PDF file. • No plagiarism; shall also attach with the Turnitin report (acceptable similarity percentage: below 15%) (please register in advance through NTHU Library: https://learning.site.nthu.edu.tw/p/412- 1319-7120.php?Lang=en) • Conditional accept: AI only when the AI screenshot report is attached, which will also affect the grading. 4 Assessment: This course consists (but is not limited to) the following assessments: Class Participation 10%, Book Review 15%, Innovation Case Analysis 15%, Guest Speaker Reflection 5%, Midterm Project 30%, Final Group Presentation 10%, Final Group Report 15%. Assessing materials must be uploaded on eeclass in advance, with less tolerance for additional adjustment/improvement after the deadline (need to be discussed). Audience Scoring will be conducted in class, with group-based scoring from other groups to value each criterion; Peer Scoring will be managed within a group, and each group member will evaluate teammates’ contributions individually. No roll-call in class, random call is included in class participation, once one fails to answer random calls up to four times, they will be failed. docs.text: National Tsing Hua University College of Technology Management Course Syllabus 科號 Course Number 11410IPMT3013 00 學分 Credit 3 人數限制 Size of Limit 50 中文名稱 Course Title 科技價值鏈管理：專利策略與佈局 英文名稱 Course English Title Technology Value Chain Management: Patent Strategy and Portfolio Planning 任課教師 Instructor 賴怡君 教師聯絡方式 Contact Information Email: lai-ic@mx.nthu.edu.tw 上課時間 Time R2R3R4 上課教室 Room TSMC 台積 421 先修科目 Prerequisite(s) 無 本課程對應之學習目標與核心能力 Aligned Learning Goals and Learning Objectives ▪ 培養基礎專利知識。 Develop foundational knowledge in patents. ▪ 了解創新價值和創新保護的重要性，以及如何運用專利進行策略布局。 Understand innovation value and the importance of innovation protection, and how to apply patents for strategic positioning. ▪ 培養如何運用專利來追蹤技術和創新軌跡的概念。 Develop the concept of applying patents to track technology and innovation trajectories. 課程目標 Course Objectives ▪ 本課程為同學奠定專利的基礎知識，了解專利作為智慧財產權保護的一環，對創 新價值有何影響。 This course establishes a foundational understanding of patents, helping students recognize the role of patents as a form of intellectual property protection and their impact on innovation value. ▪ 除了創新價值的保護，並了解如何進行專利管理和佈局，以維持可持續的競爭 力。 In addition to understanding how innovation value is protected, students will learn how to manage and strategically position patents to sustain competitive advantage. ▪ 第二學期會有延伸課程，更深入進入應用專利資料庫進行技術和創新軌跡探索的 資料操作面。 A follow-up course in the second semester will explore hands-on data applications in greater depth, focusing on the use of patent databases to analyze technology and innovation trajectories. 課程說明 Course Description ▪ 課程包含授課與小組報告，報告以小組為單位；學期涵蓋兩次小組討論，每次一 小時。小組過程中教師會逐一至每一小組了解討論狀態並反饋，協助小組完成期 末報告。 The course consists of lectures and group projects. Reports will be submitted by groups. There will be two group discussion sessions during the semester, each lasting National Tsing Hua University College of Technology Management Course Syllabus one hour. During these sessions, the instructor will approach each group to understand their progress, provide feedback, and support them in completing the final project ▪ 期中報告以小組為單位，每組提案一企業（跨國企業為佳），作為期末報告的分 析標的。報告內容包含標的企業簡介、選擇該企業原因、預期會在期末分析的競 爭者。 The midterm report is group-based. Each group will propose one company (preferably a multinational enterprise) as the subject of analysis for the final project. The report should include a company overview, reasons for selection, and expected competitors to be analyzed in the final report. ▪ 期末報告以小組為單位，分析期中提案企業的專利管理策略；分析內容應包括但 不限於：企業核心技術、專利授權與策略聯盟、訴訟概況、主要競爭者（競爭者 地理分佈、競爭者技術佈局）、未來策略建議。 The final report is also group-based and should analyze the patent management strategy of the selected company. The analysis should include, but is not limited to: core technologies, patent licensing and strategic alliances, litigation status, key competitors (including their geographic distribution and patent strategies), and future strategic recommendations. ▪ 期中報告以投影片檔案繳交，期末報告包含口頭報告與投影片檔案繳交；檔案可 用傳統 PPT、或雲端製作轉 PDF 等形式。 The midterm report should be submitted as a slide deck. The final report includes both an oral presentation and submission of slides. Files may be submitted as traditional PowerPoint presentations or as cloud-based presentations exported to PDF. 課程關鍵字 Course Keywords 專利、智慧財產權、專利佈局、專利策略、創新價值 Patents, Intellectual Property, Patent Portfolio, Patent Strategy, Innovation Value 指定用書 Textbooks Gassmann, O., Bader, M. A., & Thompson, M. J. (2020). Patent Management: Protecting Intellectual Property and Innovation. Springer. ISBN: 9783030590086. 參考書籍 References United States Department of Commerce (2025). Patents and How to Get One: A Practical Handbook. Anson Street Press. ISBN: 9781023586078. 教學方式 Teaching Approach ▪ 課程包含授課與小組報告，報告以小組為單位；學期涵蓋兩次小組討論，每次一 小時。小組過程中教師會逐一至每一小組了解討論狀態並反饋，協助小組完成期 末報告。 The course includes lectures and group projects, with all reports completed in groups. There will be two group discussion sessions during the semester, each lasting one hour. During these sessions, the instructor will approach each group to observe their discussion progress, provide feedback, and assist in the development of their final report. ▪ 第一學期以奠定專利基礎知識和理解專利佈局策略為重點，第二學期後的延伸課 程將進一步應用專利資料庫進行技術和創新軌跡探索。 The first semester focuses on building foundational knowledge of patents and understanding strategic patent portfolio planning. A follow-up course in the second semester will further apply patent databases to explore technology and innovation National Tsing Hua University College of Technology Management Course Syllabus trajectories. 評分標準 Grading ▪ 小組期中報告(投影片檔案)：20% Group Midterm Report (slide deck): 20% ▪ 小組討論參與：20% Group Discussion Participation: 20% ▪ 小組成員互評：5% Peer Evaluation within Group: 5% ▪ 小組期末報告(口頭+投影片檔案)：55% Group Final Report (oral presentation + slide deck): 55% 教學進度 Course Schedule ▪ Week 1: 課程介紹 ▪ Week 2: 智慧財產權基礎概念：價值與權利 ▪ Week 3: 專利起草：如何撰寫專利；含分組案例解讀練習 ▪ Week 4: 專利保護策略：攻擊型與防禦型策略 ▪ Week 5: 專利保護策略：互補型策略 ▪ Week 6: 專利評估與估值 ▪ Week 7: 專利佈局管理 ▪ Week 8: 專利商業化與小組討論 I：期末標的企業選擇 ▪ Week 9: 專利商業化 ▪ Week 10: 大型組織內的專利處理流程 ▪ Week 11: 各產業專利管理 I ▪ Week 12: 各產業專利管理 II ▪ Week 13: 新科技環境中的專利管理 I ▪ Week 14: 新科技環境中的專利管理 II ▪ Week 15: 專利指標與小組討論 II: 期末報告研討 ▪ Week 16: 期末口頭報告 採用下列何項 AI 使用規則 (Indicate which of the following options you use to manage student use of the AI) (2)有條件開放：同學可使用 AI 協助學習，在繳交報告時應註明應用 AI 工具在哪些地 方，讓老師評估每位同學的實際學習狀況。 (2) Conditionally open: Students are allowed to use AI tools to assist with learning. When submitting reports, students must indicate how AI tools were applied, so the instructor can accurately assess each student's actual learning progress. 課程相關連接 Course Related Links 國立清華大學 eLearn 數位學習平台 elearn.nthu.edu.tw

docs.name: 光電子學一
docs.text: 11410IPT 514000 課程綱要表 課程名稱 (中文) 光電子學一 (英文) Photonics I 開課單位 電機系 授課教師 李依珊 課程代碼 IPT 5140 選課性質 ⎕必修■選修 學分數 3 開課年級 碩博 先修科目或先備能力 Prerequisites Electromagnetic theory 課程概述 本課程全面介紹光電子學與光子學的基本原理與實際應用。學生將深入探討光的 行為及其與物質的交互作用、各類光子元件的運作原理，以及這些元件在現代科技 中的整合應用。課程設計旨在為學生建立紮實的理論基礎與實作能力。 This course provides a comprehensive introduction to the fundamental principles and practical applications of optoelectronics and photonics. Students will explore the behavior of light and its interaction with matter, the operation of photonic devices, and the integration of these components in modern technologies. The curriculum is structured to build a strong foundation in both theoretical concepts and practical device operation. 課程目標 在課程結束時，學生將能夠： 1. 理解並應用光的基本性質包含傳播、發射與偵測的物理原理 2. 分析與建模主要光電子與光子元件的性能 3. 設計基礎的光子系統，用於光通訊、感測與訊號處理等應用 4. 解讀並運用各權威教科書所提供的理論架構 By the end of the course, students will be able to: 1. Understand and apply the physics of light propagation, emission, and detection 2. Analyze and model the performance of key optoelectronic and photonic devices 3. Design basic photonic systems for applications such as optical communication, sensing, and signal processing 4. Interpret and apply the theoretical frameworks provided by leading texts in the field 教科書 自編教材 lecture notes 參考書 1. Principles of Photonics, Liu, Jia-Ming, Cambridge University Press. 2. Optoelectronics and Photonics: Principles and Practices, Safa O. Kasap, Prentice Hall, ISBN10: 0201610876. 3. Fundamentals of Photonics, Bahaa E. A. Saleh and Malvin V. Teich, Wiley- Interscience, ISBN-10: 0471358320. 教學要點概述 講義編選 自己編寫 教學方法 ☑講授 ☑討論互動 評量方式 作業 Homework assignment 20% 出席 Attendance 10% 期中考 Midterm 35% 期末考 Final exam 35% 課程綱要 單元主題 單元綱要 (Week 1-4) 1 – Introduction to Photonics 2 - Optical Properties of Materials 3 - Optical Wave Propagation (Week 5-7) 4 - Optical Coupling 5 - Optical Interference 6 - Optical Resonance Midterm (Week 9-13) 7 - Optical Absorption and Emission 8 - Optical Amplification 9 - Laser Oscillation (Week 14-15) 10 - Optical Modulation 11 - Photodetection Optional Review of the Quantum theory Final 生成式人工智慧倫理聲明：禁止使用 經仔細考量後，本課程授課教師認為不宜於此門課程當中使用生成式人工智慧於課堂學習當 中。因本課程的內容於生成式 AI 中尚有諸多錯誤，且容易影響學生對基礎核心知識之判讀。 根據本校公布之佈的「大學教育場域 AI 協作、共學與素養培養指引」，本門課程採取禁止使 用，以下為相關的監管機制 修讀本門課程之學生應注意本門課不得繳交使用生成式人工智慧所產出的作業、報告或個人心 得。若經查核發現，教師、學校或相關單位有權重新針對作業或報告重新評分或不予計分。 修讀本課程之學生於選課時視為同意以上倫理聲明。 Unit I: Fundamentals of Photonics (Weeks 1–4) Week 1: Introduction to Photonics  What is photonics? Historical development  Overview of applications (telecom, sensors, imaging, quantum)  Basic EM theory of light Week 2: Wave Optics  Maxwell’s equations in dielectric media  Polarization, interference, and diffraction  Complex refractive index and absorption Week 3: Geometrical Optics and Gaussian Beams  Snell’s law, total internal reflection  Paraxial approximation  Gaussian beam propagation and beam quality Week 4: Light-Matter Interaction  Absorption, spontaneous and stimulated emission  Einstein coefficients  Optical gain and cross-sections Unit II: Optical Waveguides and Cavities (Weeks 5–6) Week 5: Optical Waveguides and Fibers  Planar and slab waveguides  Step-index and graded-index fibers  Dispersion, attenuation, and modes Week 6: Optical Resonators  Fabry-Pérot cavities  Quality factor (Q), finesse  Mode structure and losses Unit III: Optoelectronic Devices (Weeks 7–11) Week 7: Semiconductors and Band Structures  Direct vs. indirect bandgap  Effective mass, density of states  Carrier recombination and diffusion Week 8: Light Emitting Diodes (LEDs)  Radiative recombination  Internal and external quantum efficiency  Design considerations and materials (e.g., GaAs, InGaN) Week 9: Semiconductor Lasers  Gain medium and threshold condition  Laser diode structures: Fabry–Pérot, DFB, VCSELs  Temperature and current effects Week 10: Photodetectors  Photoconductors, p-n and p-i-n photodiodes  Avalanche photodiodes (APDs), SPADs  Responsivity, quantum efficiency, noise Week 11: Optical Modulators and Switches  Electro-optic, acousto-optic, and thermo-optic effects  Mach–Zehnder modulators  High-speed modulation Unit IV: Applications and Integration (Weeks 12–14) Week 12: Photonic Integrated Circuits (PICs)  SOI and III-V platforms  Passive and active components  Coupling, splitters, multiplexers Week 13: Photonic Systems and Applications  Fiber optic communications  LIDAR and biomedical sensing  Emerging applications (quantum photonics, neuromorphic) Week 14: Review, Projects, and Future Trends  Student presentations/project demos (optional)  Emerging research topics  Final review and Q&A

docs.text: 超快光學−課程大綱 (11410 IPT 543000, Ultrafast Optics) 一、課程說明(Course Description) 本課程旨在介紹超短(10-12~10-15 秒)雷射光脈衝之產生、量測、傳播、色散管理及其應 用。此一技術提供的超精密時間解析度可用以觀測前所未知的分子、准粒子短暫動態。 所產生之巨大亮度(>1023 W/cm2)足以突破原子基本引力，或驅動物質產生顯著之非線 性效應，從而獲得一系列新的(如中紅外光、極紫外光)同調光譜成份。本課程所需要的 背景知識為：傅立葉轉換、電磁平面波，並具備運用數學軟體(如 Matlab)之能力。 This subject is designed to introduce generation, measurement, propagation, dispersion management and applications of ultrashort (10-12-10-15 sec) laser pulses. The ultrahigh temporal resolution enabled by this technique can trace the fleeting dynamics of molecules or quasi particles. The gigantic peak intensity (up to 1023 W/cm2) can overrun the atomic force, or generate a series of new coherent spectral components (e.g. mid-infrared, extreme ultraviolet) by strong nonlinear interaction with materials. The prerequisites include Fourier transform, electromagnetic plane waves and the ability to conduct numerical simulation with package software (e.g. Matlab). 二、教科書(Text Book) 自編講義(Lecture slides, pdf files will be offered at the beginning of semester.) 三、參考書籍(References) Andrew Weiner, Ultrafast Optics, Wiley, 2009. (ISBN: 978-0-471-41539-8) 四、教學方式(Teaching Method) 開放式課程影片預習、隨堂討論及問答、課堂講授、團隊專題 (OpenCourseWare video preview, discussion and Q&A in class, lectures, group project) 五、教學進度(Syllabus) 1. Introduction and review (6 hours) 2. Active mode-locking (1 hour) 3. Light-matter interaction (5 hours) 4. Passive mode-locking (6 hours) 5. Pulse measurement by correlation techniques (4 hours) 6. Pulse measurement by FROG and SPIDER (4 hours) 7. Dispersion and dispersion management (5 hours) 8. Flexible topics on request (6 hours) 9. Term project in the form of group competition 六、成績考核(Evaluation) 教師考核(20%)，期中考(30%)，期末考(25%)，團隊專題(15%)，作業(10%) Instructor’s assessment(20%), midterm exam(30%), final exam (25%), group projects (15%), homework assignments (10%) 七、可連結之網頁位址(Useful links) 數位學習平台(E-learning)：eeclass.nthu.edu.tw 開放式課程(Open Course Ware)：ocw.nthu.edu.tw/ocw/index.php?page=course&cid=206& 八、生成式人工智慧使用規則(Generative Artificial Intelligence access rules) 本課程同意學生利用人工智慧(AI)進行協作或互學。根據本校公布之「大學教育場域 AI 協作、共學與素養培養指引」，本課程採取有條件開放，以下說明如何使用生成式 AI 於課程產出。 學生須於課堂作業或報告中的「標題頁註腳」或「引用文獻後」簡要說明如何使用生 成式 AI 進行議題發想、文句潤飾或結構參考等使用方式。若經查核使用 卻無在作業 或報告中標明，教師、學校或相關單位有權重新針對作業或報告重新評分或不予計分。 本門課授課教材或學習資料若有引用自生成式 AI，教師也將在投影片或口頭標注。 修讀本課程之學生 於選課時視為同意以上倫理聲明。

Gasvik, Kjell J, “ Optical Metrology ”, John Wiley Sons Ltd, 2002 2. Douglas B. Murphy, “Fundamentals of Light Microscopy and Electronic Imaging”, A John Wiley & Sons, Inc., 2001 3. Alexander H. Slocum, “ Optical Sensor systems”, Precision Machine Design chapter 4, Prentice-Hall, Inc. 1992 4. Alain C. Diebold, “ Handbook of Silicon Semiconductor Metrology”, Marcel Dekker, Inc., 2001 yku@itri.org.tw 5 Grading • Oral presentation and research report 40% Original idea & novel innovation are highly encouraged. • Final exam. 40% : lecture notes • Bonus points 20% : Presence & properly answering.

docs.nameEn: Deep Learning in Biomedical Optical Imaging
docs.text: National Tsing Hua University Fall 2023 11310IPT 553000 Deep Learning in Biomedical Optical Imaging Lecturer Prof. Hung-Wen Chen Email: hungwen@mx.nthu.edu.tw Course Overview In this course, you will learn: (1) the foundational knowledge of deep learning algorithms, build neural networks from scratch via Python, and furthermore get familiar with different frameworks such as Pytorch, Tensorflow, and Keras. (2) The principle of different biomedical optical imaging technologies will be introduced as well. Finally, (3) a final project on medical imaging is required. We also offer (4) the opportunities of earning free official certificates from Nvidia Deep Learning Institute and DeepLearning.AI from Coursera as well, which might be helpful for your future career development. Grading  Homework (35 %): Assignments to get familiar with basic deep learning programming.  Midterm (30 %): Basic concepts of deep learning and related mathematical derivation.  Final Project Presentation (20 %): A project presentation of a research paper related to the deep learning application in medical imaging and the code implementation of the  Creativity Report (15 %): A Provide a detailed analysis of your model implementation on a given image dataset.
