docs.text: 1 國立清華大學課程大綱 科號 Course Number 11410IPTH100800 學分 Credit 1 人數限制 Class Size 90 中文名稱 Course Title 生涯導航 英文名稱 Course English Title Career planning and life 任課教師 Instructor 常善媚 上課時間 Time 每週五，第 5, 6 堂 上課教室 Room 台達館 課程簡述（Course Description） 本課程旨在幫助同學探索生涯發展方向，規劃個人學習與職涯藍圖。課程內容涵蓋清華大學 各學院與學制介紹、學習壓力與情緒管理、自我能力與興趣評估，以及生涯與職涯規劃等主 題。同學將透過課堂討論、團體會談與個別會談，深入了解自身的學習需求與發展潛能。此 外，課程將協助同學評估學習成效，並透過期中與期末報告進行大學生涯的自我分析與反 思，最終制定具體的學習與職涯行動計畫，提升未來發展的自信與適應能力。 This course is designed to help students explore their career paths and plan their academic and professional development. It covers key topics such as an introduction to the colleges and academic programs at NTHU, stress and emotion management, self-assessment of skills and interests, and career planning. Through class discussions, group meetings, and individual consultations, students will gain a deeper understanding of their learning needs and personal growth potential. Additionally, the course guides students in assessing their progress and reflecting on their experiences through midterm and final reports. By the end of the course, students will develop concrete academic and career action plans, enhancing their confidence and adaptability for future challenges. 課程目標 (Course Objectives) 1. 認識清華各學院系所，規劃學習藍圖 2 2. 了解自我與他人、學習壓力與情緒管理，建構生活藍圖 3. 評估自我的能力與興趣，規劃未來學習，策畫學業藍圖 4. 學習生涯規劃、職涯探索，架構人生藍圖 By the end of this course, students will be able to： 1. have a basic understanding of all the departments of NTHU 2. learn stress management and emotion regulation, and know themselves and others better 3. assess their own competency and interests and design their learning plan accordingly 4. plan and explore their potential career 欲培養之核心能力 (Core capability to be cultivated by this course) 1. 培養社會關懷與同理心 （Developing social concern and empathy.） 2. 社會變遷因應能力（To adapt to social change） 3. 生活實踐能力（To practice） 4. 跨領域能力（To cross disciplinary boundaries） 課程內容 (Course Content) ● 關鍵字(Course keywords) 生涯規劃 (Career Planning)、自我評估 (Self-Assessment)、學習藍圖 (Learning Roadmap)、職涯探索(Career Exploration)、情緒管理 (Emotion Management) ● 課程大綱 (Detailed Course Syllabus) Topic 1 課程簡介&介紹清華學院學士班教育宗旨 Philosophy and goals of Tsing Hua Interdisciplinary Program 2 關於領域探索與選課原則，我要說的是… About the exploration of different fields and principles of course selection, I am going to tell you… 3 3 學生常用校園資源介紹 Introduction of resources for students on campus 4 清華學院相關學制介紹 (延後分流、實驗教育、客制化學習) Introduction of different academies in Tsing Hua College (postponed tracking, Experimental Education, Customization Learning) 5 學院介紹：理學院、藝術學院 Introduction of colleges: Science & Arts 6 學院介紹：工學院、生科院 Introduction of colleges: Engineering and Life Science 7 學院介紹：人社院、原科院 Introduction of colleges: Humanities Social Sciences and Nuclear Science 8 學院介紹：電資院、教育學院 Introduction of colleges: Electrical Engineering and Computer Science & Education 9 學院介紹：科管院 Introduction of colleges: Technology Management 學習藍圖評估與再規劃 (期中報告) Evaluation of learning plan and re-organization 10 團體會談(1) Group Meetings (1) 11 團體會談 (2) Group Meetings (2) 12 團體會談 (3) Group Meetings (3) 13 個別會談 (1) individual meeting (1) 14 個別會談 (2) individual meeting (2) 15 個別會談 (3) individual meeting (3) 16 期末報告：大學生涯自我分析報告 4 Final presentation: self-evaluation of college years ● 指定用書與課堂材料(Textbook and Course Materials) 本課程主要使用授課老師自行編排的講義與學習單。 This course primarily uses instructor-prepared handouts and learning worksheets. ● 推薦書目與參考資料 (Recommended Books and Reference) 比爾, 柏內特, 戴夫, & 埃文斯. (2016)。 做自己的生命設計師: 史丹佛最夯的生涯規畫課, 用 [設計思考] 重擬問題, 打造全新生命藍圖 (Vol. 135). 大塊文化。 許郁文譯 (2021)。發現你的天職：三大步驟，讓你選系、就業、轉職或創業不再迷惘。台 北: 如何。 ● 教學方式 (Teaching Method) 講述法、小組討論、情境演練 Lecture, Group discussion, Scenario-based exercises ● 成績考核 (Evaluation) 1. 出席率：出席率佔學期成績之 10%。 2. 課堂參與：包含課堂中進行的活動、討論的參與，該堂課未到則無法獲得課堂參與分數， 課堂參與佔學期成績之 25%。 3. 團體會談一次：請於學期結束之前於老師 office hour 時間約一次會談，會談以團進團出 的方式進行，與老師預約會談需於一周前報名。團體會談佔學期成績之 15%。 4. 期中報告：「我的能力與喜好的自我評估」，請依照老師上課時說明的方式進行撰寫。期 中報告佔學期成績之 20%。 5. 期末報告：心得請依據上課內容撰寫，並以三個問題為主要撰寫大綱：（一）我的大學生 活目標為何？（二）我要用什麼方式達到這個目標？（三） 我擁有或可創造什麼資源來 達到這個目標？心得繳交方式為書面報告，至少 1500 字。期末報告佔學期成績之 30%。 Requirements: 1. Attendance (10/100): Attendance accounts for 10% of the semester grade. 5 2. Class Participation (25/100): This includes participation in activities and discussions during class. If a class is missed, participation points for that class cannot be earned. Class participation accounts for 25% of the semester grade.Group Meetings (15/100): Please schedule a group meeting with the instructor once during the semester. Each meeting should be scheduled before one week. 3. Midterm Assignment (20/100): Please complete the "Self-Assessment of Personal Competency and Interests" as instructed in class. 4. Final Report (30/100): The wrap-up is based on the content of the lectures. It is necessary to write this report with three questions as an outline. First, what is my goal during the study period? Second, what should I do to achieve this goal? Third, what resources can I find or create to achieve the goal? The final report should be submitted as a Word or PDF file and should be no less than 2 pages (A4) (minimum 1500 words). ● AI 使用規則 (Indicate which of the following options you use to manage student use of the AI) 本課程允許有條件使用 AI。學生在提交作業時，必須明確說明如何在課程產出中使用生成 式 AI，並提供與 AI 互動的記錄或連結。 學生使用 AI 的規範： AI 的使用需符合特定條件。學生必須清楚說明如何在課程產出中使用生成式 AI。更多詳情 請參閱 《大學教育場域 AI 協作、共學與素養培養指引》。 網站：https://ctld.nthu.edu.tw/var/file/217/1217/img/4991/712376723.pdf This course allows the conditional use of AI. When submitting assignments, students must specify how they used generative AI in their coursework and provide a record or link to their interactions with AI. AI Usage Guidelines for Students: AI use is permitted under certain conditions. Students must clearly state how they utilized generative AI in their coursework. For more details, please refer to the Guidelines for AI 6 Collaboration, Co-Learning, and Literacy Development in Higher Education. Website: https://ctld.nthu.edu.tw/var/file/217/1217/img/4991/712376723.pdf

docs.name: 視覺傳達設計
docs.text: 國立清華大學課程大綱 科號 Course Number 11410IPTH101100 學分 Credit 2 人數限制 Class Size 12 中文名稱 Course Title 視覺傳達設計 英文名稱 Course English Title Visual Communication Design 任課教師 Instructor 徐慈璟(HSU, TZU-CHING) 上課時間 Time M5M6 上課教室 Room EDU 教 103 課程簡述(必填) (最多 500 個中文字) 本欄位資料會上傳教育部課程網 Brief Course Description (required) (50-200 words if possible, up to 1000 letters) 創新設計思考：現今軟體學習管道多元，設計工具的方便容易讓人忽略設計思考的重要性。本課 程將以設計史切入，講述並探討各時期視覺傳達設計的角色、製作手法以及成效評估。並以設計 案例、實作的方式帶領同學，從概念發想、提出設計規劃到設計執行，以循序漸進的方式，培養 學生跨域整合的創意思維。 視覺規劃與執行能力：創新思維需透過有視覺溝通的技巧，方能獲得大眾的共鳴。因此在視覺規 劃與執行實務的能力需並進培養。期中將以專案方式，進行字型、系統規劃、符號以及資訊圖表 設計(Infographic design)等領域的練習。 行銷企劃能力：如何說個好故事，將會是未來重要的溝通能力。視覺傳達設計更可視為是一項利 器，透過課程規劃，藉由比較不同閱讀群體對視覺設計品的需求差異,幫助學生理解「設計不只 是美觀，更是溝通與服務」的核心。 課程內容「中文暨英文關鍵字」(必填) 至少 5 個,每個關鍵字至多 20 個中文,以半形逗點分隔 Please fill in at least 5 course keywords (up to 40 letters for each keyword) and use commas to separate them.(required) 平面設計進階，視覺傳達，五感創意，溝通同理，行銷服務 課程大綱(必填)Detailed Course Syllabus ● 課程說明(Course Description) 藉由課堂講述與實作練習，將具有平面設計基礎之學生，輔以視覺排版、介面差異做為設計進階 學習。除延續設計基礎概念，本課程將介紹不同閱讀族群與其閱讀需求的差異，進行相關視覺化 練習。作業安排的部分將以循序漸進的方式，先以自我觀察出發，設計自我履歷，再延伸至向外 關懷的方式，依不同閱讀需求設計，讓設計更能落實實際需求。 上課方式會以直接在教室討論實作，需能攜帶筆電或可進行編排之電子設備。 能於課堂使用 AI 輔助，但各項作業會再與同學確認採用範圍。 ● 指定用書(Text Books) ● 成績考核(Evaluation) ● 參考書籍(References) 1. Ellen Lupton、Jennifer Cole Phillips 著，2008，新平面設計原理 Graphic Design The New Basics， 龍溪 2. Ellen Lupton 著，2010，Thinking with Type: A Critical Guide for Designers, Writers, Editors, & Students?，Princeton Architectural Pr 3. 王受之/著，2000，世界現代平面設計，藝術家 ● 教學方式(Teaching Method) 學期評量： 平時出席 10% 平時作業 40% 期中發表與出席 20% 期末發表與出席 30% ● 教學進度(Syllabus) 周次 課程主軸 課堂作業 1 課程與學習目標介紹 2 字體進階：字體家族與可變字體 觀察日常印刷品的排版差異 同一段文字的三種字型使用 3 格線系統 觀察日常印刷品的排版 同一段文字的三種排版練習 4 實驗排版與解構主義（Postmodern） 同一段文字的三種排版練習 (老師提供文字) 5 跨媒體設計：數位與印刷差異 6 AI 與自動化排版工具 7 資訊設計與資料視覺化 以自我平時蒐藏品進行練習 8 期中提案討論 以自我履歷為主題，進行相關設計 9 期中作品展示 10 不同閱讀群體的排版應用(一)：兒童 觀察日常印刷品的排版並實作 11 不同閱讀群體的排版應用(二)：銀髮 觀察日常印刷品的排版並實作 12 不同閱讀群體的排版應用(三)：多語系 觀察日常印刷品的排版並實作 13 不同閱讀群體的排版應用(四)：文化與實驗 觀察日常印刷品的排版並實作 14 期末提案討論 選定一族群，發起一個活動 設計 A1 活動海報、A3 小廣告、 活動問卷設計、電子廣告設計 15 期末提案討論 16 期末作品展示 ● 採用下列何項 AI 使用規則(Indicate which of the following options you use to manage student use of the AI) (1) 有條件開放，請註明如何使用生成式 AI 於課程產出 Conditionally open; please specify how generative AI will be used in course output 可參考下列網頁範例 See the following web page for examples. https://curricul.site.nthu.edu.tw/p/404-1208-248357.php?Lang=zh-tw ● 可連結之網頁位址 相關網頁(Personal Website)

docs.name: 健康心理學
docs.text: 1 國立清華大學課程大綱 科號 Course Number 11410IPTH101600 學分 Credit 2 人數限制 Class Size 30 中文名稱 Course Title 健康心理學 英文名稱 Course English Title Health Psychology 任課教師 Instructor 常善媚 上課時間 Time 每週三，第 7, 8 堂 上課教室 Room 教育館 104 教室 Course Description(課程簡述) Health psychology is an interdisciplinary field that applies theories and concepts from psychology to the study of human well-being, illness, and healthcare. This course is designed to help students explore how psychology can be used to promote health while gaining insight into themselves, others, and their environment. By learning how psychology can improve health, students can better understand how to support their own well-being and that of others. 健康心理學被定義為一個跨領域的學門，它應用心理學的理論和概念於人類的幸福、疾病和醫療保 健相關研究。本課程幫學生了解如何應用心理學促進健康，同時深入了解自己、他人、與環境。經 學習從心理學的概念來改善健康的方式，學生可以更好地理解如何幫助自己和他人。 Course Objectives (課程目標) By the end of this course, students will be able to: 1. Explore how psychology influences and is applied to health care. 2. Understand the major psychosocial factors that contribute to health behaviors and the development of 2 disease. 3. Learn to apply their knowledge of psychology in the development, implementation, and evaluation of health programs. 4. Students will be able to assess their own health status and formulate their own health goals and health plans. 1. 探討心理學如何影響並應用於醫療保健。 2. 理解影響健康行為及疾病發展的主要心理社會因素。 3. 學習如何將心理學知識應用於健康計畫的制定、實施與評估。 4. 學生將能夠評估自身的健康狀況，並制定個人的健康目標與健康計畫。 Core capability to be cultivated by this course (欲培養之核心能力) 1. Attendance ➢ Pre-test: At the beginning of each week of the course, participants must answer five multiple- choice questions related to the content of the weekly preview. ➢ Worksheets: During the two-hour weekly class, participants will complete a worksheet. This worksheet must be turned in before the end of the course. 出席率 ➢ 課前測驗：每週課程開始時，學員需回答五道與當週預習內容相關的選擇題。 ➢ 學習單：在每週兩小時的課程中，學員需完成一份學習單，並於課程結束前提交。 6 1. Group discussion and participation Your attendance and participation are expected and will be documented. Much of the work in class involves collaboration and discussion, as human knowledge is socially constructed. You should contribute to the group work, raise your hands to share ideas and ask questions, and avoid using digital devices (e.g., cellphones, laptops, iPad, etc.) for reasons irrelevant to the class activities. You should make every effort to attend class and be on time, and you must be in the classroom for the entire time to receive full credit for the attendance. 小組討論與課堂參與 你的出席與參與是必要的，並將被記錄下來。課堂中的許多活動都涉及合作與討論，因為人類 的知識是透過社會互動建構而成的。你應積極參與小組討論，舉手發表意見並提出問題，並避 免使用與課程無關的數位設備（如手機、筆記型電腦、iPad 等）。你應盡力準時到課，並全程 參與課堂活動，才能獲得完整的出席與參與分數。 2. Midterm assignment ➢ Choose a topic from the second through eighth week topics and record a two-minute video. This video must contain two parts: The first part is to introduce your topic and share the main concepts from the course content, i.e., Like a YouTuber; the second part is for you to share your own experiences on the topic, your advice, or your goals and plans. In the video you can choose to show your face or not, but in addition to the sound, the video also contains video/pictures. ➢ You will upload the video to your "YouTube" and set public to share with other participants. (Please #HealthPsyNTHU) ➢ There are three important dates for the Midterm Report: - On 11/1 in class, you must turn in your midterm report topic. - You must upload your video before 11/8 11PM and shard your video address. - Before 11/14 at 11PM you must view everyone's videos and feedback. 期中作業 ➢ 選擇一個主題（從第二週至第八週的課程主題中選擇），並錄製一段 兩分鐘的影片。影 片需包含兩個部分： 第一部分：介紹你的主題，並分享與課程內容相關的核心概念，就像 YouTuber 一樣。 7 第二部分：分享你個人的相關經驗、建議，或你的目標與計畫。在影片中，你可以選擇是否 露臉，但除了聲音之外，影片還需包含影像或圖片。 ➢ 影片上傳： 請將影片上傳至 YouTube，並設定為公開，以便與其他同學分享。（請標記 #HealthPsyNTHU） ➢ 期中報告的三個重要日期： 11/1（課堂上）：需提交你的期中報告主題。 11/8 晚上 11 點前：需上傳影片並分享影片連結。 11/14 晚上 11 點前：需觀看所有同學的影片並提供回饋。 3. Final presentation and report ➢ The final presentation and report is a group report. The teacher divides the students into groups and lets each group choose the topic on which they want to make a report. The group members are determined by the teacher. Group assignments are determined after all students in the class have been identified. ➢ Each group is free to choose which topics related to health psychology they would like to explore. ➢ The oral presentation will be 20 minutes per group. After the oral report, a PPT file must be submitted. ➢ The content of the report must cite at least two research reports on the topic. ➢ Points will be calculated for the content of the report, detailed understanding of the research findings, and the contribution of each individual in the group. 期末報告與展示 ➢ 期末報告與展示為小組報告，由老師分組，並讓各組選擇報告主題。小組成員將由老師分 配，分組作業會在全班名單確定後進行。 ➢ 各組可自由選擇 與 健康心理學 相關的主題進行探討。 ➢ 口頭報告時間：每組報告時間為 20 分鐘。口頭報告結束後，需提交 PPT 檔案。 ➢ 報告內容要求：需引用至少兩篇 與主題相關的研究報告。 8 ➢ 評分標準：報告內容的完整性、對研究結果的深入理解，以及每位組員的貢獻，都將列入 評分標準。 ● Indicate which of the following options you use to manage student use of the AI (AI 使用規則) This course allows the conditional use of AI. docs.text: 1 國立清華大學課程大綱 科號 Course Number 11410IPTH101700 學分 Credit 3 人數限制 Class Size 30 中文名稱 Course Title 參與觀察與資料分析 英文名稱 Course English Title Participant Observation and Data Analysis 任課教師 Instructor 常善媚 上課時間 Time 每週二（7, 8, 9 節） 上課教室 Room 教育館 103 教室 課程簡述 (Course Description) 本課程旨在介紹田野研究與參與觀察法的核心概念與實務操作。課程將引導同學學習如何運用參與觀 察與訪談技巧，進入特定場域進行觀察、訪談並撰寫田野筆記。同時，課程將探討如何基於參與觀察 所得資料設計調查問卷，並嘗試分析不同類型的資料（如質性資料、量化數據、政府大型資料、社群 網站爬蟲資料等）。最後，課程將指導同學撰寫研究結果，培養綜合運用多種研究方法進行社會調查 與分析的能力。 This course introduces the fundamental concepts and practical applications of field research and participant observation methods. It guides students in using participant observation and interview techniques to enter specific research settings, conduct observations and interviews, and take field notes. Additionally, the course explores how to design survey questionnaires based on participant observation data and analyze various types of data, including qualitative and quantitative data, large-scale government datasets, and social media web- scraped data. Finally, students will learn how to synthesize and present their research findings, developing skills in integrating multiple research methods for social inquiry and analysis. 2 課程目標 (Course Objectives) 1. 了解田野研究與參與觀察的基本概念。 2. 練習參與觀察的資料蒐集。 3. 就感興趣的主題進行文獻查找與閱讀。 4. 進行所蒐集之質性與量性資料分析。 5. 進行研究結果撰寫的練習。 6. 探討參與觀察可能面臨的倫理議題。 1. understand the basic concepts of field studies and participant observation. 2. collect data through the method of participant observation. 3. conduct literature reviews on the topic of your interest. 4. analyze the quantitative and qualitative data collected. 5. practice writing up the results of the study. 6. explore the potential ethical issues of participant observation 欲培養之核心能力 (Core capability to be cultivated by this course) 1. 培養社會關懷與同理心 （Developing social concern and empathy.） 2. 社會變遷因應能力（To adapt to social change） 3. 生活實踐能力（To practice） 4. 慎思明辨能力（To think critically） 5. 跨領域能力（To cross disciplinary boundaries） 課程內容 (Course Content) ● 關鍵字(Course keywords) 參與觀察, 田野研究, 內容分析, 質性研究, 描述性統計 participant observation, field study, content analysis, qualitative research, descriptive statistics 3 ● 課程大綱 (Detailed Course Syllabus) No Topics Reading Homework 1 課程導讀與介紹 Introduction 2 參與觀察法的特徵與用途 Features and application of participant observation method Ch 1. 反思心得 1 3 參與者角色：既參與、又觀察 As a participant, we engage and observe Ch 2. 反思心得 2 4 田野在哪裡? docs.text: 科號 Course Number 11410IPTH102100 學分 Credit 3 人數限制 Class Size 20 中文名稱 Course Title 社會性農耕、身心健康與永續發展教育 英文名稱 Course English Title Social Farming, Well-being, and Sustainable Development Education 任課教師 Instructor 薛曉華 上課時間 Time 五 234 節 上課教室 Room 教育館教室、視需要前往南大校區 1319 教室與南大校區攬星農園 課程簡述(必填) (最多 500 個中文字) 本欄位資料會上傳教育部課程網 Brief Course Description (required) (50-200 words if possible, up to 1000 letters) 本課程聚焦於社會性農耕（Social Farming）、身心健康與永續發展教育的交叉領 域，探討農耕如何促進社會融合、心理健康與生態永續。課程將結合實作、理論與案例 分析，引導學生理解農耕如何成為社區共融、教育創新與生態保育的關鍵實踐。 本課程適合對農耕療癒、特殊教育、社會創新、環境教育感興趣的學生，將提供跨 學科的視角，並邀請相關領域的實踐者與專家進行分享，讓學生能夠在理論與實踐之間 建立連結。 課程目標 1、理解社會性農耕的概念與實踐：探討農耕如何促進身心健康、社會融合與教育發 展。 2、探索農耕與身心健康的關聯：分析農耕在心理治療、壓力管理、復健與社會情緒學 習（SEL）中的應用。 3、學習永續發展教育的策略：理解如何透過農耕培養學生的環境責任感與永續意識的 生活方式。 4、參與實作與田野研究：透過實地訪問、農場實作與課題探究，培養學生的觀察與行 動能力。 5、設計社會性農耕專案：學生將規劃設計一個小型的社會性農耕教育，並在學期末進 行發表。 本門課主要綜合了社會性農耕、身心健康與永續發展教育的核心理念，並透過跨領域的學習方 法，幫助學生從理論到實作，發展應用於教育與社會創新的能力。歡迎有志者協力同行！ 課程內容「中文暨英文關鍵字」(必填) 至少 5 個,每個關鍵字至多 20 個中文,以半形逗點分隔 Please fill in at least 5 course keywords (up to 40 letters for each keyword) and use commas to separate them.(required) 社會性農耕、學習農園、農療育、綠色照護、永續發展教育 Social Farming, Learning Farms, Therapeutic Agriculture, Green Care, and Sustainable Development Education 課程大綱(必填)Detailed Course Syllabus ● 課程說明(Course Description) 週次 主題 內容概述 第一部分：場域認識導覽 & 理念鋪陳~~大觀園 1. ( 9/5 ) 課程導論：課程架構與期待、學習目標；農園、幸福感、永續發展 2.( 9/12 )社會性農耕概念與發展：社會性農耕的歷史、案例與發展趨勢 3.( 9/19 )農耕與身心健康：農耕與心理健康，園藝療法與生態療癒,認識 24 節氣--秋分 4.( 9/26 )農耕與社會融合：弱勢群體（特殊需求者等）如何透過農耕參與社會 （國際與本土的案例尋旅） 5.( 10/3 )永續發展教育概論：聯合國 SDGs（永續發展目標）與農耕教育的關聯, 思考與實作具生態永續的中秋節慶 第二部分：社會性農耕/農場的實地體驗 & 案例探究~~故事篇 6. ( 10/10 ) 國慶假日 7. ( 10/17 ) 社會性農耕與自然實務體驗：農園的綠色療育體驗； 參與 10/18（六）大新竹食農嘉年華 8. (10/24 )臺灣光復節放假 9.( 10/31 )大學校園農耕與食農教育體驗：攬星農園的食農教育與節氣美學 10. ( 11/7 )田野走訪：大學校園農園的社會性農耕場域，走訪攬星農園 (11/7 立冬) 農耕與實踐者個別訪談：社會農耕、園藝療法、農場教育工作者分享經驗 11. ( 11/14 ) 校園農園案例研究：探討校園農園如何推動身心健康與永續教育 高峰國小、Kist 峨眉國中實踐故事 第三部分：方案與實踐~~創新設計篇 12. ( 11/21 )農耕教育設計工作坊：學生分組設計社會性農耕教育方案、融合理念解說 13.( 11/28 )方案設計：「幼兒、兒童組」「少年、青年組」社會性農園的初步構想 14.( 12/5 )方案設計：「成年熟齡組」「高齡長輩組」社會性農園的初步構想；手作湯圓 15.( 12/12 )期末設計發表會：各組報告設計方案與未來發展可能性 16. ( 12/19 )總結與課程回顧 學習反思與未來應用 教學方法： • 講授與討論：提供理論背景，並透過小組討論深化理解。 • 案例分析：分析國內外社會性農耕、食農教育與永續發展的實踐案例。 • 實作體驗：透過校園或社區農園的操作，讓學生親身參與農耕活動。 • 田野調查：參訪農場、社區計畫，與實踐者對話。 • 方案設計：學生需規劃設計一個小型的社會性農耕教育方案，並於期末發表。 評量方式 項目 比例 說明 課堂參與 20% 出席、討論表現與學習態度 田野調查報告 20% 參訪後撰寫反思報告 農耕實作紀錄 20% 參與實作與紀錄學習心得 期末專案 40% 設計並發表社會性農耕教育計畫 預期學習成果 1. 能夠解釋社會性農耕、身心健康與永續發展的關聯。 2. 能夠分析農耕如何應用於教育、心理健康與社會融合。 3. 能夠實作農耕相關活動，並紀錄與反思學習過程。 4. 能夠規劃設計小個小型的社會性農耕教育計畫，並評估其影響。 參考文獻 教師主編教材 成虹飛、薛曉華~~耕讀學堂相關研究 • Haubenhofer, D., Hassink, J., van der Meulen, H., & van den Berg, A. (2010). Benefits of Green Care Farms for Mental Health Recovery. Psychiatric Services. • Pretty, J. (2002). Agri-Culture: Reconnecting People, Land, and Nature. Earthscan. • Steiner, R. (1924). Agriculture Course. Biodynamic Farming and Gardening Association. • UN (2015). Sustainable Development Goals. United Nations. 採用下列何項 AI 使用規則(Indicate which of the following options you use to manage student use of the AI) (1) 有條件開放，請註明如何使用生成式 AI 於課程產出 Conditionally open; please specify how generative AI will be used in course output 可參考下列網頁範 例 See the following web page for examples. https://curricul.site.nthu.edu.tw/p/404-1208-248357.php?Lang=zh-tw ● 可連結之網頁位址 相關網頁(Personal Website)

docs.text: 國立清華大學課程大綱 科號 Course Number 11410IPTH205100 學分 Credit 9 人數限制 Class Size 中文名稱 Course Title 實驗教育實習專題 A 英文名稱 Course English Title Experimental Education Internship A 任課教師 Instructor 指導教授 上課時間 Time 每學年度學期間 每周實習五天。 上課教室 Room 實習單位 課程簡述(必填) (最多 500 個中文字) 本欄位資料會上傳教育部課程網 Brief Course Description (required) (50-200 words if possible, up to 1000 letters) 本課程依據學士班實驗教育方案審核通過之學習計畫書執行，學生需於修課前提交實習申請表 及計畫書。經相關單位審核通過後，方可修讀本課程。課程旨在促進學生將理論知識與實務經 驗相結合，培養綜合分析與解決問題的能力，並增強其在相關專業領域的實踐技能。 課程內容「中文暨英文關鍵字」(必填) 至少 5 個,每個關鍵字至多 20 個中文,以半形逗點分隔 Please fill in at least 5 course keywords (up to 40 letters for each keyword) and use commas to separate them.(required) 強化學生對職場環境的適應能力,培養獨立研究與解決問題的能力,學術理論與實務技術的綜合運 用,強化學生在特定領域的專業能力,培養學生的實務技能與職業素養 課程大綱(必填)Detailed Course Syllabus ● 課程說明(Course Description) 本課程讓學生在指導下進行專題研究，培養獨立研究與問題解決能力，並提升專業應用。 ● 指定用書(Text Books) 由教授指定。 ● 參考書籍(References) 由教授指定。 ● 教學方式(Teaching Method) 在實習單位進行為期四至六個月的實習，每週實習五個工作 天。實習內容以實習單位的安排為主，並需遵循指導教授及實習單位督導的指導。 ● 教學進度(Syllabus) 由教授指定。 ● 成績考核(Evaluation) 實習成績將由指導教授、授課教授及實習單位督導共同評定，該學期實習結束務必繳交實習 心得報告書。 *以上項目需於加簽提交專題課程大綱時，依規定敘明清楚。 ● 採用下列何項 AI 使用規則 (1) 完全開放使用且無須註明 Unrestricted use with no disclosure required (2) 有條件開放，請註明如何使用生成式 AI 於課程產出 Conditionally open; please specify how generative AI will be used in course output (3) 禁止使用，請註明相關的監管機制 Prohibited use; please specify relevant oversight (4) 本課程無涉及 AI 使用 Not applicable 可參考下列網頁範例 See the following web page for examples. https://curricul.site.nthu.edu.tw/p/404-1208-248357.php?Lang=zh-tw ● 可連結之網頁位址 相關網頁(Personal Website) 本課程之 AI 使用規則依授課指導教授訂定，需於加簽提交專題課程大綱時，依規定敘明清楚。

docs.name: 基因體資料分析
docs.text: 課程資訊 及 課程大綱 課程名稱 (中文) 基因體資料分析 課程名稱 (英文) Analysis of Genomic Data 授課教師 張筱涵 上課時間 MnM5 開課年級 碩士班一年級 學分數 2 人數限制 15 先修科目 無(以加簽方式選課) 是否英文授課 否 課程簡述 Brief Course Description (required) This course explores computational approaches and tools for studying genetic variation and evolutionary processes across diverse organisms. Students will learn foundational concepts in bioinformatics and population genetics, as well as modern methods, including simulations and machine learning models, for analyzing genome-scale data. Through lectures and real-data projects, students will develop the ability to interpret genetic diversity and evolutionary patterns from a computational perspective. 關鍵字 Bioinformatics, Population genetics, Data analysis, Computational approaches, Statistics 課程大綱 Detailed Course Syllabus 一、課程說明(Course Description) This course explores computational approaches and tools for studying genetic variation and evolutionary processes across diverse organisms. Students will learn foundational concepts in bioinformatics and population genetics, as well as modern methods, including simulations and machine learning models, for analyzing genome-scale data. Through lectures and real-data projects, students will develop the ability to interpret genetic diversity and evolutionary patterns from a computational perspective. 二、指定用書(Text Books) 無 三、參考書籍(References) • Hartl, D. L., & Clark, A. G. (2007). Principles of Population Genetics (4th ed.). Sinauer Associates. • Gillespie, J. H. (2004). Population Genetics: A Concise Guide (2nd ed.). Johns Hopkins University Press. 四、教學方式(Teaching Method) Lectures, paper reading, discussions, project work, and student presentations. 五、教學進度(Syllabus) 9/1: Introduction to Genomics 9/8: Population genetics I 9/15: Population genetics II 9/22: Population genetics III 9/29: 孔子誕辰紀念日補假 10/6: 中秋節放假 10/13: Genomic databases, gene prediction and annotation 10/20: BLAST and multiple sequence alignment 10/27: Project idea presentation and discussion 11/3: Phylogeny 11/10: Computer simulations and machine learning methods 11/17: Paper presentation and discussion 11/24: Paper presentation and discussion 12/1: Independent project work 12/8: Project presentation and discussion Population genetics include genetic variation, genetic drift, effective population size, population structure, coalescent theory, natural selection, quantitative genetics 六、成績考核(Evaluation) • Class participation (25%) • Paper presentation (25%) • Project and project presentation (50%) 本課程鼓勵學生在透明與負責任的原則下，適度使用 AI 工具進行 課業協作。學生應在報告的標題頁註腳或引用文獻後，簡要說明如 何使用生成式 AI 進行議題發想、文句潤飾或結構參考等內容。在 「書面報告」中，禁止使用生成式 AI 工具進行撰寫。如未明確標 註或是違反規定，教師有權重新評分或不予計分。

docs.nameEn: Introduction to System-on-Chip and its Applications
docs.text: Introduction to System-on-Chip and its Applications (系統晶片應用簡介) (3 units) (Elective, for senior and graduate students) Prof. Ching-Te Chiu (邱瀞德) COM 524200 Phone:03-573-1208 M6M7M8 Office: 台達館 621 室 classroom:Delta106 Email: chiusms@cs.nthu.edu.tw Office hour: W5W6 Course Description This course introduces what is System-on-Chip (SoC), benefits of using SoC, system architecture, design methodology and its applications. It uses several SoC designs, such as computer chip sets, cell phone IC, multimedia ICs, wireless communication ICs, information appliances and interface ICs, as examples to illustrate the top-down IC design flow, Intellectual Property(IP), system platform design and their market applications. The computer chip sets cover personal computer architectures, memory and peripheral I/O interface chip design. The cell phone IC covers heterogeneous multi-processor (HMP). The wireless communication includes CDMA, OFDM and LTE 4G chip designs. The multimedia ICs covers audio, still image, and video ICs. Course Objective This course is intended for students to understand the SoC current status, existing SoC systems and their applications. Pre-requisite -none Textbook • ppt lectures Course Outline and Schedule ◼ I. SoC 簡介 ◼ 1. Introduction to Integrated Circuit/SoC ◼ 2. SoC architecture and platform ◼ 3. SoC Semiconductor Process ◼ II. Computer SoC Systems and its Applications ◼ 1. Introduction to Computer SoC ◼ 2. CISC Architecture and Intel CPU ◼ 3. RISC Architecture and ARM CPU ◼ 4. Server CPU ◼ 5. GPU ◼ III. Memory ◼ 1. Introduction to memory (SRAM/DRAM/Harddisk) ◼ 2. Flash Memory (NOR/NAND Flash) ◼ 3. New generation nonvolatile memory (RRAM/MRAM) ◼ 4. In-Memory Computing ◼ 5. High Bandwidth Memory (HBM) ◼ IV. Graphic SoC (GPU) ◼ 1. Computer Graphic ◼ 2. Graphic Processor (GPU) Architecture ◼ 3. Nvidia GPU ◼ 4. GPU for Deep Learning ◼ V. Interface (Interconnect IC) ◼ 1. PCI-E (Peripheral Component Interconnect-Express) ◼ 2. USB (Universal Serial Bus) ◼ 3. DP (Display Port) ◼ 4. HDMI (High Definition Multimedia Interface) ◼ VI. Multimedia SoC ◼ 1. Video CODEC ◼ 2. H.265/HEVC Video Decoder (VP9) ◼ 3. H.266 (VVC) (Versatile Video Coding) ◼ 4. Video Streaming ◼ 5. Speech CODEC ◼ 6. High Dynamic Range (HDR) ◼ 7. 3D Video IC ◼ 8. 360 degree video IC ◼ VII. Display technologies ◼ 1. Liquid Crystal Display (LCD)/ ◼ 2. Light Emitting Diode (LED) ◼ 3. Organic LED (OLED) ◼ 4. Quantum Dot LED (QLED) ◼ 5. Mini-LED and Micro-LED ◼ 6. Touch Panel ◼ VIII. Video Game SoC ◼ 1. Microsoft XBOX ◼ 2. PlayStation (PS5) ◼ 3. Nintendo Switch ◼ IX. Augmented Reality/Virtual Reality ◼ 1. HTC VR ◼ 2. Microsoft HoloLens (holographic VR) ◼ 3. Oculus SLAM ◼ 4. AR/VR glass ◼ X. Wireless Data Transmission (Modem IC/Cellphone) ◼ 1 LTE ◼ 2 5G ◼ 3 Qualcomm 5G IC ◼ 4 MediaTek ◼ 5. Cellphone System ◼ XI. Wireless Interface (Interconnect IC) ◼ 1 Bluetooth ◼ 2 RFID (Radio Frequency Identification) ◼ 3 USB (Universal Serial Bus) ◼ 4 NFC (Near Field Communication) ◼ 5 Zigbee ◼ XII Wearable Devices ◼ 1. Sensors ◼ 2. Apple watch ◼ 3. Exercise monitor ◼ 4. Bio-condition monitor ◼ XIII Application Systems ◼ 1. Social Network ◼ 2. Apps on mobile or Tablet devices ◼ 3. Internet of Things ◼ 4. Drone ◼ 5. Self-Driving Cars ◼ 6. Biometric Recognition System (fingerprint, iris, face, gait, etc) ◼ 7. 3D Sensing ◼ 8. Blockchain Individual Projects: Each student selects a topic from provided System_on_chip technologies list, provides deep core technologies, and market analysis, then give a presentation and a written report. Individual Project 1. Select a topic from the SoC list 2. Project must cover ◼ Definition of the technology/Devices/SoC ◼ Applications ◼ System Architecture ◼ Core Module Technology (based on a technical paper) ◼ SoC Architecture ◼ Market Analysis 3. Oral presentation in English - ppt 25min 4. Written report in English –pdf Final Projects: Divide students into groups by fourth week. docs.name: 互動設計
docs.text: 1 ISA 557900: 互動設計 Interaction Design 教師: 許有真 (ychsu@mx.nthu.edu.tw ‧研究室: 綜二館 B 棟 416) 上課時間: W 34N (10:10-1:00)． 地點: 炯朗館 127 =============================================================== 課程說明 隨著新科技的持續研發及進入生活與工作中，我們有更多機會去操作各類科技系統，而良好的使用 者體驗也更為迫切。人機互動從使用者角度來看人與電腦間的互動，並透過系統性的設計流程來達 到良好的系統設計。本課程將從人性因素及人與科技互動角度來了解科技的互動設計過程。透過閱 讀書籍文獻來了解人因與設計流程相關概念，並藉由作業學習如何從使用者研究到系統使用性測試 之完整流程的各項設計考量因素。修讀本課程後，未來在開發軟體或各類系統時將能以更為多元縝 密的角度，思考如何設計出符合使用者需求並具備良好使用者體驗的互動科技。 教學方式 部分課程將透過課堂討論與實作將概念應用於系統之設計過程。課程包含活動如下: ● 老師授課 ● 小組導讀 ＋CHI 短論文介紹 ● 課堂討論活動：配合該周文章主題及作業進度，於課堂內進行討論。 ● 實作計劃：系統使用者測試、從使用者研究至雛型概念的設計。 書籍講義 ● 教科書: Interaction Design: Beyond Human-Computer Interaction (5th or 6th Edition), by Preece, Rogers and Sharp. 2019/2023. ● Contextual Design: Design for Life (2nd Edition), by Karen Holtzblatt and Hugh Beyer. 2017. （閱讀章 節：C6, C11, C13） ● 其他補充文章 課堂作業 ● 小組導讀 PPT ＆短論文 ● 期中作業: 系統使用性測試 ● 期末作業: 使用者分析與雛形設計 2 ● 閱讀摘要與心得 成績考核 ● 出席 10% ● 小組討論 ＆ 課堂參與及提問 5% ● 文章摘要與心得 7.5%，短論文介紹 2.5% ● 導讀 20% ● 期中作業 25% ● 期末作業 30% 教學進度 每周包含: 老師講解、同學導讀、課堂討論。 W 授課內容 (內容將視情況調整) 1 課程介紹＆ 分組 ＆ 影片導覽 2 Introducing to interaction design 3 Understanding and conceptualizing interaction 4 Usability engineering I 5 Usability engineering II 6 Understanding the user 7 Emotion and social aspect 8 期中報告 9 Contextual design 10 運動會 11 Persona 12 Task analysis 13 Envision: conceptual design and Storytelling 14 Prototype construction 15 Final project presentation ＆演講 16 Final project presentation

docs.text: 114 學年 網路藝術 (Internet Art) 課程介紹 課程名稱：網路藝術 (Internet Art) 課程科號：11410ISA 683200 課程網址： http://fbilab.org/xn/netart （資料更新中） 任課教師：許素朱(小牛) <xn.techart@gmail.com> 課程助教：待聘 上課時間：週(三) 15:30-18:20PM 上課地點：台達館教室待定 學生於本課程使用 AI 的聲明：本課程內容對 AI＋Art 有深入探討，作業也鼓勵學生與 AI 做創意共創與討溣 課程目標： 此課程由 國立清華大學資訊系統與應用研究所 與 國際跨院碩（科技藝術組）合開，透 過課程的安排，讓科技與人文藝術不同背景的同學彼此碰撞、學習，更一起創作。 「網路藝術」非指狹義的視覺藝術，而是廣義的「創意」，是以網路為創作的媒介或平 台，去從事藝術、哲學、網路社會行為現象之議題探討，或是從事相關議題探討的創意實 作。 數位時代的藝術語言/程式語言/社會語言，其新維度不斷的增加，它們正面臨著令人振 奮的挑戰，而藝術創作者、媒體技術者、甚至一般民眾將要如何去面對、要如何去選擇？本 課程目的期望透過課程的學習、創意實作，讓學生對 21 世紀的網路媒介有深刻思考。 課程教學方式：  課程中要求 2~3 位跨領域背景同學組成小組，一起探討報告相關網路議題，一起切磋 共創課程指定創意作業。  課程中將介紹網路發展史、網路藝術之發展史。另外會介紹、分析近年網路藝術之國 際作經典案例 (Text Art/Web Art , Information Art, IoT Installation Art , Social Networking Art、AI Generated Art)，以及國際以網路為媒介的創意實作案例介紹。  【IoT Cross Media】創意實作單元：本學期課程的實作單元，將以科技藝術研究中心 過去所研發的「IoT Cross Media」技術為核心基礎，教導學生 IoT 的軟硬體實作與系 統整合，最後做出創意應用。過去「IoT Cross Media」技術曾應用至「印象清華 2018-物聯網科技藝術節」、「印象清華 2019-躍介科技藝術節」、「印象清華 2022- 元宇宙天文科普藝術節」，相關應用也與 AI 結合發表至國際一些國際研討會上。  【課程小作業】單元： ① netChat 創意小作業：以網路任何聊天媒介(如 GPT, Grok, Gemini, DeepSeek …)， 自訂「主題」來探討 AI 當代社會中是扮演「順水推舟」或是「造反有理？」做出相 對應之實驗性辯證探討。 ② 偏見-AI 生成創意小作業：以「偏見(Bias)」為主題，運用 AI 圖像或文字工具，做 實驗性小應用創作與探討。  【國際經典案例】小組討論單元： 小組需闡述案例中的議題主張、執行方式與社會影響。小組採用「Group Discussion」 討論方式，報告內容包含： - Summary：對案例做總結介紹。 - Keyword：對案例之關鍵字做定義、重要性說明。 - Background：對案例的背景探索說明 (含作者背景、背後動機與影響 - Connection：對案例之延伸影響議題探討、相關類似作品介紹、影響力與啟發聯 想。 評分：  課程出席、課堂表現(25%) (個人、小組)。  國際案例-小組討論 (15%) (小組) ： 教師評分、同學互評 [小組成績、個人成績]  netChat 創意小作業(15%) (小組) ： 教師評分、同學互評 [小組成績、個人成績] 每組報告 20 分鐘  偏見-AI 生成創意小作業 (15%) (個人)：教師評分、同學互評  IoT Cross Media 專題實作 (30%) (小組創作)， [小組成績、個人成績] 週課表： 週次 課程內容 備註 [01] - 09/03 ■ 課程介紹 [02] - 09/10 ■ 網路發展史介紹 & 網路藝術發展史 [03] - 09/17 ■ Text Art + chatGPT 國際案例分析探討、網路文學+文字意象 chatGPT 衝擊與探討 [04] - 09/24 ■ Information Art ＆ Big Data 國際案例分析探討、資訊 encode/decode 探討 [05] - 10/01 ■ IoT Cross Media – 實作 (1) 感測與無線傳輸元件焊接 [06] - 10/08 ■ IoT Cross Media –實作(2) 應用物件嵌入 IoT Cross Media 晶片模組 [07] - 10/15 ▲國際經典案例-小組報告 ※小組作業報告 [08] - 10/22 ■ IoT Cross Media –實作(3) 手機撈取/倒入 APP（設計 [09] - 10/29 ■ IoT Cross Media –實作(4) 系統整合 [10] - 11/05 ■ IoT Installation Art 國際案例分析探討 裝置的無形探討 [11] - 11/12 ▲ netChat 創意小作業 ※小組作業報告 [12] - 11/19 ■ AI 在藝術的典範轉移 ■ AI 生成藝術應用 [13] - 11/26 ■ 過去學生作業分享 ■ IoT Cross Media 實作預報告 [14] - 12/03 ▲ IoT Cross Media 實作展示與報告 ※小組專題實作報告 [15] - 12/10 ■ Social Networking Art 國際案例分析、數位行動藝術探討 [16] - docs.text: 1 Institute of Service Science, College of Technology Management, National Tsing Hua University Course Syllabus Programming for Business Analytics (PBA) – Undergraduate Course Duration: Sep. 2025 – Dec. 2025 Instructor: Jaewon Yoo (jaewon.yoo@iss.nthu.edu.tw) Class Time: Monday, 14:20 pm- 17:20 pm TAs: TBA Classroom: TSMC Bldg. R421 COURSE DESCRIPTION: This introductory undergraduate-level course leverages R to equip students with the fundamental skills required for robust business data analysis. The course is designed to address both practical programming skills and the conceptual understanding necessary to apply data science effectively in business contexts. Specifically, at the end of the semester you should be able to: • Data Visualization and Wrangling: Students will learn to summarize and visualize data, transforming messy data into tidy, analyzable formats. • Causality and Regression Analysis: The course emphasizes evaluating claims about causality and using linear regression to conduct data analysis, crucial for drawing meaningful conclusions in business. • Statistical Uncertainty: Understanding and quantifying uncertainty in data analysis are core components of the curriculum, enabling students to make informed decisions. • Professional Tools: Mastery of professional tools such as R, RStudio, git, and GitHub will be developed, ensuring students are well-prepared for real-world data analytics tasks. By the end of this course, students will not only be proficient in handling complex business datasets but will also appreciate the importance of meticulous data analysis. The goal is to inspire a passion for data analysis and foster a community among students to deepen their learning and enhance their collaborative skills. This course welcomes students from any background who are interested in developing foundational data analysis skills applicable to the business sector. RECOMMENDED TEXTBOOKS: We will use the following books in this class. Students are expected to complete the assigned reading before joining class, which will assist in understanding the lecture materials and foster in-class discussions. Students can purchase either a hard copy or e-book version of the books. Be aware that it might take time for the textbooks to be delivered so if you plan to take the course, please make sure to place your order early enough so the books arrive in time. 1. [MD] Ismay, Chester and Albert Y. Kim. 2022. Statistical Inference via Data Science: A ModernDive into R and the Tidyverse. 2. [QSS] Imai, Kosuke and Nora Webb Willaims. 2022. Quantitative Social Science: An Introduction with Tidyverse, 2022. Princeton University Press. 3. [IMS] Mine Cetinkaya-Rundel and Johanna Hardin. 2021. Introduction to Modern Statistics. OpenIntro. 2 4. [AAG] R for Everyone: Advanced Analytics and Graphics, 2nd Edition by Jared P. Lander, O'Reilly Media, 2017. 5. [VT] Visualize This: The Flowing Data Guide to Design, Visualization, and Statistics by Nathan Yau, John Wiley & Sons, 2011. SOFTWARE TOOLS: Students will use the R statistical programming language to write and run the codes for the assignments and in-class exercises. R is an open-source language that can be used free of charge and can be downloaded from https://www.r-project.org/. For improved productivity and convenience, students will also use RStudio, a widely used integrated development environment (IDE) for R which is available at https://www.rstudio.com/products/rstudio/ for download. If you use a MacBook with the M1 chip/Apple silicon, RStudio might not work on your machine. If it does not, you can also use Visual Studio Code to edit your codes which can be downloaded at https://code.visualstudio.com/. COURSE EVALUATION: Grading Policy Performance in this course is assessed through a blend of practical assignments, participation, and quizzes, designed to gauge your proficiency in understanding of the materials we will cover throughout the semester. Here are how each portion of course contributes to the overall grade: Category Percent of Final Grade Assignments 35% Problem Sets 20% Quizzes & In-Class Exercises 20% Attitude/Participation 10% Attendance 15% Course Requirements 1. AI Use Policy*: Students are permitted to utilize AI tools or Large Language Models (LLMs; e.g., ChatGPT, Claude 2, Bard) responsibly as aids for brainstorming and generating initial drafts for assignments. However, it is imperative that the final submission predominantly reflects the student's understanding and personal input. To maintain academic integrity, students who choose to use AI tools must adhere to the following guidelines: a. Thorough Explanation: Students must provide a detailed explanation of how the AI tool was used in the completion of the assignment. b. Original AI Responses: Alongside their submission, students are required to submit the original responses generated by the AI tool. 3 c. Critical Evaluation and Personal Input: Students should critically evaluate the AI- generated content and clearly indicate the portions of the work that have been modified or expanded upon with their own insights and understanding. d. Proper Attribution: Proper attribution should be given to the AI-generated content used, clearly indicating the sections that are AI-generated. ** Remember, attempting to cheat the system by heavily relying on AI-generated content without substantial personal input is ultimately the student's loss, as it undermines the learning process and personal growth. 2. Academic Honesty and Plagiarism*: All work submitted for academic evaluation must be the student’s own. The penalty for violation of academic integrity will result in a zero for that assignment for the first time. Subsequent violation(s) will result in a failing grade for the course. Plagiarism will also not be tolerated. Academic dishonesty comprises of, but is not limited to, the following: • Cheating: Copying from other students’ quizzes and assignments or allowing others to copy from one’s own. • Plagiarism: Using other people’s original work without giving appropriate credit or acknowledgment to the authors or sources. • Self-plagiarism: Submitting a piece of work in more than one course without the explicit permission of the instructors involved. • Misrepresentation of authorship: Submitting work as one’s own, which has been prepared by or purchased from others. Students will be asked to upload their submission materials to Turnitin.com, an online plagiarism checker, to ensure academic integrity. Read more about online submission on http://learning.site.nthu.edu.tw/p/412-1319-7120.php?Lang=en. 3. Attendance: All students are expected to attend every class. Please bring your own hard copy of the course materials, which will be distributed by the instructor before class. If you have any urgent reason to miss a class, you are still responsible for the materials covered during the class and are expected to complete the required work. Attendance will be taken on a regular basis and will count towards your participation score (15%). Class missing will cause about 1% loss of final grade. Students who miss a class should inform me or the TA prior to the class via email or phone call. 4. Assignments: There will be a total of FIVE assignments throughout the semester. The assignments will be relevant to our class topic and most likely will require you to run and report a statistical method we will cover in class. For instance, after we cover ordinary least squares (OLS) estimation, students will be asked to run a dataset (to be provided by the instructor) and report the results in a simple article format. Students will be required to write a brief report using R Markdown/Quarto for the assignment. Each assignment is worth 7% of the final grade. Assignments are to be submitted on the due date. Late submissions will be penalized 1 percentage point of the assignment’s weight per day (e.g., for an assignment worth 7 % of the course grade, turning it in 3 days late caps the attainable score at 4 %). 5. Problem Sets: Throughout the semester, you will be required to complete problem sets that make up 20% of your final grade. These problem sets will consist of a mix of exercises taken from the 4 recommended textbooks and are designed to reinforce your understanding of key concepts covered in class. 6. Quizzes & in-class exercises: To keep the learning momentum going, students will be asked to complete multiple quizzes about the course materials throughout the semester. In order to foster learning, students will also be given in-class exercises, some of which will be graded & will count towards the final letter grade. 7. Attitude/participation: In class, the most important thing for the students is to stay active and engaged about the topic being discussed. Positive contributions to class discussions will increase your score towards attitude. When we discuss a topic in class, effective discussions are only possible if everyone is well prepared. Please, be prepared to open and engage in discussions with your opinions and thoughts. TENTATIVE WEEKLY SCHEDULE: Week Topics Prepare before class In-class deliverable #1 Introduction to PBA: • Welcome and motivation: why learn programming & business analytics? • Overview of course details * Read AAG Chap 1 and 2 after class. Read: Course syllabus Self-introduction on Canvas general discussion board #2 The nuts and bolts of R programming: • Review of programming structures • Different types of programming errors • Let’s take a touR! • Operators for R programming • What can we do with R? Recap of Basic Statistics: • Probability and inference • Random variables (r.v.s) • Probability distributions • Expectations? Spread? Read: AAG Ch 4.3, 5, and 6 VT Ch 1 and 2 Install R & R Studio Complete Swirl R Tutorials 1: Basic Building Blocks 2: Workspace and Files 3: Sequences of Numbers #3 Data Types and Structures: • Numeric, character/string, logical, dates & times • Vectors, Matrices, and arrays • Lists and data frames Data Visualization for Exploratory Analysis I: • Building plots by layers • Histograms and boxplots • Grouped data * In-class group exercises Read: AAG Ch 3, 4, 7.1, 9, & 10 AAG Ch 27 and 28 VT Ch 3 and 4 Read a handout for ‘Reporting Tools (R Markdown and Quarto)’ 5 #4 User-Defined Functions in R: • Creating & nesting fn. • Local vs. global var. • Scoping rules in R • Creating binary operators Data Visualization II • Principles of analytic graphics * In-class group exercises Read: AAG Ch 7.2 and 11 VT Ch 5 and 6 MD Ch 1-2 AS1 (The Nuts and Bolts of R Programming for Business Analytics) Complete group formation survey #5 Data Wrangling: • Operating on rows • Operating on columns • Operating on groups • Creating barplots Read: AAG Ch 14, 15, and 16 VT Ch 7 MD Ch 3 #6 Causality: • What is it? • Randomized experiments • Calculating effects • Observational studies Read: QSS Ch 2.1-2.5 #7 Relationships and Importing/Tidying Data: • Z-Scores and standardization • Correlation • Pivoting data longer • Joining datasets Read: AAG Ch 11 MD Ch 4 QSS Ch 3.5-3.6 AS2 (Visualization & Causality: Air Pollution and Job Training Program) #8 Prediction: • Predicting election outcomes • Loops • Evaluating the predictions • Time-series plot * Review: causal effect estimation for AS2 Read: AAG 4.7 and 12 VT Chap 8 and 9 #9 Regression: • Prediction • Modeling with a line • Linear regression in R • Model fit Read: MD Ch 5 QSS Ch 4.1 and 4.2.1- 4.2.4 #10 More on Regression: • Multiple regression • Categorical independent variables * In-class group exercises Read: MD Ch 6.1-6.2 QSS Ch 4.2.6-4.3.2 AS3 (Regression & Prediction: Ethnic Bias and Voter Turnout) #11 Sampling and Sampling Distribution: • Sampling exercise and framework • Random var. and probability distributions • Normal variables and the central limit theorem Read: MD Ch 7 6 #12 Bootstrap and Confidence Intervals: • Resampling from our samples • Bootstrap CIs for a difference in means • Bootstrap CIs for a difference in ATEs • Computing and interpreting CIs Read: AAG Chap 18 and 19 MD Ch 8 IMS Ch 12 #13 Hypothesis Testing: • Hypothesis testing using [infer] • Two-sample tests • Two-sample permutation tests • Issues with hypothesis testing • Power analysis Read: MD Ch 9 IMS Ch 11 AS4 (Bootstrapping: Rags to Riches TV & Economic Mobility) #14 Individual meeting by appointment. (no in-class meeting) #15 Models of Uncertainty: • Using the normal for inference • CI for experiments • Inference for linear regression Read: IMS Ch 13 AS5 (Hypothesis Testing) #16 Inference for Linear Regression: • Uncertainty estimation for regression • Presenting OLS regressions • Wrapping up the class Read: QSS Ch 7.3 Notes: The course schedule is subject to change if necessary (AAG, VT, MD, QSS, and IMS, refer to ‘Recommended Textbooks’ in Page 1; AS: assignment). Assignments are due at the beginning of the class on the submission date.

docs.text: 1 SYLLABUS ISS5065: Quantitative Research Methods in Marketing Fall Semester 2025 Instructor: Yi-Chun Ou Class time: 9.00 – 12.00 Thursdays email: ycou@iss.nthu.edu.tw Class location: 406 TSMC Building Office location: 828A TSMC Building Office hour: by appointments COURSE DESCRIPTION The course provides an opportunity to work in small groups. The groups will complete and present a marketing project. To complete the project, the students will learn the required quantitative analytical methods and have a good understanding of relevant marketing theories and. In addition to group work, the course will have three individual assessments. COURSE OBJECTIVES The course aims to develop students’ team-working, along with an understanding of how to implement a proper marketing project in a quantitative perspective. The students will be able to apply a range of learned marketing knowledge and analytical skills to making realistic managerial recommendations/insights and maximizing the impact of research findings in marketing settings. Specifically, the objectives cover (1) developing a conceptual framework and hypotheses, (2) designing a questionnaire and collecting data, (3) examining item reliability and validity, (4) doing analyses regarding moderators and mediators, and (5) providing practical recommendations to managers based on analytical outcomes. LEARNING METHODS The course combines different learning methods: lectures, group discussions, and data analysis practice. READING LIST • Suggested textbooks Field, Andy (2018). Discovering statistics using IBM SPSS statistics. London: Sage Edge. Field, Andy, Jeremy Miles, and Zoe Field (2012). Discovering statistics using R. London: Sage Edge. Field’s books provide a conceptual understanding of statistics and detail the steps of analyses. The book in 2018 (2012) introduced statistical software of SPSS (R). The course will mainly use R. However, if you are interested in learning or getting more familiar with SPSS, the 2018 book is good to start with. In addition, the 2018 book has good materials for learning moderators and mediators. Verhoef, Peter, Edwin Kooge, and Natasha Walk (2016). Creating value with big data analytics. New York: Routledge. 2 The book lists important customer metrics and discusses how to use analytics to create value for clients. • Academic articles The reading list of academic articles will be provided in the first week. SOFTWARE We will use RStudio for this module. GRADING • Group work • Group report (5000 words max.) 30% • Group presentation (30 mins max. + 15-20 mins Q&A) 20% • Individual work • Individual class exams 40% • Individual class attendance and engagement 10% • Note: Peer evaluation In terms of group work, to fairly assess each member’s participation and involvement, there will be peer evaluation. The result of peer evaluation has the impact on group work’s marks. I will announce the peer evaluation process during the course. • Note: Class attendance and engagement • Attendance: The class will start at 9.10 sharp. If you are not able to be on time or attend a class, inform TA and me of the reason before the class starts. A reasonable reason will not be marked down. Being 15 or more than 15 minutes late is regarded as being late. Each lateness would have 3 points down. Each absence would have 6 points down (100/16 weeks=~6). • Engagement: TA will note the number of your engagement in classes (e.g., answering/ asking questions). Below is an example of how engagement scores are calculated. The baseline engagement score is 75 for everyone. 0 time: 75 1 – 4 times: 80 5 – 7 times: 85 8 – 10 times: 90 11 – 13 times: 95 > 13 times: 100 • Note: Peer evaluation To fairly assess each member’s participation and involvement in group work, there will be peer evaluation. The result of peer evaluation has the impact on group work’s marks. Peer evaluation is applied to group work, including the in-class group discussions and the final-term group presentations. I will announce the peer evaluation process during the course. AI USAGE Conditionally open; please specify how generative AI will be used in course output 3 COURSE PLANNING Week Date Topic & Activity 1 Sep. 4 Class introduction 2 Sep. 11 Link “research objectives” to “conceptual models” Group activity: practice to generate research objectives and link the objectives to conceptual models 3 Sep. 18 Link “conceptual models” to “questionnaires” Group activity: practice to develop three conceptual models for the group project and find the items/ questions for the variables, respectively, in the models Expected group work from week 3 to week 11: Finalise three conceptual models and complete a questionnaire 4 Sep. 25 Measurement development: reliability & validity (1) Group activity: practice what is learned today 5 Oct. 2 Measurement development: reliability & validity (2) Group activity: practice what is learned today 6 Oct. 9 Individual class exam: measurement development Moderators: theory (1) Group activity: find a proper moderator for the group report 7 Oct. 16 Moderators: analyses (2) Group activity: practice what is learned today 8 Oct. 23 Moderators: analyses (3) Group activity: practice what is learned today 9 Oct. 30 Individual class exam: moderators Mediators: theory (1) Group activity: find a proper mediator for the group report 10 Nov. 6 Mediators: analyses (2) Group activity: practice what is learned today 11 Nov. 13 Mediators: analyses (3) Group activity: practice what is learned today Expected group work by week 12: Submit the three conceptual models and a questionnaire for checks (to the TA) before 17.00 November 21. After questionnaire checks, revise the questionnaire based on comments and start to collect data (300 respondents minimum) 12 Nov. 20 Individual class exam: mediators Communicate the group project report and group presentation Additional analysis: mediated moderation analysis 13 Nov. 27 Individual group meetings (30 mins per group) 14 Dec. 4 Group presentations for groups? (TBC) 15 Dec. 11 Group presentations for groups? (TBC) 16 Dec. 18 Submit the group report before 17.00 on December 18 4 WEEKLY PLANNING WEEK 1 (Sep. 4) • Learning outcomes o Have a better understanding of what this course will deliver to you and expect from you o Well consider if this course fits your learning motivation and objective • Activities o Self-introduction WEEK 2 (Sep. 11) • Learning outcomes o Learn the role of “research objectives” o Link the “research objectives” to the “conceptual models” o Understand three conceptual models ▪ Main-effect only model: independent variables + one dependent variable ▪ Moderation model: independent variables + one dependent variable + one moderator ▪ Mediation model: independent variables + one dependent variable + one mediator • Activities o Find a brand and learn to consider any “research objectives” relevant to this brand o Link the “research objectives” to “conceptual models” WEEK 3 (Sep. 18) • Learning outcomes o Recap lecture 2’s three conceptual models o Carefully select variables in the conceptual models ▪ Specific ▪ Measureable ▪ Be able to collect these variables’ data o Learn to find items/ questions measuring the variables from academic articles o Choose proper scales for the items/ questions • Activities o Find a brand and develop three “conceptual models” relevant to the brand. The practice is particularly for your group project. o Find items/ questions measuring the variables in the models if time allows. Note: the items/ questions have to be from good journals’ articles. Any ideas about what a good journal means? • Prepare for week 4: Each person will download R and RStudio, https://rstudio- education.github.io/hopr/starting.html. Or, you could simply use the keywords of “RStudio download” on Google’s search engine and then you will find a download website, which will choose a proper R and RStudio for your laptop, either Windows or MacBook. 5 WEEK 4 (Sep. 25) • Learning outcomes o Complete steps 1 – 4 in measurement development • Define variables • Find questions from academic articles • Use EFA to drop bad questions • Cronbach’s 𝛼 & composite reliability • Activities o Complete steps 1 – 4 in measurement development o In the last hour, each group will practice what is learned today. • Software: RStudio WEEK 5 (Oct. 2) • Learning outcomes o Complete two validity tests (step 5) ▪ Average variance extracted (AVE) and shared variance ▪ Confirmatory factor analysis (CFA) • Activities o Complete step 5 in measurement development o In the last hour, each group will practice what is learned today. • Software: RStudio WEEK 6 (Oct. 9) • Individual class exam: The aim of the exam is to know the extent to which the students understand the concepts and calculations of measurement development in weeks 4 and 5. • Learning outcomes o Understand the role of moderators in a theoretical perspective o Understand the role of moderators in a strategic perspective • Activities o Discuss the role of moderators o In the last hour, each group will find a proper moderator for the group project. 6 WEEK 7 (Oct. 16) • Learning outcomes o Have a better understanding of linear regression o Learn how to do moderation analysis when the moderator has a non-nominal scale (e.g., ordinal, interval, ratio) • Activities o Recap liner regression o Implement moderation analysis for a moderator with a non-nominal scale o In the last hour, each group will practice what is learned today. • Software: RStudio WEEK 8 (Oct. 23) • Learning outcomes o Better understand how to correctly interpret the impact of a moderator. I will share the group meeting schedule in week 13. Each group member is required to attend the meeting. If you are not able to, please let me know the reason beforehand. docs.text: 1 Institute of Service Science, College of Technology Management, National Tsing Hua University Course Syllabus Programming for Business Analytics (PBA) – Graduate Course Duration: Sep. 2025 – Dec. 2025 Instructor: Jaewon Yoo (jaewon.yoo@iss.nthu.edu.tw) Class Time: Thursday, 14:20 pm- 17:20 pm TAs: TBA Classroom: TSMC Bldg. R421 COURSE DESCRIPTION: This course introduces programming for business analytics using R and aims to cover a wide array of topics that are needed to utilize analytical tools to solve business problems. The course is designed to address both practical programming skills and the conceptual understanding necessary to apply data science effectively in business contexts. Specifically, at the end of the semester you should be able to have proficiency in Data Visualization and Wrangling, meaning you can summarize information clearly and turn messy datasets into tidy, analyzable formats. You will also understand Causality and Regression Analysis, allowing you to evaluate causal claims and use linear regression to draw meaningful business conclusions. A firm grasp of Statistical Uncertainty will help you quantify and interpret the limits of your findings so you can make well-informed decisions. Lastly, you will be comfortable with professional tools such as R, RStudio, git, and GitHub, ensuring you are prepared for real-world data-analytics tasks. Students will not only be proficient in handling complex business datasets but will also appreciate the importance of meticulous data analysis. In doing so, we will also attempt to inspire a passion for data analysis and create a community among the students to deepen their learning. This course welcomes students from any background who are interested in developing foundational data analysis skills applicable to the business sector. RECOMMENDED TEXTBOOKS: We will use the following books in this class. Students are expected to complete the assigned reading before joining class, which will assist in understanding the lecture materials and foster in-class discussions. Students can purchase either a hard copy or e-book version of the books. Be aware that it might take time for the textbooks to be delivered so if you plan to take the course, please make sure to place your order early enough so the books arrive in time. 1. [MD] Ismay, Chester and Albert Y. Kim. 2022. Statistical Inference via Data Science: A ModernDive into R and the Tidyverse. 2. [QSS] Imai, Kosuke and Nora Webb Willaims. 2022. Quantitative Social Science: An Introduction with Tidyverse, 2022. Princeton University Press. 3. [IMS] Mine Cetinkaya-Rundel and Johanna Hardin. 2021. Introduction to Modern Statistics. OpenIntro. 4. [AAG] R for Everyone: Advanced Analytics and Graphics, 2nd Edition by Jared P. Lander, O'Reilly Media, 2017. 2 5. [VT] Visualize This: The Flowing Data Guide to Design, Visualization, and Statistics by Nathan Yau, John Wiley & Sons, 2011. SOFTWARE TOOLS: Students will use the R statistical programming language to write and run the codes for the assignments and in-class exercises. R is an open-source language that can be used free of charge and can be downloaded from https://www.r-project.org/. For improved productivity and convenience, students will also use RStudio, a widely used integrated development environment (IDE) for R which is available at https://www.rstudio.com/products/rstudio/ for download. If you use a MacBook with the M1 chip/Apple silicon, RStudio might not work on your machine. If it does not, you can also use Visual Studio Code to edit your codes which can be downloaded at https://code.visualstudio.com/. COURSE EVALUATION: Grading Policy Performance in this course is assessed through a blend of practical assignments, participation, and quizzes, designed to gauge your proficiency in understanding of the materials we will cover throughout the semester. Here are how each portion of course contributes to the overall grade: Category Percent of Final Grade Final Project 25% Assignments 20% Problem Sets 20% Quizzes & In-Class Exercises 15% Attitude/Participation 10% Attendance 10% Course Requirements 1. AI Use Policy*: Students are permitted to utilize AI tools or Large Language Models (LLMs; e.g., ChatGPT, Claude 2, Bard) responsibly as aids for brainstorming and generating initial drafts for assignments. However, it is imperative that the final submission predominantly reflects the student's understanding and personal input. To maintain academic integrity, students who choose to use AI tools must adhere to the following guidelines: a. Thorough Explanation: Students must provide a detailed explanation of how the AI tool was used in the completion of the assignment. b. Original AI Responses: Alongside their submission, students are required to submit the original responses generated by the AI tool. 3 c. Critical Evaluation and Personal Input: Students should critically evaluate the AI- generated content and clearly indicate the portions of the work that have been modified or expanded upon with their own insights and understanding. d. Proper Attribution: Proper attribution should be given to the AI-generated content used, clearly indicating the sections that are AI-generated. ** Remember, attempting to cheat the system by heavily relying on AI-generated content without substantial personal input is ultimately the student's loss, as it undermines the learning process and personal growth. 2. Academic Honesty and Plagiarism*: All work submitted for academic evaluation must be the student’s own. The penalty for violation of academic integrity will result in a zero for that assignment for the first time. Subsequent violation(s) will result in a failing grade for the course. Plagiarism will also not be tolerated. Academic dishonesty comprises of, but is not limited to, the following: • Cheating: Copying from other students’ quizzes and assignments or allowing others to copy from one’s own. • Plagiarism: Using other people’s original work without giving appropriate credit or acknowledgment to the authors or sources. • Self-plagiarism: Submitting a piece of work in more than one course without the explicit permission of the instructors involved. • Misrepresentation of authorship: Submitting work as one’s own, which has been prepared by or purchased from others. Students will be asked to upload their submission materials to Turnitin.com, an online plagiarism checker, to ensure academic integrity. Read more about online submission on http://learning.site.nthu.edu.tw/p/412-1319-7120.php?Lang=en. 3. Attendance: All students are expected to attend every class. Please bring your own hard copy of the course materials, which will be distributed by the instructor before class. If you have any urgent reason to miss a class, you are still responsible for the materials covered during the class and are expected to complete the required work. Attendance will be taken on a regular basis and will count towards your participation score (10%). Class missing will cause about 1% loss of final grade. Students who miss a class should inform me or the TA prior to the class via email or phone call. 4. Final Project*: This is an open‐ended data analysis project on a topic of your interest. Whether you are fascinated by voting trends in presidential elections, racial disparities in policing, NBA salary distributions, or the box‐office economics of the Marvel Cinematic Universe, the core steps should involve: 1) develop a clear research question; 2) locate and prepare data that can address that question; 3) apply the analytical techniques covered in the course to answer the question. You should be able to present your findings in a format suitable for a general audience. The aim is to produce a polished, portfolio-ready project that demonstrates the skills you’ve acquired to prospective employers. Your deliverable will be a publicly accessible article or webpage that includes: a concise overview of the research question and dataset; a visualization that directly addresses the question; a table or figure presenting a regression model and a plain-language explanation of the results; and a brief paragraph discussing the study’s limitations, threats to inference, and how the analysis could be improved (for instance, by collecting better data). Finally, 4 the piece must link to a GitHub repository containing all code used to load, clean, analyze, and visualize the data and to generate the article. The data collection and cleaning must be meaningful -- it’s not sufficient to simply use a pre- cleaned data from an R package. Self-collected data is allowed and even encouraged, though beware you may need to undergo the Institutional Review Board (IRB) review process to be able to use the data for your final project. Milestone Course Week Creating a GitHub Repository 4 Data and Proposal 6 First Visualization 9 First Analysis 11 Final Report 15 5. Assignments: There will be a total of FIVE assignments throughout the semester. The assignments will be relevant to our class topic and most likely will require you to run and report a statistical method we will cover in class. For instance, after we cover ordinary least squares (OLS) estimation, students will be asked to run a dataset (to be provided by the instructor) and report the results in a simple article format. Students will be required to write a brief report using R Markdown/Quarto for the assignment. Each assignment is worth 4% of the final grade. Assignments are to be submitted on the due date. Late submissions will be penalized 1 percentage point of the assignment’s weight per day (e.g., for an assignment worth 4% of the course grade, turning it in 2 days late caps the attainable score at 2%). 6. Problem Sets: Throughout the semester, you will be required to complete problem sets that make up 20% of your final grade. These problem sets will consist of a mix of exercises taken from the recommended textbooks and are designed to reinforce your understanding of key concepts covered in class. 7. Quizzes & in-class exercises: To keep the learning momentum going, students will be asked to complete multiple quizzes about the course materials throughout the semester. In order to foster learning, students will also be given in-class exercises, some of which will be graded & will count towards the final letter grade. 8. Attitude/participation: In class, the most important thing for the students is to stay active and engaged about the topic being discussed. Positive contributions to class discussions will increase your score towards attitude. When we discuss a topic in class, effective discussions are only possible if everyone is well prepared. Please, be prepared to open and engage in discussions with your opinions and thoughts. TENTATIVE WEEKLY SCHEDULE: Week Topics Prepare before class In-class deliverable 5 #1 Introduction to PBA: • Welcome and motivation: why learn programming & business analytics? • Overview of course details * Read AAG Chap 1 and 2 after class. Read: Course syllabus Self-introduction on Canvas general discussion board #2 The nuts and bolts of R programming: • Review of programming structures • Different types of programming errors • Let’s take a touR! • Operators for R programming • What can we do with R? Recap of Basic Statistics: • Probability and inference • Random variables (r.v.s) • Probability distributions • Expectations? Spread? Read: AAG Ch 4.3, 5, and 6 VT Ch 1 and 2 Install R & R Studio Complete Swirl R Tutorials 1: Basic Building Blocks 2: Workspace and Files 3: Sequences of Numbers #3 Data Types and Structures: • Numeric, character/string, logical, dates & times • Vectors, Matrices, and arrays • Lists and data frames Data Visualization for Exploratory Analysis I: • Building plots by layers • Histograms and boxplots • Grouped data * In-class group exercises Read: AAG Ch 3, 4, 7.1, 9, & 10 AAG Ch 27 and 28 VT Ch 3 and 4 Read a handout for ‘Reporting Tools (R Markdown and Quarto)’ #4 User-Defined Functions in R: • Creating & nesting fn. • Local vs. global var. • Scoping rules in R • Creating binary operators Data Visualization II • Principles of analytic graphics * In-class group exercises Read: AAG Ch 7.2 and 11 VT Ch 5 and 6 MD Ch 1-2 AS1 (The Nuts and Bolts of R Programming for Business Analytics) Complete group formation survey #5 Data Wrangling: • Operating on rows • Operating on columns • Operating on groups • Creating barplots Read: AAG Ch 14, 15, and 16 VT Ch 7 MD Ch 3 #6 Causality: • What is it? • Randomized experiments • Calculating effects • Observational studies Read: QSS Ch 2.1-2.5 6 #7 Relationships and Importing/Tidying Data: • Z-Scores and standardization • Correlation • Pivoting data longer • Joining datasets Read: AAG Ch 11 MD Ch 4 QSS Ch 3.5-3.6 AS2 (Visualization & Causality: Air Pollution and Job Training Program) #8 Prediction: • Predicting election outcomes • Loops • Evaluating the predictions • Time-series plot * Review: causal effect estimation for AS2 Read: AAG 4.7 and 12 VT Chap 8 and 9 #9 Regression: • Prediction • Modeling with a line • Linear regression in R • Model fit Read: MD Ch 5 QSS Ch 4.1 and 4.2.1- 4.2.4 #10 More on Regression: • Multiple regression • Categorical independent variables * In-class group exercises Read: MD Ch 6.1-6.2 QSS Ch 4.2.6-4.3.2 AS3 (Regression & Prediction: Ethnic Bias and Voter Turnout) #11 Sampling and Sampling Distribution: • Sampling exercise and framework • Random var. and probability distributions • Normal variables and the central limit theorem Read: MD Ch 7 #12 Bootstrap and Confidence Intervals: • Resampling from our samples • Bootstrap CIs for a difference in means • Bootstrap CIs for a difference in ATEs • Computing and interpreting CIs Read: AAG Chap 18 and 19 MD Ch 8 IMS Ch 12 #13 Hypothesis Testing: • Hypothesis testing using [infer] • Two-sample tests • Two-sample permutation tests • Issues with hypothesis testing • Power analysis Read: MD Ch 9 IMS Ch 11 AS4 (Bootstrapping: Rags to Riches TV & Economic Mobility) #14 Individual meeting by appointment. (no in-class meeting) #15 Models of Uncertainty: • Using the normal for inference • CI for experiments • Inference for linear regression Read: IMS Ch 13 AS5 (Hypothesis Testing) 7 #16 Inference for Linear Regression: • Uncertainty estimation for regression • Presenting OLS regressions • Wrapping up the class Read: QSS Ch 7.3 Notes: The course schedule is subject to change if necessary (AAG, VT, MD, QSS, and IMS, refer to ‘Recommended Textbooks’ in Page 1; AS: assignment). Assignments are due at the beginning of the class on the submission date.

docs.text: 1 Institute of Service Science, National Tsing Hua University Service Oriented Architecture Fall 2025 Duration: Sep 2025 – Dec 2025 Class Time: Mondays, 9am-12pm Facebook Group: facebook.com/groups/ISS.SOAD Instructor: Soumya Ray (soumya.ray@iss.nthu.edu.tw) Assistant: 何捷睿 Jerry Ho (on MS Teams) How do companies like Netflix, Airbnb, or ChatGPT continuously innovate their service? Innovation requires systems that we can confidently extend, redesign, retest, and redeploy. In this class, you will learn the best practices to develop the back-end systems that power scalable and innovative services. This class is ideal for students with strong programming backgrounds who want to one day be: Senior developers: develop scalable, extensible applications in startups and large enterprises Tech leads: design and architect complex IT solutions, lead and mentor other developers IT product managers: manage sophisticated IT teams, understand complex IT solutions What techniques will I learn? Learn architectural and refactoring techniques to create systems that are easy to maintain and extend: Domain Driven Design: layered architecture that separates business logic from infrastructure and presentation Continuous Integration: automated unit & integration tests in to ensure correct system behavior on multiple platforms Functional flow: monads, transactions, railway-oriented programming to explicitly manage errors What tools will we use? Cloud Services: Amazon AWS, RedisCloud, Heroku Distributed Systems: Web APIs, Apps, Microservices Data Stores: Relational databases & key-value stores; local, hosted, and cloud-based solutions Reactive UX: background jobs, message queues, web sockets, reactive front-end elements Responsive UI: mobile-first, responsive web-interfaces DevOps: Continuous development and integration Version Control: git, Github Flow, rebase, pull requests How much coding should I already know? You should be able to create a basic application using: a) Object-oriented programming: any OOP language such as Javascript, Python, PHP, Java, Ruby, C#, C++, etc. b) Basic web page design: HTML + CSS c) Database design: Relational design + ERD + SQL This class will use the Ruby programming language, but the techniques are relevant to any language We will use services like PostGres, AWS, and Heroku but the skills you learn apply to any tech stack The platforms and tools you will use are free up to the requirements of small businesses How will I be graded? Individual Development Effort: 80% (from your code contributions on Github and other HW) Attendance + Online Discussion: 20% (you must share your thoughts in-class or MS Teams) 2 INTRODUCTION Service Orientation Service Providers Service Architecture Meet Your Tools Architecture Matters IT systems become slow and as they grow in complexity. How are leading IT companies managing their code? Let’s learn how to improve innovation and bring joy. Coding Style and Conventions Programming Tools Idiomatic Coding “Good” Code Writing Confident Code We are all afraid to show our code. How can we become confident at coding and be proud of what we make? Let’s start by following the best practices of clean coding. Let’s quantify what it means to have good code using metrics. Object-Orientation Procedural Code Objects and Message Passing Composition, Metaprogramming, and more Capturing objects Why is object orientation so prevalent in business programming? We will dig deep into the philosophy of OOP and how to use it elegantly. (evening workshop: Git/Gitflow) Git Version Control Workshop Web APIs Serialization/Deserialization API Exploration API Library Getting down with data We will develop our first library to extract, transform, and load data from interesting APIs. Testing and Tooling Testing Tools Library Tools UPSTART: Elevator Pitch Fast and Reliable Tests Testing applications with external resources is unreliable and inconvenient. Let’s use stubs to capture and replay data flows. And let’s upgrade our code management tools. LAYERED ARCHITECTURE Application Architecture Challenges of Enterprise Architecture Enterprise Design Patterns MVC Architecture Layered architecture Even a simple modular architecture will make your code clean, will make you more confident to change your code, and will let you sleep better at night. Database Infrastructure Databases and Infrastructure Is MVC Enough? The Repository Pattern Layered architecture Even a simple modular architecture will make your code clean, will make you more confident to change your code, and will let you sleep better at night. Domain Driven Design Domain Complexity Domain Modeling Cloud Deployment What’s your value proposition? The value of our software comes from its domain logic. Let’s make our code match our business language. Presentation Layer Sessions and Error Checking Acceptance Testing Refactoring Views Real artists ship! Let’s see how to design and build an interface responsibly. And then let’s deploy our system early and often using continuous integration, delivery, and deployment. 3 Application Layer Form Objects Service Objects Monadic Chains Managing our Transactions Our controllers are getting fat! We will see how to encapsulate and test major use cases of the user experience. DISTRIBUTED ARCHITECTURE API-centric Architecture Creating a Web API Representational State Transfer - REST Layered API Architecture Growing Pains Our systems must be able to scale up and also respond to many types of clients: web applications, mobile apps, etc. Can we split our system into two without major headaches? Caching and Performance Network Latency Proxy Caching Reverse-Proxy Caching Multitasking 1 All this network input/output is making our service slow. We’ve got to learn to multitask: let’s start new things while waiting for machines to respond. Asynchronocity Concurrency Parallelism Background Workers Multitasking Some tasks need a long time to finish. Can we start serving new users while still processing old tasks? Let’s use concurrency, queues and workers to handle all our tasks. Reactive Architecture Reactive Architecture Web Sockets PubSub Pattern Show me some progress Users hate waiting. Let’s give them a real-time peek at what our system is doing. But HTTP is sometimes not enough: time to bring out websockets. PRODUCT LAUNCH (evening workshop: Docker) Docker Containers and Images DockerHub and Cloud Deployment Show and Tell UPSTART: Presentations Why Architecture Matters What’s Next It’s show time! Let’s see what amazing things we have made. See how confident and proud we can be of our code! And let’s talk about what we will accomplish in future. Artificial Intelligence (AI) Use Policy Grounded in the principles of transparency and responsibility, this course encourages students to leverage Generative AI (GenAI) like ChatGPT and Github CoPilot, and other coding resources like StackOverflow to enhance their learning and improve the quality of their course outputs. This means students may use GenAI or other resources with no restrictions or disclosure. However, we expect students to carefully study, verify, and suitably alter their GenAI assisted solutions to match requirements and reflect their genuine learning.

docs.text: Cross-cultural Marketing Communication (跨文化行銷溝通) Institute of Service Science, National Tsing Hua University Fall Semester, 2025 COURSE INFORMATION MEETING TIME Monday, 9:20 am to 12 pm LOCATION CTM (TSMC) ROOM 430, OR ONLINE DEPENDING ON THE PANDEMIC SITUATION INSTRUCTOR Chen-Ya Wang (王貞雅) Office: 855 TSMC Building E-Mail: cywang@iss.nthu.edu.tw Office hours：By appointment Teaching Assistant: COURSE DESCRIPTION In an increasingly interconnected global business environment it is crucial that marketers recognize how a better understanding of cultural differences can help improve performance. This course offers a framework for analyzing cultures within global marketing. A cross-cultural approach (i.e., comparisons of national marketing systems and local consumer behavior in various countries), as well as an intercultural approach (i.e. the study of marketing/service interaction between people from different cultures) are adopted. This course is helpful for those who wish to improve their cultural awareness or start their career outside their native countries. COURSE OBJECTIVES By completing this course and its requirements, students are expected to: 1. identify and describe the multiplicity of cultures as they relate to marketing communications; 2. explain principles, concepts and theories of marketing that can be applied in the global marketplace; 3. compare and contrast current/practical marketing issues as a result of cultural focus or negligence; 4. use theoretical frameworks and real-world learnings to design marketing communication strategies with a cultural mindset; 5. develop communication and presentation skills in a multi-cultural environment. LEARNING METHODS This course is based on a combination of lectures, classroom discussions, experiential activities, case studies, and marketing projects. MATERIALS Reading materials will be assigned each week. Please see the reading list on EEclass. STUDENT LEARNING ASSESSMENT Class Participation (incl. in-class quizzes, activities and discussions of articles/cases) 33% Team Article Presentation 14% Experiential Exercises 8% Country and Case Presentation 15% Final Team Project 20% Exam 10% (Letter Grade) Definition A+ (All goals achieved beyond expectation) Exceptional A (All goals achieved) Superb A- (All goals achieved, but need some polish) Excellent B+ (Some goals well achieved) Very Good B (Some goals adequately achieved) Good B- (Some goals achieved with minor flaws) Acceptable to Adequate C+ (Minimum goals achieved) Barely adequate *Please note that B is already a good grade in this class. ACADEMIC HONESTY I assume that all students do their own work and credit all work or thought taken from others (including those ONLINE!). Plagiarism will result in a huge reduction of your final course grade of even “F”. Since plagiarism is a matter of fact, not of the student’s intention, it is crucial that acknowledgment of the sources be accurate and complete. Always provide references and be sure to put quotation marks if your paragraph is exactly someone else’s work. CLASS SCHEDULE * This course schedule may be subject to change.
