docs.name: 臺灣原住民族文化概論
docs.text: 國立清華大學課程大綱 科號 Course Number KTLT133100 學分 Credit 2 人數限制 Class Size 10 中文名稱 Course Title 臺灣原住民族文化概論 英文名稱 Course English Title Introduction to Taiwan’s Aboriginal Culture 任課教師 Instructor 伍杜米將（OTO MICYANG） 上課時間 Time T5T6 上課教室 Room 9429 課程簡述(必填) (最多 500 個中文字) 本欄位資料會上傳教育部課程網 Brief Course Description (required) (50-200 words if possible, up to 1000 letters) 台灣是個多族群的社會，在歷史過程中，外來的國家體制尚未進入這塊島嶼時，就已經是多族 群的部落社會彼此共同生活在當中。在多年後的今日，台灣原住民族人口僅佔約全國口的 2.5%，這還不包括未受政府認定具原住民身分的平埔族群。 究竟哪些人是台灣的原住民?他們的文化樣貌如何?在當代生活的處境又是如何? 台灣一般社會 的認知仍僅在學校課本概述性介紹的層面，在缺乏文化與處境之理解的情況下，容易以自身文 化的角度做片面的詮釋、產生誤解與刻板印象。 台灣原住民族的生活樣貌，在歷史過程中已經有很大的改變，若要認識台灣原住民族，除了過 去傳統生活的樣貌，亦需要認識其在歷史過程當中的處境，並從當代原住民族的社會境遇，反 思語境空間的流失以及當前的部落樣貌。 課程內容「中文暨英文關鍵字」(必填) 至少 5 個,每個關鍵字至多 20 個中文,以半形逗點分隔 Please fill in at least 5 course keywords (up to 40 letters for each keyword) and use commas to separate them.(required) 原住民(indigenous) 民族(people) 文化 (culture) 生活(life) 殖民(colonial) 課程大綱(必填)Detailed Course Syllabus ● 課程說明(Course Description) 本課程將從生活文化與歷史變遷的角度，來思考台灣原住民的文化內涵。 在歷史變遷的過程中，台灣原住民族的境遇，對生活文化的影響有哪一些。 亦將從當代原住民族的社會境遇，反思語境空間的流失以及當前的部落樣貌。 本課程將搭配紀錄片來討論原民文化要素之解析，並應用在期末分組報告中。 ● 指定用書(Text Books) ● 參考書籍(References) 《文化》1998，巨流出版社。 《日治時期台灣總督府理番政策》1997，文英堂出版。 《原運 30 年-回顧與前瞻》2004，前衛出版社。 《不上街的運動－台灣原住民族姓名權運動》2004，臺北：台灣原住民族政策協會。 《編織家園》2022，主流出版。 (參考資料於課堂陸續補充) ● 教學方式(Teaching Method) 課程以簡報方式執行，部分搭配影片賞析，進行討論 課程內容將滾動調整，每週討論 ● 教學進度(Syllabus) 週次 日期 課程內容 備註 1 09/03 課程介紹與分組。 台灣原住民族的簡介。 2 09/10 談原住民定義。 3 09/24 南島語族與台灣原住民族 4 10/01 文化概念 5 10/08 文化概念 6 10/15 紀錄片: 倒酒的人 影片 7 10/22 台灣原住民族歷史境遇 8 10/29 台灣原住民族整體境遇 9 11/05 期中報告與討論(1):原住民族的文化議題 10 11/12 期中報告與討論(2):原住民族的文化議題 11 11/19 從《編織家園》談 當代原民處境的轉變 12 11/26 語境與文化概念 13 12/03 從環境空間看部落文化現況 14 12/10 談文創與文化消費 15 12/17 紀錄片:親愛的米酒我把你打敗了 影片 16 12/24 期末報告與討論:各族介紹 17 12/31 期末報告與討論:各族介紹 18 01/07 期末報告與討論:各族介紹 ● 成績考核(Evaluation) 【期中報告】-觀察提問與討論，是否開始參酌課堂提供之觀念，從不同角度觀察原民社會，佔 30%。 【期末報告】-練習應用課堂之資訊，進行相關課題之歸納、解析或評判，來深度介紹一個族群，佔 30%。 【出席率】-涉及課堂討論，佔 40% ● 採用下列何項 AI 使用規則(Indicate which of the following options you use to manage student use of the AI) (1) 完全開放使用且無須註明 Unrestricted use with no disclosure required (2) 有條件開放，請註明如何使用生成式 AI 於課程產出 Conditionally open; please specify how generative AI will be used in course output (3) 禁止使用，請註明相關的監管機制 Prohibited use; please specify relevant oversight (4) 本課程無涉及 AI 使用 Not applicable 可參考下列網頁範例 See the following web page for examples. https://curricul.site.nthu.edu.tw/p/404-1208-248357.php?Lang=zh-tw ● 可連結之網頁位址 相關網頁(Personal Website)

docs.text: 1 國立清華大學課程大綱 科號 Course Number 學分 Credit 3 人數限制 Class Size 中文名稱 Course Title 低資源語言之自然語言處理專題 英文名稱 Course English Title Special Topics in Natural Language Processing for Low-Resource Languages 任課教師 Instructor 林書宇、呂菁菁 上課時間 Time 星期二 16:30~19:20 上課教室 Room 課程簡述(最多 500 個中文字) 本欄位資料會上傳教育部課程網 Brief Course Description (required) (50-200 words if possible, up to 1000 letters) 在大型語言模型與人工智慧技術快速發展的時代，低資源語言的永續發展與應用設計成為全球語言學與科技界共 同關注的重要議題。本課程以自然語言處理（NLP）為核心，帶領學生了解各種針對低資源語言的處理技術與實 作策略，特別聚焦於臺灣本土語言（如閩南語、客家語、原住民族語等）在 NLP 應用中的挑戰與可能。課程涵 蓋語料建置、詞性標註、機器翻譯、情緒分析、零樣本學習、大型語言模型應用等主題，並介紹跨領域最新研究 成果。不要求程式背景，強調語言學知識的轉譯與實踐，適合文科背景學生修習。透過閱讀文獻、實作專案展 示，期待修課學生能初步掌握低資源語言技術應用的關鍵能力，為臺灣本土語言延續與發展開創新局。 課程內容「中文暨英文關鍵字」 至少 5 個,每個關鍵字至多 20 個中文,以半形逗點分隔 Please fill in at least 5 course keywords (up to 40 letters for each keyword) and use commas to separate them.(required) 中文關鍵詞：低資源語言, 自然語言處理, 語料建置, 語料標註, 大型語言模型 英文關鍵詞：Low-Resource Languages, Natural Language Processing, Corpus Construction, Corpus Annotation, Large Language Models 2 課程大綱 Detailed Course Syllabus ● 參考書籍(References) Silberztein, M., & SpringerLink. (2024). Linguistic resources for natural language processing : on the necessity of using linguistic methods to develop NLP software (Max. Silberztein, Ed.). Springer Nature Switzerland. https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-031-43811-0 ● 教學方式(Teaching Method) (1) 基礎概念講解 (2) 文獻導讀 (3) 工具實作 (4) 與實務案例討論 (5) 業界場域參訪 ● 成績考核(Evaluation) 1. 推薦 YouTube 影片及上傳簡報 (70%) 2. 期末報告提案 (5%) 3. 期末報告 (連同問卷調查) (25%) 3 ● 教學進度(Syllabus) 1. 課程介紹與低資源語言概論 TED Talk: Why Indigenous Languages Matter https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=g2HiPW_qSrs&themeRefresh=1 2. 自然語言處理的基礎概念 What is NLP? https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fLvJ8VdHLA0 3. 低資源語言面臨的挑戰 Challenges for Low-resource Languages https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vkENJ2hYUzY 4. 語料庫建立基礎與實務 Corpus Linguistics Introduction https://www.bilibili.com/video/BV14A4y1S7Mu/ https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=H3tzIs_lumA 5. 自動語音辨識技術介紹 How Speech Recognition Works https://developer.nvidia.com/zh-cn/blog/essential-guide-to-automatic-speech-recognition- technology/ https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XI_wvot4I6o 6. 簡易語音辨識工具的實際操作 Using Google's Speech-to-Text https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Ze1_C-oKZZc 7. 機器翻譯的基本概念與應用案例 Breaking the Language Barrier https://www.ted.com/talks/tomás_mikolov_breaking_the_language_barrier https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cvi62sJDs_g https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=smOyDyuHPxY 8. NLP 技術在課堂互動中的創新應用 Innovative Classroom NLP Applications https://flipedu.parenting.com.tw/article/009473 https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=GzwBRzpoP5k https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zyhoYUSCzGs https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=occhMh2qvzE&t=6543s 15. NLP 技術與本土語言文化保存 Preserving Languages through Technology https://www.ted.com/talks/david_peterson_why_language_is_humanity_s_greatest_invention https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Z50T-tslrgs https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=woVsGkH0GO8 https://taiwan-lingu.ist/ 5 16. 期末發表 ● 課程說明(Course Description) 在大型語言模型（LLMs）與人工智慧（AI）技術迅速發展的當下，全球正積極關注低資源語言的保存與發 展。臺灣的閩南語、客家語與南島語等本土語言，文化底蘊深厚，亦時而面臨資源匱乏與邊緣化的處境。本課程 以自然語言處理（NLP）為核心，結合最新國際研究與在地語言關懷，協助學生理解並實作適用於低資源語言的 語言科技。 本課程專為文科背景碩士生設計，強調語言學知識在技術應用中的關鍵角色。無需程式或數學背景，學生將 透過實作任務學習語料建置、詞性標註、情感分析、機器翻譯、零樣本學習與大型語言模型應用。課堂中亦將介 紹跨語言經驗、語音轉寫、語料展示、分類工具設計等範例，引導學生親自規劃一項以臺灣語言為核心的 NLP 任務提案。期待學生在這門課中不僅建立跨域能力，更成為臺灣語言延續的重要推動者。 對於過去對程式設計或數理能力感到沒有自信的學生，本課程將以友善且循序漸進的方式，協助學生克服對 技術領域的陌生與焦慮。本課程並不以培養程式專家為目標，而是鼓勵學生以自身的語言專業切入，理解並參與 自然語言處理的實務應用，將語言的溫度與文化的深度帶入技術發展之中。語言學者所具備獨特的觀察力與文化 敏感度，正是當代語言科技應用中不可或缺的核心資產。我們期待每位學生都能在這堂課中突破限制、發現可 能，並重新認識自己作為語言學者的潛力與價值。 這是一門專為研究臺灣本土語言——如閩南語、客家語與各原住民族語——的學生設計的跨域課程。課程目 標不是讓修課學生成為程式高手，而是讓修課學生明白：即使不擅程式，也能成為推動語言延續與科技應用的重 要關鍵。 在這門課程裡，學生將學習到： (一) 自然語言處理工具如何應用於低資源語言； (二) 現行語言模型如何運作，以及哪些地方需要語言學家的專業判斷與介入； (三) 實際案例分析：過去成功的少數語言技術應用與語料建構經驗； (四) 如何與資訊工程師、資料科學家對話，並用語言學的知識定義需求與目標； (五) 初步使用語言處理平台與工具（如語料庫建置、語音轉寫、字詞標註與模型微調），不要求數學背景，重視 學習動機與語言關懷。 修習本課程後，學生可望具備將語言學知識轉化為自然語言處理（NLP）應用的核心能力。即使沒有程式背 景，也能使用現成工具獨立完成低資源語言的小型技術專案，為自己的碩士論文或研究開創更多跨領域的可能。 同時，學生也將培養與資訊工程師、資料科學家溝通的基礎語彙與實作經驗，未來不論從事語言教學、語言保 存、數位人文研究、文化科技、或進一步投入 AI 與語言科技產業，皆具備實務參與與創新貢獻的潛力。 ●指定閱讀文章(Text Books) (1) Agyei, E., Zhang, X., Bannerman, S., Quaye, A. B., Yussi, S. B., & Agbesi, V. K. (2024). Low resource Twi- English parallel corpus for machine translation in multiple domains (Twi-2-ENG). Information Retrieval (Boston), 27(1), 17-. https://doi.org/10.1007/s10791-024-09451-8 6 (2) Baishya, D., & Baruah, R. (2024). Part-of-speech Tagging for Low-resource Languages: Activation Function for Deep Learning Network to Work with Minimal Training Data. docs.name: 人工智慧時代中重審言語行為理論
docs.nameEn: Revisiting Speech-Act Theories in the Age of AI
docs.text: 1 國立清華大學課程大綱 科號 Course Number EMI 課程 學分 Credit 3 人數限制 Class Size 中文名稱 Course Title 人工智慧時代中重審言語行為理論 (Offered in English) 英文名稱 Course English Title Revisiting Speech-Act Theories in the Age of AI 任課教師 Instructor 呂菁菁 上課時間 Time 星期三 (同“語言學通論” 時間) 上課教室 Room 課程簡述(最多 500 個中文字) 本欄位資料會上傳教育部課程網 Brief Course Description (required) (50-200 words if possible, up to 1000 letters) 本課程從語言哲學與語用學的經典理論出發，結合當代語言科技發展，重新探討語言如何不只是傳遞資訊，更是 「行動」的方式。課程聚焦於言語行為的分類、間接性、語境依賴、多模態溝通與人機互動等核心議題，並引導 學生理解語言在社會建構、倫理判準與 AI 應用中的新角色。除理論探討外，課程亦涵蓋第二語言習得與跨文化語 用研究，強調批判性閱讀與研究設計能力。期末報告將模擬實際研究提案，幫助學生未來進行語用學研究或語言 科技應用開發。本課程特別適合語言學、語用學、哲學、數位人文、AI 語言應用等領域有興趣的研究生。 課程內容「中文暨英文關鍵字」 至少 5 個,每個關鍵字至多 20 個中文,以半形逗點分隔 Please fill in at least 5 course keywords (up to 40 letters for each keyword) and use commas to separate them.(required) 中文關鍵詞：言語行為, 語用學, 語境, 間接語言, 禮貌策略、文化詮釋 英文關鍵詞：Speech Acts, Pragmatics, Context, Indirect Speech, Politeness Strategies, Cultural Interpretation 2 ●指定用書 (Text Books) (1) Fogal, D., Harris, D. W., & Moss, M. (Eds.). (2018). New work on speech acts (First edition.). Oxford University Press. (2) Jucker, A. H. (2024). Speech acts : discursive, multimodal and diachronic (1st ed.). Cambridge University Press. (3) Lee, C., & SpringerLink. (2018). Researching and teaching second language speech acts in the Chinese context. Springer Singapore. https://doi.org/10.1007/978-981-10-8980-0 (4) Ogiermann, E., & Garcés-Conejos Blitvich, P. (Eds.). (2019). From speech acts to lay understandings of politeness : multilingual and multicultural perspectives. Cambridge University Press. (5) Ruytenbeek, N. (2021). Indirect speech acts. Cambridge University Press. ● 教學方式(Teaching Method) 在第一堂課，授課教師將發給同學整學期每週的討論問題清單，並提供相關的背景閱讀資料作為準備。每週上課 時，老師會先介紹當週的關鍵概念，並帶領學生進一步拆解段落結構、圖表內容與重要術語，幫助大家掌握核心 知識。課程最後，學生將以英語分享自己對該週討論問題的想法，並進行全班討論。這樣的課堂互動設計，旨在 幫助一開始對於以英語閱讀及表達感到生疏或不自信的同學，在授課教師與同儕的支持下，逐步建立理解與表達 能力。 ● 參考書籍(References) Derakhshan, A., Shakki, F., & SpringerLink. (2023). Instructed second language pragmatics for the speech acts of request, apology, and refusal : a meta-analysis. Springer Nature Switzerland. https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-031-37093-9 3 ● 教學進度(Syllabus) 各週教學主題: 第 1 週：從 Austin 到 AI：言語行為理論為何成為語言哲學與語用學的基石 第 2 週：案例分析如何在社交語境中對「暗示」、共識建立與對話紀錄三者之間的語用關係 第 3 週：句式與語用力量：命令句、語氣與規範判準 第 4 週：言語內容與言語力道：區分與重新建構類別 第 5 週：間接言語行為的理論基礎與語意挑戰 第 6 週：認知與關聯理論下的語用推理與理解 第 7 週：禮貌策略、間接性與社會語境的交互作用 第 8 週：人工智慧對對間接語言的處理策略與尚未解決的問題 第 9 週：禮貌與不禮貌的視角 第 10 週：跨語言與跨文化語用常規：社會語境中的言語行為 第 11 週：在數位時代電子郵件、討論區、即時訊息等情境中的語用特徵 第 12 週：全球化與文化詮釋：面子考量與語言政治 第 13 週：L1 與 L2 中的言語行為能力發展：語用習得與可教性問題 第 14 週：文化概念與語用表現：以華語學習者為例的語言轉移與文化影響 第 15 週：從研究到教學設計：言語行為能力的培養與言語行為的教學設計策略 第 16 週：學生進行期末研究提案發表，提案內容需包括：理論基礎、研究設計、語用目標與應用面向 ● 成績考核(Evaluation) (一) 課前閱讀每週指定閱讀文獻章節（25%）； (二) 課堂參與與討論貢獻（25%）； (三) 期末報告 (書面) （50%）。 ● 課程說明(Course Description) AI 時代的溝通需求，特別是語用理解、意圖辨識、禮貌策略、自動回應與責任分配問題，正急需我們以更新 的方法重讀經典、拓展視野。因此，我們「重審」的是一套在 AI 應用浪潮下被重新賦能的理論資產，也是一次語 言學與技術人文思維的交叉再定位。 傳統的言語行為理論，自 Austin 與 Searle 提出以來，主要針對人類交際中語言的行動本質進行分類與分析。 然而，在當代語言科技快速演進下，AI 系統已不再只是「處理語言的工具」，而是積極參與人類溝通的對話主體 ——無論是在客服機器人、語音助理、AI 教學系統，乃至法律、醫療與教育場域的語言生成任務中，AI 如何理 解、產出、甚至被期望執行某種言語行為，言語行為理論面臨了前所未有的應用挑戰。本課程之所以採用「重 審」為主軸，正是希望引導學生重新思考這一語言哲學經典理論在 AI 語境下的適切性、侷限與潛能。 在這樣的背景下，Fogal, Harris 與 Moss 編著的 New Work on Speech Acts（2018）為我們提供了理論 4 基礎的再深化與挑戰；Jucker（2024）對於言語行為在多模態、歷時與語境中的再詮釋，使我們看到其應用範圍 的擴展；Ruytenbeek（2021）深入分析間接言語行為，更直接呼應 AI 語言模型如何處理語用含義的難題；Lee （2018）與 Ogiermann & Garcés-Conejos Blitvich（2019）則讓我們看到語言教學與文化語用中的言語行為 如何被學習、誤解與在跨文化語境中再建構。 本課程的期末報告設計，旨在培養學生未來能夠獨立從事「言語行為」（speech acts）研究時所需的研究設 計能力與批判思維。相較於單純的文本分析或心得書寫，本課程更重視研究方法的選擇與論證，因為在語用學與 語言哲學的交會領域中，如何設計一個合理、有效且具說服力的研究架構，是進入學術對話的第一步。 因此，期末報告將採「研究計畫提案」的形式，請修課同學仿作 Derakhshan, Shakki (2023) 的研究架構，撰寫 一份具備完整研究思考脈絡的提案。學生可根據自己感興趣的言語行為議題（如請求、拒絕、道歉、稱讚、婉轉 策略等），提出未來可能實作的研究構想，並在報告中包含以下五個核心部分： 1. Overview of Theoretical Frameworks：簡述將採用的理論架構，並說明其與你的研究主題有何關聯。 2. Empirical Background：回顧與主題相關的實證研究，提出研究缺口與你的切入點。 3. Design of the Study：清楚陳述研究對象、語料來源或實驗方法、變項設定與分析方式。 4. Expected Results：根據設計與理論，預測可能觀察到的結果與語用行為趨勢。 5. Pedagogical Implications and Future Research Directions：說明研究成果可能帶來的教學應用價值，並 提出未來進一步研究的方向。 修習《AI 時代中重審言語行為理論》這門課後，學生將具備跨越語言哲學、語用學與人工智慧應用之間的理 論整合與分析能力。他們將能深入理解言語行為背後的語意邏輯、社會功能與語境依賴性，並進一步掌握如何將 這些知識應用於當代語言科技情境中，例如人機互動、對話系統設計、跨文化語用教學，或是針對社會議題進行 語言行為批判分析。對未來有志從事語言學研究、第二語言教學、AI 語言應用、社會語言觀察或語言與倫理交叉 領域的學生而言，本課程將奠定紮實的理論基礎與實務對話能力，使他們不僅能跟上語言科技的腳步，更有能力 提出深具批判性與文化敏感度的回應與創新觀點。 ● 採用下列何項 AI 使用規則(Indicate which of the following options you use to manage student use of the AI)： 有條件開放，請註明如何使用生成式 AI 於課程產出 Conditionally open; please specify how generative AI will be used in course output

docs.name: 臺灣語言研究實驗設計專題
docs.nameEn: Experimental Research Design in the Study of Taiwanese Languages
docs.text: 1 國立清華大學課程大綱 科號 Course Number 學分 Credit 3 人數限制 Class Size 中文名稱 Course Title 臺灣語言研究實驗設計專題 英文名稱 Course English Title Experimental Research Design in the Study of Taiwanese Languages 任課教師 Instructor 呂菁菁 上課時間 Time 星期四 16:30~19:20 上課教室 Room 課程簡述(最多 500 個中文字) 本欄位資料會上傳教育部課程網 Brief Course Description (required) (50-200 words if possible, up to 1000 letters) 本課程旨在培養學生以事件相關腦電位（ERPs）作為工具，進行語言處理歷程的實驗研究設計能力。課程將介紹 ERP 的基本概念與語言應用，並以臺灣語言為核心，探討詞彙、語音、語法、語用、雙語處理與語言障礙等主 題。每週課堂以一篇已完成的學位論文為範例，深入說明實驗設計流程、刺激材料製作、數據結果與理論連結。 學生將透過期中報告回應課堂案例，反思個人興趣；期末報告則鼓勵學生發展屬於自己的語言實驗構想。適合對 語言與腦科學整合應用有興趣，特別是未來計畫將 ERP 納入碩士論文研究的同學修習。 課程內容「中文暨英文關鍵字」 至少 5 個,每個關鍵字至多 20 個中文,以半形逗點分隔 Please fill in at least 5 course keywords (up to 40 letters for each keyword) and use commas to separate them.(required) 中文關鍵詞：臺灣語言研究, 語言研究實驗, 實驗設計, 事件相關電位, 語言處理歷程 英文關鍵詞：Taiwanese Languages, Experimental Linguistic Research, Experimental Design, Event-Related Potentials (ERP), Language Processing 2 課程大綱 Detailed Course Syllabus ● 課程說明(Course Description) 你是否曾經好奇，我們的腦中如何理解語言？語音、語意、語法甚至語用的處理，是否能在大腦中被「看 見」？本課程專為語言研究所學生設計，將帶領同學實際走入語言與腦神經科學的交集領域，學習如何以「事件 相關腦電位（Event-Related Potentials, ERPs）」這項工具，進行語言處理歷程的實驗設計與分析。 這門課將聚焦在臺灣語言言就與語言教學相關的主題，並以每週一個語言研究案例為核心，說明實驗設計的 完整歷程——從問題設定、材料設計、受試者安排、數據收集，到結果解釋與理論啟發。所有案例皆出自真實的 學位論文，涵蓋多樣研究面向，包括： 1. 以圖片命名任務探討詞彙與語意處理； 2. 雙語者（國語與台語）腦中語言運作的比較； 3. 華語與臺灣語言語音差異的腦波反應； 4. 學生語法學習風格與語法掌握的神經對應； 5. 腦傷病人不同部位損傷與語言功能障礙的關聯； 6. 探索唐詩與數學文字題中語法結構的腦中反應； 7. 語用態度（如心智理論、換位思考）的腦電生理表徵。 本課程不要求神經語言學或腦波分析的先備知識，將以深入淺出的方式帶領修課學生建立以下能力： (一) 跨域能力：培養語言研究與腦神經科學整合的視野與能力； (二) 理論與應用連結：能以實驗結果回應語言理論問題，並進行批判性思考； (三) 抽象研究目標落地能力：啟發學生將語言議題轉化為具體、可測量的實驗假設； (四) 實驗設計實作經驗：理解 ERP 實驗設計邏輯，可做為未來碩士論文實作藍圖； (五) 資料詮釋力：初步掌握 ERP 數據閱讀與詮釋的基礎技巧。 適合修習對象為： 對語言在大腦中如何運作感到好奇，並有志以腦波實驗作為碩士論文研究方法的學生。本課程特別適合研究臺灣 本土語言（如臺灣閩南語、客語、原住民族語等）、雙語現象、語言教育或語言障礙等議題的同學。 3 ● 參考書籍(References) Cong, F., Ristaniemi, T., Lyytinen, H., & World Scientific. (2015). Advanced signal processing on brain event-related potentials filtering ERPs in time, frequency and space domains sequentially and simultaneously. World Scientific. ● 教學進度(Syllabus) 各週主題安排： 第 1 週：課程導論與 ERP 基礎 第 2 週：語意處理：N400 的理論與經典研究 第 3 週：圖片命名與語意層次處理 第 4 週：聽覺 vs 視覺語言處理：腦部反應與來源定位 第 5 週：論旨角色處理與語法語意界線 第 6 週：語用理解與大腦處理：素材形式的影響 第 7 週：語用與禮貌預期違反：社會語言學與 ERP 第 8 週：老化與語言處理：年齡對 ERP 反應的影響 第 9 週：期中討論與 ERP 實驗設計實作工作坊 第 10 週：失語症與詞彙處理：語法類別的神經反應 第 11 週：語碼轉換與語意交互效應 第 12 週：語音感知與磁吸效應：感知與產出的分離 第 13 週：心理詞彙庫中的變體儲存：方言與腔調研究 第 14 週：語言策略與學習者變異：ERP 在英語學習研究中的應用 第 15 週：ERP 在臨床應用中的價值：失語症理解能力的評估 第 16 週：期末總結與修課同學研究提案發表 ● 成績考核(Evaluation) 本課程採兩份書面作業作為主要評量工具，幫助同學統整所學、培養思考與設計語言實驗的能力： (一) 期中報告（50%）： 針對課程前七週所討論的實驗範例，選出一篇自己最喜歡的研究，說明選擇這篇的原因。學生可以從研究主題、 材料設計、結果呈現方式，或是它的啟發切入，清楚描述自己與該研究之間的「連結感」。這份作業鼓勵學生開 始思考自己有興趣的語言研究類型與可能性。 (二) 期末報告（50%）： 回顧整學期所介紹的範例，挑出自己最有共鳴、最能想像自己也可以進行的研究方向，進一步嘗試擬出一份簡單 的實驗設計草案。內容需包含： 1. 研究問題與假設； 2. 預期的實驗材料或任務； 3. 推估可能出現的 ERP 結果； 4. 若出現這樣的結果，會對語言理論或語言使用理解帶來哪些可能的啟示。 4 ●各週指定閱讀書籍(Text Books) (2) 華語、閩南語語句中論旨角色語義成分違反—事件相關腦電位研究 https://hdl.handle.net/11296/3wwkwa (3) 以圖片促發詞彙之事件相關腦電位研究 https://hdl.handle.net/11296/4wxabk (4) 台語失語症病人詞彙理解之腦事件相關電位研究 https://hdl.handle.net/11296/j2s6t8 (5) 以事件相關腦電位評估失語症患者的理解能力之研究 https://hdl.handle.net/11296/24a7tq (6) 台灣客家話語用理解及其腦事件相關電位研究 https://hdl.handle.net/11296/9yyx7r (7) 閩南語稱呼語與語用場合之事件相關腦電位 https://hdl.handle.net/11296/x7yrj6 (8) 年老與語言衰退的關係－台語詞彙語義處理之腦事件相關電位研究 https://hdl.handle.net/11296/t2avc4 (10) 失語症患者詞彙語義理解之事件相關腦電位研究 https://hdl.handle.net/11296/x8rm6c (11) 台華雙語人語碼轉換之腦事件相關電位研究 https://hdl.handle.net/11296/33pemt (12) 雙語人之感知磁吸效應:腦事件相關電位研究 https://hdl.handle.net/11296/3789rn (13) 語言變體之事件相關電位研究: 以閩南語次方言為例 https://hdl.handle.net/11296/huczjc (14) 以事件相關腦電位探討台灣大學生英語詞彙多義性理解能力與學習策略相關之研究 https://hdl.handle.net/11296/t9q8x5 (15) 台灣閩南語次方言語音感知之腦事件相關電位研究 https://hdl.handle.net/11296/vxw2w2 5 ● 教學方式(Teaching Method) 教學方式包含由授課教師進行理論講授、案例導讀、實作操作、以及引導全班同學進行批判性反思。 ● 採用下列何項 AI 使用規則(Indicate which of the following options you use to manage student use of the AI)： 有條件開放，請註明如何使用生成式 AI 於課程產出 Conditionally open; please specify how generative AI will be used in course output

docs.name: 閱讀理論與閱讀教學
docs.text: 上課時間：Tue, 13:20~16:20 Fall 2025 3 Credits 課程名稱：閱讀理論與閱讀教學 教師：陳明蕾 email:chen.minglei@mx.nthu.edu.tw 課程介紹 語⾔能⼒⼀般可區分為聽、說、讀、寫四個⾯向，其中「聽」與「讀」同屬於接收 性語⾔技能。然⽽，這兩者在⼈類演化歷程中卻具有本質性的差異：聽⼒理解是⼈類隨 ⽣理成熟⾃然習得的能⼒，⽽閱讀則是⼈類⽂化發展過程中後天建構的產物。在歷史 上，閱讀能⼒⻑期被視為知識菁英階層的專屬能⼒。雖然⽂字系統⾃古即存在，但在承 載⽂字符號的載體尚未能⼤量複製的時代（例如仰賴⼿抄⽺⽪紙、⽵簡等），閱讀的學習 與應⽤受限於資源與權⼒的分配。直到⼗五世紀印刷術的發展，閱讀才逐漸進⼊更廣泛 的社會階層。隨著現代學校制度的推展與啟蒙時代⺠主、⼈權觀念的成熟，閱讀成為每 個⼈都應享有的基本權利，不再是少數⼈的特權，⽽是公⺠參與、個⼈⾃主與教育平權 的基礎。 然⽽，「如何教閱讀」或是「如何有效的教會學⽣具備閱讀能⼒」，⾄今仍是教育領 域中最複雜且具有⾼度公共意義的挑戰之⼀。閱讀需要個體將視覺符號（⽂字）轉換為 語⾔⾳義的表徵，這不僅倚賴視覺辨識與語⾳對應的能⼒，還涉及注意⼒、⼯作記憶、 語⾔理解與背景知識等多重⼼理歷程。也因此，閱讀並⾮⾃然⽽然就能掌握的技能，⽽ 是必須透過有計畫、有系統的教學才能有效發展。 閱讀能⼒的定義，也隨著⽂字載體與媒介技術的演變⽽不斷擴展。從過去以紙本為 主的線性⽂字閱讀，到今⽇以圖⽂並陳、動態呈現為主的數位⽂本，再到⽣成式⼈⼯智 能所產出的多樣化內容樣態，閱讀所需的能⼒與策略也隨之變化。現代讀者不僅需要解 碼與理解書⾯語⾔，還需具備跨模態的辨識能⼒、數位素養，以及對⼈⼯智慧⽣成內容 的判讀與批判性思維。 閱讀教學不能僅依賴經驗傳承或教學直覺，⽽必須建⽴在嚴謹的研究基礎上。閱讀 能⼒內涵的擴充與變化，讓閱讀教學不再只是教學⽣具備紙本閱讀能⼒，⽽是教導學⽣ 如何在多元媒介環境中進⾏訊息接收、判斷與意義建構。在教育場域中，我們⾯對的是 能⼒差異巨⼤的學⽣群體，包含語⾔學習者、學習困難學⽣與⽂化弱勢群體。若無實證 ⽀持，所採⾏的教學⽅法可能不僅無效，甚⾄導致學⽣錯失關鍵的閱讀發展機會。因 此，教育研究有責任回答：什麼樣的閱讀教學有效？為什麼有效？對誰有效？在什麼條 件下有效？ 上課時間：Tue, 13:20~16:20 Fall 2025 3 Credits 本課程將以「閱讀的科學（Science of Reading, SoR）」為基礎，帶領學⽣理解閱讀是 ⼀項複雜、層層交織的⼼理語⾔歷程，並深⼊探討 SoR 如何發展出有效的閱讀教學原 則。本課程透過⽂獻閱讀協助修課學⽣累積紮實的學理，並透過案例研討與教學設計模 擬，協助學⽣掌握閱讀教學設計原則。 此外，⾯對⽣成式⼈⼯智能（Generative AI，GenAI）⽇益成熟且普及，本課程也會 從再概念化(Reconceptualization)的⾓度，探討 GenAI 對閱讀理論與教學的可能衝擊。例 如 GenAI 所⽣成的⽂本快速進⼊教育現場，形式多樣、語意複雜，對傳統閱讀理論架構 形成挑戰。如何協助第⼀線教學實踐⼈員，有效回應科技發展，並兼顧閱讀發展之認知 階段，是閱讀教學研究⼈責無旁貸之處。 課程⽬標: 1. 理解閱讀作為⽂化建構的⼼理語⾔能⼒ 引導學⽣從語⾔演化與⽂化歷史的視⾓出發，認識閱讀在語⾔系統中的特殊 性，掌握閱讀與聽說寫的本質差異，理解閱讀能⼒如何在不同時代與媒介條件下 被形構與擴展。 2. 掌握閱讀理解與閱讀教學的理論基礎 深⼊研讀「閱讀的科學」（Science of Reading）相關理論與研究，理解閱讀歷程 中的認知、語⾔與神經機制，並能評析各種閱讀教學法的理論基礎與實證⽀持。 3. 發展實證導向的閱讀教學設計能⼒ 培養學⽣能根據理論與研究設計閱讀教學活動，並能針對不同學習者（如語⾔ 學習者、學習困難學⽣、多語環境學⽣）進⾏教學調整與策略擬定，強化教學實 務的反思與設計能⼒。 4. 探究 AI 時代下的閱讀教學再概念化 思辨⽣成式⼈⼯智慧（GenAI）如何改變⽂本形態、閱讀歷程與教學需求，並能 從再概念化的觀點探討閱讀教學的未來樣貌，回應數位素養、多模態閱讀與批判 性理解的挑戰。 上課時間：Tue, 13:20~16:20 Fall 2025 3 Credits 課程要求（CourseRequirements） 本課程著重於理論與實務的整合，強調閱讀教學的科學基礎與時代脈絡的再省思， 學生需具備積極參與、主動探究與批判性思維。課程評量依下列項目進行： 導讀報告與口頭發表（30%） 每位學生需負責導讀一篇指定核心文獻，進行口頭簡報並引導課堂討論。鼓勵學 生善用生成式人工智慧（GenAI）作為知識協作工具，但需於簡報中清楚註明其使用方式 與生成對話歷程。 週次學習心得撰寫（30%） 每週課後撰寫一篇約 500–800 字之學習心得，內容應涵蓋本週導讀文獻之反思、 教師講授重點與個人理解。可使用 GenAI 輔助，且附上與 AI 對話的部分紀錄以佐證思 路歷程與學習投入。 期末報告（30%） 學生需選擇一個閱讀理論與教學相關主題，撰寫期末個人研究報告，內容需結合 理論探究與教學應用，文獻資料充分，論證嚴謹，字數建議為 4,000–6,000 字。可使用 GenAI 輔助，且附上與 AI 對話的部分紀錄以佐證思路歷程與論證能力。 同儕回饋書面意見（10%） 每位學生需針對每位同儕的期末研究報告提供一份具建設性的書面回饋，鼓勵提 供理論連結、問題釐清與深化建議。 AI 使用規則說明: 有條件開放，請註明如何使用生成式 AI 於課程產出 Conditionally open; specify generative AI usage in course output. 課程其它說明: 本課程需全程參與，即第一周開始的加退選期間即應全程參與課程。 上課時間：Tue, 13:20~16:20 Fall 2025 3 Credits 日期 主題 內容 1 09/02 課程介紹與說明 閱讀是什麼？語言能力中的閱讀特性與文化歷程 2 09/09 心理學與閱讀教學 Rayner, K., Foorman, B. R., Perfetti, C. A., Pesetsky, D., & Seidenberg, M. S. (2001). How Psychological Science Informs the Teaching of Reading. Psychological Science in the Public Interest, 2, 31-74. http://dx.doi.org/10.1111/1529-1006.00004 3 09/16 複雜的閱讀，簡單的觀點 Hoover, W. A., & Gough, P. B. (1990). The simple view of reading. Reading and Writing: An Interdisciplinary, 2(2), 127–160. https://doi.org/10.1007/BF00401799 4 09/23 閱讀其實真的不簡單 Kim, Y.-S. G. (2020). Hierarchical and dynamic relations of language and cognitive skills to reading comprehension: Testing the direct and indirect effects model of reading (DIER). Journal of Educational Psychology, 112(4), 667–684. https://doi.org/10.1037/edu0000407 5 09/30 閱讀需要動機與調節 Duke, Nell K.; Cartwright, Kelly B. (2021). This course consists of two parts. In the first part, Rudolf Steiner’s theory of three-folding society and its applications worldwide will be introduced and discussed, and the second part will focus on multi- and cross- cultural as well as current social issues in the local context. 授課方式 Medium of Instruction 教師講授、課堂議題討論與文獻閱讀。 Lectures and class discussions will be conducted both in Chinese and English. 評量方式 Assessment 課堂出席 attendance 10% 課堂參與 Class Participation 20% 期中報告 (含口頭與書面報告) Mid-term Report 30% 期末報告 (含口頭與書面報告) Final Report 40% 課程進度 Course Schedule NOTE: Topics and timings are subject to change 第一部份 三元社會的理論與實踐 Part One:Three-folding Society: Theories and Applications Date tentative content July 6th (6 hrs.) 課程介紹 Introduction 教育的目的 The purposes of education – an overview 另類與實驗教育 Alternative and Experimental Education 社會更新的動力(三元社會)Impulse for the renewal of society (three-folding) July 7th (6 hrs.) 社會更新的動力(三元社會) Impulse for the renewal of society (three-folding) 華德福教育的目的—理想之所在 The purposes of Steiner education – the place of ideals 理想與華德福教育的關聯: 理論、組織與教室內 How this relates to Steiner education, in theory, organizationally and in the classroom 史代納的生態動能: 華德福教育中的生態學 Steiner’s ecological impulses Ecology in education, in Waldorf education in particular 第二部份 社會文化脈絡中的華德福教育 Part Two: Steiner education in context Date tentative content July 8th (6 hrs.) 環境與文化 Environment and Culture 華德福教育的文化遺—在世界各地的變遷 1920-2020 The cultural inheritance of Steiner education Changes in the world 1920-2020 傳統—創新連續體 The tradition–innovation continuum 史代納課程取徑 (理念的、書面的、教學的、支持的、隱藏 的、評量的、虛無的、….) Please leave messages on eeclass, using the “personal messages” function. eeclass eeclass 2 prepared by Vicky Hsu Course Aims / Description 1. Primary aim This one-year course is designed to enhance students’ overall English competence through listening, speaking, and reading activities plus grammar review and vocabulary development. A four-skill coursebook plus a self-access learning project will be integrated to design learning tasks and provide opportunities for students to practice language learning strategies, get exposed to English in any form, and develop their confidence and fluency in the classroom and outside the classroom. After having taken this course, students are expected to consolidate their knowledge of English language and engage themselves more confidently and fluently in authentic communication in everyday settings and even in school settings. 2. Subsidiary aim In this class, students will have the opportunity to 1. review and practice grammar points and sentence structures, especially concerning verb tenses, to describe and discuss a variety of topics and issues related to their life 2. build up theme-based vocabulary and also academic words for and through reading and listening to conversations, interviews, talks, and lectures 3. practice academic skills such as outlining, summarizing, paraphrasing, and critical thinking while listening, reading, speaking and writing 4. manage and present information, perspectives, or problem-solving/decision-making in speaking and writing tasks or activities 3. Corresponding CEFR Can-do statements (B2) Reception Listening LISTENING TO RADIO, AUDIO & RECORDINGS B2 Can understand most radio documentaries and most other recorded or broadcast audio material delivered in standard dialect and can identify the speaker’s mood, tone, etc. [listening to radio, audio & recordings] Reception Reading OVERALL READING COMPREHENSION B2 Can read with a large degree of independence, adapting style and speed of reading to different texts and purposes, and using appropriate reference sources selectively. Has a broad active reading vocabulary, but may experience some difficulty with low- frequency vocabulary. [overall reading comprehension] READING FOR INFORMATION & ARGUMENT B2 Can understand articles and reports concerned with contemporary problems in which the writer adopts particular stances or viewpoints. [reading for information & argument] 3 prepared by Vicky Hsu Interaction Spoken Speaking INFORMAL DISCUSSION (WITH FRIENDS) B2 Can account for and sustain his/her opinions in discussion by providing relevant explanation, arguments and comments. [informal discussion (with friends)] INFORMATION EXCHANGE B2 Can pass on detailed information reliably. [information exchange] Production Spoken Speaking OVERALL SPOKEN PRODUCTION B2 Can give clear, detailed description and presentations on a wide range of subjects related to his/her field of interest, expanding and supporting ideas with subsidiary points and relevant examples. [overall spoken production] ADDRESSING AUDIENCES B2 Can give a clear, prepared presentation, giving reasons in support of or against a particular point of view and giving the advantages and disadvantages of various options. [addressing audiences] Reception Communi cation Strategies IDENTIFYING CUES & INFERRING (SPOKEN & WRITTEN) B2 Can use a variety of strategies to achieve comprehension, including listening for main points, checking comprehension by using contextual clues. [identifying cues & inferring (spoken & written)] EAP Interaction Communi cation Strategies COOPERATING B2 Can give feedback on and follow up statements and inferences and so help the development of the discussion. [cooperating] EAP ASKING FOR CLARIFICATION B2 Can ask follow-up questions to check that he/she has understood what a speaker intended to say, and get clarification of ambiguous points. [asking for clarification] Working with Text NOTE-TAKING (LECTURES, SEMINARS, ETC.) B2 Can understand a clearly structured lecture on a familiar subject, and can take notes on points which strike him/her as important, even though he/she tends to concentrate on the words themselves and therefore to miss some information. [note-taking (lectures, seminars, etc.) EAP PROCESSING TEXT 4 prepared by Vicky Hsu B2 Can summarize a wide range of factual and imaginative texts, commenting on and discussing contrasting points of view and the main themes. [processing text] EAP Communicative Language Competence Range GENERAL LINGUISTIC RANGE B2+ Can express him/herself clearly and without much sign of having to restrict what he/she wants to say. [processing text] VOCABULARY RANGE B2 Has a good range of vocabulary for matters connected to his/her field and most general topics. [vocabulary range] Control GRAMMATICAL ACCURACY B2+ Good grammatical control. Occasional “slips” or non-systematic errors and minor flaws in sentence structure may still occur, but they are rare and can often be corrected in retrospect. [grammatical accuracy] VOCABULARY CONTROL B2 Lexical accuracy is generally high, though some confusion and incorrect word choice does occur without hindering communication. [vocabulary control] ORTHOGRAPHIC CONTROL B2 Can produce clearly intelligible continuous writing, which follows standard layout and paragraphing conventions. [orthographic control] EAP B2 Spelling, punctuation and layout are accurate but may show signs of mother tongue influence. [orthographic control] Sociolinguistic SOCIOLINGUISTIC APPROPRIATENESS B2 Can with some effort keep up with and contribute to group discussions even when speech is fast and colloquial. [sociolinguistic appropriateness] Pragmatic FLEXIBILITY B2 Can adjust to the changes of direction, style and emphasis normally found in conversation. Class attendance, lesson preparation and active class participation are required.  As you are all present whenever the instructor takes the roll, you will get 60% in this category Attendance and Participation. 經常性點名，全勤者可得「出席與參與」項目中的 60%成績。  Each skip will cost 2 points from the category Attendance and Participation (up to 15 points in the final grade). 未假不到課（翹課），每 次從「出席與參與」成績（占學期成績 15 分）扣 2 分。  If you are absent in case of UNCONTROLLABLE situations (e.g. illness, NTHU Q&A 6 prepared by Vicky Hsu emergency, important occasions, etc.), please apply for a leave on the Student Leave System on Academic Information System of National Tsing Hua University or on the iNTHU app (from the Office of Student Affair website), with clear leave information, including leave type, leave period, and reasons (must be clear and valid enough for the teacher’s approval). As the reasons or the documents are not clear, valid or sufficient enough, the teacher may deny the application. 遇不可抗力情形需請假者，請於本校校務資訊系統上的學生請假系統或下載 iNTHU APP，填寫資料（請假類別、請假日期、請假事由）。請假事由須合理並敘述清楚，提供老 師是否准假之參考。請假單上的理由或所附證明文件不清楚或不充分時，該次請假申請得不予 核准。  Please observe the information you are expected to offer for each of the following leave types:  For sick leave, please describe severe symptoms and medical treatments you have been taking in the box “Reason.” 請病假時，請於理由欄位說明影響上課之顯著症狀，就醫或服 藥等處理。  For personal leave, please describe the uncontrollable event and how it makes you absent from the class. 請事假時，請於理由欄位敘明事件，並說明該事件如何致使你無法前來上 課。  No leave application will be approved on the dates of presentations, peer evaluations, and midterm/final exams. Please care for your health and reserve the time for these important class activities. 報告、同儕互評、期中／期末考當日不得請假。請注意身心健康 並為這些重要課程活動預留時間。  There will be NO make-up exams or presentations unless you apply for leave with valid and official reasons for your absence beforehand. 無合理且正式的缺課原因，將不予補考 或補行報告。  You are expected to apply for leave before the class you are absent from. Any overdue leave application must be made within 7 days from the last day of absence. 請假已事先申請為原 則。逾期請假申請必須於 7 日內補請。未能於規定期間申請者，均以曠課論。  Being late for more than 10 minutes (with no valid excuses) is treated as absence from that hour. Being late for more than 30 minutes is treated as absence from the whole class. 無故 遲到逾 10 分鐘，以該小時未到課紀錄。遲到逾 30 分鐘，視為該次上課未到課。  No points will be deducted for your ATTENDANCE as long as your approved leave is no more than 6 hours. However, you may lose points for your PARTICIPATION or in-class practices scheduled on the date of your absence. 核准的請假時數未逾 6 小時，不扣出席成績。惟當日 如有上課練習或小組活動，請假者無法參與或完成，將無法獲得該次練習或該項評量成績。換 言之，缺課仍可能影響「參與」與「作業」等成績。  If you skip class for more than 8 hours, your course withdrawal may NOT be approved, and you will get 0 credits for this course. 無故不到課逾 8 小時者，將不予同意其停修申請，亦無 法取得本課程學分。  A student will fail to get the 2 credits for missing 5 classes, including the ones due to any kinds of leaves. 缺課達五次（含各類請假缺課）者，將無法從本課程獲取任何學分。 7 prepared by Vicky Hsu 2. Absence from a class is no excuse for failing to complete in-class practices, to submit assignments in time, or to get informed of assignments or the class you have missed. It is your responsibility to hand in the assignments within 5 days (weekends & holidays included) and to reach your classmates or the instructor and refer to the course platform (eeclass) for the relevant information concerning what has been covered in the class. You may ask a classmate of yours to help with assignment submission and collection of assignment worksheets, if any. You may make an appointment with the instructor for assignment worksheets. 缺席與請假不得作為未 能完成當日上課練習、無法及時繳交作業或不知道該次課後作業之藉口。缺席與請假者負有及時 （五日內）繳交作業，並透過同學、課程平台，或親自聯繫老師了解該次上課內容與課後作業之 責。（可委託同學代為繳交作業或拿取作業單，或自行前來教師研究室繳交或領取。） 3.  Assignments are expected to be completed and submitted by the due date. No late submission will be accepted or graded unless the instructor approves or grants your application for extension of submission. 作業請按時繳交（或上傳）。未獲教師同意可延遲繳 交者或超過寬限期，其遲交作業不批改、不計分。  Your absence CANNOT be an assumption that you are entitled to hand in the late assignments far later (more than 5 days) or until your next presence. 請勿自以為逾期的作業可以自行延遲超過五 日，或下次出現時才繳交。  NO full credit for late submission/Penalty for late submission: 10% of the total mark awarded will be deducted for each working day after the submission date. 每遲交一日。扣 10%成績。 Late Submission Mark Awarded After Penalty Number of days late Penalty Original grade 90 Original grade 60 1 10% 81 54 2 20% 72 48 3 30% 63 42 4 40% 54 36 5 50% 45 30 More than 5 days Grade of zero awarded 遲交逾 5 日，不計分  Frequent late submissions with no valid excuses or under controllable circumstances will NOT be accepted or graded since the third late assignment. 無合理原因或非為不可抗力情形 的慣性遲交作業，第三份起將不予批改與計分。 4. Plagiarism on assignments and cheating on the exam is absolutely unacceptable. If someone is found plagiarizing or cheating, it means he/she will get a zero point for that assignment or exam. 嚴禁抄襲與作弊。抄襲與作弊者，學期成績以不及格處理。情節重大時，將提報至相關單 位依校規處理。 5. AI-assisted reports and assignments are allowed in limited instances: AI can be used to prepare for reports and assignments by brainstorming and tentative revision, but students must show how AI helps them reach the result. 僅限使用生成式 AI 於作業或報告之準備（如腦力激盪與初步 8 prepared by Vicky Hsu 修訂等），學生須註明 AI 如何用於協作其作業或報告。 6. Penalty for no or poor participation in pair or group work Students are expected to take part in pair or group activities. Failure to engage in these activities (due to you absence or lateness) will lead to reductions in grades awarded. Sometimes the reduction may be suggested by other group members; in other circumstances, the instructor may reduce the grade awarded without reference to other group members. 學生負有參與雙人 或小組活動之義務。如因個人遲到或缺席導致小組活動無法順利進行，請假或缺席者該次活動成 績將以扣分或甚至 0 分計算。 7.  Mobile devices are only used for educational purposes relevant to the subject or tasks in the classroom setting with the permission of or at the request of the instructor. Using mobile devices for studying other subjects or entertaining purposes is absolutely prohibited. Students who violate the regulation will be considered absent from the class or asked to leave the classroom. 行動裝置僅限於學習活動，使用須獲得老師同意或遵照老師指示。嚴禁 使用行動裝置研習其他課程或娛樂使用。違反規定者，以「未到課」處置，亦得請違規者離開 教室。  During class students are not to be seen with a cell phone in hand or on the desk. Mobile phones are expected to be turned off or switched to a silent mode. 課程進行時，請關閉行動 電話或轉為靜音模式。未獲教師指示或許可，不得於上課時間使用或放置於桌上。 8. The syllabus, handouts, and returned assignments should be kept at least until the end of this semester for later reference or the final exam. 課程相關各項文件請妥為保存至學期結束。 Teaching Activities  Lectures 口頭講授  Pair/Group discussion 配對／分組討論  Assignments 作業  Student presentations 學生報告  Quizzes 小考  online practice 線上練習 Classroom Languages English 80 % Mandarin 20 % Tentative Weekly Schedule WEEK DATE Coursebook Units/Topics Tentative Learning Tasks Academic Language Skills 1 9/1 Course orientation Diagnostic assessment Pre-course questionnaire Using and learning English in college 2 9/8 File 2A Doctor, doctor! and Presentation Guide 1. Purpose The podcasting practice aims to present your understanding of Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and to express your concerns and inspiration about making your city (your home city or the city you are living in) or your community (the area around your campus or your dormitory) a better place to live in the future 2. In your podcast, you are expected to a. identify a problem you are concerned about in your city or community b. define/explain what SDGs are and which SDG you are going to focus on c. share SDG cases or examples related to a similar problem as an inspiration d. propose practical solutions to the problem 3. References: https://www.un.org/sustainabledevelopment/ https://www.parenting.com.tw/article/5091099 永續發展目標 17 項目標及台灣實例 https://futurecity.cw.com.tw/article/1867 SDGs 懶人包》什麼是永續發展目標 SDGs？ 4. Presentation a. Mode of presentation a pre-recorded PODCAST by each individual student  Your podcast can be a solo storytelling, an interview, or a repurposed content show.  You must host the show, and your voice is identifiable in the podcast.  You and your guest(s) MUST speak English in the podcast.  You may ask your classmates, friends, or family members to be your guest(s) if your podcast is designed as an interview. b. Suggested Length of presentation 3-4 minutes for a solo storytelling/talk 4-5 minutes for an interview or for a repurposed content show c. Deadline for uploading the podcast (audio file) and the script (PDF file) to eeclass LANG1020 01 (M1M2) LANG1020 08 (M3M4) LANG1020 20 (R1R2) Podcast upload October 31 October 31 November 3 Peer Review (8-10 podcasts) November 1-3 November 1-3 November 4-6  Peer and self evaluation will be conducted in Week 10. Each student will be assigned 8-10 podcasts for evaluation right after the deadline. You will have 2-3 days to complete the peer evaluation by grading on eeclass and commenting under each podcast. 14 prepared by Vicky Hsu  Each podcast will be evaluated with a rubric in terms of the five categories: Content – the speaker’s knowledge and insight, relevant information and quality details (beyond the obvious), in-depth research, catchy and clever opening (topic, purpose, & sequence of events for the podcast), engaging and informative discussion/narration, and effective and impressive ending Language Use – good use of storytelling or narrative structure, effective use of open-ended and follow-up questions for interview, and good choice of words and phrases for spoken communication Delivery – well-rehearsed for grammar, vocabulary, cadence, and rhythm to keep the audience engaged; intelligible & in a conversational style Audio/Sound Design – clear recording of narration or interview, free of extraneous noise, proper use of ambient sound and sound effects Technical Production/Teamwork – adequate podcast length, smooth transition, equal contribution of teammates, accurate and well-written script 5. Preparation  Work as an individual or a team (recruiting and managing team members)  Choose an SDG as a topic  Develop and maintain the research (extracting relevant and interesting information) and podcast schedule (discussions and meetings)  Organize and schedule rehearsing and recording sessions  Manage sound quality and edit the podcast episode  keep track of the deadline and ensure that your podcast and script are uploaded on time Reminder: This podcasting practice is NOT aimed at demonstrating your talents for collecting and presenting information or expressing your opinions about SDGs. You are expected to extract practicable and feasible actions for your audience. As a general rule, podcasts are a form of entertainment. People tend to listen to podcasts to learn more about a topic or keep up with current events in a relaxing or entertaining way. 6. Points to ponder  Who are you speaking to? What is the effective way to speak to your audience?  What do you expect to happen to your audience?  What do you expect the audience to remember? (Don’t be greedy. Think about how much you remember after attending a one- or two-hour lecture.)  How would you arrange the information to have your audience become aware of the SDG in your podcast?  In what way can you deliver the key points more efficiently and effectively? 15 prepared by Vicky Hsu LANG 1010 _____ Upper-Intermediate English I Student ID ____________ Name _________________ Date _____ Podcasting－Rubric for Peer Evaluation Criteria ExcepƟonal Great Good DisappoinƟng A disaster Audience percepƟon (20%) I finished listening to the podcast, and I enjoyed the podcast episode. Content (30%) The audience gets hooked soon and effortlessly follows the whole podcast episode. The speaker(s) makes the audience learn the connecƟon of SDGs to audiences’ lives by offering appropriate and sufficient examples and explanaƟons either in a funny way or in a comprehensible way. (SDGs) The audience is at ease with the podcast episode though it sounds someƟmes a bit boring. The speaker has no idea of the topic and the podcast episode at all. 16 prepared by Vicky Hsu Criteria ExcepƟonal Great Good DisappoinƟng A disaster Performance (20%) The speaker demonstrates enthusiasm about the topic during the podcast. The speaker holds the audience's aƩenƟon with good use of volume and voice inflecƟon (rhythm, tone, emphasis), and moderate speech rate. The speaker sounds like reading from notes through the enƟre podcast. He or she speaks i in low volume and monotonous tone. Preparedness (15%) The speaker is completely prepared and must have had sufficient rehearsals. 。 The speaker is preƩy prepared and may have had several rehearsals. The speaker is somewhat prepared but might have had a couple of rehearsals. The speaker does not seem prepared and may have lacked rehearsals. The speaker is obviously unprepared at all. 17 prepared by Vicky Hsu Criteria ExcepƟonal Great Good DisappoinƟng A disaster Originality, CreaƟvity & Dynamics (15%) The design of the podcast rocks, with an excellent combinaƟon of intro, talks/conversaƟons, outro, and even sound effects. It is unique and does not like other podcast episodes I have listened to. The SDG is effecƟvely delivered in the podcast, in a well-organized framework of the SDG, examples close to our lives, and comprehensible explanaƟons/interpretaƟon. The design of the podcast engages the audience with a nice combinaƟon of intro, talks/conversaƟons, and outro. It has similar components as other podcast episodes I have listened to. The SDG is clearly delivered in the podcast, but it does not go with examples or explanaƟons close to our lives. The design of the podcast may not be as interesƟng or fantasƟc as intro, talks/conversaƟons, or outro is not well connected to one another. It has similar components as other podcast episodes I have listened to. Not every secƟon of the podcast is closely connected to SDG. Some parts are strange and do not serve any purpose. SDG The design of the podcast is confusing or disorganized. The podcast appeared forced and hard to follow. The SDG seldom runs through the podcast episode. Many parts are weird and full of irrelevant informaƟon. It sounds like parts of it were thrown together at the last minute. SDG The podcast lacks design and creaƟvity. It did not observe the guidelines of the podcasƟng project. Or it doesn’t sound done. The SDG hardly runs through the podcast episode. The podcast sounds as if it is not shaped yet, sƟll rough. In other words, you are expected to transfer skills, strategies, and knowledge in your self-paced and self-regulated learning to the exams, assignments, discussions, and presentations this semester.) Also, these online exercises may help you prepare for the speaking and speaking tests of BESTEP（培力英檢）. Tasks: Three speaking exercises and three writing exercises will be assigned on TEEMI for your self- paced and self-regulated practices during the semester (week 4-week 14). In the speaking sector, you will be practicing: 1. Listen and Answer (Part 1 Task 2) 2. Situational Question and Answer (Part 2 Task 1) 3. The course incorporates a four-skill coursebook and a self-access learning project to provide structured learning tasks and opportunities for independent practice. Students will also be introduced to essential academic English skills, such as summarizing texts and writing structured essays, as well as practicing note-taking and understanding lectures to improve their ability to engage with academic materials. Primary aim Upper-intermediate English I is an integrated course designed to develop students' four English skills (i.e., listening, speaking, reading, & writing) with an emphasis on speaking and listening. In this course, students will: -Identify listening problems and develop listening strategies and skills, -Gain confidence in speaking and improve speaking fluency, pronunciation, and conversation strategies, -Develop general reading skills, including word skills and comprehension strategies. 2. Subsidiary aim In this class, students will have opportunity to 1. listen to authentic English-speaking topics such as English news reports, daily life conversations or English documentary video clips and personal presentation. 2. review and practice grammar points and sentence structures to describe and discuss a variety of topics and issues related to their life 3. build up theme-based vocabulary and even academic words for and through reading and listening to conversations, interviews, talks, and lectures 4. practice academic skills such as outlining, summarizing, critical thinking while listening, reading, speaking and writing 2 revised by KWONG 5. manage and present information, perspectives, or problem-solving in speaking and writing tasks or activities 3. Corresponding CEFR Can-do statements LISTENING AS A MEMBER OF A LIVE AUDIENCE B2 Can follow the essentials of lectures, talks and reports and other forms of academic/professional presentations which are propositionally and linguistically complex. [listening as a member of a live audience] EAP EOP LISTENING TO ANNOUNCEMENTS & INSTRUCTIONS B2 Can understand announcements and messages on concrete and abstract topics spoken in standard dialect at normal speed. [listening to announcements & instructions] LISTENING TO RADIO, AUDIO & RECORDINGS B2 Can understand most radio documentaries and most other recorded or broadcast audio material delivered in standard dialect and can identify the speaker’s mood, tone, etc. [listening to radio, audio & recordings] WATCHING TV & FILM B2 Can understand most TV news and current affairs programs. [watching TV & film] Reception Reading OVERALL READING COMPREHENSION B2 Can read with a large degree of independence, adapting style and speed of reading to different texts and purposes, and using appropriate reference sources selectively. Has a broad active reading vocabulary, but may experience some difficulty with low- frequency vocabulary. [overall reading comprehension] READING CORRESPONDENCE B2 Can read correspondence relating to his/her field of interest and readily grasp the essential meaning. [reading correspondence] EOP READING FOR INFORMATION & ARGUMENT B2 Can understand articles and reports concerned with contemporary problems in which the writer adopts particular stances or viewpoints. [reading for information & argument] Interaction Spoken Speaking OVERALL SPOKEN INTERACTION B2 Can interact with a degree of fluency and spontaneity that makes regular interaction, and sustained relationships with native speakers quite possible without imposing strain on either party. [overall spoken interaction] 3 revised by KWONG B2 Can highlight the personal significance of events and experiences, account for and sustain views clearly by providing relevant explanations and arguments. [overall spoken interaction] CONVERSATION B2 Can engage in extended conversation on most general topics in a clearly participatory fashion, even in a noisy environment. [conversation] B2 Can convey degrees of emotion and highlight the personal significance of events and experiences. [conversation] INFORMAL DISCUSSION (WITH FRIENDS) B2 Can account for and sustain his/her opinions in discussion by providing relevant explanation, arguments and comments. [informal discussion (with friends)] EAP EOP Produc tion Spoken Speaking SUSTAINED MONOLOGUE: DESCRIBING EXPERIENCE B2 Can give clear, detailed description on a wide range of subjects to his/her field of interest. [sustained monologue: describing experience] Reception Communic ation Strategies IDENTIFYING CUES & INFERRING (SPOKEN & WRITTEN) B2 Can use a variety of strategies to achieve comprehension, including listening for main points, checking comprehension by using contextual clues. [identifying cues & inferring (spoken & written)] EAP Interactio n Communic ation Strategies ASKING FOR CLARIFICATION B2 Can ask follow-up questions to check that he/she has understood what a speaker intended to say, and get clarification of ambiguous points. [asking for clarification] Working with Text Communicative Language Competence NOTE-TAKING (LECTURES, SEMINARS, ETC.) B2 Can understand a clearly structured lecture on a familiar subject, and can take notes on points which strike him/her as important, even though he/she tends to concentrate on the words themselves and therefore to miss some information. The student never attends class nor submits assignments. 2. The student is absent or asks for leave with NO valid excuses for more than 4 classes. 3. The student never explains to or discusses with the teacher his/her difficulty in taking care of this subject. 4. The student neither offers valid excuses on his application for course withdrawal nor notifies the teacher beforehand. 學生如遇有以下情形，其停修申請將不予「同意」 1. 學生未曾到課或繳交任何作業。 2. 學生無故缺席或未有證明之請假超過四次 3. 學生從未向老師解釋、或與之討論，修讀本課程時的困難 4. 學生未在停修申請上敘明或以其他通訊方式告知老師停修本課程之原因 避免學生規避「低修」學分數而選課，或以其他理由選課但不上課等情事 提醒：請於選課前參考課程大綱，了解評分方式、各週進度。並於第一堂課進一步了 解作業、報告、考試的規劃與所需處理時間。評估自已的學習量能，避免修課失衡。 Instructor & Contact Information Name Email Office & Tel Office Hour 徐桂平 Vicky Hsu personal messaging on eeclass1 綜二館 B 側 209 ( 34417) Tuesday 10:00 A.M.-12:00 P.M. 綜二館 B 側 209 1 No email via eeclass will be replied to, for the sender’s email address does not belong to the student. Please leave messages on eeclass, using the “personal messages” function. eeclass eeclass 2 prepared by Vicky Hsu Course Aims / Description 1. Primary aim This one-year course is designed to enhance students’ overall English competence through listening, speaking, and reading activities plus grammar review and vocabulary development. A four-skill coursebook plus a self-access learning project will be integrated to design learning tasks and provide opportunities for students to practice language learning strategies, get exposed to English in any form, and develop their confidence and fluency in the classroom and outside the classroom. After having taken this course, students are expected to consolidate their knowledge of English language and engage themselves more confidently and fluently in authentic communication in everyday settings and even in school settings. 2. Subsidiary aim In this class, students will have the opportunity to 1. review and practice grammar points and sentence structures, especially concerning verb tenses, to describe and discuss a variety of topics and issues related to their life 2. build up theme-based vocabulary and also academic words for and through reading and listening to conversations, interviews, talks, and lectures 3. practice academic skills such as outlining, summarizing, paraphrasing, and critical thinking while listening, reading, speaking and writing 4. manage and present information, perspectives, or problem-solving/decision-making in speaking and writing tasks or activities 3. Corresponding CEFR Can-do statements (B2) Reception Listening LISTENING TO RADIO, AUDIO & RECORDINGS B2 Can understand most radio documentaries and most other recorded or broadcast audio material delivered in standard dialect and can identify the speaker’s mood, tone, etc. [listening to radio, audio & recordings] Reception Reading OVERALL READING COMPREHENSION B2 Can read with a large degree of independence, adapting style and speed of reading to different texts and purposes, and using appropriate reference sources selectively. Has a broad active reading vocabulary, but may experience some difficulty with low- frequency vocabulary. [overall reading comprehension] READING FOR INFORMATION & ARGUMENT B2 Can understand articles and reports concerned with contemporary problems in which the writer adopts particular stances or viewpoints. [reading for information & argument] 3 prepared by Vicky Hsu Interaction Spoken Speaking INFORMAL DISCUSSION (WITH FRIENDS) B2 Can account for and sustain his/her opinions in discussion by providing relevant explanation, arguments and comments. [informal discussion (with friends)] INFORMATION EXCHANGE B2 Can pass on detailed information reliably. [information exchange] Production Spoken Speaking OVERALL SPOKEN PRODUCTION B2 Can give clear, detailed description and presentations on a wide range of subjects related to his/her field of interest, expanding and supporting ideas with subsidiary points and relevant examples. [overall spoken production] ADDRESSING AUDIENCES B2 Can give a clear, prepared presentation, giving reasons in support of or against a particular point of view and giving the advantages and disadvantages of various options. [addressing audiences] Reception Communi cation Strategies IDENTIFYING CUES & INFERRING (SPOKEN & WRITTEN) B2 Can use a variety of strategies to achieve comprehension, including listening for main points, checking comprehension by using contextual clues. [identifying cues & inferring (spoken & written)] EAP Interaction Communi cation Strategies COOPERATING B2 Can give feedback on and follow up statements and inferences and so help the development of the discussion. [cooperating] EAP ASKING FOR CLARIFICATION B2 Can ask follow-up questions to check that he/she has understood what a speaker intended to say, and get clarification of ambiguous points. [asking for clarification] Working with Text NOTE-TAKING (LECTURES, SEMINARS, ETC.) B2 Can understand a clearly structured lecture on a familiar subject, and can take notes on points which strike him/her as important, even though he/she tends to concentrate on the words themselves and therefore to miss some information. [note-taking (lectures, seminars, etc.) EAP PROCESSING TEXT 4 prepared by Vicky Hsu B2 Can summarize a wide range of factual and imaginative texts, commenting on and discussing contrasting points of view and the main themes. [processing text] EAP Communicative Language Competence Range GENERAL LINGUISTIC RANGE B2+ Can express him/herself clearly and without much sign of having to restrict what he/she wants to say. [processing text] VOCABULARY RANGE B2 Has a good range of vocabulary for matters connected to his/her field and most general topics. [vocabulary range] Control GRAMMATICAL ACCURACY B2+ Good grammatical control. Occasional “slips” or non-systematic errors and minor flaws in sentence structure may still occur, but they are rare and can often be corrected in retrospect. [grammatical accuracy] VOCABULARY CONTROL B2 Lexical accuracy is generally high, though some confusion and incorrect word choice does occur without hindering communication. [vocabulary control] ORTHOGRAPHIC CONTROL B2 Can produce clearly intelligible continuous writing, which follows standard layout and paragraphing conventions. [orthographic control] EAP B2 Spelling, punctuation and layout are accurate but may show signs of mother tongue influence. [orthographic control] Sociolinguistic SOCIOLINGUISTIC APPROPRIATENESS B2 Can with some effort keep up with and contribute to group discussions even when speech is fast and colloquial. [sociolinguistic appropriateness] Pragmatic FLEXIBILITY B2 Can adjust to the changes of direction, style and emphasis normally found in conversation. [flexibility] COHERENCE B2 Can use a limited number of cohesive devices to link his/her utterance into clear, coherent discourse, though there may be some “jumpiness” in a long contribution. [coherence] EAP 5 prepared by Vicky Hsu 英文核心能力指標 University Student Core Competency Indicators 1. 英語溝通與表達能力 (ability to communicate and express oneself in English) 30% 2. 深度分析與組織思考的能力 (ability to think critically and organize ideas logically in English) 10% 3. 英語學習策略與技巧 (knowledge of English learning strategies and techniques) 30% 4. 對英語與多元文化的國際視野 (global views of English and multicultural diversity) 15% 5. 善用英語學習資源，培養獨立學習英語的習慣與能力 (ability to use existing English learning resources and development of independent self-learning habit) 15% Teaching Materials and References Uniform textbook Christina Latham-Koenig, Clive Oxenden, and Kate Chomacki. MS Forms (for assignments & quizzes) Grading Scheme 1. Attendance and participation (cf. Requirements and rules 1, 2, 6, and 7) 15% 2. Assignments (& quizzes) (cf. Requirements and rules 3-5) 25% 3. Final exam (File 2A, File 3A & File 4A) (cf. Requirements and rules 4) 30% 4. Presentatin (an individual podcast on SDGs) 10% 5. Academic English Skills practices (AI-assisted or TEEMI platform) 10% 6. Self-access learning project (6-8 tasks related to grammar, public speaking, & topics in AEF 4) 10% Note: The percentage of this grading scheme is subject to possible adjustments. To be announced. Requirements & Rules 1. Class attendance, lesson preparation and active class participation are required.  As you are all present whenever the instructor takes the roll, you will get 60% in this category Attendance and Participation. 經常性點名，全勤者可得「出席與參與」項目中的 60%成績。  Each skip will cost 2 points from the category Attendance and Participation (up to 15 points in the final grade). 未假不到課（翹課），每 次從「出席與參與」成績（占學期成績 15 分）扣 2 分。  If you are absent in case of UNCONTROLLABLE situations (e.g. illness, NTHU Q&A 6 prepared by Vicky Hsu emergency, important occasions, etc.), please apply for a leave on the Student Leave System on Academic Information System of National Tsing Hua University or on the iNTHU app (from the Office of Student Affair website), with clear leave information, including leave type, leave period, and reasons (must be clear and valid enough for the teacher’s approval). As the reasons or the documents are not clear, valid or sufficient enough, the teacher may deny the application. 遇不可抗力情形需請假者，請於本校校務資訊系統上的學生請假系統或下載 iNTHU APP，填寫資料（請假類別、請假日期、請假事由）。請假事由須合理並敘述清楚，提供老 師是否准假之參考。請假單上的理由或所附證明文件不清楚或不充分時，該次請假申請得不予 核准。  Please observe the information you are expected to offer for each of the following leave types:  For sick leave, please describe severe symptoms and medical treatments you have been taking in the box “Reason.” 請病假時，請於理由欄位說明影響上課之顯著症狀，就醫或服 藥等處理。  For personal leave, please describe the uncontrollable event and how it makes you absent from the class. 請事假時，請於理由欄位敘明事件，並說明該事件如何致使你無法前來上 課。  No leave application will be approved on the dates of presentations, peer evaluations, and midterm/final exams. Please care for your health and reserve the time for these important class activities. 報告、同儕互評、期中／期末考當日不得請假。請注意身心健康 並為這些重要課程活動預留時間。  There will be NO make-up exams or presentations unless you apply for leave with valid and official reasons for your absence beforehand. 無合理且正式的缺課原因，將不予補考 或補行報告。  You are expected to apply for leave before the class you are absent from. Any overdue leave application must be made within 7 days from the last day of absence. 請假已事先申請為原 則。逾期請假申請必須於 7 日內補請。未能於規定期間申請者，均以曠課論。  Being late for more than 10 minutes (with no valid excuses) is treated as absence from that hour. Being late for more than 30 minutes is treated as absence from the whole class. 無故 遲到逾 10 分鐘，以該小時未到課紀錄。遲到逾 30 分鐘，視為該次上課未到課。  No points will be deducted for your ATTENDANCE as long as your approved leave is no more than 6 hours. However, you may lose points for your PARTICIPATION or in-class practices scheduled on the date of your absence. 核准的請假時數未逾 6 小時，不扣出席成績。惟當日 如有上課練習或小組活動，請假者無法參與或完成，將無法獲得該次練習或該項評量成績。換 言之，缺課仍可能影響「參與」與「作業」等成績。  If you skip class for more than 8 hours, your course withdrawal may NOT be approved, and you will get 0 credits for this course. 無故不到課逾 8 小時者，將不予同意其停修申請，亦無 法取得本課程學分。  A student will fail to get the 2 credits for missing 5 classes, including the ones due to any kinds of leaves. 缺課達五次（含各類請假缺課）者，將無法從本課程獲取任何學分。 7 prepared by Vicky Hsu 2. Absence from a class is no excuse for failing to complete in-class practices, to submit assignments in time, or to get informed of assignments or the class you have missed. It is your responsibility to hand in the assignments within 5 days (weekends & holidays included) and to reach your classmates or the instructor and refer to the course platform (eeclass) for the relevant information concerning what has been covered in the class. You may ask a classmate of yours to help with assignment submission and collection of assignment worksheets, if any. You may make an appointment with the instructor for assignment worksheets. 缺席與請假不得作為未 能完成當日上課練習、無法及時繳交作業或不知道該次課後作業之藉口。缺席與請假者負有及時 （五日內）繳交作業，並透過同學、課程平台，或親自聯繫老師了解該次上課內容與課後作業之 責。（可委託同學代為繳交作業或拿取作業單，或自行前來教師研究室繳交或領取。） 3.  Assignments are expected to be completed and submitted by the due date. No late submission will be accepted or graded unless the instructor approves or grants your application for extension of submission. 作業請按時繳交（或上傳）。未獲教師同意可延遲繳 交者或超過寬限期，其遲交作業不批改、不計分。  Your absence CANNOT be an assumption that you are entitled to hand in the late assignments far later (more than 5 days) or until your next presence. 請勿自以為逾期的作業可以自行延遲超過五 日，或下次出現時才繳交。  NO full credit for late submission/Penalty for late submission: 10% of the total mark awarded will be deducted for each working day after the submission date. 每遲交一日。扣 10%成績。 Late Submission Mark Awarded After Penalty Number of days late Penalty Original grade 90 Original grade 60 1 10% 81 54 2 20% 72 48 3 30% 63 42 4 40% 54 36 5 50% 45 30 More than 5 days Grade of zero awarded 遲交逾 5 日，不計分  Frequent late submissions with no valid excuses or under controllable circumstances will NOT be accepted or graded since the third late assignment. 無合理原因或非為不可抗力情形 的慣性遲交作業，第三份起將不予批改與計分。 4. Plagiarism on assignments and cheating on the exam is absolutely unacceptable. If someone is found plagiarizing or cheating, it means he/she will get a zero point for that assignment or exam. 嚴禁抄襲與作弊。抄襲與作弊者，學期成績以不及格處理。情節重大時，將提報至相關單 位依校規處理。 5. AI-assisted reports and assignments are allowed in limited instances: AI can be used to prepare for reports and assignments by brainstorming and tentative revision, but students must show how AI helps them reach the result. 僅限使用生成式 AI 於作業或報告之準備（如腦力激盪與初步 8 prepared by Vicky Hsu 修訂等），學生須註明 AI 如何用於協作其作業或報告。 6. Penalty for no or poor participation in pair or group work Students are expected to take part in pair or group activities. Failure to engage in these activities (due to you absence or lateness) will lead to reductions in grades awarded. Sometimes the reduction may be suggested by other group members; in other circumstances, the instructor may reduce the grade awarded without reference to other group members. 學生負有參與雙人 或小組活動之義務。如因個人遲到或缺席導致小組活動無法順利進行，請假或缺席者該次活動成 績將以扣分或甚至 0 分計算。 7.  Mobile devices are only used for educational purposes relevant to the subject or tasks in the classroom setting with the permission of or at the request of the instructor. Using mobile devices for studying other subjects or entertaining purposes is absolutely prohibited. Students who violate the regulation will be considered absent from the class or asked to leave the classroom. 行動裝置僅限於學習活動，使用須獲得老師同意或遵照老師指示。嚴禁 使用行動裝置研習其他課程或娛樂使用。違反規定者，以「未到課」處置，亦得請違規者離開 教室。  During class students are not to be seen with a cell phone in hand or on the desk. Mobile phones are expected to be turned off or switched to a silent mode. 課程進行時，請關閉行動 電話或轉為靜音模式。未獲教師指示或許可，不得於上課時間使用或放置於桌上。 8. The syllabus, handouts, and returned assignments should be kept at least until the end of this semester for later reference or the final exam. 課程相關各項文件請妥為保存至學期結束。 Teaching Activities  Lectures 口頭講授  Pair/Group discussion 配對／分組討論  Assignments 作業  Student presentations 學生報告  Quizzes 小考  online practice 線上練習 Classroom Languages English 80 % Mandarin 20 % Tentative Weekly Schedule WEEK DATE Coursebook Units/Topics Tentative Learning Tasks Academic Language Skills 1 9/1 Course orientation Diagnostic assessment Pre-course questionnaire Using and learning English in college 2 9/8 File 2A Doctor, doctor! and Presentation Guide 1. Purpose The podcasting practice aims to present your understanding of Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and to express your concerns and inspiration about making your city (your home city or the city you are living in) or your community (the area around your campus or your dormitory) a better place to live in the future 2. In your podcast, you are expected to a. identify a problem you are concerned about in your city or community b. define/explain what SDGs are and which SDG you are going to focus on c. share SDG cases or examples related to a similar problem as an inspiration d. propose practical solutions to the problem 3. Presentation a. Mode of presentation a pre-recorded PODCAST by each individual student  Your podcast can be a solo storytelling, an interview, or a repurposed content show.  You must host the show, and your voice is identifiable in the podcast.  You and your guest(s) MUST speak English in the podcast.  You may ask your classmates, friends, or family members to be your guest(s) if your podcast is designed as an interview. b. Suggested Length of presentation 3-4 minutes for a solo storytelling/talk 4-5 minutes for an interview or for a repurposed content show c. Deadline for uploading the podcast (audio file) and the script (PDF file) to eeclass LANG1020 01 (M1M2) LANG1020 08 (M3M4) LANG1020 20 (R1R2) Podcast upload October 31 October 31 November 3 Peer Review (8-10 podcasts) November 1-3 November 1-3 November 4-6  Peer and self evaluation will be conducted in Week 10. Each student will be assigned 8-10 podcasts for evaluation right after the deadline. You will have 2-3 days to complete the peer evaluation by grading on eeclass and commenting under each podcast. 14 prepared by Vicky Hsu  Each podcast will be evaluated with a rubric in terms of the five categories: Content – the speaker’s knowledge and insight, relevant information and quality details (beyond the obvious), in-depth research, catchy and clever opening (topic, purpose, & sequence of events for the podcast), engaging and informative discussion/narration, and effective and impressive ending Language Use – good use of storytelling or narrative structure, effective use of open-ended and follow-up questions for interview, and good choice of words and phrases for spoken communication Delivery – well-rehearsed for grammar, vocabulary, cadence, and rhythm to keep the audience engaged; intelligible & in a conversational style Audio/Sound Design – clear recording of narration or interview, free of extraneous noise, proper use of ambient sound and sound effects Technical Production/Teamwork – adequate podcast length, smooth transition, equal contribution of teammates, accurate and well-written script 5. Preparation  Work as an individual or a team (recruiting and managing team members)  Choose an SDG as a topic  Develop and maintain the research (extracting relevant and interesting information) and podcast schedule (discussions and meetings)  Organize and schedule rehearsing and recording sessions  Manage sound quality and edit the podcast episode  keep track of the deadline and ensure that your podcast and script are uploaded on time Reminder: This podcasting practice is NOT aimed at demonstrating your talents for collecting and presenting information or expressing your opinions about SDGs. You are expected to extract practicable and feasible actions for your audience. As a general rule, podcasts are a form of entertainment. People tend to listen to podcasts to learn more about a topic or keep up with current events in a relaxing or entertaining way. 6. Points to ponder  Who are you speaking to? It integrates a four-skill coursebook and related extensive learning materials to engage students in rigorous practice sessions focused on listening, reading, speaking, vocabulary, and grammar. Provided with intensive learning tasks on various topics, students should have been able to effectively apply the language strategies and knowledge acquired during the course to their daily English comprehension and communication in authentic settings. Subsidiary aim In this course students will have opportunities to 1. expand both general and academic words and expressions relevant to various topics through targeted exercises and activities. 2. review grammar structures and apply grammatical concepts in context to refine accuracy. 3. improve their listening skills such as anticipating, listening for opinions, and note- taking to extract essential information and connect main ideas with the use of a variety of audio/video materials including conversations, announcements, interviews, lectures, and etc. 2 4. learn to read a wide range of texts with comprehension skills such as scanning for specific information, comparing and contrasting ideas, skimming for main ideas and summarizing. 5. engage in interactive discussions through which they practice precise and fluent expression of their observations, experiences, opinions, and feedbacks on different general or academic topics. CEFR Can-do Statements (B2) Reception Listening OVERALL LISTENING COMPREHENSION B2 Can follow extended speech and complex lines of argument provided the topic is reasonably familiar, and the direction of the talk is sign-posted by explicit markers. [overall listening comprehension] B2+ Can understand standard spoken language, live or broadcast, on both familiar and unfamiliar topics normally encountered in personal, social, academic or vocational life. Only extreme background noise, inadequate discourse structure and/or idiomatic usage influence the ability to understand. [overall listening comprehension] EAP EOP UNDERSTANDING INTERACTION BETWEEN NATIVE SPEAKERS B2 Can with some effort catch much of what is said around him/her, but may find it difficult to participate effectively in discussion with several native speakers who do not modify their language in any way. [understanding interaction between native speakers] LISTENING TO ANNOUNCEMENTS & INSTRUCTIONS B2 Can understand announcements and messages on concrete and abstract topics spoken in standard dialect at normal speed. [listening to announcements & instructions] LISTENING TO RADIO, AUDIO & RECORDINGS B2+ Can understand recordings in standard dialect likely to be encountered in social, professional or academic life and identify speaker viewpoints and attitudes as well as the information content. [listening to radio, audio & recordings] EAP EOP Reception Reading OVERALL READING COMPREHENSION B2 Can read with a large degree of independence, adapting style and speed of reading to different texts and purposes, and using appropriate reference sources selectively. Has a broad active reading vocabulary, but may experience some difficulty with low- frequency vocabulary. [overall reading comprehension] READING FOR ORIENTATION B2 Can scan quickly through long and complex texts, locating relevant details. [reading for orientation] EAP Intera ction Spoke n Speaking OVERALL SPOKEN INTERACTION B2 Can interact with a degree of fluency and spontaneity that makes regular interaction, and sustained relationships with native speakers 3 quite possible without imposing strain on either party. [overall spoken interaction] CONVERSATION B2 Can engage in extended conversation on most general topics in a clearly participatory fashion, even in a noisy environment. [conversation] INFORMAL DISCUSSION (WITH FRIENDS) B2 Can take an active part in informal discussion in familiar contexts, commenting, putting point of view clearly, evaluating alternative proposals and making and responding to hypotheses. [informal discussion (with friends)] B2 Can with some effort catch much of what is said around him/her in discussion, but may find it difficult to participate effectively in discussion with several native speakers who do not modify their language in any way. [informal discussion (with friends)] B2 Can account for and sustain his/her opinions in discussion by providing relevant explanation, arguments and comments. [informal discussion (with friends)] EAP EOP Production SpokenSpeaking OVERALL SPOKEN PRODUCTION B2 Can give clear, detailed description and presentations on a wide range of subjects related to his/her field of interest, expanding and supporting ideas with subsidiary points and relevant examples. [overall spoken production] EAP EOP Receptio n Communi cation Strategies IDENTIFYING CUES & INFERRING (SPOKEN & WRITTEN) B2 Can use a variety of strategies to achieve comprehension, including listening for main points, checking comprehension by using contextual clues. [identifying cues & inferring (spoken & written)] EAP Working with Text Communicative Language Competence NOTE-TAKING (LECTURES, SEMINARS, ETC.) B2 Can understand a clearly structured lecture on a familiar subject, and can take notes on points which strike him/her as important, even though he/she tends to concentrate on the words themselves and therefore to miss some information. [note-taking (lectures, seminars, etc.) EAP PROCESSING TEXT B2 Can summarize a wide range of factual and imaginative texts, commenting on and discussing contrasting points of view and the main themes. [processing text] EAP B2 Can summarize extracts from news items, interviews or documentaries containing opinions, argument and discussion. [processing text] EAP VOCABULARY RANGE B2 Has a good range of vocabulary for matters connected to his/her field and most general topics. [vocabulary range] Control GRAMMATICAL ACCURACY 4 B2 Shows a relatively high degree of grammatical control. Does not make mistakes which lead to misunderstanding. [grammatical accuracy] VOCABULARY CONTROL B2 Lexical accuracy is generally high, though some confusion and incorrect word choice does occur without hindering communication. Your personal scheduling or preference of taking courses during your college stay will NOT be a valid excuse for the teacher to take your request for extra course registration into account. 停修條件 The student’s application for course withdrawal will NOT be approved if 1. The student never attends class nor submits assignments. 2. The student is absent or asks for leave with NO valid excuses for more than 6 classes. 3. The student never explains to or discusses with the teacher his/her difficulty in taking care of this subject. 4. The student neither offers valid excuses on his application for course withdrawal nor notifies the teacher beforehand. 學生如遇有以下情形，其停修申請將不予「同意」 1. 學生未曾到課或繳交任何作業。 2. 學生無故缺席或未有證明之請假超過六次 3. 學生從未向老師解釋、或與之討論，修讀本課程時的困難 4. 學生未在停修申請上敘明或以其他通訊方式告知老師停修本課程之原 因 Instructor & Contact Information: Name Email Office & Tel Office Hour 吳聖鵬 hank.spwu@gmail.com N/A N/A Course Aims / Description Primary aim This one-year course is designed to enhance students’ overall English competence through listening, speaking, and reading activities plus grammar review and vocabulary development. A four-skill coursebook plus a self-access learning project will be integrated to design learning tasks and provide opportunities for students to practice language learning strategies, compare and synthesize ideas and arguments, and develop their confidence and fluency in and outside the classroom. After having taken this course, students are expected to consolidate their knowledge of English language and engage themselves more confidently and fluently in authentic communication in everyday settings and expand academic vocabulary and 3 knowledge of definitions and parts of words, such as prefixes, suffixes and roots. Subsidiary aim In this course students will have opportunities to 1. review and practice grammar points and sentence structures to describe and discuss a variety of topics and issues related to their life 2. build up theme-based vocabulary and even academic words for and through reading and listening to conversations, interviews, talks, and lectures 3. practice academic skills such as outlining, summarizing, critical thinking while listening, reading, speaking and writing 4. manage and present information, perspectives, or problem-solving in speaking and writing tasks or activities Corresponding CEFR Can-do statements 1. Can understand the main ideas of propositionally and linguistically complex speech of both concrete and abstract topics in a standard dialect, including technical discussions in his/her field of specialization. [overall listening comprehension] 2. Can follow the essentials of lectures, talks and reports and other forms of academic/professional presentations which are propositionally and linguistically complex. [listening as a member of a live audience] 3. Can read with a large degree of independence, adapting style and speed of reading to different texts and purposes, and using appropriate reference sources selectively. Has a broad active reading vocabulary, but may experience some difficulty with low-frequency vocabulary. [overall reading comprehension] 4. Can interact with a degree of fluency and spontaneity that makes regular interaction, and sustained relationships with native speakers quite possible without imposing strain on either party. [overall spoken interaction] 5. Can give clear, detailed description and presentations on a wide range of subjects related to his/her field of interest, expanding and supporting ideas with subsidiary points and relevant examples. [overall spoken production] 6. Can write clear, detailed texts on a variety of subjects related to his/her field of interest, synthesizing and evaluating information and arguments from a number of sources. [overall written production] 7. Can pass on detailed information reliably. [propositional precision] 4 英文核心能力指標 University Student Core Competency Indicators 1. 英語溝通與表達能力 (ability to communicate and express oneself in English) [30%] 2. 深度分析與組織思考的能力 (ability to think critically and organize ideas logically in English) [10%] 3. 英語學習策略與技巧 (knowledge of English learning strategies and techniques) [30%] 4. 對英語與多元文化的國際視野 (global views of English and multicultural diversity) [15%] 5. 善用英語學習資源，培養獨立學習英語的習慣與能力 (ability to use existing English learning resources and development of independent self-learning habit) [15%] Teaching Materials and References Textbook(s) Christina Latham-Koenig, Clive Oxenden, and Kate Chomacki.
