All students must enroll through the course selection system by random assignment. 停修條件 Withdrawal Conditions The student’s application for course withdrawal will NOT be approved if 1. The student is absent for more than 5 classes: The student never explains to or discusses with the teacher his/her difficulty in taking care of this subject. 2. The student did not inform the teacher in advance of the reason for withdrawing from the course through any means of communication (Line, email). 學生如遇有以下情形，其停修申請將[不予同意] 1. 學生缺席超過五次，期間從未想老師解釋，或與之老論，修讀本課 程的困難。 2. 學生未事先以任何通訊方式(line, e-mail)告知老師停修本課程之 原因。 Instructor & Contact Information: Name Email Office & Tel Office Hour 劉美慈 M.T. Liu liumeitzu@gapp.nthu.edu.tw N/A N/A 2 Course Aims / Description Primary aim This one-year course aims to enhance students’ overall English competence by developing their listening, speaking, reading, and writing skills. Through interactive activities, grammar review, and vocabulary expansion, students will strengthen their ability to communicate effectively in both everyday and academic contexts. The course incorporates a four-skill coursebook and a self-access learning project to provide structured learning tasks and opportunities for independent practice. Students will also be introduced to essential academic English skills, such as summarizing texts and writing structured essays, as well as practicing note-taking and understanding lectures to improve their ability to engage with academic materials. By the end of the course, students are expected to demonstrate greater confidence and fluency in authentic communication, whether in daily interactions or academic discussions. Subsidiary aim In this class, students will have opportunities to 1. review and practice grammar points and sentence structures to describe and discuss a variety of topics and issues related to their life 2. build up theme-based vocabulary and even academic words for and through reading and listening to conversations, interviews, talks, and lectures 3. practice academic skills such as outlining, summarizing, and critical thinking while listening, reading, speaking, and writing 4. present information, perspectives, or problem-solving in speaking and writing tasks or activities Corresponding CEFR Can-do statements 1. [LISTENING]: Can understand the main ideas of propositionally and linguistically complex speech of both concrete and abstract topics in a standard dialect, including technical discussions in his/her field of specialization. 2. [READING]: Can quickly identify the content and relevance off news items, articles and reports on a wide range of professional topics, deciding whether closer study is worthwhile. 3. [SPOKEN INTERACTION]: Can use the language fluently, accurately and effectively on a wide range of general, academic, vocational or leisure topics, marking clearly the relationships between ideas. 4. [WRITTEN PRODUCTION]: Can write letters conveying degrees of emotion and highlighting the personal significance of events and experiences and commenting on the correspondent’s news and views. 5. [SOCIOLINGUISTIC APPROPRIATENESS]: Can express him/herself confidently, clearly and politely in a formal or informal register, appropriate to the situation and the person(s) concerned. 3 英文核心能力指標 University Student Core Competency Indicators 1. 英語溝通與表達能力 (ability to communicate and express oneself in English) 30% 2. 深度分析與組織思考的能力 (ability to think critically and organize ideas logically in English) 20% 3. 英語學習策略與技巧 (knowledge of English learning strategies and techniques) 20% 4. 對英語與多元文化的國際視野 (global views of English and multicultural diversity) 20% 5. 善用英語學習資源，培養獨立學習英語的習慣與能力 (ability to use existing English learning resources and development of independent self-learning habit) 10% Teaching Materials and References Textbook(s) Christina Latham-koenig, Clive Oxenden, and Kate Chomachi.(2021) American English File 4, 3rd Edition. New York: Oxford University Press. VoiceTube / YouTube / Podcast 4. Online news stories Requirements & Rules: 1.Class attendance and class participation:  Attendance is taken every session throughout the semester. You have a total of four opportunities for leave without penalty. Sick leave, official leave, personal leave, mental health leave (activated on the third time with school-parent concern), and menstrual leave no proof is required. All leave requests should be submitted through the school’s online System。 Starting from the fifth time(inclusive), points will be deducted. This applies to all types of leave.  Five absences (with approved requests) or three absences (without requests) will result 4 in a failing grade.  Lateness: Unless an unavoidable reason is provided, a 20% deduction will be applied.  Class Participation: In-class assignments (pair work) and answering questions. 請特別留意，這門課很注重出席率，因此如果經批准的請假累計達到五次以上 (包含五次)， 或是有三次沒有來也沒有請假（包含三次），這門課程就會不及格。 2. Assignment: No make-up submissions.  In the first week, I’ll open the assignment submission period, which will last until the deadline. You’ll have plenty of time to submit. Therefore, no excuses for absence will be accepted for late submissions.  Absence from a class is no excuse for submitting assignments in time or ignoring assignments or the class you have missed. It is your responsibility to ask your classmates what has been covered in the class. 3. No make-up exams or presentation: If a group presentation is “crippled” due to your lateness or absence, you will receive no grade on the presentation. 4. Mobile phone/ tablets: make sure to mute or turn off your mobile phone before class begins. During the class, no access to mobile devices is allowed unless permission is given for a specific learning task or activity. 5. Plagiarism / Cheating :  plagiarism on assignments and cheating on the exam is absolutely unacceptable. 6. The student neither offers valid excuses on his application for course withdrawal nor notifies the teacher beforehand. 學生如遇有以下情形，其停修申請將不予「同意」 1. 學生未曾到課或繳交任何作業。 2. 學生無故缺席或未有證明之請假超過四次 3. 學生從未向老師解釋、或與之討論，修讀本課程時的困難 4. 學生未在停修申請上敘明或以其他通訊方式告知老師停修本課程之原因 避免學生規避「低修」學分數而選課，或以其他理由選課但不上課等情事 提醒：請於選課前參考課程大綱，了解評分方式、各週進度。並於第一堂課進一步了 解作業、報告、考試的規劃與所需處理時間。評估自已的學習量能，避免修課失衡。 Instructor & Contact Information Name Email Office & Tel Office Hour 徐桂平 Vicky Hsu personal messaging on eeclass1 綜二館 B 側 209 ( 34417) Tuesday 10:00 A.M.-12:00 P.M. 綜二館 B 側 209 1 No email via eeclass will be replied to, for the sender’s email address does not belong to the student. Please leave messages on eeclass, using the “personal messages” function. eeclass eeclass 2 prepared by Vicky Hsu Course Aims / Description 1. Primary aim This one-year course is designed to enhance students’ overall English competence through listening, speaking, and reading activities plus grammar review and vocabulary development. A four-skill coursebook plus a self-access learning project will be integrated to design learning tasks and provide opportunities for students to practice language learning strategies, get exposed to English in any form, and develop their confidence and fluency in the classroom and outside the classroom. After having taken this course, students are expected to consolidate their knowledge of English language and engage themselves more confidently and fluently in authentic communication in everyday settings and even in school settings. 2. Subsidiary aim In this class, students will have opportunities to 1. review and practice grammar points and sentence structures to describe and discuss a variety of topics and issues related to their life, 2. build up theme-based vocabulary and even academic words for and through reading and listening to conversations, interviews, talks, and lectures, 3. practice academic skills such as outlining, summarizing, and critical thinking while listening, reading, speaking, and writing, 4. present and explain information, perspectives, or problem-solving in speaking and writing tasks or activities. 3. Corresponding CEFR Can-do statements (B2) Reception Listening LISTENING TO RADIO, AUDIO & RECORDINGS B2 Can understand most radio documentaries and most other recorded or broadcast audio material delivered in standard dialect and can identify the speaker’s mood, tone, etc. [listening to radio, audio & recordings] Reception Reading OVERALL READING COMPREHENSION B2 Can read with a large degree of independence, adapting style and speed of reading to different texts and purposes, and using appropriate reference sources selectively. Has a broad active reading vocabulary, but may experience some difficulty with low- frequency vocabulary. [overall reading comprehension] READING FOR INFORMATION & ARGUMENT B2 Can understand articles and reports concerned with contemporary problems in which the writer adopts particular stances or viewpoints. [reading for information & argument] 3 prepared by Vicky Hsu Interaction Spoken Speaking INFORMAL DISCUSSION (WITH FRIENDS) B2 Can account for and sustain his/her opinions in discussion by providing relevant explanation, arguments and comments. [informal discussion (with friends)] INFORMATION EXCHANGE B2 Can pass on detailed information reliably. [information exchange] Production Spoken Speaking OVERALL SPOKEN PRODUCTION B2 Can give clear, detailed description and presentations on a wide range of subjects related to his/her field of interest, expanding and supporting ideas with subsidiary points and relevant examples. [overall spoken production] ADDRESSING AUDIENCES B2 Can give a clear, prepared presentation, giving reasons in support of or against a particular point of view and giving the advantages and disadvantages of various options. [addressing audiences] Reception Communi cation Strategies IDENTIFYING CUES & INFERRING (SPOKEN & WRITTEN) B2 Can use a variety of strategies to achieve comprehension, including listening for main points, checking comprehension by using contextual clues. [identifying cues & inferring (spoken & written)] EAP Interaction Communi cation Strategies COOPERATING B2 Can give feedback on and follow up statements and inferences and so help the development of the discussion. [cooperating] EAP ASKING FOR CLARIFICATION B2 Can ask follow-up questions to check that he/she has understood what a speaker intended to say, and get clarification of ambiguous points. [asking for clarification] Working with Text NOTE-TAKING (LECTURES, SEMINARS, ETC.) B2 Can understand a clearly structured lecture on a familiar subject, and can take notes on points which strike him/her as important, even though he/she tends to concentrate on the words themselves and therefore to miss some information. [note-taking (lectures, seminars, etc.) EAP PROCESSING TEXT 4 prepared by Vicky Hsu B2 Can summarize a wide range of factual and imaginative texts, commenting on and discussing contrasting points of view and the main themes. [processing text] EAP Communicative Language Competence Range GENERAL LINGUISTIC RANGE B2+ Can express him/herself clearly and without much sign of having to restrict what he/she wants to say. [processing text] VOCABULARY RANGE B2 Has a good range of vocabulary for matters connected to his/her field and most general topics. [vocabulary range] Control GRAMMATICAL ACCURACY B2+ Good grammatical control. Occasional “slips” or non-systematic errors and minor flaws in sentence structure may still occur, but they are rare and can often be corrected in retrospect. [grammatical accuracy] VOCABULARY CONTROL B2 Lexical accuracy is generally high, though some confusion and incorrect word choice does occur without hindering communication. [vocabulary control] ORTHOGRAPHIC CONTROL B2 Can produce clearly intelligible continuous writing, which follows standard layout and paragraphing conventions. [orthographic control] EAP B2 Spelling, punctuation and layout are accurate but may show signs of mother tongue influence. [orthographic control] Sociolinguistic SOCIOLINGUISTIC APPROPRIATENESS B2 Can with some effort keep up with and contribute to group discussions even when speech is fast and colloquial. [sociolinguistic appropriateness] Pragmatic FLEXIBILITY B2 Can adjust to the changes of direction, style and emphasis normally found in conversation. [flexibility] COHERENCE B2 Can use a limited number of cohesive devices to link his/her utterance into clear, coherent discourse, though there may be some “jumpiness” in a long contribution. [coherence] EAP 5 prepared by Vicky Hsu 英文核心能力指標 University Student Core Competency Indicators 1. 英語溝通與表達能力 (ability to communicate and express oneself in English) 30% 2. 深度分析與組織思考的能力 (ability to think critically and organize ideas logically in English) 10% 3. 英語學習策略與技巧 (knowledge of English learning strategies and techniques) 30% 4. 對英語與多元文化的國際視野 (global views of English and multicultural diversity) 15% 5. 善用英語學習資源，培養獨立學習英語的習慣與能力 (ability to use existing English learning resources and development of independent self-learning habit) 15% Teaching Materials and References Uniform textbook Christina Latham-Koenig, Clive Oxenden, and Kate Chomacki. Requirements & Rules 1. Class attendance, lesson preparation and active class participation are required.  As you are all present whenever the instructor takes the roll, you will get 60% in this category Attendance and Participation. 經常性點名，全勤者可得「出席與參與」項目中的 60%成績。  Each skip will cost 2 points from the category Attendance and Participation (up to 15 points in the final grade). 未假不到課（翹課），每 次從「出席與參與」成績（占學期成績 15 分）扣 2 分。  If you are absent in case of UNCONTROLLABLE situations (e.g. illness, NTHU Q&A 6 prepared by Vicky Hsu emergency, important occasions, etc.), please apply for a leave on the Student Leave System on Academic Information System of National Tsing Hua University or on the iNTHU app (from the Office of Student Affair website), with clear leave information, including leave type, leave period, and reasons (must be clear and valid enough for the teacher’s approval). As the reasons or the documents are not clear, valid or sufficient enough, the teacher may deny the application. 遇不可抗力情形需請假者，請於本校校務資訊系統上的學生請假系統或下載 iNTHU APP，填寫資料（請假類別、請假日期、請假事由）。請假事由須合理並敘述清楚，提供老 師是否准假之參考。請假單上的理由或所附證明文件不清楚或不充分時，該次請假申請得不予 核准。  Please observe the information you are expected to offer for each of the following leave types:  For sick leave, please describe severe symptoms and medical treatments you have been taking in the box “Reason.” 請病假時，請於理由欄位說明影響上課之顯著症狀，就醫或服 藥等處理。  For personal leave, please describe the uncontrollable event and how it makes you absent from the class. 請事假時，請於理由欄位敘明事件，並說明該事件如何致使你無法前來上 課。  No leave application will be approved on the dates of presentations, peer evaluations, and midterm/final exams. Please care for your health and reserve the time for these important class activities. 報告、同儕互評、期中／期末考當日不得請假。請注意身心健康 並為這些重要課程活動預留時間。  There will be NO make-up exams or presentations unless you apply for leave with valid and official reasons for your absence beforehand. 無合理且正式的缺課原因，將不予補考 或補行報告。  You are expected to apply for leave before the class you are absent from. Any overdue leave application must be made within 7 days from the last day of absence. 請假已事先申請為原 則。逾期請假申請必須於 7 日內補請。未能於規定期間申請者，均以曠課論。  Being late for more than 10 minutes (with no valid excuses) is treated as absence from that hour. Being late for more than 30 minutes is treated as absence from the whole class. 無故 遲到逾 10 分鐘，以該小時未到課紀錄。遲到逾 30 分鐘，視為該次上課未到課。  No points will be deducted for your ATTENDANCE as long as your approved leave is no more than 6 hours. However, you may lose points for your PARTICIPATION or in-class practices scheduled on the date of your absence. 核准的請假時數未逾 6 小時，不扣出席成績。惟當日 如有上課練習或小組活動，請假者無法參與或完成，將無法獲得該次練習或該項評量成績。換 言之，缺課仍可能影響「參與」與「作業」等成績。  If you skip class for more than 8 hours, your course withdrawal may NOT be approved, and you will get 0 credits for this course. 無故不到課逾 8 小時者，將不予同意其停修申請，亦無 法取得本課程學分。  A student will fail to get the 2 credits for missing 5 classes, including the ones due to any kinds of leaves. 缺課達五次（含各類請假缺課）者，將無法從本課程獲取任何學分。 7 prepared by Vicky Hsu 2. Absence from a class is no excuse for failing to complete in-class practices, to submit assignments in time, or to get informed of assignments or the class you have missed. It is your responsibility to hand in the assignments within 5 days (weekends & holidays included) and to reach your classmates or the instructor and refer to the course platform (eeclass) for the relevant information concerning what has been covered in the class. You may ask a classmate of yours to help with assignment submission and collection of assignment worksheets, if any. You may make an appointment with the instructor for assignment worksheets. 缺席與請假不得作為未 能完成當日上課練習、無法及時繳交作業或不知道該次課後作業之藉口。缺席與請假者負有及時 （五日內）繳交作業，並透過同學、課程平台，或親自聯繫老師了解該次上課內容與課後作業之 責。（可委託同學代為繳交作業或拿取作業單，或自行前來教師研究室繳交或領取。） 3.  Assignments are expected to be completed and submitted by the due date. No late submission will be accepted or graded unless the instructor approves or grants your application for extension of submission. 作業請按時繳交（或上傳）。未獲教師同意可延遲繳 交者或超過寬限期，其遲交作業不批改、不計分。  Your absence CANNOT be an assumption that you are entitled to hand in the late assignments far later (more than 5 days) or until your next presence. 請勿自以為逾期的作業可以自行延遲超過五 日，或下次出現時才繳交。  NO full credit for late submission/Penalty for late submission: 10% of the total mark awarded will be deducted for each working day after the submission date. 每遲交一日。扣 10%成績。 Late Submission Mark Awarded After Penalty Number of days late Penalty Original grade 90 Original grade 60 1 10% 81 54 2 20% 72 48 3 30% 63 42 4 40% 54 36 5 50% 45 30 More than 5 days Grade of zero awarded 遲交逾 5 日，不計分  Frequent late submissions with no valid excuses or under controllable circumstances will NOT be accepted or graded since the third late assignment. 無合理原因或非為不可抗力情形 的慣性遲交作業，第三份起將不予批改與計分。 4. Plagiarism on assignments and cheating on the exam is absolutely unacceptable. If someone is found plagiarizing or cheating, it means he/she will get a zero point for that assignment or exam. 嚴禁抄襲與作弊。抄襲與作弊者，學期成績以不及格處理。情節重大時，將提報至相關單 位依校規處理。 5. AI-assisted reports and assignments are allowed in limited instances: AI can be used to prepare for reports and assignments by brainstorming and tentative revision, but students must show how AI helps them reach the result. 僅限使用生成式 AI 於作業或報告之準備（如腦力激盪與初步 8 prepared by Vicky Hsu 修訂等），學生須註明 AI 如何用於協作其作業或報告。 6. Penalty for no or poor participation in pair or group work Students are expected to take part in pair or group activities. Failure to engage in these activities (due to you absence or lateness) will lead to reductions in grades awarded. Sometimes the reduction may be suggested by other group members; in other circumstances, the instructor may reduce the grade awarded without reference to other group members. 學生負有參與雙人 或小組活動之義務。如因個人遲到或缺席導致小組活動無法順利進行，請假或缺席者該次活動成 績將以扣分或甚至 0 分計算。 7.  Mobile devices are only used for educational purposes relevant to the subject or tasks in the classroom setting with the permission of or at the request of the instructor. Using mobile devices for studying other subjects or entertaining purposes is absolutely prohibited. Students who violate the regulation will be considered absent from the class or asked to leave the classroom. 行動裝置僅限於學習活動，使用須獲得老師同意或遵照老師指示。嚴禁 使用行動裝置研習其他課程或娛樂使用。違反規定者，以「未到課」處置，亦得請違規者離開 教室。  During class students are not to be seen with a cell phone in hand or on the desk. Mobile phones are expected to be turned off or switched to a silent mode. 課程進行時，請關閉行動 電話或轉為靜音模式。未獲教師指示或許可，不得於上課時間使用或放置於桌上。 8. ____ Podcasting on SDGs—Task prompts and Presentation Guide 1. Purpose The podcasting practice aims to present your understanding of Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and to express your concerns and inspiration about making your city (your home city or the city you are living in) or your community (the area around your campus or your dormitory) a better place to live in the future 2. In your podcast, you are expected to a. identify a problem you are concerned about in your city or community b. define/explain what SDGs are and which SDG you are going to focus on c. share SDG cases or examples related to a similar problem as an inspiration d. propose practical solutions to the problem 3. References: https://www.un.org/sustainabledevelopment/ https://www.parenting.com.tw/article/5091099 永續發展目標 17 項目標及台灣實例 https://futurecity.cw.com.tw/article/1867 SDGs 懶人包》什麼是永續發展目標 SDGs？ 4. Presentation a. Mode of presentation a pre-recorded PODCAST by each individual student  Your podcast can be a solo storytelling, an interview, or a repurposed content show.  You must host the show, and your voice is identifiable in the podcast.  You and your guest(s) MUST speak English in the podcast.  You may ask your classmates, friends, or family members to be your guest(s) if your podcast is designed as an interview. b. Suggested Length of presentation 3-4 minutes for a solo storytelling/talk 4-5 minutes for an interview or for a repurposed content show c. Deadline for uploading the podcast (audio file) and the script (PDF file) to eeclass LANG1020 01 (M1M2) LANG1020 08 (M3M4) LANG1020 20 (R1R2) Podcast upload October 31 October 31 November 3 Peer Review (8-10 podcasts) November 1-3 November 1-3 November 4-6  Peer and self evaluation will be conducted in Week 10. Each student will be assigned 8-10 podcasts for evaluation right after the deadline. You will have 2-3 days to complete the peer evaluation by grading on eeclass and commenting under each podcast. 14 prepared by Vicky Hsu  Each podcast will be evaluated with a rubric in terms of the five categories: Content – the speaker’s knowledge and insight, relevant information and quality details (beyond the obvious), in-depth research, catchy and clever opening (topic, purpose, & sequence of events for the podcast), engaging and informative discussion/narration, and effective and impressive ending Language Use – good use of storytelling or narrative structure, effective use of open-ended and follow-up questions for interview, and good choice of words and phrases for spoken communication Delivery – well-rehearsed for grammar, vocabulary, cadence, and rhythm to keep the audience engaged; intelligible & in a conversational style Audio/Sound Design – clear recording of narration or interview, free of extraneous noise, proper use of ambient sound and sound effects Technical Production/Teamwork – adequate podcast length, smooth transition, equal contribution of teammates, accurate and well-written script 5. Preparation  Work as an individual or a team (recruiting and managing team members)  Choose an SDG as a topic  Develop and maintain the research (extracting relevant and interesting information) and podcast schedule (discussions and meetings)  Organize and schedule rehearsing and recording sessions  Manage sound quality and edit the podcast episode  keep track of the deadline and ensure that your podcast and script are uploaded on time Reminder: This podcasting practice is NOT aimed at demonstrating your talents for collecting and presenting information or expressing your opinions about SDGs. You are expected to extract practicable and feasible actions for your audience. As a general rule, podcasts are a form of entertainment. People tend to listen to podcasts to learn more about a topic or keep up with current events in a relaxing or entertaining way. 6. Points to ponder  Who are you speaking to? What is the effective way to speak to your audience?  What do you expect to happen to your audience?  What do you expect the audience to remember? (Don’t be greedy. Think about how much you remember after attending a one- or two-hour lecture.)  How would you arrange the information to have your audience become aware of the SDG in your podcast?  In what way can you deliver the key points more efficiently and effectively? 15 prepared by Vicky Hsu LANG 1010 _____ Upper-Intermediate English I Student ID ____________ Name _________________ Date _____ Podcasting－Rubric for Peer Evaluation Criteria ExcepƟonal Great Good DisappoinƟng A disaster Audience percepƟon (20%) I finished listening to the podcast, and I enjoyed the podcast episode. Content (30%) The audience gets hooked soon and effortlessly follows the whole podcast episode. The speaker(s) makes the audience learn the connecƟon of SDGs to audiences’ lives by offering appropriate and sufficient examples and explanaƟons either in a funny way or in a comprehensible way. (SDGs) The audience is at ease with the podcast episode though it sounds someƟmes a bit boring. The speaker makes the audience learn the connecƟon of SDGs to audiences’ lives by offering appropriate and sufficient examples and explanaƟons. (SDGs) The audience has difficulty understanding the podcast episode. The speaker offers examples but insufficient or inappropriate explanaƟons or connecƟons to SDGs or audiences’ lives. The content is not well-organized. SDGs The audience is disappointed or uncomfortable with the podcast episode. The speaker demonstrates liƩle understanding of SDGs or the examples, so The speaker offers illogical or incorrect explanaƟons. The informaƟon is not well- organized and even off-topic. SDGs The audience soon learns that the podcast is NOT a worthy listening. The speaker has no idea of the topic and the podcast episode at all. 16 prepared by Vicky Hsu Criteria ExcepƟonal Great Good DisappoinƟng A disaster Performance (20%) The speaker demonstrates enthusiasm about the topic during the podcast. The speaker holds the audience's aƩenƟon with good use of volume and voice inflecƟon (rhythm, tone, emphasis), and moderate speech rate. The speaker pronounces mostly everything clearly and correctly. The speaker demonstrates some enthusiasƟc feelings about the topic. The speaker raises the audience's understanding and awareness of most points. The speaker uses a clear and lively voice, but the tone is a bit flat. The speaker pronounces most words clearly and correctly. The speaker demonstrates mixed feelings about the topic and raises the audience's understanding and awareness of some points. The speaker speaks in uneven volume with liƩle voice variaƟon. Or The speaker sounds like reading from the notes. The speaker shows liƩle interest in the topic presented. The speaker fails to raise audience’s understanding or even confuses the audience. The speaker sounds like reading mostly from the notes, not talking to the audience. The speaker speaks in low volume with liƩle voice variaƟon. The speaker shows no interest in the topic presented. The speaker fails to increase the audience’s knowledge or awareness of the issue. The speaker sounds like reading from notes through the enƟre podcast. He or she speaks i in low volume and monotonous tone. Preparedness (15%) The speaker is completely prepared and must have had sufficient rehearsals. 。 The speaker is preƩy prepared and may have had several rehearsals. The speaker is somewhat prepared but might have had a couple of rehearsals. The speaker does not seem prepared and may have lacked rehearsals. The speaker is obviously unprepared at all. 17 prepared by Vicky Hsu Criteria ExcepƟonal Great Good DisappoinƟng A disaster Originality, CreaƟvity & Dynamics (15%) The design of the podcast rocks, with an excellent combinaƟon of intro, talks/conversaƟons, outro, and even sound effects. It is unique and does not like other podcast episodes I have listened to. The SDG is effecƟvely delivered in the podcast, in a well-organized framework of the SDG, examples close to our lives, and comprehensible explanaƟons/interpretaƟon. The design of the podcast engages the audience with a nice combinaƟon of intro, talks/conversaƟons, and outro. It has similar components as other podcast episodes I have listened to. The SDG is clearly delivered in the podcast, but it does not go with examples or explanaƟons close to our lives. docs.text: 1 prepared by Kevin Chiang National Tsing Hua University Upper-intermediate English I 中高級英文一 Fall 2025 Course Number LANG 101021 Credits 2 Classroom 綜二館 教室 105 Class hours □ Monday □ Tuesday □ Wednesday ■ Thursday □ Friday ■ 8:00A.M. – 9:50A.M. □ 10:10A.M. – 12:00P.M. 學生身分別 □ 頂標生 ■ 前標生 □ 中級生 □ 初級生 Instructor & Contact Information: Name Email Office & Tel Office Hour Kevin Chiang khc72003@gmail.com -- -- 加簽說明 □ 不開放人工加簽。所有學生須由選課系統亂數選課。 ■ 開放人工加簽 1-3 位學生。學生符合以下條件，得於第 1 週上課 時，向老師提出加簽申請。老師簽署申請表後，申請表送英語教育中心辦 公室。由老師進行線上簽核。  條件 1：必須於第一週到課 Requirement #1: Attend the first class  條件 2：由老師依其、申請意願、必要性、及申請先後順序認定，由老 師再第一週課前以電子郵件回覆，直至額滿為止。 Requirement #2: Depending on his/her intention provided, necessity, and sequence of application, the teacher will notify those who are enrolled before it reaches the maximum capacity allowed. 提醒：學生修讀英文領域課程，請依本校規劃選課之修業年級選課。如因個人考量， 未對應年級而逕自改於其他修業年級選課之英文領域課程，或指定加簽某特定課程， 英語教育中心與任課教師將礙難配合或處理。 Reminder: Please take the required English courses in accordance with the scheduled curriculum offered by our school. Your personal scheduling or preference of taking courses during your college stay will NOT be a valid excuse for the teacher to take your request for extra course registration into account. Course Description Primary Aim This one-year course is designed to enhance students’ overall English competence through listening, 2 prepared by Kevin Chiang speaking, and reading activities plus grammar review and vocabulary development. A four-skill coursebook plus a self-access learning project will be integrated to design learning tasks and provide opportunities for students to practice language learning strategies, get exposed to English in any form, and develop their confidence and fluency in the classroom and outside the classroom. After having taken this course, students are expected to consolidate their knowledge of English language and engage themselves more confidently and fluently in authentic communication in everyday settings and even in school settings. In this class, students will have opportunities to 1. review and practice grammar points and sentence structures to describe and discuss a variety of topics and issues related to their lives, 2. build up theme-based vocabulary and even academic words for and through reading and listening to conversations, interviews, talks, and lectures, 3. present and explain information, perspectives, or problem-solving in speaking and writing tasks or activities. Secondary Aim 1. Students are required to practice their speaking skill, including daily conversation and formal presentation, by practicing at class and get feedback from their classmates. 2. They should be able use and review the grammar they learned before college in oral and written form. 3. Each of the student needs to write a self-studying plan for the semester at the beginning and review how well he/she has completed at the end of semester. 4. Students are required to learn how to write formal essays in various genres and review their peers’. Also, they will get their peers feedback and revise their own accordingly. 5. They should practice listening skill both in the classroom and outside the classroom and show their result in self-learning review sheet. CEFR Can-do Statements (B2 and B2+) Reception Listening OVERALL LISTENING COMPREHENSION B2 Can understand the main ideas of propositionally and linguistically complex speech of both concrete and abstract topics in a standard dialect, including technical discussions in his/her field of specialization. [overall listening comprehension] EAP EOP LISTENING AS A MEMBER OF A LIVE AUDIENCE B2 Can follow the essentials of lectures, talks and reports and other forms of academic/professional presentations which are propositionally and linguistically complex. [listening as a member of a live audience] EAP EOP LISTENING TO ANNOUNCEMENTS & INSTRUCTIONS B2 Can understand announcements and messages on concrete and abstract topics spoken in standard dialect at normal speed. [listening to announcements & instructions] 3 prepared by Kevin Chiang B2+ Can understand recordings in standard dialect likely to be encountered in social, professional or academic life and identify speaker viewpoints and attitudes as well as the information content. [listening to radio, audio & recordings] EAP EOP READING CORRESPONDENCE B2 Can read correspondence relating to his/her field of interest and readily grasp the essential meaning. [reading correspondence] EOP READING INSTRUCTIONS B2 Can understand lengthy, complex instructions in his/her field, including details on conditions and warnings, provided he/she can reread difficult sections. [reading instructions] EAP EOP Interaction Spoken Speaking OVERALL SPOKEN INTERACTION B2+ Can use the language fluently, accurately and effectively on a wide range of general, academic, vocational or leisure topics, marking clearly the relationships between ideas. [overall spoken interaction] EAP EOP INFORMAL DISCUSSION (WITH FRIENDS) B2 Can take an active part in informal discussion in familiar contexts, commenting, putting point of view clearly, evaluating alternative proposals and making and responding to hypotheses. [informal discussion (with friends)] B2+ Can express his/her ideas and opinions with precision, present and respond to complex lines of argument convincingly. [informal discussion (with friends)] EAP EOP Interaction Written Writing OVERALL WRITTEN INTERACTION B2 Can express news and views effectively in writing, and relate to those of others. [overall written interaction] CORRESPONDENCE B2 Can write letters conveying degrees of emotion and highlighting the personal significance of events and experiences and commenting on the correspondent’s news and views. [correspondence] Production Spoken Speaking OVERALL SPOKEN PRODUCTION B2 Can give clear, detailed description and presentations on a wide range of subjects related to his/her field of interest, expanding and supporting ideas with subsidiary points and relevant examples. [overall spoken production] EAP EOP ADDRESSING AUDIENCES B2 Can give a clear, prepared presentation, giving reasons in support of or against a particular point of view and giving the advantages and disadvantages of various options. [addressing audiences] EAP 4 prepared by Kevin Chiang Interaction Communication Strategies TAKING THE FLOOR (TURNTAKING) B2 Can intervene appropriately in discussion, exploiting appropriate language to do so. EAP EOP B2 Can initiate, maintain, and end discourse appropriately with effective turntaking. ASKING FOR CLARIFICATION B2 Can ask follow-up questions to check that he/she has understood what a speaker intended to say, and get clarification of ambiguous points. [asking for clarification] MONITORING & REPAIR B2 Can make a note of “favorite mistakes” and consciously monitor speech for it/them. [monitoring & repair] EAP C1 Can backtrack when he/she encounters a difficulty and reformulate what he/she wants to say without fully interrupting the flow of speech. [monitoring & repair] EAP EOP Control GRAMMATICAL ACCURACY B2+ Good grammatical control. Occasional “slips” or non- systematic errors and minor flaws in sentence structure may still occur, but they are rare and can often be corrected in retrospect. [grammatical accuracy] VOCABULARY CONTROL B2 Lexical accuracy is generally high, though some confusion and incorrect word choice does occur without hindering communication. [vocabulary control] 英文核心能力指標 University Student Core Competency Indicators 1. 英語溝通與表達能力 (ability to communicate and express oneself in English) 30% 2. 深度分析與組織思考的能力 (ability to think critically and organize ideas logically in English) 10% 3. 英語學習策略與技巧 (knowledge of English learning strategies and techniques) 30% 4. 對英語與多元文化的國際視野 (global views of English and multicultural diversity) 15% 5. 善用英語學習資源，培養獨立學習英語的習慣與能力 (ability to use existing English learning resources and development of independent self-learning habit) 15% Teaching materials and References Uniform textbook Christina Latham-Koenig, Clive Oxenden, and Kate Chomacki. Final Exam 30% Requirements & Rules 1. Class attendance, lesson preparation and active class participation are required. *Attendance will be taken almost every session throughout the semester. If you are all present, you will get 80 (i.e., the primitive score) in the category “Attendance and Participation.” Each absence from class costs 10 from this primitive score. Being late for more than 10 minutes is treated as absence from that hour (5 will be deducted). If your absence or leave hours reach 12 hours (one third of the total class hours), you will NOT be allowed to take the final exam. The first one leave with valid proof cause no grade deduction, but more than 1 leave will result in deduction in Attendance and Participation. EMAILING for your absence or leave is A MUST to get the instructor’s approval. Please present the valid proof to complete the leave procedures WITHIN TWO WEEKS from the next day of your absence. 2. Absence from a class is no excuse for not submitting the due assignments or not knowing the given assignment and what has been discussed in that class. It is your responsibility to submit the due assignments as you get well and ask your classmates or me what has been covered or assigned in the class. Any late submission of the homework will be blocked automatically by the system. You have got to send a request to unblock and submit your homework later. You will be deducted 5 points for any single day of late submission. 3. CHEATING on the exam and PLAGIARISM in assignments or presentations are ABSOLUTELY NOT PERMITTED. If someone is found cheating or plagiarizing, it means he/she will get a zero point for that exam, the assignment, or the presentation. 4. There will be NO MAKE-UP EXAMS unless you have valid and official reasons for absence or leave BEFOREHAND. 5. Make sure to mute or turn off your mobile phone before class begins. During the class, no access to mobile devices (phones, tablets) is allowed unless permission is given for a specific learning task or activity. 6. No handouts or assignment worksheets are reissued. Please manage and keep them in a safe place or condition. 6 prepared by Kevin Chiang 7 Artificial Intelligence (AI) application software generated reports or assignments are not allowed: As a high-intermediate English I/II student, only content completed by a him/herself or as part of an assigned group is accepted. Those were found using AI-generated report will not be accepted and treated as score zero. Liu liumeitzu@gapp.nthu.edu.tw N/A N/A 2 Course Aims / Description Primary aim This one-year course aims to enhance students’ overall English competence by developing their listening, speaking, reading, and writing skills. Through interactive activities, grammar review, and vocabulary expansion, students will strengthen their ability to communicate effectively in both everyday and academic contexts. The course incorporates a four-skill coursebook and a self-access learning project to provide structured learning tasks and opportunities for independent practice. Students will also be introduced to essential academic English skills, such as summarizing texts and writing structured essays, as well as practicing note-taking and understanding lectures to improve their ability to engage with academic materials. By the end of the course, students are expected to demonstrate greater confidence and fluency in authentic communication, whether in daily interactions or academic discussions. Subsidiary aim In this class, students will have opportunities to 1. review and practice grammar points and sentence structures to describe and discuss a variety of topics and issues related to their life 2. build up theme-based vocabulary and even academic words for and through reading and listening to conversations, interviews, talks, and lectures 3. practice academic skills such as outlining, summarizing, and critical thinking while listening, reading, speaking, and writing 4. present information, perspectives, or problem-solving in speaking and writing tasks or activities Corresponding CEFR Can-do statements 1. Primary aim Upper-intermediate English I is an integrated course designed to develop students' four English skills (i.e., listening, speaking, reading, & writing) with an emphasis on speaking and listening. In this course, students will: -Identify listening problems and develop listening strategies and skills, -Gain confidence in speaking and improve speaking fluency, pronunciation, and conversation strategies, -Develop general reading skills, including word skills and comprehension strategies. 2. A four-skill textbook plus a self‐access learning project will be integrated to construct learning tasks and provide opportunities for students to practice language learning strategies, get exposed to English in any form, and develop their confidence and fluency in the classroom and outside the classroom. After having taken this course, students are expected to build a solid foundation for their current and future academic activities in English language and engage themselves more confidently and fluently in authentic communications, in both academic settings and everyday life. Can express news and views effectively in writing, and relate to those of others. 7. Has a sufficient range of language to be able to give clear descriptions, express viewpoints and develop arguments without much conspicuous searching for words, using some complex sentence forms to do so. Primary aim This one-year course is designed to enhance freshman students’ overall English competence. A four-skill coursebook plus a self-access learning project will be integrated to meet students’ need for the language practically and academically. After having taken this course, they are expected to consolidate their knowledge of English language, build up a learning routine, and acquire more access to learning recourses. 2. The student never attends class nor submits assignments. 2. The student is absent or asks for leave with NO valid excuses for more than 6 classes. 3. The student never explains to or discusses with the teacher his/her difficulty in taking care of this subject. 4. The student neither offers valid excuses on his application for course withdrawal nor notifies the teacher beforehand. 學生如遇有以下情形，其停修申請將不予「同意」 1. 學生未曾到課或繳交任何作業。 2. 學生無故缺席或未有證明之請假超過六次 3. 學生從未向老師解釋、或與之討論，修讀本課程時的困難 4. 學生未在停修申請上敘明或以其他通訊方式告知老師停修本課程之原 因 Instructor & Contact Information: Name Email Office & Tel Office Hour 吳聖鵬 hank.spwu@gmail.com N/A N/A Course Aims / Description Primary aim This one-year course is designed to enhance students’ overall English competence through listening, speaking, and reading activities plus grammar review and vocabulary development. A four-skill coursebook plus a self-access learning project will be integrated to design learning tasks and provide opportunities for students to practice language learning strategies, compare and synthesize ideas and arguments, and develop their confidence and fluency in and outside the classroom. After having taken this course, students are expected to consolidate their knowledge of English language and engage themselves more confidently and fluently in authentic communication in everyday settings and expand academic vocabulary and 3 knowledge of definitions and parts of words, such as prefixes, suffixes and roots. Subsidiary aim In this course students will have opportunities to 1. review and practice grammar points and sentence structures to describe and discuss a variety of topics and issues related to their life 2. build up theme-based vocabulary and even academic words for and through reading and listening to conversations, interviews, talks, and lectures 3. practice academic skills such as outlining, summarizing, critical thinking while listening, reading, speaking and writing 4. manage and present information, perspectives, or problem-solving in speaking and writing tasks or activities Corresponding CEFR Can-do statements 1. Can understand the main ideas of propositionally and linguistically complex speech of both concrete and abstract topics in a standard dialect, including technical discussions in his/her field of specialization. [overall listening comprehension] 2. Can follow the essentials of lectures, talks and reports and other forms of academic/professional presentations which are propositionally and linguistically complex. [listening as a member of a live audience] 3. Can read with a large degree of independence, adapting style and speed of reading to different texts and purposes, and using appropriate reference sources selectively. Has a broad active reading vocabulary, but may experience some difficulty with low-frequency vocabulary. [overall reading comprehension] 4. Can interact with a degree of fluency and spontaneity that makes regular interaction, and sustained relationships with native speakers quite possible without imposing strain on either party. [overall spoken interaction] 5. Can give clear, detailed description and presentations on a wide range of subjects related to his/her field of interest, expanding and supporting ideas with subsidiary points and relevant examples. [overall spoken production] 6. Can write clear, detailed texts on a variety of subjects related to his/her field of interest, synthesizing and evaluating information and arguments from a number of sources. [overall written production] 7. Can pass on detailed information reliably. [propositional precision] 4 英文核心能力指標 University Student Core Competency Indicators 1. 英語溝通與表達能力 (ability to communicate and express oneself in English) [30%] 2. 深度分析與組織思考的能力 (ability to think critically and organize ideas logically in English) [10%] 3. 英語學習策略與技巧 (knowledge of English learning strategies and techniques) [30%] 4. 對英語與多元文化的國際視野 (global views of English and multicultural diversity) [15%] 5. 善用英語學習資源，培養獨立學習英語的習慣與能力 (ability to use existing English learning resources and development of independent self-learning habit) [15%] Teaching Materials and References Textbook(s) Christina Latham-Koenig, Clive Oxenden, and Kate Chomacki. The student never attends class nor submits assignments. 2. The student is absent or asks for leave with NO valid excuses for more than 6 classes. 3. The student never explains to or discusses with the teacher his/her difficulty in taking care of this subject. 4. The student neither offers valid excuses on his application for course withdrawal nor notifies the teacher beforehand. 學生如遇有以下情形，其停修申請將不予「同意」 1. 學生未曾到課或繳交任何作業。 2. 學生無故缺席或未有證明之請假超過六次 3. 學生從未向老師解釋、或與之討論，修讀本課程時的困難 4. 學生未在停修申請上敘明或以其他通訊方式告知老師停修本課程之原 因 Instructor & Contact Information Name Email Office & Tel Office Hour 湯智群 chihtang.nthu@gmail.com By appointment By appointment ; Announcements such as classroom rearrangements, additional readings, exam details, grades, 2 etc., will be posted on eLearn platform as an announcement with an email notification Course Aims / Description Primary Aim This English course is designed to enhance students' understanding and usage of vocabulary and expressions commonly found in everyday life. The course is divided into three levels, each aimed at progressively improving students' ability to express ideas clearly and confidently in both workplace and social settings. In addition to speaking skills, the course also focuses on developing listening, reading, and writing abilities, providing a comprehensive understanding of English grammatical structures. By the end of the course, students will be better equipped to communicate effectively and navigate various situations with ease. Whether you're looking to improve your professional communication or enhance your social interactions, this course will provide the tools you need to succeed. Subsidiary Aim Explore secondary objectives that support the main aims, such as developing specific skills or knowledge. By the end of the session, students should have a clearer understanding of how to identify and select main, subsidiary, and personal aims for their lessons, as well as the various factors that influence these decisions. They will also gain practical experience in evaluating and refining lesson objectives to enhance teaching effectiveness and learner outcomes. [overall listening comprehension] EAP EOP UNDERSTANDING INTERACTION BETWEEN NATIVE SPEAKERS B2 Can with some effort catch much of what is said around him/her, but may find it difficult to participate effectively in discussion with several native speakers who do not modify their language in any way. [understanding interaction between native speakers] LISTENING AS A MEMBER OF A LIVE AUDIENCE B2 Can follow the essentials of lectures, talks and reports and other forms of academic/professional presentations which are propositionally and linguistically complex. [listening as a member of a live audience] EAP EOP LISTENING TO ANNOUNCEMENTS & INSTRUCTIONS 3 B2 Can understand announcements and messages on concrete and abstract topics spoken in standard dialect at normal speed. [listening to announcements & instructions] LISTENING TO RADIO, AUDIO & RECORDINGS B2 Can understand most radio documentaries and most other recorded or broadcast audio material delivered in standard dialect and can identify the speaker’s mood, tone, etc. [listening to radio, audio & recordings] WATCHING TV & FILM B2 Can understand most TV news and current affairs programs. [watching TV & film] Reception Reading OVERALL READING COMPREHENSION B2 Can read with a large degree of independence, adapting style and speed of reading to different texts and purposes, and using appropriate reference sources selectively. Has a broad active reading vocabulary, but may experience some difficulty with low- frequency vocabulary. [overall reading comprehension] READING CORRESPONDENCE B2 Can read correspondence relating to his/her field of interest and readily grasp the essential meaning. [reading correspondence] EOP READING FOR ORIENTATION B2 Can scan quickly through long and complex texts, locating relevant details. [reading for orientation] EAP B2 Can quickly identify the content and relevance off news items, articles and reports on a wide range of professional topics, deciding whether closer study is worthwhile. [reading for orientation] EAP EOP READING FOR INFORMATION & ARGUMENT B2 Can understand articles and reports concerned with contemporary problems in which the writer adopts particular stances or viewpoints. [reading for information & argument] B2+ Can obtain information, ideas and opinions from highly specialized sources within his/her field. [reading for information & argument] EAP EOP READING INSTRUCTIONS B2 Can understand lengthy, complex instructions in his/her field, including details on conditions and warnings, provided he/she can reread difficult sections. [reading instructions] EAP EOP n SpokeSpeaking OVERALL SPOKEN INTERACTION B2 Can interact with a degree of fluency and spontaneity that makes regular interaction, and sustained relationships with native speakers 4 quite possible without imposing strain on either party. [overall spoken interaction] B2 Can highlight the personal significance of events and experiences, account for and sustain views clearly by providing relevant explanations and arguments. [overall spoken interaction] B2+ Can use the language fluently, accurately and effectively on a wide range of general, academic, vocational or leisure topics, marking clearly the relationships between ideas. [overall spoken interaction] UNDERSTANDING NATIVE SPEAKER INTERLOCUTOR B2 Can understand in detail what is said to him/her in the standard spoken language even in a noisy environment. [understanding native speaker interlocutor] CONVERSATION B2 Can engage in extended conversation on most general topics in a clearly participatory fashion, even in a noisy environment. [conversation] B2 Can sustain relationships with native speakers without unintentionally amusing or irritating them or requiring them to behave other than they would with a native speaker. [conversation] INFORMAL DISCUSSION (WITH FRIENDS) B2 Can take an active part in informal discussion in familiar contexts, commenting, putting point of view clearly, evaluating alternative proposals and making and responding to hypotheses. [informal discussion (with friends)] B2 Can with some effort catch much of what is said around him/her in discussion, but may find it difficult to participate effectively in discussion with several native speakers who do not modify their language in any way. [informal discussion (with friends)] B2 Can account for and sustain his/her opinions in discussion by providing relevant explanation, arguments and comments. [informal discussion (with friends)] EAP EOP FORMAL DISCUSSION (MEETINGS) B2 Can participate actively in routine and non-routine formal discussion. [formal discussion (meetings)] EAP EOP B2 Can follow the discussion on matters related to his/her field, understand in detail the points given prominence by the speaker. [formal discussion (meetings)] EAP EOP GOAL-ORIENTED COOPERATION (E.G., REPAIRING A CAR, DISCUSSING A DOCUMENT, ORGANIZING AN EVENT) 5 B2 Can understand detailed instructions reliably. [goal-oriented cooperation (e.g., repairing a car, discussing a document, organizing an event)] B2 Can help along the progress of the work by inviting others to join in, say what they think, etc. [goal-oriented cooperation (e.g., repairing a car, discussing a document, organizing an event)] B2 Can outline an issue or a problem clearly, speculating about causes or consequences, and weighing advantages and disadvantages of different approaches. [goal-oriented cooperation (e.g., repairing a car, discussing a document, organizing an event)] EAP EOP INFORMATION EXCHANGE B2 Can pass on detailed information reliably. [information exchange] B2 Can give a clear, detailed description of how to carry out a procedure. [information exchange] EAP EOP B2 Can synthesize and report information and arguments from a number of sources. [information exchange] EAP EOP INTERVIEWING AND BEING INTERVIEWED B2 Can take initiatives in an interview, expand and develop ideas with little help or prodding from an interviewer. [interviewing and being interviewed] EOP Interaction Written Writing OVERALL WRITTEN INTERACTION B2 Can express news and views effectively in writing, and relate to those of others. [overall written interaction] CORRESPONDENCE B2 Can write letters conveying degrees of emotion and highlighting the personal significance of events and experiences and commenting on the correspondent’s news and views. [correspondence] Production Spoken Speaking OVERALL SPOKEN PRODUCTION B2 Can give clear, detailed description and presentations on a wide range of subjects related to his/her field of interest, expanding and supporting ideas with subsidiary points and relevant examples. [overall spoken production] EAP EOP SUSTAINED MONOLOGUE: DESCRIBING EXPERIENCE B2 Can give clear, detailed description on a wide range of subjects to his/her field of interest. [sustained monologue: describing experience] SUSTAINED MONOLOGUE: PUTTING A CASE (E.G., IN A DEBATE) 6 B2 Can develop a clear argument, expanding and supporting his/her points of view at some length with subsidiary points and relevant examples. [sustained monologue: putting a case (e.g., in a debate)] EAP EOP B2 Can explain a viewpoint on a topical issue giving the advantages and disadvantages of various options. [sustained monologue: putting a case (e.g., in a debate)] EAP EOP PUBLIC ANNOUNCEMENTS B2 Can deliver announcements on most general topics with a degree of clarity, fluency and spontaneity which causes no strain or inconvenience t the listener. [public announcements] ADDRESSING AUDIENCES B2 Can give a clear, prepared presentation, giving reasons in support of or against a particular point of view and giving the advantages and disadvantages of various options. [addressing audiences] EAP B2 Can take a series of follow-up questions with a degree of fluency and spontaneity which poses no strain for either him/herself or the audience. [addressing audiences] Production Written OVERALL WRITTEN PRODUCTION B2 Can write clear, detailed texts on a variety of subjects related to his/her field of interest, synthesizing and evaluating information and arguments from a number of sources. [overall written production] EAP EOP CREATIVE WRITING B2 Can write clear, detailed descriptions on a variety of subjects related to his/her field of interest. [creative writing] B2 Can write a review of a film, book, or play. [creative writing] EAP EAP REPORTS & ESSAYS B2 Can write an essay or report which develops an argument, giving reasons in support of or against a particular point of view and explaining the advantages and disadvantages of various options. [reports & essays] EAP EOP B2 Can synthesize information and arguments from a number of sources. [reports & essays] EAP Receptio n Communi cation Strategies IDENTIFYING CUES & INFERRING (SPOKEN & WRITTEN) B2 Can use a variety of strategies to achieve comprehension, including listening for main points, checking comprehension by using contextual clues. [identifying cues & inferring (spoken & written)] EAP 7 Interaction Communi cation Strategies TAKING THE FLOOR (TURNTAKING) B2 Can intervene appropriately in discussion, exploiting appropriate language to do so. [taking the floor (turntaking)] EAP EOP B2 Can initiate, maintain, and end discourse appropriately with effective turntaking. [taking the floor (turntaking)] B2 Can initiate discourse, take his/her turn when appropriate and end conversation when he/she needs to, though he/she may not always do this elegantly. [taking the floor (turntaking)] B2 Can use stock phrases (e.g., “That’s a difficult question to answer”) to gain time and keep the turn whilst formulating what to say. [taking the floor (turntaking)] COOPERATING B2 Can help the discussion along on familiar ground, confirming comprehension, inviting others in, etc. [cooperating] ASKING FOR CLARIFICATION B2 Can ask follow-up questions to check that he/she has understood what a speaker intended to say, and get clarification of ambiguous points. [asking for clarification] PLANNING B2 Can plan what is to be said and the means to say it, considering the effect on the recipient(s). [planning] COMPENSATING B2 Can use circumlocution and paraphrase to cover gaps in vocabulary and structure. [compensating] EAP MONITORING & REPAIR B2 Can correct slips and errors if he/she becomes conscious of them or if they have led to misunderstandings. [monitoring & repair] B2 Can make a note of “favorite mistakes” and consciously monitor speech for it/them. [monitoring & repair] EAP Working with Text NOTE-TAKING (LECTURES, SEMINARS, ETC.) [note-taking (lectures, seminars, etc.) EAP PROCESSING TEXT B2 Can summarize a wide range of factual and imaginative texts, commenting on and discussing contrasting points of view and the main themes. [processing text] EAP 8 B2 Can summarize extracts from news items, interviews or documentaries containing opinions, argument and discussion. [processing text] EAP B2 Can summarize the plot and sequence of events in a film or play. [processing text] EAP Communicative Language Competence Range GENERAL LINGUISTIC RANGE B2 Has a sufficient range of language to be able to give clear descriptions, express viewpoints and develop arguments without much conspicuous searching for words, using some complex sentence forms to do so. [general linguistic range] EAP B2+ Can express him/herself clearly and without much sign of having to restrict what he/she wants to say. [processing text] VOCABULARY RANGE B2 Has a good range of vocabulary for matters connected to his/her field and most general topics. [vocabulary range] Control GRAMMATICAL ACCURACY B2 Shows a relatively high degree of grammatical control. Does not make mistakes which lead to misunderstanding. [grammatical accuracy] VOCABULARY CONTROL B2 Lexical accuracy is generally high, though some confusion and incorrect word choice does occur without hindering communication. [vocabulary control] PHONOLOGICAL CONTROL B2 Has a clear, natural pronunciation and intonation. [phonological control] ORTHOGRAPHIC CONTROL B2 Can produce clearly intelligible continuous writing, which follows standard layout and paragraphing conventions. [orthographic control] EAP EOP B2 Spelling, punctuation and layout are accurate but may show signs of mother tongue influence. [orthographic control] Sociolinguistic SOCIOLINGUISTIC APPROPRIATENESS B2 Can with some effort keep up with and contribute to group discussions even when speech is fast and colloquial. [sociolinguistic appropriateness] B2 Can sustain relationships with native speakers without intentionally amusing or irritating them or requiring them to behave other than they would with a native speaker. [sociolinguistic appropriateness] B2 Can express him/herself appropriately in situations and avoid crass errors of formulation. [sociolinguistic appropriateness] 9 Pragmatic FLEXIBILITY B2 Can adjust to the changes of direction, style and emphasis normally found in conversation. [flexibility] B2 Can vary formulation of what he/she wants to say. [flexibility] TAKING THE FLOOR (TURNTAKING) B2 Can intervene appropriately in discussion, exploiting appropriate language to do so. [taking the floor (turntaking)] B2 Can initiate, maintain and end discourse appropriately with effective turntaking. [taking the floor (turntaking)] B2 Can initiate discourse, take his/her turn when appropriate and end conversation when he/she needs to, though he/she may not always do this elegantly. Kakga 80921005l@gapps.ntnu.edu.tw Upon request Course Aims / Description Primary aim This year-long course is designed to strengthen students’ overall academic English proficiency through integrated listening, speaking, and reading activities, complemented by grammar review and vocabulary expansion. The curriculum incorporates a four-skill coursebook alongside a self-access learning project, fostering active engagement in language learning both inside and outside the classroom. Through carefully designed tasks, students will develop effective learning strategies, gain exposure to authentic English in various contexts, and build confidence in their communication skills. By the end of the course, students are expected to consolidate their language knowledge and communicate more fluently and confidently in both everyday interactions and academic settings. 2 Subsidiary aim This course provides students with the opportunity to: 1. Review and apply essential grammar structures and sentence patterns to effectively describe and discuss a range of topics and issues relevant to their lives. 2. Develop theme-based academic vocabulary, including high-frequency academic terms, through engagement with various reading and listening materials such as conversations, interviews, lectures, and talks. 3. Enhance academic skills, including outlining, summarizing, note-taking, and critical thinking, while integrating listening, reading, speaking, and writing activities. 4. Present and articulate information, perspectives, and problem-solving approaches through structured speaking and writing tasks. 5. Foster academic English proficiency in alignment with Taiwan’s Bilingual Nation 2030 policy, equipping students with the necessary language skills to engage confidently in academic and professional settings in an increasingly bilingual environment. 3. Corresponding CEFR Can-do statements Can-do statement #1 [LISTENING] can with some effort catch much of what is said around me, but may find it difficult to understand a discussion between several speakers who do not modify their language in any way. Can-do statement #2 [READING] can understand articles, reports and reviews in which the writers express specific points of view. Can-do statement #3 [SPEAKING INTERACTION] can take an active part in conversation, expressing clearly my points of view, ideas or feelings naturally with effective turn-taking. Can-do statement #4 [SPEAKING PRODUCTION] can present a topical issue in a critical manner and weigh up the advantages and disadvantages of various options. Can-do statement #5 [WRITTEN PRODUCTION] can write at length about topical issues, even though complex concepts may be oversimplified, and can correct many of my mistakes in the process. Can-do statement #6 [STRATEGIES] can generally correct slips and errors if I become aware of them or if they have led to misunderstandings. Can-do statement #7 [QUALITY OF LANGUAGE] can link what I say or write into clear, well-organized text, though I may not always do this smoothly so there may be some “jumps.” 4. Corresponding EAP Can-do statements Listening ＊Recognising lecture structure: understanding relationships in the lecture understanding relations within the sentence/complex sentences importance markers, signposts. 3 ＊Deducing the meaning of unfamiliar words and word groups. ＊Recognizing implications: information not explicitly stated recognising the speaker's attitude. Evaluating the importance of information - selecting information. Speaking ＊Making a presentation: the structure of presentations making and using notes to speak from. ＊Introducing the topic giving the information in detail sequencing, describing similarities and differences comparing and contrasting illustrating a point - giving examples and referring to research emphasising a point summarising and concluding. ＊Controlling the discussion: leading the discussion changing the subject - moving on speeding up things coming to a conclusion. Reading ＊Understanding meaning: deducing the meaning of unfamiliar words and word groups relations within the sentence/complex sentences implications - information not explicitly stated, conceptual meaning, e.g. comparison, purpose, cause, effect. ＊Understanding relationships in the text: - text structure the communicative value of sentences relations between the parts of a text through lexical and grammatical cohesion devices and indicators in discourse. Writing ＊Using sources: making notes and writing up notes - paraphrasing, summarising, quoting & referring to sources, writing a bibliography. ＊Writing descriptions of places, objects etc classifying and categorising comparing and contrasting reporting and narrating. ＊Describing processes and developments: expressing purpose, means and method, degrees of certainty, reasons and explanations/cause and effect describing developments and changes describing a sequence of events/time relations. 英文核心能力指標 University Student Core Competency Indicators 1. 英語溝通與表達能力 20% (ability to communicate and express oneself in English) 2. 深度分析與組織思考的能力 20% (ability to think critically and organize ideas logically in English) 3. 英語學習策略與技巧 20% (knowledge of English learning strategies and techniques) 4. 對英語與多元文化的國際視野 20% (global views of English and multicultural diversity) 5. 善用英語學習資源，培養獨立學習英語的習慣與能力 20% (ability to use existing English learning resources and development of independent self-learning habit) 4 Teaching materials and References Uniform textbook Christina Latham-Koenig, Clive Oxenden, and Kate Chomacki. (2021) American English File 4, 3rd Edition. New York: Oxford University Press. ISBN: 978-0-19-490685-2 CEFR Scale □ B2+ ■ B2 □ B1 □ A2+ □ A2 Platform for course material Teachers may upload the teaching materials such as audio files, lectures slides, assignments, quizzes, and supplementary materials or hyperlinks to either of the learning platforms: eeclass https://eeclass.nthu.edu.tw eLearn https://elearn.nthu.edu.tw Grading Policy 1. Attendance and participation 20% 2. Midterm exam 20% 3. Final Exam 20% 4. Assignments & quizzes 20% 5. Presentations/Role plays/Show-n-Tell 20% Note: The percentage of this grading scheme is subject to possible adjustments. To be announced. Requirements & Rules 1. Class attendance, lesson preparation and active class participation are required.  As you are all present whenever the instructor takes the roll, you will get 60% in this category Attendance and Participation. 經常性點名，全勤者可得「出席與參與」項目中的 60%成績。  Each skip will cost 2 points from the category Attendance and Participation (up to 15 points in the final grade). 未假不到課（翹課），每 次從「出席與參與」成績（占學期成績 15 分）扣 2 分。  If you are absent in case of UNCONTROLLABLE situations (e.g. illness, emergency, important occasions, etc.), please apply for a leave on the Student Leave System on Academic Information System of National Tsing Hua University or on the iNTHU app (from the Office of Student Affair website), with clear leave information, including leave type, leave period, and reasons (must be clear and valid enough for the teacher’s approval). As the reasons or the documents are not clear, valid or sufficient enough, the teacher may deny the application. 遇不可抗力情形需請假者，請於本校校務資 訊系統上的學生請假系統或下載 iNTHU APP，填寫資料（請假類別、請假日期、請假事由）。請假 事由須合理並敘述清楚，提供老師是否准假之參考。請假單上的理由或所附證明文件不清楚 或不充分時，該次請假申請得不予核准。  Please observe the information you are expected to offer for each of the following leave NTHU 學生請假 Q&A 5 types:  When requesting sick leave, please specify in the reason column the significant symptoms affecting your ability to attend class, as well as any medical consultation or medication taken. Only those who provide a doctor's certificate of diagnosis are eligible to submit makeup assignments. Medical receipts or prescription slips are not considered official proof of sick leave. 請病假時，請於理由欄位說明影響上課之顯著症狀，就醫或服藥等處 置。只有提出請假當日的醫生診斷證明者才能補交作業，就醫收據或藥單都不算病假正式證 明。  For personal leave, please describe the uncontrollable event and how it makes you absent from the class. 請事假時，請於理由欄位敘明事件，並說明該事件如何致使你無法前來上 課。  No leave application will be approved on the dates of presentations, peer evaluations, and midterm/final exams. Please care for your health and reserve the time for these important class activities. 報告、同儕互評、期中／期末考當日不得請假。請注意身心健康 並為這些重要課程活動預留時間。  There will be NO make-up exams or presentations unless you apply for leave with valid and official reasons for your absence beforehand. 無合理且正式的缺課原因，將不予補考 或補行報告。  You are expected to apply for leave before the class you are absent from. Any overdue leave application must be made within 7 days from the last day of absence. 請假已事先申請為原 則。逾期請假申請必須於 7 日內補請。未能於規定期間申請者，均以曠課論。  Being late for more than 10 minutes (with no valid excuses) is treated as absence from that hour. No late submission will be accepted or graded unless the instructor approves or grants your application for extension of submission. 作業請按時繳交（或上傳）。未獲教師同意可延遲繳 交者或超過寬限期，其遲交作業不批改、不計分。  Frequent late submissions with no valid excuses or under controllable circumstances will 6 NOT be accepted or graded since the third late assignment. 無合理原因或非為不可抗力情形 的慣性遲交作業，第三份起將不予批改與計分。 4. Plagiarism on assignments and cheating on the exam is absolutely unacceptable. If someone is found plagiarizing or cheating, it means he/she will get a zero point for that assignment or exam. 嚴禁抄襲與作弊。抄襲與作弊者，學期成績以不及格處理。情節重大時，將提報至相關單 位依校規處理。 5. AI-assisted reports and assignments are allowed in limited instances: AI can be used to prepare for reports and assignments by brainstorming and tentative revision, but students must show how AI helps them reach the result. 僅限使用生成式 AI 於作業或報告之準備（如腦力激盪與初步 修訂等），學生須註明 AI 如何用於協作其作業或報告。 6. Penalty for no or poor participation in pair or group work Students are expected to take part in pair or group activities. Failure to engage in these activities (due to you absence or lateness) will lead to reductions in grades awarded. Sometimes the reduction may be suggested by other group members; in other circumstances, the instructor may reduce the grade awarded without reference to other group members. 學生負有參與雙人 或小組活動之義務。如因個人遲到或缺席導致小組活動無法順利進行，請假或缺席者該次活動成 績將以扣分或甚至 0 分計算。 7.  Mobile devices are only used for educational purposes relevant to the subject or tasks in the classroom setting with the permission of or at the request of the instructor. Using mobile devices for studying other subjects or entertaining purposes is absolutely prohibited. Students who violate the regulation will be considered absent from the class or asked to leave the classroom. 行動裝置僅限於學習活動，使用須獲得老師同意或遵照老師指示。嚴禁 使用行動裝置研習其他課程或娛樂使用。違反規定者，以「未到課」處置，亦得請違規者離開 教室。  During class students are not to be seen with a cell phone in hand or on the desk. Mobile phones are expected to be turned off or switched to a silent mode. 課程進行時，請關閉行動 電話或轉為靜音模式。未獲教師指示或許可，不得於上課時間使用或放置於桌上。 8.
